title: 6.1.1 Establish the current identity and domain
text: id="611-establish-the-current-identity-and-domain">6.1.1 Establish the current identity and domain §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A Windows session, or domain credentials on Kali. A Windows username alone does not establish the identity used for network authentication . Where to look: Start in the current Windows token and logon context; then inspect domain/DC discovery, DNS records and time. On Kali, use the explicit domain credentials and resolver context in the complete procedure. Expected behavior / secure boundary: A member workstation can identify its domain and DC when its DNS and connectivity work. A local account, a /netonly process or a remote session can have different local and network identities. Multiple DCs are normal; the PDC emulator is not the only usable LDAP or Kerberos server. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.1.1.1 Baseline identity, DC and time checks
text: id="6111-baseline-identity-dc-and-time-checks">6.1.1.1 Baseline identity, DC and time checks Run: Windows. Requires: Current token; domain/DC queries additionally need a usable domain/network context. Effect: Reads identity, discovery and time state. whoami /all echo %USERDNSDOMAIN% echo %USERDOMAIN% echo %LOGONSERVER% nltest /dsgetdc:DOMAIN nltest /dclist:DOMAIN w32tm /query /status <h2

title: 6.1.1.2 PowerShell domain and DNS queries
text: id="6112-powershell-domain-and-dns-queries">6.1.1.2 PowerShell domain and DNS queries Run: Windows PowerShell. Requires: Domain .NET context for the domain query; DNS connectivity for SRV lookups. Effect: Reads directory/DNS state. [System.DirectoryServices.ActiveDirectory.Domain]::GetCurrentDomain() Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.DOMAIN Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _kerberos._tcp.DOMAIN What this checks: whoami describes the process token. Domain environment variables are clues, not proof of successful authentication. nltest discovers a DC; SRV lookups test the naming layer. A plausible time source is useful, but does not itself prove the clock agrees with the KDC . <h2

title: 6.1.1.3 Interpret the output
text: id="6113-interpret-the-output">6.1.1.3 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. whoami: EXAMPLE\analyst USERDNSDOMAIN: example.test DC: \\DC01.example.test Address: \\192.0.2.10 Domain Name: example.test Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at EXAMPLE\analyst The current token names a domain-style identity. Record its SID /groups and how this session was obtained. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups DC01.example.test / 192.0.2.10 A discovered DC name and address. Check the required service route; do not treat discovery as an LDAP bind. §6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain No DC found Discovery failed in this context. Check DNS and route; this does not prove the credentials are wrong. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary Stop when: The local/network identity, domain/DC and relevant naming/time/route dependencies are recorded. Revisit only when: Identity, DC, resolver, clock or source route changes. <h2

title: 6.1.1.4 Decide and continue
text: id="6114-decide-and-continue">6.1.1.4 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation Domain/DC naming and the required protocol work: enumerate users, groups and shares. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups Ruled out in this context This is a local account with no domain authentication context: obtain or select a supported domain query context first. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope Inconclusive / failed check Discovery or time checks fail: repair that dependency before judging an account or technique. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary <h2

title: 6.1.1.5 Tooling and complete procedure
text: id="6115-tooling-and-complete-procedure">6.1.1.5 Tooling and complete procedure Windows built-ins first; PowerShell DNS/.NET alternatives require Windows domain connectivity. No RSAT prerequisite for the native baseline. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants . Study mechanisms and alternatives . Shared concepts . §6.6.2 — Choose an approach .

title: 6.3.5 Select a credential source on a controlled host
text: id="635-select-a-credential-source-on-a-controlled-host">6.3.5 Select a credential source on a controlled host §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output An authorized host/session with known effective token and privileges. Ordinary-user access does not grant access to every credential source. Where to look: Start with current-user tickets and application configuration. For elevated contexts, choose among LSASS, matched SAM/SYSTEM, SECURITY/SYSTEM, Credential Manager/DPAPI or DC-specific NTDS/replication according to the exact question. Expected behavior / secure boundary: Protected process access, VBS/Credential Guard and user/machine DPAPI boundaries can prevent collection. Missing registry values do not prove protection is off. Modern Windows does not guarantee plaintext passwords in LSASS. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.3.5.1 Baseline token and protection checks
text: id="6351-baseline-token-and-protection-checks">6.3.5.1 Baseline token and protection checks Run: Windows. Requires: Current token; registry/process information can be restricted. Effect: Reads privilege/protection clues; does not dump LSASS. whoami /all tasklist /fi "imagename eq lsass.exe" reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v RunAsPPL reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v LsaCfgFlags reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard /v LsaCfgFlags <h2

title: 6.3.5.2 Runtime protection checks using CIM
text: id="6352-runtime-protection-checks-using-cim">6.3.5.2 Runtime protection checks using CIM Run: Windows PowerShell. Requires: CIM availability and access to the local DeviceGuard class. Effect: Reads runtime security-service state. Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard | Select-Object SecurityServicesConfigured,SecurityServicesRunning,VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus What this checks: The commands establish token/process/protection context before choosing a collector. They do not themselves dump credentials. A configured protection value and running security service are different kinds of evidence. <h2

title: 6.3.5.3 Interpret the output
text: id="6353-interpret-the-output">6.3.5.3 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Token: medium integrity; Administrators SID deny-only LSASS process exists RunAsPPL registry query: value not found Memory read: access denied Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at Deny-only / medium token The process is not equivalent to an elevated administrative token. Inspect usable privileges and the appropriate local escalation path. §6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain LSASS exists Normal Windows process presence. No secret residency or readable memory is proved. §6.3.5.1 — Select a credential source on a controlled host Missing value / denied read Protection and access remain unresolved. Use runtime/protection evidence and an alternative authorized source; do not assume an empty store. §6.3.5.1 — Select a credential source on a controlled host Stop when: One source is matched to actual token rights and protection state. Revisit only when: Privilege, logon session, protection state or source access changes. <h2

title: 6.3.5.4 Decide and continue
text: id="6354-decide-and-continue">6.3.5.4 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation Exact source rights and protection conditions are satisfied: use its bounded canonical collection procedure. §6.3.5.5 — Select a credential source on a controlled host Ruled out in this context Only ordinary-user access is available: remain with user-readable sources or escalate first. §6.2.3.1 — Interpret scripts, configuration and exposed secrets Inconclusive / failed check Collection is denied/empty: identify the failed layer and retain uncertainty. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary <h2

title: 6.3.5.5 Tooling and complete procedure
text: id="6355-tooling-and-complete-procedure">6.3.5.5 Tooling and complete procedure whoami, tasklist, reg and CIM are baseline state checks. Mimikatz, offline parsers and secretsdump are source-specific later choices, with exact privileges and protections documented in the owning procedure. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants . Study mechanisms and alternatives . Shared concepts . §6.6.2 — Choose an approach .

title: 6.5.1 Diagnose the failed boundary
text: id="651-diagnose-the-failed-boundary">6.5.1 Diagnose the failed boundary §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output The exact command/context, observed output or error, current source host and the last boundary known to work. Where to look: Walk inward: invocation/runtime -> route -> listener/protocol/TLS -> identity syntax -> authentication -> authorization -> operation -> output channel. Record whether the command reached each layer. Expected behavior / secure boundary: Read restrictions and incomplete collection are common. Empty data can mean a filter, scope, pagination, permission or freshness issue. A tool crash before network traffic says nothing about the target's vulnerability state. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.5.1.1 Baseline selection
text: id="6511-baseline-selection">6.5.1.1 Baseline selection Select the prerequisite check indicated by the interpreted result below. This chooser requires no additional tool or state change. What this checks: Use the error to choose one discriminating check. Repeating the same command or switching tool names without changing a hypothesis usually adds little evidence. <h2

title: 6.5.1.2 Interpret the output
text: id="6512-interpret-the-output">6.5.1.2 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. A: connection timed out B: STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE C: authentication succeeded; ACCESS_DENIED on file read D: collection complete; zero Session edges Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at A timeout No successful protocol exchange was established. Check source route, listener and relevant transport. §6.1.2.1 — Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity B logon failure The selected authentication attempt failed. Check local/domain syntax, material type, account state and protocol support. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope C denied file read Authentication and object authorization had different outcomes. Retain valid identity; inspect other permitted objects or rights. §6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON D zero Session edges The collection has no session evidence. Check whether Session was collected, collection rights and freshness; do not assert no users are logged on. §6.2.8.1 — Enumerate using BloodHound and validate relationships Stop when: The last successful layer and one discriminating next check are recorded. Revisit only when: New evidence changes the failed layer; do not repeat a disproven path unchanged. <h2

title: 6.5.1.3 Decide and continue
text: id="6513-decide-and-continue">6.5.1.3 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation The failed condition is domain naming, DC selection or time context: repair that dependency before retrying the relevant protocol. §6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain Ruled out in this context The condition is disproven in this context: close that hypothesis and choose another lead. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups Inconclusive / failed check Evidence is unavailable: label inconclusive and record what would resolve it. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary <h2

title: 6.5.1.4 Tooling and complete procedure
text: id="6514-tooling-and-complete-procedure">6.5.1.4 Tooling and complete procedure Use the smallest relevant native or protocol-specific check already linked by the chosen investigation. No additional failure-scanner or universal automation tool is required. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants . Study mechanisms and alternatives . Shared concepts . §6.6.2 — Choose an approach .

title: 6.2.3 Interpret scripts, configuration and exposed secrets
text: id="623-interpret-scripts-configuration-and-exposed-secrets">6.2.3 Interpret scripts, configuration and exposed secrets §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output Read permission to a particular file. Write permission or an execution trigger has not been established. Where to look: Read the selected file and its referenced configuration paths. Look for server/database names, service identities, connection strings, deployment secrets and legacy preference XML. For a writable script, identify who consumes it and when before claiming execution. Expected behavior / secure boundary: Scripts often contain harmless paths and usernames. Sensitive secrets should not be available to unrelated readers. A writable file becomes an execution opportunity only if a useful consumer actually executes or loads the controlled content. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.2.3.1 Baseline — Shell
text: id="6231-baseline--shell">6.2.3.1 Baseline — Shell Run: Kali / Linux, working copy. Requires: Selected SYSVOL files already retrieved into ./sysvol; matching legacy cpassword artifact. Effect: Reads local files and decrypts a candidate offline; no login validation. grep -Rni 'cpassword' ./sysvol gpp-decrypt 'C_PASSWORD' What this checks: This command is the conditional legacy-GPP branch, not a universal SYSVOL step. A cpassword attribute is a specific clue to a recoverable stored value; ordinary policy XML is not. General file inspection and selective retrieval are covered on the shares page. <h2

title: 6.2.3.2 Interpret the output
text: id="6232-interpret-the-output">6.2.3.2 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. <Properties userName="EXAMPLE\svc_deploy" cpassword="SYNTHETIC_PLACEHOLDER" /> Another file: \\APP01\Deploy\install.ps1 Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at userName + cpassword A legacy preference credential candidate, not a validated login. Preserve context privately; recover using the source procedure and validate the resulting account/material. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope APP01 path A newly discovered application/deployment location. Add it to the map, establish scope and test access. §6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights A script is writable Control of a file only. Identify the consumer, run-as identity and trigger; do not assume logon scripts run as SYSTEM. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions Stop when: The selected artifact is classified and its useful references or secret candidates are recorded. Revisit only when: A new readable path, decryption context or consuming process appears. <h2

title: 6.2.3.3 Decide and continue
text: id="6233-decide-and-continue">6.2.3.3 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation A recovered candidate authenticates: map its exact identity and useful rights. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope Ruled out in this context The password is stale/disabled or the consumer never reaches the file: reject that proposed transition. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups Inconclusive / failed check An attribute/path is missing or permissions prevent inspection: keep that branch inconclusive. §6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON <h2

title: 6.2.3.4 Tooling and complete procedure
text: id="6234-tooling-and-complete-procedure">6.2.3.4 Tooling and complete procedure Existing SMB/native file readers are sufficient for ordinary inspection. gpp-decrypt is only the legacy cpassword branch; do not add a cracking workflow without a matching artifact. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants . Study mechanisms and alternatives . Shared concepts . §6.6.2 — Choose an approach .

title: 6.6.1 AD terminology and output fields
text: id="661-ad-terminology-and-output-fields">6.6.1 AD terminology and output fields §6 — Chapter 6 | 6.6 Study aids <h2

title: 6.6.1.1 SID
text: id="6611-sid">6.6.1.1 SID A security identifier names a principal. Resolve the account/domain and controlled group membership before treating an ACE as usable. <h2

title: 6.6.1.2 memberOf
text: id="6612-memberof">6.6.1.2 memberOf A direct membership backlink. It is not a complete list of nested memberships, primary-group relationships or effective rights. <h2

title: 6.6.1.3 SPN
text: id="6613-spn">6.6.1.3 SPN A service principal name associates a Kerberos service instance with an account. It is not a password-strength or reachability result. <h2

title: 6.6.1.4 ACE
text: id="6614-ace">6.6.1.4 ACE One access-control entry: trustee, operation, allow/deny and applicability. It is not the whole effective-access decision. <h2

title: 6.6.1.5 DACL
text: id="6615-dacl">6.6.1.5 DACL The discretionary ACL describing access rules on an object. Evaluate the relevant complete rules and trustee context. <h2

title: 6.6.1.6 ObjectAceType
text: id="6616-objectacetype">6.6.1.6 ObjectAceType A GUID identifying the attribute, property set or extended operation scoped by an object-specific ACE; interpret it with the right and object type. <h2

title: 6.6.1.7 ActiveDirectoryRights
text: id="6617-activedirectoryrights">6.6.1.7 ActiveDirectoryRights Operations represented by an AD ACE. A displayed right still needs trustee, deny, inheritance and object-specific applicability checks. <h2

title: 6.6.1.8 SecurityIdentifier
text: id="6618-securityidentifier">6.6.1.8 SecurityIdentifier The trustee SID field commonly emitted by PowerView Get-DomainObjectAcl. Resolve it separately; -ResolveGUIDs resolves operation GUIDs, not every principal name. <h2

title: 6.6.1.9 IdentityReference
text: id="6619-identityreference">6.6.1.9 IdentityReference A principal-reference property used by some ACL APIs. Do not assume every PowerView object emits it; inspect the returned properties when a projection is blank. <h2

title: 6.6.1.10 integrity level
text: id="66110-integrity-level">6.6.1.10 integrity level A Windows mandatory-integrity label on the current token. Medium integrity and membership in Administrators do not establish an elevated usable token. <h2

title: 6.6.1.11 token
text: id="66111-token">6.6.1.11 token A process/logon security context. Group attributes, privileges, integrity and network credentials affect different operations. <h2

title: 6.6.1.12 LUID
text: id="66112-luid">6.6.1.12 LUID A locally unique identifier used for a logon session. It is not the domain SID, and another session cache generally needs additional access. <h2

title: 6.6.1.13 TGT
text: id="66113-tgt">6.6.1.13 TGT A ticket-granting ticket for a realm, used to request service tickets when its identity, lifetime and KDC conditions are valid. <h2

title: 6.6.1.14 service ticket
text: id="66114-service-ticket">6.6.1.14 service ticket A Kerberos ticket targeting a service/SPN. Authentication with it still leaves service authorization to be checked. <h2

title: 6.6.1.15 KDC
text: id="66115-kdc">6.6.1.15 KDC The Kerberos key distribution service. Route, realm, DNS/SPN and time failures differ from rejected credentials. <h2

title: 6.6.1.16 effective permission
text: id="66116-effective-permission">6.6.1.16 effective permission The operation actually allowed after the current trustee memberships, allow/deny rules, scope, inheritance and object-specific restrictions are considered. <h2

title: 6.6.1.17 authentication
text: id="66117-authentication">6.6.1.17 authentication Establishing an identity through a protocol. Success does not automatically permit a share read, remote logon or execution. <h2

title: 6.6.1.18 authorization
text: id="66118-authorization">6.6.1.18 authorization The permission decision for the requested object or operation after identity context is established. <h2

title: 6.6.1.19 inconclusive
text: id="66119-inconclusive">6.6.1.19 inconclusive The available observation cannot establish or rule out the hypothesis. Name the missing evidence and the check that could resolve it. <h2

title: 6.6.1.20 HasSession
text: id="66120-hassession">6.6.1.20 HasSession A time-sensitive collected computer/user session relationship. Check source, freshness and host control; it does not guarantee readable or reusable credentials. <h2

title: 6.6.1.21 AdminTo
text: id="66121-adminto">6.6.1.21 AdminTo A candidate administrative relationship to a computer. Validate current rights, route, compatible service and token/policy constraints. <h2

title: 6.6.1.22 AddMember
text: id="66122-addmember">6.6.1.22 AddMember A candidate right to change group membership. Verify the controlled trustee and effective member-write permission, then separately check what membership enables. <h2

title: 6.6.1.23 DCOnly
text: id="66123-dconly">6.6.1.23 DCOnly A SharpHound collection choice focused on DC/directory data. It does not establish live workstation-session coverage. Use the field together with its object, identity and operation. A vocabulary match alone never proves a useful attack path. PowerView ACL implementation | Shared mechanisms

title: 6.2.6 Validate host-specific access rights
text: id="626-validate-host-specific-access-rights">6.2.6 Validate host-specific access rights §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output Known credentials and scoped candidate hosts. A directory group or graph edge suggests a host right but does not prove service reachability. Where to look: Check host-specific administrative and remote-logon rights, reachable service ports and endpoint policy. Prioritize hosts connected to your group memberships or application clues instead of trying every execution tool everywhere. Expected behavior / secure boundary: Ordinary domain membership does not grant local administration on every computer. SMB authentication , share access, WinRM execution and RDP logon are separate authorizations. Administrative SMB context is host-specific. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.2.6.1 Baseline — Shell
text: id="6261-baseline--shell">6.2.6.1 Baseline — Shell Run: Kali / Linux. Requires: SMB route, explicit credentials and correctly scoped account identity. Effect: Authenticates to the selected host; authentication may generate logs and affect lockout state. nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares What this checks: NetExec validates the selected SMB account context. A success label concerns that protocol and host. Its administrative indicator is a lead for service-control access, not proof of an existing shell or rights over the directory. <h2

title: 6.2.6.2 Interpret the output
text: id="6262-interpret-the-output">6.2.6.2 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. SMB APP01 445 [+] EXAMPLE\analyst:PASSWORD (Pwn3d!) SMB DB01 445 [+] EXAMPLE\analyst:PASSWORD WinRM APP01: Access is denied Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at APP01 administrative indicator The tool reports administrative SMB context on APP01. Check an appropriate SMB execution mechanism and its prerequisites. §6.4.3.1 — Execute using SMB or WMI mechanisms DB01 authentication success The identity authenticated over SMB. Enumerate relevant shares/rights; no execution follows automatically. §6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON WinRM denied That endpoint denied this attempt. Check endpoint authorization and account syntax; preserve SMB evidence. §6.4.2.1 — Access using WinRM or RDP Stop when: The selected protocol authentication and operation-specific authorization are distinguished. Revisit only when: New credentials, host policy, endpoint rights or connectivity appears. <h2

title: 6.2.6.3 Decide and continue
text: id="6263-decide-and-continue">6.2.6.3 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation A reachable service authorizes the needed operation: choose its matching access method. §6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism Ruled out in this context One endpoint denies access: rule out only that endpoint/current context. §6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON Inconclusive / failed check Port or protocol preflight failed: diagnose routing before judging credentials. §6.1.2.1 — Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity <h2

title: 6.2.6.4 Tooling and complete procedure
text: id="6264-tooling-and-complete-procedure">6.2.6.4 Tooling and complete procedure NetExec provides protocol-specific candidates on Kali. Built-in/native checks and PowerView Find-LocalAdminAccess are alternatives; host RPC/firewall restrictions affect coverage. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants . Study mechanisms and alternatives . Shared concepts . §6.6.2 — Choose an approach .

title: 6.3.4 Kerberoasting — selection and output
text: id="634-kerberoasting--selection-and-output">6.3.4 Kerberoasting — selection and output §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A valid domain identity, selected SPN -owning account, usable KDC route and a reason its resulting identity matters. Where to look: Enumerate SPNs first. Rank the owning account's groups/rights, account type and likely password feasibility, then request only the relevant ticket material. Map any recovered identity back to host and object rights. Expected behavior / secure boundary: Authenticated service-ticket requests are normal Kerberos behavior. Their offline-guessable encrypted component creates a password-strength issue for susceptible accounts; SPN presence alone is not a misconfiguration. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.3.4.1 Enumerate without requesting tickets — Shell
text: id="6341-enumerate-without-requesting-tickets--shell">6.3.4.1 Enumerate without requesting tickets — Shell Run: Kali / Linux with Impacket. Requires: Valid domain identity and directory route. Effect: Enumerates SPNs without the displayed command requesting every TGS. impacket-GetUserSPNs -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER' <h2

title: 6.3.4.2 Request one selected user — Shell
text: id="6342-request-one-selected-user--shell">6.3.4.2 Request one selected user — Shell Run: Kali / Linux with Impacket. Requires: Valid domain identity, selected account/SPN and KDC route. Effect: Requests selected offline ticket material; no verified password is implied. impacket-GetUserSPNs -request-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile kerberoast-TARGET_USER.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' What this checks: The enumeration form lists account/SPN candidates without requesting all service tickets . The selected request form in the owning procedure narrows collection; a returned cipher still needs a verified offline guess. <h2

title: 6.3.4.3 Interpret the output
text: id="6343-interpret-the-output">6.3.4.3 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. ServicePrincipalName: MSSQLSvc/DB01.example.test:1433 Name: svc_reports MemberOf: Reporting Operators Cipher prefix: $krb5tgs$23$ Cracking result: Exhausted Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at svc_reports + SPN A service-identity candidate. Establish why its rights are useful before spending on guessing. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups $krb5tgs$23$ An RC4 TGS verifier if the full material was returned. Select the matching format; other encryption types require other modes. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope Exhausted The tested candidate strategy found no matching password. Do not infer that the account has no password or the target is patched; improve justified candidates or move on. §6.3.4.1 — Kerberoasting — selection and output Stop when: A selected account has a justified value/feasibility decision and any returned material is classified. Revisit only when: New account rights or an evidence-backed candidate strategy changes feasibility. <h2

title: 6.3.4.4 Decide and continue
text: id="6344-decide-and-continue">6.3.4.4 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation Useful account plus recovered verified password: validate its identity/access and re-enumerate. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope Ruled out in this context No useful downstream rights or infeasible password strategy: deprioritize. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions Inconclusive / failed check Ticket request failed: diagnose account/SPN, authentication , KDC and encryption separately. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary <h2

title: 6.3.4.5 Tooling and complete procedure
text: id="6345-tooling-and-complete-procedure">6.3.4.5 Tooling and complete procedure Kali impacket-GetUserSPNs is the baseline; Rubeus is a Windows alternative. Match returned cipher format to installed Hashcat/John support; no online spraying is implied. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants . Study mechanisms and alternatives . Shared concepts . §6.6.2 — Choose an approach .

title: 6.3.8 Validate LAPS and gMSA read access
text: id="638-validate-laps-and-gmsa-read-access">6.3.8 Validate LAPS and gMSA read access §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A selected computer or managed service account and evidence of the relevant delegated secret-read/decryption rights. Where to look: Inspect the applicable LAPS schema/attributes and read permissions on the named computer; for gMSA inspect the allowed managed-password readers and resulting blob format. Tie the material to its exact host/account. Expected behavior / secure boundary: LAPS and gMSA are protective management mechanisms. Merely seeing their objects is not a vulnerability. Secret-bearing attributes should be restricted; encrypted Windows LAPS content additionally depends on permitted decryption context. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.3.8.1 Baseline — Shell
text: id="6381-baseline--shell">6.3.8.1 Baseline — Shell Run: Kali / Linux with bloodyAD. Requires: LDAP authentication , matching schema/object and effective secret-read/decryption rights. Effect: Reads selected sensitive attributes; does not grant those rights. <h3

title: 6.3.8.1.1 Classic LAPS: password for the relevant computer's local administrator
text: id="63811-classic-laps-password-for-the-relevant-computers-local-administrator">6.3.8.1.1 Classic LAPS: password for the relevant computer's local administrator # Classic LAPS: password for the relevant computer's local administrator bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ get object 'COMPUTER$' --attr ms-Mcs-AdmPwd <h3

title: 6.3.8.1.2 Windows LAPS: returned content/format depends on schema and protection
text: id="63812-windows-laps-returned-contentformat-depends-on-schema-and-protection">6.3.8.1.2 Windows LAPS: returned content/format depends on schema and protection # Windows LAPS: returned content/format depends on schema and protection bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ get object 'COMPUTER$' --attr msLAPS-Password <h3

title: 6.3.8.1.3 gMSA: inspect the allowed managed-password attribute
text: id="63813-gmsa-inspect-the-allowed-managed-password-attribute">6.3.8.1.3 gMSA: inspect the allowed managed-password attribute # gMSA: inspect the allowed managed-password attribute bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ get object 'GMSA$' --attr msDS-ManagedPassword What this checks: The examples query selected attributes under an explicit identity. Classic and Windows LAPS use different attributes/formats. A gMSA managed-password blob must be decoded by a compatible implementation before treating derived key material as an authentication input. <h2

title: 6.3.8.2 Interpret the output
text: id="6382-interpret-the-output">6.3.8.2 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Computer: APP01$ Attribute: ms-Mcs-AdmPwd Result: readable value (redacted) gMSA result: encoded managed-password blob Another result: attribute absent Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at APP01 LAPS value A secret associated with that computer's managed local account. Establish the actual account name/current value and validate on APP01. §6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism gMSA blob Structured managed-password material. Decode with the documented compatible tool; it is not a ready-to-use NT hash string. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope Attribute absent Could be schema, empty data, permissions or wrong object. Do not conclude LAPS is disabled from this output alone. §6.3.8.1 — Validate LAPS and gMSA read access Stop when: The named account/host, attribute format and effective read/decryption boundary are known. Revisit only when: Secret rotation, schema, identity or delegated read/decryption rights changes. <h2

title: 6.3.8.3 Decide and continue
text: id="6383-decide-and-continue">6.3.8.3 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation Permitted read/decryption yields typed material: map its account and compatible access. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope Ruled out in this context The identity lacks the necessary read/decryption right: rule out this branch in that context. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions Inconclusive / failed check Missing/opaque attribute: distinguish schema, protection and access before deciding. §6.3.8.1 — Validate LAPS and gMSA read access <h2

text: id="6384-tooling-and-complete-procedure">6.3.8.4 Tooling and complete procedure bloodyAD queries selected LDAP attributes; Windows LAPS/RSAT tools and compatible gMSA parsers are alternatives. Directory authentication, schema support and effective rights are prerequisites. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants . Study mechanisms and alternatives . Shared concepts . §6.6.2 — Choose an approach .

title: 6.3.2 Classify recovered credentials and their scope
text: id="632-classify-recovered-credentials-and-their-scope">6.3.2 Classify recovered credentials and their scope §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output An artifact from a readable file, selected offline recovery or an authorized credential source. Its account scope and format must be known before reuse. Where to look: Record the artifact's originating host/object, username/domain or local scope, format and protection. Distinguish plaintext, NT hash, Net-NTLM response, cached verifier, AES key, TGT / service ticket , certificate and DPAPI blob. Expected behavior / secure boundary: A hash-looking string is not a universal login credential. SAM describes local accounts; cached-domain verifiers are not directly passable NT hashes; a service ticket is scoped to a service identity and validity conditions. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.3.2.1 Baseline selection
text: id="6321-baseline-selection">6.3.2.1 Baseline selection Select the prerequisite check indicated by the interpreted result below. This chooser requires no additional tool or state change. What this checks: Choose the next protocol only after classification. This prevents running password, hash and ticket commands against incompatible material. Use the complete credential procedures for format-specific cracking and validation. <h2

title: 6.3.2.2 Interpret the output
text: id="6322-interpret-the-output">6.3.2.2 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Origin: APP01 matched SAM + SYSTEM Account: Administrator Material: local-account NT hash Target proposal: DC01 / domain Administrator Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at APP01 SAM A member host's local-account source. Treat the identity as APP01-local unless separate evidence supports reuse. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope NT hash May support NTLM-compatible authentication . Check tool support, target account scope, NTLM policy and authorization . §6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism Proposed domain Administrator use An unsupported identity jump. Do not equate local and domain accounts sharing a name. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups Stop when: Origin, identity scope, material format and a compatible next use are established. Revisit only when: A new parser result, account mapping or protocol policy changes compatibility. <h2

title: 6.3.2.3 Decide and continue
text: id="6323-decide-and-continue">6.3.2.3 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation Format, identity, route and supported authentication match: validate the selected service. §6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism Ruled out in this context A captured response is supplied to an NT-hash option: reject that incompatible use. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope Inconclusive / failed check Origin/format/account is unknown: classify it before trying tools. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope <h2

title: 6.6.2 Choose an enumeration approach
text: id="662-choose-an-enumeration-approach">6.6.2 Choose an enumeration approach §6 — Chapter 6 | 6.6 Study aids <h2

title: 6.6.2.1 Choose by question and access
text: id="6621-choose-by-question-and-access">6.6.2.1 Choose by question and access Approach Choose it when Needs Useful output / limit Native Windows net.exe / domain tools You need a quick user/group/domain baseline from the current Windows context Usable domain/network context; relevant tool installed Names, memberships and policy; expand interesting objects and do not assume complete nesting RSAT ActiveDirectory cmdlets The module is already installed and structured properties or recursive membership help Module availability plus permitted authenticated queries Structured objects; absence of RSAT is an environment fact, not a missing domain ADSI / DirectorySearcher Windows has no RSAT and you can state the LDAP query explicitly .NET directory access, correct base/filter and authentication context Built-in controlled queries; handle paging and missing/denied attributes Authenticated LDAP from Kali You have credentials and directory connectivity but no suitable Windows session Correct server/naming context, supported auth/TLS and client Attribute/filter control; a successful bind is not every attribute or operation right Reviewed PowerView Convenient AD-oriented joins/ACL queries answer the current question Compatible loaded script and correct network identity Rich candidates; confirm emitted fields and effective rights rather than trusting a familiar command name SharpHound / BloodHound You need relationships across objects and candidate paths Compatible collector/deployment, directory context and extra rights/routes for selected host methods Join/rank edges; manual validation, collection scope and freshness remain necessary SMB file interaction The question concerns share/list/read/write boundaries or a referenced artifact Reachable server, explicit account scope and object rights Actual file access; it does not substitute for LDAP object rights or prove execution <h2

title: 6.6.2.2 Selection examples
text: id="6622-selection-examples">6.6.2.2 Selection examples No RSAT on a domain client -> start with native reads, then ADSI or reviewed PowerView for the missing attribute. A graph shows AddMember -> query the exact group ACE and trustee membership. A share lists a configuration -> test that file read, not a graph query. Directory-only collection has no sessions -> collect only the useful selected-host evidence when its prerequisites are met. <h2

title: 6.6.2.3 Stop and switch
text: id="6623-stop-and-switch">6.6.2.3 Stop and switch Switch when the current method cannot observe the required fact, its query is denied, or its coverage is insufficient. Record that limitation first. A different tool performing the same denied operation under the same identity may add no evidence. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions §6.2.8.1 — Enumerate using BloodHound and validate relationships Complete native, ADSI, LDAP and PowerView commands

title: 6.4.1 Select a compatible remote-access mechanism
text: id="641-select-a-compatible-remote-access-mechanism">6.4.1 Select a compatible remote-access mechanism §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output Typed credential material, exact local/domain account scope, a scoped target and a known source/vantage point. Where to look: First check the service route. Then separate authentication from the target service's authorization . Match password, NT hash, AES key, ticket or certificate to a client that supports that mechanism. Expected behavior / secure boundary: A valid account can lack every remote-logon right on a given host. SMB service control, WinRM, WMI/DCOM and RDP have different services, ports and policy requirements. One protocol's success cannot be generalized to another. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.4.1.1 Baseline preflight from Kali
text: id="6411-baseline-preflight-from-kali">6.4.1.1 Baseline preflight from Kali Run: Kali / Linux. Requires: Explicit scoped destination and the actual initiating route. Effect: Network probing/service identification; no authentication or execution proof. nmap -Pn -sT -sV -p 135,139,445,3389,5985,5986 TARGET -oN movement-preflight.txt getent hosts TARGET_HOST date -u <h2

title: 6.4.1.2 Preflight using Windows PowerShell
text: id="6412-preflight-using-windows-powershell">6.4.1.2 Preflight using Windows PowerShell Run: Windows PowerShell. Requires: Actual initiating host, DNS and selected TCP connectivity. Effect: Reads resolver/time state and makes selected connection checks. Resolve-DnsName TARGET_HOST Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 445 Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 5985 Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 3389 w32tm /query /status What this checks: Preflight checks transport from the host that will initiate the actual connection. RPC endpoint mapper reachability alone does not prove dynamic RPC will work. A tunnel must carry the selected protocol and name resolution. <h2

title: 6.4.1.3 Interpret the output
text: id="6413-interpret-the-output">6.4.1.3 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Source: Kali via SOCKS TARGET: TCP/445 reachable; TCP/5985 refused Credential: domain NT hash SMB authentication: succeeds; administrative rights unverified Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at 445 reachable A transport route to SMB. Validate supported NTLM authentication and required share/service-control rights. §6.4.3.1 — Execute using SMB or WMI mechanisms 5985 refused No usable WinRM listener was reached at that endpoint. Do not repeat WinRM password guesses to solve a listener problem. §6.4.2.1 — Access using WinRM or RDP NT hash A potential NTLM input. Choose a client supporting it; ordinary password-only RDP is not equivalent. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope Stop when: Material type, route and one endpoint-specific authorization hypothesis are matched. Revisit only when: A new identity, listener, route or endpoint permission changes the match. <h2

title: 6.4.1.4 Decide and continue
text: id="6414-decide-and-continue">6.4.1.4 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation SMB connectivity, compatible authentication and the selected service-control execution rights are verified: use the SMB mechanism section. §6.4.3.1 — Execute using SMB or WMI mechanisms Ruled out in this context The method requires rights or a transport you lack: choose a supported alternative. §6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON Inconclusive / failed check Authentication succeeds but action is denied: preserve the valid account and investigate authorization. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary <h2

title: 6.4.1.5 Tooling and complete procedure
text: id="6415-tooling-and-complete-procedure">6.4.1.5 Tooling and complete procedure nc/Test-NetConnection checks are transport baselines. NetExec can validate selected protocols; Evil-WinRM, Impacket, WinRS and FreeRDP are access-specific choices, not interchangeable fallbacks. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants . Study mechanisms and alternatives . Shared concepts . §6.6.2 — Choose an approach .

title: 6.6.5 Test the notes and record friction
text: id="665-test-the-notes-and-record-friction">6.6.5 Test the notes and record friction §6 — Chapter 6 | 6.6 Study aids <h2

title: 6.6.5.1 Cold usability check
text: id="6651-cold-usability-check">6.6.5.1 Cold usability check Choose one unopened practice case. Use the numbered notes without a walkthrough or a path hint. Produce an evidence-bound next decision, not just an attack name. Bring your attempt back to the tutor for review; this page does not mark you passed. <h2

title: 6.6.5.2 Capture one concrete friction point
text: id="6652-capture-one-concrete-friction-point">6.6.5.2 Capture one concrete friction point Section number: Starting access/context: Exact synthetic output line that confused me: What I thought it meant: Missing explanation, prerequisite or link: Next check I selected and why: Assistance used: Keep actual target details and secrets in private lab records. This template creates no online submission and sends no messages. <h2

title: 6.6.5.3 Turn feedback into a bounded repair
text: id="6653-turn-feedback-into-a-bounded-repair">6.6.5.3 Turn feedback into a bounded repair Fix the owning explanation, field definition, command context or receiving link; avoid adding another disconnected page. Verify command preservation and links, then use a fresh paper case to test the repair. A tool/environment failure, documentation gap and learner skill gap are separate possibilities. <h2

title: 6.6.5.4 Measure usefulness
text: id="6654-measure-usefulness">6.6.5.4 Measure usefulness Record whether you found the right section, identified the decisive evidence, avoided an unsupported claim and justified the next check. Retention and later independent target execution are separate assessments. No score or mastery is inferred before you attempt the case.

title: 6.3.7 Choose a permission-backed identity transition
text: id="637-choose-a-permission-backed-identity-transition">6.3.7 Choose a permission-backed identity transition §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A verified effective right on a specific directory object, a useful intended transition and authorization for the selected state change during later practice. Where to look: Match the object class and right to its consumer: group member write, password reset, SPN write, DACL /owner change, computer delegation attribute or key credential. Select the smallest change that provides the required capability. Expected behavior / secure boundary: Administrative delegation can intentionally allow these operations. The security question is whether your controlled trustee has unintended useful control. A password reset replaces the password; it does not recover the old one and cannot restore an unknown original secret. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.3.7.1 Baseline selection
text: id="6371-baseline-selection">6.3.7.1 Baseline selection Select the prerequisite check indicated by the interpreted result below. This chooser requires no additional tool or state change. What this checks: This is a mechanism chooser, not a command to run every modification. Its complete procedure holds distinct command variants and cleanup requirements. Group changes often need a refreshed token /ticket and should be verified against the relevant service. <h2

title: 6.3.7.2 Interpret the output
text: id="6372-interpret-the-output">6.3.7.2 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Controlled: EXAMPLE\analyst -> Support Effective right: write member on Helpdesk Helpdesk capability: remote-management membership on APP01 Missing: refreshed authentication and APP01 endpoint check Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at Write member on Helpdesk A candidate group-membership transition after effective-right validation. Preserve current membership and select the explicit scoped modification procedure. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions Remote-management membership A possible host access capability. Check actual endpoint policy, route and updated authentication context. §6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights Membership changed successfully Directory state changed only. Verify the new token/service access; do not claim a session yet. §6.5.2.1 — Re-enumerate after an identity or host change Stop when: One useful permission-backed transition and its verification/cleanup requirements are selected. Revisit only when: Effective control or the target group/host capability changes. <h2

title: 6.3.7.3 Decide and continue
text: id="6373-decide-and-continue">6.3.7.3 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation The change produces verified useful rights: map the new identity state and continue. §6.5.2.1 — Re-enumerate after an identity or host change Ruled out in this context The target group grants no needed capability: do not modify it merely because you can. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups Inconclusive / failed check The right or cleanup plan is unclear: return to effective-ACL validation. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions <h2

title: 6.3.1 Interpret password policy before credential validation
text: id="631-interpret-password-policy-before-credential-validation">6.3.1 Interpret password policy before credential validation §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A domain query context. The goal is to understand validation risk and identify applicable policy, not begin password spraying. Where to look: Read domain password and lockout policy, then account-specific restrictions and any applicable fine-grained policy. Keep known prior failures and the selected protocol in view. Expected behavior / secure boundary: A threshold is only one part of lockout behavior. Duration, observation window, fine-grained policies, existing failures and other systems using the account matter. A displayed zero threshold is not blanket permission for unrestricted guessing. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.3.1.1 Baseline policy using native Windows commands
text: id="6311-baseline-policy-using-native-windows-commands">6.3.1.1 Baseline policy using native Windows commands Run: Windows. Requires: Usable domain query context. Effect: Reads a domain-policy view; not every account-effective policy. net accounts /domain <h2

title: 6.3.1.2 Policy enumeration using PowerView
text: id="6312-policy-enumeration-using-powerview">6.3.1.2 Policy enumeration using PowerView Run: Windows PowerShell with reviewed PowerView. Requires: Loaded module and permitted domain policy reads. Effect: Reads policy data; no password guessing. Get-DomainPolicyData | Select-Object -ExpandProperty SystemAccess What this checks: net accounts provides a domain-policy view. PowerView exposes related fields, but neither output by itself establishes the effective policy for every user or a safe guessing budget. <h2

title: 6.3.1.3 Interpret the output
text: id="6313-interpret-the-output">6.3.1.3 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Lockout threshold: 5 Lockout duration: 30 minutes Lockout observation window: 30 minutes Known prior failures for selected account: unknown Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at Threshold 5 A displayed lockout setting. Do not translate it into five available attempts. §6.3.1.1 — Interpret password policy before credential validation Prior failures unknown The account may already be close to lockout. Avoid guessing; prefer supported evidence/offline analysis. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope Correct password but denied logon Credential validity and logon authorization differ. Check identity scope, logon type and restrictions. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary Stop when: Applicable policy limitations and unknown prior account state are recorded. Revisit only when: Account-specific policy or lockout state changes; do not infer a guessing budget. <h2

title: 6.3.1.4 Decide and continue
text: id="6314-decide-and-continue">6.3.1.4 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation A justified credential needs validation: perform the scoped supported check and record its protocol/context. §6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism Ruled out in this context Lockout/rate-limit evidence appears: stop that testing path. §6.3.1.1 — Interpret password policy before credential validation Inconclusive / failed check Effective policy or prior state is unknown: do not invent a safe spray rate. §6.3.1.1 — Interpret password policy before credential validation <h2

title: 6.6.4 Unanswered changed-condition cases
text: id="664-unanswered-changed-condition-cases">6.6.4 Unanswered changed-condition cases §6 — Chapter 6 | 6.6 Study aids These are unanswered paper exercises. Attempt a case before opening its explanations. Do not execute commands or infer practical competence from this page. For each case write: observed facts; unsupported claim; missing prerequisite; one exact numbered next check and its expected decisive evidence; how the changed condition changes the decision. <h2

title: 6.6.4.1 Case 01 — Membership
text: id="6641-case-01--membership">6.6.4.1 Case 01 — Membership The account query shows Domain Users and Support. A teammate calls the account a local administrator on APP01. No host-right evidence is provided. Then Support membership is removed while the existing shell remains open. What is established? What is still inconclusive or ruled out? Which numbered subsection would you use next, and why? <h2

title: 6.6.4.2 Case 02 — Share boundary
text: id="6642-case-02--share-boundary">6.6.4.2 Case 02 — Share boundary SMB authentication and directory listing succeed. Reading config.ini is denied. A different script can be read and names FS01. Then a new credential is recovered from a different authorized artifact. What is established? What is still inconclusive or ruled out? Which numbered subsection would you use next, and why? <h2

title: 6.6.4.3 Case 03 — Service identity
text: id="6643-case-03--service-identity">6.6.4.3 Case 03 — Service identity A user account owns an MSSQLSvc SPN . No useful rights are known, and offline candidate testing is exhausted. Then a verified directory permission makes that account materially more useful. What is established? What is still inconclusive or ruled out? Which numbered subsection would you use next, and why? <h2

title: 6.6.4.4 Case 04 — ACE applicability
text: id="6644-case-04--ace-applicability">6.6.4.4 Case 04 — ACE applicability A visible member-write ACE names an unresolved SID . You know the selected object is a group. Then the SID resolves to a group unrelated to every controlled identity. What is established? What is still inconclusive or ruled out? Which numbered subsection would you use next, and why? <h2

title: 6.6.4.5 Case 05 — Collection scope
text: id="6645-case-05--collection-scope">6.6.4.5 Case 05 — Collection scope A DCOnly import contains group and ACL relationships but no session edges. A colleague concludes no administrators are logged on. Then a targeted host collection returns access denied. What is established? What is still inconclusive or ruled out? Which numbered subsection would you use next, and why? <h2

title: 6.6.4.6 Review after your attempt
text: id="6646-review-after-your-attempt">6.6.4.6 Review after your attempt Compare the reasoning with the relevant numbered chapter. General notes are allowed; record any hint and independently retest an equivalent changed-condition case later. No answer key is embedded in these cases. §6.6.5 — Record where the notes failed you

text: id="60-ad-quick-reference">6.0 AD quick reference §6 — AD Notes | §6.5.3 — How to read output | §6.5.4 — Expected behavior Start with your current access. Read the question, open one check, interpret its output and validate the missing condition. Commands are concept-study references; practical execution remains deferred until the practice phase. text: id="602-follow-the-clue--check">6.0.2 Follow the clue — check What you observed Next investigation Account without Kerberos preauthentication §6.3.3 — AS-REP material and failure interpretation User-backed service SPN §6.3.4 — Selected Kerberoasting and account value Password, hash, ticket or opaque secret §6.3.2 — Classify material before reuse A usable directory-object right §6.3.7 — Choose a permission-backed identity change Delegated secret-read rights §6.3.8 — LAPS / gMSA scope and protection Possible domain-root replication rights §6.3.9 — DCSync prerequisites Controlled host with a useful credential lead §6.3.5 — Select the credential source , then §6.3.6 — inspect tickets Certificate/delegation/GPO evidence §6.3.10 — Conditional branch chooser <h2

title: 6.0.3 Move and recover — check
text: id="603-move-and-recover--check">6.0.3 Move and recover — check §6.3.1 — Password policy before credential validation ; do not spray by default. §6.4.1 — Match the credential to a reachable, authorized service . §6.4.2 — WinRM/RDP authorization and second-hop failures . §6.4.3 — SMB/WMI execution versus its output channel . §6.1.2 — Routes, naming and pivot connectivity . §6.5.1 — Failure layer and empty-output interpretation . §6.5.2 — Re-enumerate after any identity, host, privilege or route change . A feature being present is not a finding, and a failed collection is not proof of absence.

title: 6.5.3 Read and classify command output
text: id="653-read-and-classify-command-output">6.5.3 Read and classify command output §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.1 — Failure diagnosis <h2

title: 6.5.3.1 Before running a command
text: id="6531-before-running-a-command">6.5.3.1 Before running a command Write one question it should answer. Record source host, local identity, network identity, target object/service and the access required. Know whether it reads data, requests a ticket, collects secrets, creates a session or modifies state. <h2

title: 6.5.3.2 Read in this order
text: id="6532-read-in-this-order">6.5.3.2 Read in this order Did the command run? Import/runtime failures are local failures. Did it reach the right endpoint? Names, route, listener and protocol precede account conclusions. Did authentication succeed? Distinguish it from the later authorization check. Which object/operation succeeded? Share listing is not file reading; file writing is not execution. Which exact field changes the next decision? Trustee, GUID, group, SPN , account scope, ticket validity or host right. What is still missing? State the next discriminating check rather than assuming a complete attack. <h2

title: 6.5.3.3 Worked example: share access
text: id="6533-worked-example-share-access">6.5.3.3 Worked example: share access Synthetic observations: Authentication: succeeded as EXAMPLE\analyst Share listing: Deploy visible Directory listing: config.ini visible File read: ACCESS_DENIED Remote execution: not tested Observed: authentication and listing succeeded; the selected file read was denied. Unsupported: knowing the file contents, finding credentials or having remote execution. Next: inspect another relevant permitted object or investigate the effective file permission if its contents are necessary. Retest this denied file after a genuinely relevant identity/rights change. <h2

title: 6.5.3.4 Empty output is a question, not an answer
text: id="6534-empty-output-is-a-question-not-an-answer">6.5.3.4 Empty output is a question, not an answer Check scope/base DN, filters, pagination, permissions, collection method and freshness. For example, zero Session edges after DCOnly collection does not establish zero active sessions: the relevant host collection was not performed. <h2

title: 6.5.3.5 Save a useful observation
text: id="6535-save-a-useful-observation">6.5.3.5 Save a useful observation Observation: exact output and context Interpretation: only what that output supports Candidate: useful capability it might enable Missing condition: exact prerequisite not yet established Next check: what would discriminate the hypothesis Decision: enabled after validation / ruled out here / inconclusive Keep actual outputs and secrets in private lab records. Use recognition practice for unanswered paper cases after studying the annotated examples.

title: 6.5.2 Re-enumerate after an identity or host change
text: id="652-re-enumerate-after-an-identity-or-host-change">6.5.2 Re-enumerate after an identity or host change §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A newly validated credential, session, privilege level, host, domain identity or network route. The transition must have actual verification evidence. Where to look: Re-establish host/identity/ token /network context. Revisit memberships, object rights, readable shares/configuration, service-specific host access, tickets/sources and routes that can differ under the new state. Expected behavior / secure boundary: Two apparently ordinary users can have different delegated rights. A high-privilege token on one member host is not automatically domain administration. Refreshed group membership may not be present in an old token/cache. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.5.2.1 Baseline selection
text: id="6521-baseline-selection">6.5.2.1 Baseline selection Select the prerequisite check indicated by the interpreted result below. This chooser requires no additional tool or state change. What this checks: The baseline verifies the new state rather than continuing from an assumed identity. Record what changed and revisit only the checks whose prerequisites could now differ. <h2

title: 6.5.2.2 Interpret the output
text: id="6522-interpret-the-output">6.5.2.2 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Before: EXAMPLE\analyst on APP01, user token After: EXAMPLE\svc_reports on APP01, user token New evidence: Finance share readable; local admin unverified Original failed path: Helpdesk group write still denied Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at New identity, same host A changed authorization context. Recheck relevant group/object/share/host rights. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups Finance readable A new data capability. Inspect selected useful files; do not claim execution. §6.2.3.1 — Interpret scripts, configuration and exposed secrets Old path still denied No new support for that branch. Keep it closed and follow the new file/identity evidence. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups Stop when: The new state is verified and only the checks affected by it are queued. Revisit only when: Another identity, host, privilege or route transition occurs. <h2

title: 6.3.9 Validate domain replication rights
text: id="639-validate-domain-replication-rights">6.3.9 Validate domain replication rights §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A domain identity with suspected effective replication rights at the domain root. Member-server administrator access is not sufficient. Where to look: Validate the domain naming-context security descriptor and controlled trustee membership. Resolve replication extended rights and necessary access conditions, then select a bounded account-specific replication proof during practice. Expected behavior / secure boundary: DC replication and narrowly delegated replication services are legitimate. Unintended secret-replication rights on a controlled principal are highly consequential. Successful LDAP/SMB authentication does not establish DRS authorization . These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.3.9.1 Baseline — Windows PowerShell
text: id="6391-baseline--windows-powershell">6.3.9.1 Baseline — Windows PowerShell Run: Windows PowerShell with reviewed PowerView. Requires: Read access to the real domain naming-context security descriptor. Effect: Reads replication-right candidates; this command does not perform DCSync. Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ObjectAceType -match 'Replication-Get-Changes' } What this checks: The displayed ACL query selects replication-right candidates at the domain naming context; replace the entire naming-context DN with the actual domain DN. It is not a complete effective-access calculation. After validation, the linked procedure uses an account-specific replication proof rather than full-domain collection by default. <h2

title: 6.3.9.2 Interpret the output
text: id="6392-interpret-the-output">6.3.9.2 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Principal: EXAMPLE\sync_reader Domain-root rights: Get-Changes + Get-Changes-All Account-specific DRS request: access denied Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at Rights listed A replication candidate, not the final effective-access result. Resolve scope, trustee, GUIDs and applicable rules. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions DRS access denied The selected operation failed authorization or a related condition. Recheck effective rights and identity; retain previously proven authentication. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions One account secret returned Selected domain material was obtained in that context. Classify it and preserve bounded evidence; do not infer every other objective is complete. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope Stop when: Domain-root effective-right candidates and the bounded next validation are recorded. Revisit only when: The controlled trustee, domain-root rights or DRS route changes. <h2

text: id="6393-decide-and-continue">6.3.9.3 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation Effective rights and protocol prerequisites are verified: select the bounded canonical procedure. §6.3.9.4 — Validate domain replication rights Ruled out in this context Only local administrative rights are present: reject DCSync as an automatic consequence. §6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights Inconclusive / failed check Timeout or denied operation: distinguish routing/RPC from rights and credential problems. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary <h2

title: 6.1.2 Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity
text: id="612-validate-routes-naming-and-pivot-connectivity">6.1.2 Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A known source host/vantage point and scoped destination. If pivoting is needed, first establish the pivot's real interfaces/routes and connectivity. Where to look: Draw source -> tunnel/forward -> destination service, plus DNS and any callback/delivery paths. Test the connection from the actual initiating host. Use a fixed forward for one service, SOCKS for supported TCP clients or a routed tunnel when its capabilities are needed. Expected behavior / secure boundary: A host can reach a subnet that Kali cannot. SOCKS does not automatically carry raw SYN, ICMP, UDP or every DNS request. An IP route working does not establish Kerberos FQDN/ SPN correctness. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.1.2.1 Baseline network position on Linux
text: id="6121-baseline-network-position-on-linux">6.1.2.1 Baseline network position on Linux Run: Controlled Linux host. Requires: Current shell; some process/socket ownership fields require more privilege. Effect: Reads interfaces, routes, neighbors, listeners and resolver configuration. id ip -brief address ip route ip neigh ss -lntup cat /etc/resolv.conf <h2

title: 6.1.2.2 Baseline network position on Windows
text: id="6122-baseline-network-position-on-windows">6.1.2.2 Baseline network position on Windows Run: Controlled Windows host. Requires: Current shell; some fields can be restricted. Effect: Reads token and network position. whoami /all ipconfig /all route print arp -a netstat -ano What this checks: These are network-position discovery commands, not an instruction to install a tunnel. Use the owning pivot procedure to select OpenSSH, Chisel or Ligolo-ng after understanding direction, privileges and transport. <h2

title: 6.1.2.3 Interpret the output
text: id="6123-interpret-the-output">6.1.2.3 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Kali -> APP01 TCP/443: reachable APP01 -> DC01 TCP/389: reachable Kali -> DC01 TCP/389: timeout SOCKS client TCP connection works; raw scan fails Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at APP01 can reach DC01 The pivot has a potential service path. Choose a compatible forward/proxy/route from Kali via APP01. §6.1.2.1 — Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity Kali timeout Direct Kali reachability was not established. Do not interpret it as a rejected domain password. §6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain Raw scan fails through SOCKS The tool may be using an unsupported transport. Select TCP-connect/native-proxy behavior or the appropriate routed solution. §6.1.2.1 — Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity Stop when: The required service, DNS and any callback path are tested from the correct source. Revisit only when: A host, interface, subnet, tunnel or connection direction changes. <h2

title: 6.1.2.4 Decide and continue
text: id="6124-decide-and-continue">6.1.2.4 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation The required transport and DNS path work: retry the one relevant service check. §6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism Ruled out in this context The pivot itself cannot reach the service: a tunnel cannot invent upstream reachability. §6.1.2.1 — Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity Inconclusive / failed check Callback or DNS is untested: retain the separate gap rather than declaring the whole route working. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary <h2
